ISBN: 9798300122027 DEDICATION Presented with gratitude to my beloved H.H. Sri Sri Ravi Shankar And to my beloved partner, Carly Two individuals I met who know Unconditional Love About the Book When the Wave Remembers the Ocean is dedicated to those who long to recognize the greater context of their existence. The book illustrates various aspects of spiritual growth and maturity. It is presented in a question-and-answer format, transcribing a series of meetings held between 2021 and 2024. These meetings were between students of the White Path and me, the author of this book and founder of the White Path.

As the author, I recommend reading this book while maintaining a gentle balance between the head and the heart. Use your intellect to understand and analyze the information, but at the same time, allow everything to penetrate - what you understand as well as what you do not yet fully grasp. This will allow the seeds of a new consciousness to be sown, sprout, and blossom. The content of the book does not aim to illustrate an absolute truth. In fact, it claims that such a thing does not exist. It merely suggests and points to a possible reality - one that you may choose for yourself. It truly depends on you choosing, again and again, to stay open and receptive, ready and available to meet and embrace life. I hope this book will inspire you to do so. With love and appreciation, Yaron Etzion Prologue

Imagine an ocean wave. For some miraculous reason, it gains self-awareness and becomes aware of its own existence. Naturally, it focuses only on its own ‘separate’ self, forgetting the ocean of which it is always a part. Immediately, the wave starts asking questions only a self-aware entity could ask. Why am I here? What is the purpose of my life? How can I express my individuality? Why do I have to be blue like all the other waves? Realizing that all waves are heading towards the shore, it recognizes the temporary nature of its existence and tries to swim the other way, saying, Are you crazy? That direction leads to our elimination! About 30 seconds later, like all other waves, it crashes into the sand and melts back into the ocean.

This is the story of humanity - arising from oneness, gaining self-awareness, flowing through life focused only on the illusion of our separate existence, asking questions that only a self-absorbed entity can ask, and inevitably crashing to merge back into oneness 80 or 90 years later. Whether it remembers or forgets, the wave has been and always will be an oceanic expression. So too are we – a pure expression of oneness. Introduction This book offers an invitation to a journey of self-discovery. Before we dive in, let’s begin by laying the groundwork so that the journey will be both efficient and meaningful. We will start off by exploring the four stages that a maturing consciousness goes through. These four stages are presented as cornerstones on the roadmap of the transformative process. With this comprehensive map before us, we will turn our attention to recognizing and cultivating the qualities that will support us on this path. These attributes will not only help us maintain our course but will also enable us to return to it swiftly whenever we find ourselves straying.

Once this foundational work is in place, we will be prepared to dive deeply into the practices and insights that await. Safe travels on this journey of growth and discovery. The Road Map to Unconditional Love White Path Meeting March, 2024 Q. I am a bit confused about the spiritual path and all the different possible ways to navigate it. Can you illustrate a complete roadmap of a spiritual path? A. Yes. I can outline a roadmap to give you an overview of the entire spiritual journey. The journey involves moving from a contracted, fearful identity to an expression of complete, unconditional love.

I’ll describe it as I have experienced personally on my journey as well as how it is described by the scriptures. Consider it as your user manual for the complete spiritual path. The journey involves four stages of a maturing consciousness. Don’t worry if you haven’t completed a stage or followed a specific order. Your path is unique, and the time you spend in each phase depends on your maturity and the identifications you may carry with your story. Let’s examine the overview of the entire journey before diving into more details and how to integrate them into our lives. The roadmap includes four stages: Stop the Suffering Grow Beyond Your Fears Embrace and Love Life Merge with Life Each of us experiences these stages in our own unique way and at our own pace. But for most of us, these are the stages we go through. Let’s look at each of the stages in more detail. Stop the Suffering

Suffering arises from the gap between what is happening and the idea you have about what should have happened. Emotions such as frustration, anger, and irritation stem from this gap. First, realize that you create this gap, and therefore, you can close it. You close the gap by choosing the present moment over ideas about it, and you regain responsibility and the power to change. How to close the gap: Add Humility: Remind yourself, I don’t truly know. Your intellect might try to convince you that you’re right and the world is wrong. Choose to see reality as it is, without your preconceived ideas. Choose an Opposite Paradigm: Align your ideas with reality to eliminate the gap, and, consequently, the suffering. If you believe someone shouldn't speak to you a certain way, change that belief to, ‘That's exactly how they should have spoken to me.’ Drop All Paradigms: Let go of all ideas and opinions about reality. Stop labeling things as good or bad, justified or unjustified. By dropping these stands, you are finally available to fully and intimately experience what is.

Example: In your daily life, this might look like catching yourself in moments of frustration such as when you are stuck in traffic and getting annoyed. Remind yourself that heavy traffic is simply what is happening right now. Let go of the idea that it should be different. Grow Beyond Your Fears You cannot avoid it. You must face your fears. Look at them directly and understand their essence. How to grow beyond your fears: Body and Breath - Release all Contractions: Fear causes physical contraction. Become aware of these contractions and breathe them out. Physically release fear without trying to analyze it too much. Practicing breathing techniques or yoga can help. Mind - Realize the Substance of Fear: Fear is just an idea about a possible future. Remind yourself that thoughts only have power if you believe them. Observe fear as just another thought or sensation, and it will lose its grip. Intellect - Investigate Your Fear: Dive deep into what you’re truly afraid of. Often, it’s the fear of losing control. Realize that control is an illusion.

Example: In your day-to-day activities, this could mean noticing when fear arises, such as fear of speaking in a meeting. Instead of avoiding it, face it directly, breathe deeply, and remind yourself that the fear is just a thought. Breathe the contraction out and become available to experience the present moment. Embrace and Love Life As you stop rejecting and fearing life, you become more available to embrace and love it. Appreciate the opportunity to experience the present moment fully, whether it's pleasurable or painful. Example: You might find yourself enjoying simple moments more deeply, like feeling grateful for your morning coffee or a walk in the park. Embracing life means fully experiencing and appreciating these moments. Merge with Life

This is the organic outcome of the first three stages. Unconditional love unites and turns separateness into oneness. You dissolve from an individual identity into something bigger. Tantric union is revealed between what used to be referred to as 'you' and life. This stage isn't something you do. It happens spontaneously as you progress on the path. Prepare your body, mind, and energy for the moment when grace decides to dawn. Example: You might experience moments of inspiration where you feel a sense of unity with everything around you. There is no more ‘I’ that identifies. These moments come naturally in life, and more often as you progress on the path. Final Thoughts Now you have the whole map. Use it as you see fit. Remember, stages might overlap and your journey is unique. The important part is to remain open and soft, allowing love to guide you naturally.

Enlightenment is not about gaining something new but shedding everything that isn’t you. It’s about realizing the unconditional love that is already present and allowing it to guide your actions naturally. Remain open and receptive, and the journey will unfold as it should. Four Pillars of a Spiritual Path Before diving into the details of the road map and how to successfully reveal your full potential, we need to discuss how to create a stable and efficient structure that would allow you to stay on the path, focused on your ultimate goal. If the structure is unstable, you will eventually find yourself distracted and being carried away by life’s drama, losing sight of what is most important to you. First and foremost, it is about you choosing to be free, and committing to this choice. To ensure that this choice leads to effective growth, it is crucial to keep four qualities alive on your path. Without these qualities, your development will always be lacking, and you may easily forget and fall astray.

When these four pillars are present in your daily routine, you won't find yourself, months later, realizing you’ve slipped back into the drama life offers you. Your growth will be much more precise and effective. The Four Pillars Seva: This is the attitude of service, your willingness to change the flow from outside-in to inside-out, filling the space around you with the abundance you have found within, reflecting your true nature. Sadhana: This is the practice, the daily reminder you give yourself of who you truly are and what matters most to you. It’s also the work you do to refine, perfect, and mature the vessel within which free consciousness expresses itself. Your physical-energetic body becomes increasingly healthy and less burdened by tension and entanglements. Satsang: This is the community, the sacred group of people with whom you share this journey of growth. They support your development, uplift you, and help you grow, as you do to them. After interacting with them, you feel elevated.

Satguru: This is the teacher, the source of inspiration. The Guru represents the ever-lasting invitation to repose in the Self. To return back home. To open your heart. Pillar I. Seva/Service White Path Meeting September, 2021 Q. I tend to forget the most important thing for me on the spiritual path and I get carried away by life’s distractions. How can I remember more and forget less? A. Four pillars - Seva, Satsang, Sadhana, and Sat Guru - can help us keep that intention alive and stay on track. In English, these might be translated to Service, Community, Practice, and Teacher. Let’s give this topic the attention it deserves and spend some time exploring the four pillars. What is Seva, and why is it so important? Why is it at the top of the list? These terms are in Sanskrit, an ancient and holy language of India, similar to how Hebrew was before it was revived to become a spoken language. It is the language in which sacred texts are written. Sanskrit is no longer commonly spoken in India.

The word Seva literally means ‘an act of a king’. Why an act of a king? Because a king has everything, at least ideally. A king has everything and does not act to take or to achieve. The image of a king here is an image of abundance. When abundance acts, there is no ulterior motive behind it. It does not act to take, receive, or gain something. There is no agenda behind it. When abundance acts, it simply expresses itself in action. Think about it. Think for a moment how it feels. We all have such moments of grace, but they are usually quite rare.

Almost everything we do, almost every action, has some personal interest behind it, an agenda. We get up in the morning to achieve something. We go to work and earn money. We eat to stop being hungry. We talk to try to convince other people. We help others to get praise. Almost every action we take, whether overtly or covertly, has a self-interest behind it, an agenda. Our actions are rarely completely clean of any idea, including the attachment we have to the result of the action - we do something to achieve a certain result. Even if we say, it's not for me, but for the benefit of humanity, I'm doing something noble and altruistic - there is still an attachment to the result. We do A so that B happens. Abundance doesn't think like that. Abundance doesn't do A so that B happens. Abundance expresses itself in action, and then the action itself is an expression of interest-free abundance. That's Seva.

Seva is first and foremost a state of mind where the direction of movement changes and reverses. If the movement has always been I act to get something from the outside in; The world owes me something; I do one thing to get something else; then, in Seva, the direction changes. It becomes I act to give this abundance. It’s not me acting, it's the abundance through me producing action. So, first of all, it's this different, new state of mind of giving or doing without any interest, without any agenda. Without an attachment to a specific result. The second significant thing to say about Seva is that it doesn't remain at the level of a state of mind. It starts as a state of mind but then that state of mind is translated into interest-free doing. This translation is essential. Seva does not just stay at the level of a state of mind. Seva, to be complete, must translate itself into action.

In my book ‘Available to Love’ I describe the Seven Levels of Existence we are all composed of - body, breath, mind, intellect, memory, ego, and Self. The four pillars we are discussing refer to all these seven levels of our existence. Seva/Service belongs to the level of Body-Breath. Our body acts to translate this abundance into action, into doing. Only then is Seva truly complete. The invitation is to do something with this abundance. Give it to someone, find an action, find a doing, find a framework, and find circumstances in which this abundance manifests and fills and gives. Seva is all about maintaining the state of mind of a king, of abundance, of fullness, which translates itself into action through the body.

Now let's take two steps back before we start with the questions. Why is it important to adopt a consciousness of service, a consciousness of interest-free giving? What we are doing is starting to train our body-mind complex towards a state of enlightenment, to a state of free consciousness. We are deliberately causing this movement to reverse within us - from outside in to inside out. We deliberately do this so that our physical and energetic body gets used to the new direction of flow. Reprogramming our Brain

You probably know that our brain consists of trillions of synapses whose wiring changes according to the brain's activity. If the brain is used to being depressed, the wiring of these synapses physically changes to encourage that, and then the depression produces more depression. Or the opposite - if we are used to being happy and content in this life, the wiring will change accordingly and encourage such an experience. While engaging in Seva, we are rewiring our brains to encourage free consciousness and invite magic within us; transforming from an abstract, philosophical idea to a direct experience. What we are doing in these meetings, among other things, is to describe the idea so that we have a concept of what free consciousness is and how it operates.

It's about building a new matrix, creating a new possibility in the mind so that as our mind matures, this possibility becomes more realistic and more accessible to us. When we practice Seva, we break out of the shell of me, me and the ego that says, I want, I need, what's in it for me? Instead, we act with the guiding principle of giving without any ulterior motive. We create a new movement, from within ourselves outward. This movement will gradually integrate into our lives as we devote attention, energy, time, and intention to it. Q. You say there's no ulterior motive, but there's an internal contradiction. An interest is always there. A. Okay, true. Let us agree that the rules of the game allow us to maintain one last interest. This interest is - I want to be free. This is the last I want that accompanies us. This I want will take us to the edge of the cliff. Once on the edge, the wanting will disappear and after that, THY WILL BE DONE.

This will happen without an I that wants anymore. However, this I want has a lot of power. Cases of consciousness that awaken spontaneously without such an I want are rare, especially in the modern world. Most cases are associated with people who dedicated themselves to this, for whom this was their choice, who made this the most important thing. They had an I want, it brought them to the edge of the cliff and there, the miracle happened. The grace. Q. Yaron, at the edge of the cliff you say there's no I anymore. That is, the I takes us all the way, and it's good that it does, but at the edge of the cliff, there is no I. If we are completely devoid of ego, what keeps us from crossing the street and getting hit by a truck?

A. The body keeps us safe. No need to worry. The body knows very well how to take care of itself. Our body’s awareness does not disappear with the fact that our consciousness becomes free. We live in a body. The body takes care of us and we take care of it. When Seva is present, we cause our body much less harm than we typically do in our daily lives. Our body takes good care of us. What disappears is the doer, the I that takes ownership and responsibility. The I that fills itself with a sense of achievement or failure. Everything is because of me, or everything is thanks to me, is the same thing. This separate and distinct I disappears. There is no I anymore. Q. So why was the ego created? We see a baby who has no ego and slowly it develops. So apparently, we do need the ego in this world. A. Yes, this question can be answered on different levels. Let’s look at two of the levels. Psychologically we need the ego to function properly in society, at least when our level of consciousness hasn't yet reached its peak of development. The ego drives us to achieve our goals.

On a spiritual level, the ego has a role as well. That I that wants is now focused on spiritual awakening or enlightenment or whatever goal it sets for itself. It can take us to the edge of the cliff. It's like asking why God put us in the Garden of Eden and then kicked us out. It's the same question. We were already there. Within all of us, there's this yearning, this thirst and longing, a vague memory somewhere that we were there, that we come from there. So, that's where we want to return. This yearning, the tension between where I am and where I want to be, this tension is what allows for the development of consciousness. It is the engine, the driving force of evolution. Q. So how does the body protect itself?

A. Easily and naturally. The body is connected to the present moment, it knows how to handle the present moment by itself. Part of our spiritual development is the ability to develop the channels of listening to and learning from the body. The body is very smart. It's a machine that took millions of years of evolution to shape. The body knows. We just need to listen to it and respond as much as possible. Sometimes the body needs a moment to maintain a healthy system. The invitation is to refine the communication skills with the body and to devote attention to what it wants, what it needs, and what is right for it. Again, it's not that the body stops functioning in the physical world. What disappears is the experience of I, I act, I operate, and I am the doer. There's no such I anymore. There's action, but no doer.

Suzanne Segal wrote a book about this called Collision with the Infinite. She was pregnant at the time she reached enlightenment. Immediately the question arose within her, “If there is no I, who will be the mother of this child?” When the child was born, she discovered that motherhood happens through her without an I taking ownership of it or an I that creates identification around it. The child received everything needed and grew up beautifully. There was no doer involved. Q. When referring to Seva, you tell us to start training proactively. Are you talking about volunteering, helping others, or something like that?

A. Yes, yes, and yes. Use your imagination. Engage in any action that doesn't have a personal interest behind which lies neediness and dependence. Another reason to add Seva to life is that it is the quickest way to get out of depression. Depression is fueled by the experience of Me! What about me? What will happen to me? To get out of depression, flip the question. Along with the question that flips, the direction of the energy flow also flips. You! What can I do for you? Tell me what you need. I am here for you. Find someone who is suffering more than you and fill them. Fill them with the little that you have. With something. With the last remnants of fuel, fill them up. You will see that it instills a lot of power and strength. The abundance within you starts to express itself, and with that expression, it grows more and more. Does Altruistic Action Truly Exist?

Q. Regarding volunteering, I think everything has an interest because people who volunteer find meaning in their lives, and sometimes they get more than they give. I don't see anyone doing something without an interest. Even someone religious serves God for an interest, for a better life. What you're saying is magical... I don't see it happening in reality. A. Why? We enlist ourselves for the cause, and the last interest we take to the bank is I want to be free. Not wanting gratitude, not a specific result for my action, not wanting the medal of the outstanding volunteer... nothing. I don't even want a smile in return. The only thing I want, the only thing that interests me, is to move towards free consciousness. That's it. That's allowed. That's within the rules of the game. Q. I don't know what the next three stages you'll discuss are, but this sounds like the hardest stage. A. To commit to action without interest? Why is it so difficult? Q. Because meaning is an interest. Feeling significant is an interest.

A. Give it up. You won't be significant. Let me repeat that. You won't be significant. In 50 years, you'll be six feet under. No one will remember. You won't be significant, that's it. Give up on this idea. As wonderful as you are today - who cares? Six feet... I go into action today not because I want to glorify my name or to create meaning. There is no meaning. I gave it up. The only thing that interests me, and nothing else interests me, is to get closer to free consciousness. To be a clear expression of free consciousness. That's it. All the rest: THY WILL BE DONE. I offer it as a tribute to the gods. Hmmm? What do you say? You're looking at me as if... what's wrong with him? What did he drink before this meeting?

Seva is the first pillar that builds a stable altar of development. The invitation is to add the attitude of Seva to your life. Allow it to transform into action. An action that constantly reminds you, while doing it, to remember - I don't want, I don't need, I don't insist on a specific result, I don't do it to receive. It's just an expression of abundance and fullness. It's an action that comes from stillness. The same stillness we encountered during meditation at the beginning of the session. Q. I think what makes this a bit tricky to implement is that even if I feel good because I did something good for someone, that itself is an interest. It's interesting to realize that I feel good about it. Even if that isn't ‘clean’ enough, I mean, I'm trying to think of examples that are truly clean where even that doesn't exist...

A. No rule says you can't feel good. It's okay to feel good. But that shouldn't be the driving force that pushes you to take action. If it so happens that you also feel good about it - great. There is always the cycle of energy moving - feminine receiving and masculine offering. That’s the natural cycle of life. The point is not to focus your intention on the result and your personal gain and loss about it. Within the Pillar of Seva, personal gains and losses are not the motivations that drive us. They will likely make us feel good because there's someone on the other side who will say thank you. We'll recognize the spark in their eyes and they'll find grace in our eyes. It feels good, why not? It's allowed. But that's not the driving force, that's not the interest, that's not the heart of the matter. It's a byproduct, a bonus. The driving force is always in the quality of giving. Q. It's not the primary interest, let's call it that. It's not wrong if it's there too, but it's not the main thing. Okay, that's more practical...

A. Seva starts as a state of mind. Seva is the state of mind of a king, of giving, of abundance, of fullness, without any ulterior motive. But for Seva to be complete, it translates into action through the body. The body moves and creates an expression, in the physical world, of this abundance. It doesn't stay at the theoretical level of a state of mind. The being translates itself into doing. The physical action helps the entire body-mind system to reorganize in the direction of this inside-out flow, right down to the level of synapses in the brain. We don’t keep it as a theoretical philosophy course. We go out and turn it into service. Otherwise, it remains just another idea, another concept. We're not here to learn concepts.

Q. Yet, I still notice, Yaron, that in certain circumstances, it's very easy for me to be in this state of mind of unconditional giving, to have a whole heart. But there are other circumstances where I get constricted again. So, I say thank God I still have work to do. I'm not leaving yet... Because if I were in a whole-hearted state all the time, I'd already be enlightened… Let’s Add Some Sound Effects… A. First of all, enlightenment is not a punishment :-) Invite it into your life. Secondly, your challenge is to consciously respond to the events happening around and within you. Many times, your responses are automatic reactions imprinted in you for years, even lifetimes. Something in reality happens and - bang! - you jump immediately. An idea comes up convincing you that no, no, this shouldn't happen! You shouldn't behave like this! You shouldn't behave like that! Suddenly - ping! - you’re triggered. Before you even understand what happened, you're already - boom! - in reaction. The challenge is to be aware enough to identify this button being pressed, but not to react.

Understand that our spiritual development is not meant to change the way reality behaves. It's not a new, complex exercise to fix reality, the movement is exactly the opposite. The movement is to recognize the perfection and fullness within the present moment. Reality is not broken and God is not confused. Never. The direction we're heading is to develop the awareness of reactivity within us without trying to fix the reality that caused this reactivity. We stop being automatons and robots, where a button is pressed and - bam! - we react uncontrollably. If someone presses our buttons and we tense up, there's no freedom there. We have no choice but to - bang! - jump and react. What?! You can't talk to me like that! A free consciousness can meet this button being pressed. It's okay. The button is allowed to be pressed, but we don't have to react automatically to the press. Do you understand what I'm saying?

Q. I become aware of why things are happening to me, but I don't react, and I even manage to catch myself and respond differently, not from the knee-jerk reaction. That doesn't mean I agree with everything that's happening, but I'm not reacting to reality anymore. I'm dealing with it from a different place. A. First, accept what is. Then, love what is. But first, accept what is. That's the direction. And if you react or find yourself misled, don’t add fuel to the fire by believing thoughts like, oh again... I forgot again... after so many years, I should have known already, because you’re putting yourself down again. If you see that your buttons are being pressed, enjoy this game for a moment. Add a smile and take a deep breath. Jai Gurudev. We'll talk more about this when we discuss Sadhana. What else...? Who's jumping into the water? As it's written in the scriptures, “The bashful one never learns.” Q. Is it not our nature to help if someone falls? To lend a hand? Isn’t that our real nature? There’s no need to train consciousness, just to simply remove the clouds covering it.

A. That's also a good analogy. I agree with you that it's our nature, but this nature is covered with so many layers of ego that sometimes we forget and it simply doesn't manifest. We're so accustomed, so conditioned, to wake up in the morning and ask life What can you do for me? that the option of moving in the opposite direction is no longer obvious. So, some retraining is required, consistent training, that reminds us of the nature you're talking about. Totally. Q. What do people do if their daily lives don't involve much interaction with others? Then what? A. Find an old lady and help her cross the street, even if she didn't intend to cross :-) There's always an opportunity, even if it's letting someone go ahead of you in line at the grocery store. No matter what, there's always something to do that doesn't have conditions or interest behind it. Do something out of love. Turn love into action. Find something that allows you to express your love outwardly, from within. This is the intention. I have love within me and I’m translating it into action.

Love doesn't require anything, ever. That is the nature of love. As long as there's a heartbeat, there are also opportunities to give this love. Don't worry. It doesn't have to be something grand that will be written about in the newspaper tomorrow. God hides in the little things… Pillar II. Sadhana/Practice White Path Meeting September, 2021 The second pillar of the spiritual path is Sadhana, which means spiritual practice - daily practice. Similar to Seva/Service, it belongs to the first three levels of existence - body, breath, and mind. Sadhana relates to the body, breath, and mind levels of existence depending on which practice we use. Now, why is this important? Why is practice critical? It is necessary for two reasons: The first reason is that it helps us remember. The second reason is that it prepares the vessel through which we manifest an awakened consciousness.

Let's discuss these two reasons for a moment. First, we all tend to forget, be distracted, drift after the drama of life, and return to suffering. Remember, our challenge is not necessarily to eliminate suffering in an absolute and irreversible way. Our challenge is to create a system that knows how to remember. When a gap opens, remember. Practice reminds us, again and again and again and again. It reminds us of two things: What is most important to me Who I am These are the two most meaningful intentions on the spiritual path. Sadhana/Practice reminds me. What is most important to me? What is more important to me than anything else? Who am I? Beyond all the noise. Beyond the distractions. Beyond all desires and needs. Beyond the dependencies. Beyond the drama. Beyond the confused identities. Who am I? Practice helps us remember, again and again. As we become more accustomed to this remembrance, to narrow the gap and to return to the knowledge of who we really are, so too will forgetfulness become a rarer event and the way back home will be shorter and more accessible.

Every aspect of the spiritual practice focuses on improving self-awareness and building a stable system of remembrance. We appreciate the emphasis on the longing to expand and grow, to expand the vessel through which we express our development, and to remember, again and again, who I am. Sadhana as a Way of Life Now, the recommendation is that when we enter practice, we make it a way of life. It's not some new task we take upon ourselves because, like with many tasks, we will ultimately look for an excuse to avoid it. When Sadhana becomes a way of life for us, we don't ask ourselves whether we feel like it or not. We do it because it's part of our daily life, our routine, like brushing our teeth. We naturally add time and attention for Sadhana. The practice of Sadhana itself is the part where each of us can choose. There are endless techniques to choose from, but before we get to the level of technique, let’s discuss the attitude we want to bring into the practice of Sadhana.

The attitude we bring is the longing to expand and grow the vessel through which we express our development. The way we translate our consciousness into life is through the body. No matter how wonderful an idea we hold in our minds as a philosophy or as an ideal, if our body is a place of filth and violence, the translation of that ideal into life itself will be problematic because we don't live in an abstract world, we live in a physical world. Navigating within this physical world is through matter, through the body. When we practice Sadhana, we are actually preparing and maturing the vessel (the body) so that the physical expression of developing towards free consciousness will be a harmonious and accurate expression free of flaws. We are cleansing this vessel. Just as we pass a cloth through a flute to remove oils and residues of saliva, we pass Sadhana through this vessel called I. We use Sadhana specifically to cleanse the body and fill it with prana.

What is prana? Prana is life energy. The cleaner this conduit of the body becomes, the stronger the flow of prana becomes. And the movement of prana is from bottom to top. From the first chakra towards the seventh chakra. The movement is upwards. Spiritual practice helps us to fill the body with prana like fueling the body and redirecting the flow anew, from the first chakra to the seventh chakra. There's a lot of wisdom about how the prana moves along the axis of the Kundalini, along these 7 chakras, and expresses itself in different qualities in the body. Deeper knowledge about this is worth diving into further if you are interested. When? Which? How Much?

Now, the practice itself is the part where each of us can choose. Some people are suited to a more active practice, some people to a quieter practice. Some people want to do something in a group, others prefer to do it alone. It doesn't matter. What does matter is that these two intentions we talked about are there and that the practice is part of our daily routine. Many techniques are available, but as far as we are concerned, there are no dos and don'ts. Choose the practice that works for you. The path I chose to be on is called Art of Living. There's a series of practices there that you can add to your daily routine, mainly related to the integration of yoga and pranayama. These are very precise and effective practices with regard to what we've talked about. They are both preparing the vessel and reminding us who we are again and again.

Anyone who is interested is welcome to take the basic course through the Art of Living. It's a wonderful course and the techniques taught there are very powerful and simple to implement. It's not something too complicated or advanced that only those who are very flexible can do. These are very basic and powerful techniques. I once taught an 87-year-old woman the Art of Living course and she enjoyed it very much. You can also use the meditations we've shared over time in our group or use meditations found online. There are many meditations by Sri Sri Ravi Shankar that you can find, here or on YouTube, to sit with. How much Sadhana to do? Every hour of your day, take a 30-second break. Take a deep breath… another one… bring back the attention to this remembrance, Ah... this is who I am, everything is fine. Every few hours take a break for 10 minutes to return to calm. Return to I am That. Once a day take a break for half an hour. Once a week take a break for an hour or two. Once a month take a break for 3-5 hours. Once every few months take a break for a day.

Once a year take a break for a week. Again and again, return and remember. Stop the regular daily routine, the race, and return to calm. You don't even need to get up from your chair. Just return for a moment and remember, Ah... right, this is who I am. Hmm? So, what do you say? I've been talking continuously for half an hour. Questions? Q. What other types of practices are there? Give an example. You say everyone does what suits them, so please give an example of a few techniques. A. The classic types are Yoga/Pranayam. Tai Chi is also a great tool that I highly recommend. It calms the entire rhythm of the system and organizes it anew. The most basic practice, the mother of all practices is… meditation. Why is meditation so basic? Meditation immediately takes you beyond all background noise and distractions, straight to the heart of the matter. Ah... this is who I am.

Meditation is the opportunity we give ourselves to look beyond the clouds and meet the sky. To look beyond all distractions and all the events that keep on changing and focus on Akṣara, the non-changing. Consciousness meets its nature that does not change, is not affected, and is not embedded because of events, or because of the realm of phenomena. So, meditation is the mother of all practices. Some people meditate through movement. While they are engaged in aerobic activity they enter a meditative state. A meditative state is a state where no action is taken. Imagine you are swimming. You enter a meditative state where the action of swimming is happening spontaneously and I am the observer of this action. I am not doing. I am not swimming. The swimming is happening without a swimmer. That's a meditative state.

Many professional athletes testify to such a state that allows them to reach improved performance simply because they are not busy with Ouch, it hurts, it's hard, I want to stop. They can simply remove themselves from the situation and look at it as if from the outside. The event is encountered through the vessel they called I. I like to experience meditation in nature. For example, I meet a tree, sit in its shade, and be in meditation. The invitation here is to encounter the opportunity that feels most natural to your system and to do it. Incorporate it into your daily routine. Hmm? What else? Q. Is there some threshold, some limit? You mentioned that it's recommended every hour to take a short break of half a minute to a minute. Is there too much in that? Or is it the more the merrier?

A. Let's assume most of us won't reach that amount. It doesn't need to bother you. Most of us are busy with the drama that life has to offer. So don't bother yourself with this question. Take a break for a few minutes once an hour and sometimes take a longer break every few hours and remind yourself who you are and what is most important to you. As the practice becomes your daily routine it will be revealed as the nature of who you are. It will no longer be some action you do with a specific intention. It will be the natural default. You are no longer ‘sitting for meditation’, but rather, your consciousness is meditative. Everything is meditation. Washing dishes is meditation. Drinking water is meditation. Looking at the snow-capped mountains is meditation. Talking to you right now is meditation. There is nothing that is not meditation because there is no me. There is no SELF taking ownership. Hmmm? What else? Who hasn't asked a question yet? Q. So this action of stopping for a moment and breathing, is that remembrance?

A. Yes, exactly. Remembrance. Preparing and maturing the vessel. The more mature our vessel is, the more the expression of consciousness maturing into life itself will be natural for us. What does it mean for a vessel to be more mature? Good that you reminded me... It means there is less tension in it. Identifying with changing events in our lives creates an experience of ‘feverishness’ - endless tension and internal unrest. The more tense we are, the more resistance we have to life.

What happens in meditation, or generally in Sadhana for that matter, is allowing this noise to dissipate and relax, to become quieter and quieter. Then the remembrance of who I am becomes exposed. Usually, this noise is so strong that it obscures the signal. ‘White noise’ is what it's called in electronics. When we allow it to dissipate the signal suddenly reveals itself. The practice allows us to reduce the level of tension and noise, to be replenished with prana - the energy of life. The next time we open our eyes and go back to life, the opportunity to express the remembrance of who I truly am will be more accessible, more natural, more seamless… effortless. Effects of Daily Sadhana Q. When you talk, Yaron, about a vessel, are you talking about the mind?

A. Yes. Sadhana also operates on the level of the mind, but it is less apparent, it is more hidden. Sadhana brings us to a meditative state of mind where the doer disappears. The experience then becomes natural and devoid of identification. The I doesn't identify with the experience. It's not me experiencing. When this occurs at the level of the mind, it's not me thinking or experiencing emotions, thoughts, sensations. It's not the ego taking ownership of the experience. Within Sadhana, the mind can encounter an endless sequence of phenomena without getting entangled, conflicted, or stuck in a specific experience. Then, a very significant degree of freedom is revealed, which may not always be apparent to us. Sadhana at the level of the mind allows freedom with the world of phenomena because we repeatedly, through the mind, recognize that thoughts, emotions, and sensations are events external to us. Just like a sneeze. Just like an itch.

A mind that can encounter thoughts and ideas as an event external to it, is a mind that gains a lot of freedom from this ability. We have a tendency to identify with the world of phenomena. We get swept away by the drama that the world of phenomena creates for us. We fall for the belief that thought is the same as truth. Right? And then drama unfolds because the nature of thought is to go from the past to the future…from the past to the future...etc. When we are identified with that stream of thoughts, several things happen. We long for what once was; we become entangled with some memory we have; we rush into the future expecting something to happen; or we fear some future reality. Again and again, we escape, riding a thought to what is not. And meanwhile, what is missed? What is there, right? Life itself. Sadhana helps the mind to encounter the world of phenomena without identifying with it. This is a very important lesson, a critical degree of freedom for those developing on the spiritual path. Thoughts - Have - No - Power

Only a clear mind can truly recognize this. Sadhana helps our mind to become more and more clear. Alright, did I explain well enough? Q. When you say ‘to prepare the vessel’ - to prepare it for what? A. To prepare it so that an awakened awareness can flow through it naturally and with no interference. Awakened awareness cannot translate itself into life if the body is a place of turmoil and violence. If the body stores tension, every expression of an awakened awareness will be distorted by that tension because the medium itself is tensed. What we're doing is preparing the body-mind system so that an awakened awareness can express itself in life, effortlessly, in a way that is not artificial.

In the end, Sadhana brings us to a state where it will be the default. Our body will be harmonious, our mind will allow it completely, and our intellect will no longer conflict with life. Prana flows freely with no complications or entanglements obstructing its natural flow along the Kundalini. The practice prepares the entire system, the body-mind, and our physical energetic system, to allow that flow so that it becomes default. Into such a body, such a physical-neurological-energetic system, an awakened awareness can translate itself into experience, into action within the physical world. Got it? All right? So, what else? Reality as a Reflection of the Story You Tell Q. You usually talk about our interaction with reality, resisting or accepting reality, which is some kind of interaction with what's happening outside of us. If the case is related to myself, to my self-image, to judgements about myself, is the approach you suggest for handling this similar or is there something else?

A. Everything you believe is translated into reality for you. Reality is very flexible. It's like material in the hands of the creator and you are the creator. When do we need self-image? When do we use self-image? When we don't know who we are, then we need images. Do you understand? The way out of this cage in which we confine ourselves is through self-knowledge. Self-knowledge will abandon the need for images and your life will become an expression of a consciousness that knows itself. Self-awareness, which knows itself, doesn't limit itself to ideas, misconceptions, regrets about the past, or fears about the future. It doesn't limit itself. An awakened consciousness allows everything. An awakened consciousness allows every possibility. You can create yourself to be whatever the moment invites you to be. You can be the softest, most flexible, comfortable person, and you can be the most powerful, most precise person. You can be the most feminine and the most masculine because your consciousness is no longer bound by any idea about itself.

The way out from the grip of images is SELF KNOWLEDGE. Every idea you have about life, about yourself, is some kind of veil, a veil that you place between yourself and life. Between yourself and your full potential. Every time there's some idea or concept, put it aside and move on. This is relevant to thoughts about the external reality just as much as it is relevant to thoughts about yourself. We're not here to collect ideas. We're here to continue to grow, and ideas only stop that. Do you understand what I'm saying? An awakened consciousness doesn't limit itself to ideas. It's not interesting. It's just another thought like an itch on the nose. Thoughts and ideas have no power. No power. Unless you believe them. If you believe then they have all the power in the world. So next time such an idea comes up about your external or internal reality... drop it. Q. About breathing, I would be happy if you could explain it to us and talk about it.

A. I can talk about breathing for two days. The secret to being aware of breathing is that for every thought and every emotion there is a different breath that is associated with it. We breathe differently when We’re angry as opposed to when we’re content. We breathe differently when we’re sad as opposed to when we’re happy. Have you noticed that? Many times, it happens under the radar. We're not so aware of it. When we're happy, for example, the inward breath is much more significant than the outward breath. When we’re sad, the outward breath is more significant than the inward breath. This world of phenomena translates itself into the physical world of the body through breathing. Breathing is the bridge between the inner world of emotion-thought-feeling and the physical world. Now, the secret is that on this bridge you can go in both directions - it's not just from the inside out. Through breathing you can also go from the physical world inward, creating a change in the inner world of emotion-thought-feeling.

If you think about it for a moment, this has far-reaching implications because this world of emotion-thought-feeling is very uncontrollable. Phenomena happens spontaneously. Suddenly there's a thought about something. Where did it come from? I don't know. I didn't ask to think about it. And now I'm stuck with this thought in my head. What do I do with this thought? I want you to not think about monkeys now. Can you do it? It doesn't work. You can't chase a thought with a thought. You need something else, and that something else is breathing. We can create different rhythms of breathing to encourage specific changes in the world of emotion-thought-feeling. That's the secret breathing hides within it. To help you strengthen your relationship with your breath I recommend practicing this guided meditation about the breath.

There are a few more things I will say. Breathing happens at this moment. It didn't happen yesterday. It won’t happen tomorrow. All anyone needs to do to live in the present moment is return to the breath. Take a deep breath. Ah, that's who I am. I'm in the present moment. I can't breathe later. I can only breathe now. Breathing also contributes greatly to cleansing the vessel, releasing it from tension, and adding prana to the body. So, whoever wants to know how to become a master of breathing is welcome to take the basic course of the Art of Living. All right, so just like Seva, we turn Sadhana into action. We're going to find opportunities to practice Sadhana throughout the coming week. Sometimes once an hour to remember, sometimes every few hours to take a break for a few minutes. A 20-minute break every day. Sometimes a longer break of half an hour to an hour a week. However many hours you can allow yourself to connect with nature, to connect with tranquility, to connect with who I am. To cleanse the vessel, to mature, to prepare it.

Hmm...? Next week we'll talk about Satsang and how important it is. Goodnight, big hugs. Pillar III. Satsang/Community White Path Meeting September, 2021 Welcome. Today we will establish the third pillar out of four that will help us create a stable framework for intentional growth - Satsang (Community). What is Satsang? Literally, ‘Sat’ means divine, and ‘Sangha’ means the group or society. Therefore, Satsang can be translated as the ‘divine audience’ or ‘divine society.’ It represents a gathering of individuals who come together to engage in spiritual practice and discourse. Let us practice together. We will play Baba Hanuman by Krishna Das. Q. I did not understand, did they film God here? A. How to address this question? God is everything… Q. I still did not understand this practice. A. When we open our collective heart, it becomes a much more meaningful event than when we do it as individuals. Q. But in the video, there is only one person.

A. Yes, the video is just an anchor around which we are synchronizing. It creates a frequency to which we can all align. When we align to that frequency and vibrate accordingly, it turns into a resonant frequency. Understanding Resonant Frequency A resonant frequency is the natural frequency at which a medium vibrates at the highest amplitude. When two bodies resonate at the same frequency, the amplitude doubles. If they contradict each other at the same frequency, the total sum of their superposition is zero. However, when they have the same amplitude at the same frequency, they complement each other, and their impact multiplies. Q. Yes, there is that story of a platoon that walked on a bridge with their steady march, and it resonated with the bridge’s resonant frequency causing it to shake until it fell. So, every building has to be designed not to resonate with potential earthquakes, etc.

A. You can watch a YouTube video about the Tacoma Bridge where the bridge was not designed with its resonant frequency in mind. It started shaking soon after opening and eventually collapsed. Similarly, when we sit for Satsang, we synchronize our intentions into one unified intention. The impact of our mutual intention is much higher than the sum of individuals sitting for Satsang. Satsang is a powerful practice that amplifies our spiritual growth by bringing us together in a divine society. By aligning our collective intentions, we can achieve much more than we could individually. Let us continue to nurture this pillar on our path to inner freedom. Q. Is that why group study is more impactful than studying alone?

A. Correct. In every spiritual path and religion, studying together is highly recommended. For instance, in Judaism, there's a practice called ‘BETZAVTA’ which means ‘togetherness’. The sharing that each of us is dedicated to is extremely meaningful. The flow from within outwards joins the mutual flow, making it much more powerful. Sharing, development, and opening of the heart are all much more powerful in a group setting. This is not something to hold on to as merely an idea. It is very important to realize this. Our studies are about coming closer to a direct experience. If we keep it as a concept, it is nice and has value, but that is only half the task. The purpose of Seva is to translate it into action. Sadhana is a daily physical practice. The same applies to Satsang. We need to find opportunities to sit together in the physical realm, walk together, and open our hearts together. To grow together, we are encouraged to move from the individual to the collective. Collective Consciousness

Let us discuss collective consciousness. First, forget all you think you know about it. Generally speaking, when you aim for growth, forgetting what you think you already know is essential, especially on the path to inner silence. Silence can express itself when we are free of preconceptions. What is collective consciousness? This question belongs to the group of leading questions. Collective consciousness is what is behind every phenomenon; what upholds matter and energy. If our own individual consciousness is the theater hall in which the play of our life is showing, then the collective consciousness is where the show of all life is played.  The collective consciousness allows the present moment to happen and to be experienced. It sustains it.

Somewhere deep inside, we know this (each of us with our own terminology). We remember that our private life is just an aspect of a much bigger event, a complete scheme of things. You can refer to the collective consciousness as a superposition of all the separated consciousnesses that are only concerned with their ‘own’ private stage on which their private life is showing. The sum of all consciousness. Some call it God. Others call it the wisdom of nature or the cosmic consciousness. The name is less important than the recognition of it. Expressing Collective Consciousness How open is our heart to express itself as an expression of that collective consciousness? When we sit for Satsang, that is the intention we bring with us - the divine crowd unifying individual consciousness into oneness. The frequency of the singing and the music helps us modulate our intention into that resonant frequency.

This is not something the intellect needs to control. It is something the heart can recognize. The more we are dedicated to the experience, the less doubtful and less afraid we are and the more influential and magical we become. Letting go of the need to understand and surrendering to the experience is key. It is great to understand, but it is not enough. Surrender in Spiritual Practice I have often heard people say, “I can’t relate to that.” My reply is that we are not here to relate but to surrender. It is less important that something feels familiar or comfortable, or that it feels foreign and threatens our set of beliefs or even contradicts them. Surrender has a melting effect. It leads to comfort in the face of every experience life can offer. Surrender recreates unconditional comfort that rediscovers itself as my true nature, not as a result of a particular circumstance.

Circumstances are not the reason for the inner comfort that you encounter. So, if you hear yourself saying something like, I don’t relate to this, know that you are putting up a wall that prevents evolution and freedom. You cannot be free when you are surrounded by walls. Q. It’s like you say, “Thoughts have no power.” Now you say, “Surrender has power - a melting power.” So, it is the opposite of resisting because resisting comes from some belief. A. Exactly. Resisting always refers to some idea about what should or shouldn't be, what is right or wrong, what is moral or immoral, and what is liked or disliked. It’s all about me, me, and mine. Can you hear that record? Can you hear that music? Surrender takes you beyond that record, beyond these resistances, allowing us more and more freedom to experience life. A free person does not relate to life by asking, Does this match my interests? My agenda? What will I gain or lose here? Such a person is no longer a slave to circumstances. They are free regardless of circumstances.

Now, if you listen to these words and say to yourself, Oh, I am so far away from this, or I am already preprogrammed, preconditioned to prefer something over another, to relate to something over another, my recommendation is not to believe that thought, it is destructive. If what is most important to you is awakened consciousness, you just installed an artificial barrier that prevents growth. Q. There is a conflict there, as that want of inner freedom is also artificial. A. Yes, but we said that this is the one last want we are allowed to keep on the path. It is within the accepted game rules. What is most important to us is to be free. That will drop eventually by itself so do not worry. We are invited to shed all other wants ourselves. Q. I enjoyed the experience of singing, like repeating a mantra.

A. In Sanskrit, that type of song is called Bhajan. You can sing it in Sanskrit. The meaning of the words is less important than the energy of the song and the frequency we are all aligned to. The way it resonates in our physical and energetic bodies is something we do not need to try to explain to ourselves. Sing it. Be with it. Open your heart to it - there is magic there far greater than what we can explain. Q. I agree. I joined the singing and within a few minutes, I sang out loud and was sorry it ended. I don’t want to say I related to it, but I surrendered to it. When I sit with my religious family and they all sing along, banging on the table, it has a similar effect. I can tear up out of joy. A. Surrendering in such moments brings us closer to our true nature, beyond intellectual understanding. This collective experience of shared energy and intention allows us to transcend individual limitations and connect deeply with our inner selves and each other. The Deeper Meaning of Satsang Q. What is the deeper meaning of Satsang?

A. Satsang is our willingness to surrender to this collective movement of consciousness that harmonizes around the same frequency and amplifies through that resonant effect. It is no longer about me, my own selfish attitude, personal challenges, difficulties, or karma. Satsang is about us melting into the group with a whole heart and a willing soul. The power of the group propels us forward and, in doing so, it propels the entire group forward. We melt into something bigger. Q. That is what happens to me in every session we have. I liked that Bhajan session but not the images. I think it would have worked better if I listened with my eyes closed. A. Can you say what bothered you in the images? Q. Yes, the adoration of an individual, a person. They took a person and made him a god. While the message there is that within each of us God exists, why do they turn a person into divinity and glorify him? Reidentified as the Collective Consciousness

A. That is exactly what we shall discuss next week - the relationship between the Guru and the disciple. The fact that you are aware of that irritation is very good. It has to start from there, with us being aware. Let us summarize all of what we just said into one word: Surrender. Go beyond the personal into the united. All that personal drama is washed away by surrendering and we melt into something bigger. The personal consciousness is reidentified as an aspect of the collective consciousness. That is Satsang. As you said, this is what we do in every session. Today we gave it a name, a form, but we do that every week. This is the invitation. Allow yourself to melt into something bigger. In this session, our growth joins the growth of the circle. The private intention is united with the collective intention of the group. The collective intention is to grow, develop, and evolve.

Become a proactive partner in the evolution of consciousness. Satsang is that sacred collective. To maintain effective and stable growth on the path to self-liberation, it is important to keep Satsang as a part of your life. In my spiritual home, the Art of Living, every evening ends with Satsang. Sharing, hugging, and loving the united presence. In every religion or spiritual path, regardless of the specifics of the ceremonies, the intention is always the same. Your contribution to the event is to be actively involved. Sing, ask, debate, hug. Be there. Do not hide behind someone else. Put yourself out there. It all boils down to the same question: What is the most important thing to you? Pillar IV. Satguru/Teacher White Path Meeting September, 2021

Now, let’s talk about Satguru. What is Satguru? ‘Guru’ means a teacher. ‘Satguru’ means a teacher that is divine, that leads to divinity. The teacher is merely a reflection of their student. The teacher themself is transparent. They don’t bring their own imprint. We know that everyone we meet offers an opportunity to see some aspect of ourselves, right? We know this from life. However, when we look at ourselves through the eyes of another person, their viewpoints, personal drama, expectations, and judgments are always mixed into the reflection. In this respect, the relationship we have with a teacher is unique because the reflection we encounter is entirely pure. The teacher reflects us without the interference of their own conditioning and opinions, making this relationship unlike any other.

In a relationship with a teacher, there is no mix of the observer's personal drama. There is no drama - only silence. Just like looking into a perfectly clear lake, the reflection shows us exactly who we are. In a relationship with a teacher, the reflection is completely clear and shows me precisely who I am. It’s said that in such a unique relationship, there is only one ego we encounter (not two as usual) and that ego is of the student. This provides a unique opportunity for rapid growth for those interested in moving towards freedom. The teacher is a home, a safe haven, a place you can always return to and rest. Love Story with a Guru

The relationship with a teacher is fundamentally a love story. Just as we have love stories with our parents, children, and friends, we also have a love story with the teacher. This love, however, is unique in that it is entirely unconditional. The teacher doesn’t love us because of what we do or even because of who we are. The teacher loves us for what we are - beyond our persona, skills, abilities, and even intentions. The teacher loves us for our essence. This is a compass that always points in the right direction. Whenever we feel lost, we can always return to this place and remember. That’s what I have to say for now. The rest I will answer through your questions. So, who wants to ask something?

Q. If you say, “Everything I see in the teacher is a reflection of my ego,” doesn’t that imply it doesn’t matter who the teacher is? Since I see myself anyway, it shouldn’t matter through whom I see myself. But I think it matters a lot who the teacher is. I guess my question is - how do I know if the teacher is right for me? It’s not even about whether the teacher is good, but if they are suitable for me. There is an issue of compatibility here. How do I find this out? How do I know I am with the right teacher for me? How Do You Know This Teacher is Right for You? A. How do you know this teacher is right for you? The same way you know you love your significant other, the one you feel most natural opening your heart to. How do you know? How can you prove it or quantify it? It’s something you just know. And if it’s not clear to you, then it’s likely not the right teacher for you.

The teacher is merely a reflection of your willingness to commit. If you are still wrapped in doubts about the teacher - wondering if they are truly suitable, or if you should find someone else - the problem isn't with the teacher. It’s your own unwillingness to commit. Once you commit then comes surrender. As you say, it doesn’t really matter. There isn’t truly one person at the end of the rainbow who, until you find them, you won’t be complete, whole, free, or fulfilled. That’s just a romantic notion with no substance behind it. It’s never about our partner or our object of desire. It’s all about our willingness to open our hearts and remain open. Everything boils down to that - time and time again remain open to what exists, to who is in front of you right now. So, the teacher is just a reflection of your unwillingness. If you are not sure if it is the right teacher for you, it's not because the teacher is not enough. It's because your heart is still closed, still wrapped in doubts. Criteria to Find the Right Guru

There is one bottom-line rule that applies to everyone - how much does your heart open? That’s all. End of discussion. How much does your heart open? Here are two more criteria to use in your search for the right teacher: 1. The teacher is well-versed in the teachings. They have a lineage, a heritage of knowledge and wisdom that they bring with them, which is the light by which they walk and the light by which they teach. They are an example of the fulfillment of this wisdom. 2. They don’t want anything from you. A teacher doesn’t need you to do something to earn their love or acceptance. A teacher doesn’t want or need anything from anyone. Under their guidance you grow, develop, and expand - not contract and shrink. Your degrees of freedom increase and expand. You discover yourself becoming freer and freer in their light. The more you become free, the more your heart opens…the heart opens…the heart opens. Q. Is a teacher like a Rabbi in a religious community?

A. I don’t know. I’ve never belonged to a religious community. I can say that a true teacher doesn't get too involved in the ‘doing’ of what is allowed and what is forbidden. Ultimately, the secret is not in the doing, so spiritual teachers don't devote energy or attention to it. When seekers ask me what to do, I always give the same answer, right? ‘Do the right thing.’ How do you know what the right thing is? It is what you would choose if you weren't afraid. That's it. It doesn’t matter. The secret isn’t there, so there’s no point in focusing on it. Three Types of Doubt Q. Are we supposed to surrender to the teacher or their teachings? A. Both. What prevents surrender? Doubt and Fear. There are three types of doubts. The first is about yourself, the second is about the method, and the third is about the teacher: The first is about yourself: I am not worthy. I am not ripe. This is a very common ailment. It’s also about not believing you have the skills, patience, or maturity. I still have a lot of work to do. I lack life skills. It’s too much for me.

The second doubt is about the method: This method is not good enough, not effective enough, not precise enough. I need something more dynamic, or more quiet, or whatever. The third doubt is about the teacher: Is the teacher truly sincere in their intentions? Isn’t there a charlatan hiding behind this façade who speaks charismatically? It’s very dangerous to relinquish control of my life to a teacher. What do they really want from me? These are the three doubts we will discover. My recommendation is to burn the doubt. Make a decision. If you still cannot commit because of doubt, then make a decision. Either you’re in or you’re out. If you’re out, fine - go find another teacher. Find another method and commit to it. It doesn’t really matter. There are a thousand ways to climb the mountain and the mountain itself is indifferent to the way you choose. What does matter is that you finally commit and rise above the doubt, because only then does the path become effective for you.

Some people have done spiritual shopping for decades. They attend all the workshops, meet all the teachers, and read all the books, but they don’t move an inch because they never truly choose anything. Some people are married to their partners their entire adult lives but never truly choose to be with them. They live side by side, managing some joint venture, but they are not truly committed to the relationship. The method doesn't matter much, nor does it matter what the teacher looks like or what they say. The key question is - does your heart open? Are you willing to commit and go beyond doubt, beyond fear, beyond natural aversion? Are you willing to open your heart, to be exposed, to be vulnerable, to be accessible, to be real, to be honest, and to bring all your pain?

The teacher becomes a dumping ground. Like those sites where you can dump waste. Pour all your pain, all your struggles, all your bitterness, all your frustration, all the excess baggage that just holds you back from developing. The teacher has room for it all. Don’t be afraid - they won’t overflow. But you have to agree to bring it and lay it down. Offer it and rest. Q. It would be true that a teacher reflects and gives me a transparent mirror of who I am, and in my interaction with them there would only be one ego, provided that the teacher is in a completely pure place. But that doesn’t always happen. Not all teachers are like that. If they are also ego-driven, if they haven't done their work, then that is not accurate. Finding such a teacher would indeed be amazing and I would learn about myself very quickly, but if they aren’t as you say, it can be dangerous.

A. You can refer back to the criteria I mentioned earlier and continue to operate by them. First, does your heart open? Second, does your teacher want something from you in order to love you? Under their guidance, do you feel your degrees of freedom expanding or contracting? Another important thing to understand is that the teacher is merely a reflection of the student. They can become a friend, a brother, a father. In my first book, I wrote a dedication to Guruji. I wrote that Guruji is for me a friend, a brother, and a father on the spiritual path. He doesn’t come with the agenda of I am above you. Someone once asked him, “You can't look me in the eye, eye to eye, at eye level.” His answer was, “That's right, I can't, but not because I put myself above you. You put yourself beneath me.” The Teacher as a Reflection

The teacher has no agenda. They are simply a reflection of what you make of them, like clay in the hands of a potter. And you are the potter. You as an individual and the group as a community. The collective energy of the group creates the teacher, their appearance, and their behavior, representing the knowledge they bring. What do you think? Q. Someone might study with several people but I sense that you lean towards exclusivity. I’d love to hear your thoughts on that. Or about changing teachers during one's life. A. Ah, changing teachers during one's life. You’re right. Imagine you’re walking in the desert and you’re very thirsty. To reach a spring you can dig a hundred 1-meter wells or one 100-meter well. You do the same amount of work but the deep well will likely get you to the water. The recommendation is truly to commit to a choice and avoid spiritual shopping as much as possible. Commit to the path, and if, along the way, you discover another path that becomes more precise for you over the years, then great, commit to the new path. That's good too.

For a period on my personal path, I followed two teachers. A dear friend once asked me, “How can you follow another teacher when the first one is so wonderful and complete?” We were in Florence at that time accompanying Guruji Sri Sri Ravi Shankar on his visit to Italy. We just visited the museum where the statute of King David is shown. So, I answered, “Imagine if I was asked to create the statue of David all over again. The first teacher I use as if King David himself was modeling for me while I work on the stone. The second teacher I use as if Michelangelo himself is teaching me the techniques of how to sculpt.” This can also happen. Q. Okay. I can attest that I had a teacher and, at some point, it no longer worked for me for several years. He was no longer my teacher, but I didn’t have another teacher, and I searched for a long time. I’m very glad I kept searching because otherwise, I wouldn’t have gotten here. My question - do you think a teacher needs to have certification? Can someone wake up one morning and feel like they are a teacher?

A. Hmm, there’s no university for enlightenment. That doesn’t exist. Free consciousness isn’t something we achieve or earn. It’s not the result of some action we’ve taken. Free consciousness is our innate nature. It’s the backdrop against which life happens and we don’t need to go elsewhere to find it or get some certificate or diploma saying, Oh, okay, you’ve earned it. It’s simply waking up from a dream to the truth, to reality. But waking up one morning and deciding that you are a teacher does not make you a teacher. The students define the teacher. The students are shaping the teacher in their own image. If there are no students, it is just a person talking to themself on the street… The Essence of a Teacher Many people have experienced a moment of complete clarity, whether as a momentary experience or one that has become a fundamental part of their lives. However, most of them did not become teachers. An awakened consciousness doesn’t necessarily translate into teaching. What makes someone a teacher is their students.

I’ll say it a thousand times. A teacher doesn't become a teacher until they have students. Teachers exist because of their disciples. They cannot claim to be a teacher if no one is following their teachings. The disciple creates the teacher. This brings me back to the disciple as someone on the path who chooses a teacher. It is he/she who creates the teacher. The energy and sincerity the disciple bring to the search translates into the teacher's teaching, not the other way around. A teacher is transparent. The disciple is the one who creates them and calls forth the teaching through them. Q. About surrendering to the teacher. This seems very difficult for some people - it’s a really tough point. What is he, a cult leader? What’s the deal?

A. Usually what's hiding behind this is the fear of losing control. We’ve heard stories of people who surrendered to a teacher and the teacher took advantage of them - took their money, and their relationships. So, this vigilance has its place because such events have occurred and still occur. That’s why it’s worthwhile to use the criteria I mentioned earlier to determine if the teacher is truly right for you. But the secret is, after evaluating… surrender. If you cannot surrender to this teacher, because they do not fit the criteria, find another one. A teacher doesn't have to be an authoritative figure placed above you or someone whose picture you need to light candles in front of every evening to be a proper devotee. Ramana Maharshi said that everything he knows, he learned from the mountain he lived by. Osho said that everything he knows, he learned from the river flowing by his childhood home. If what teaches you is a tree in a field or a book on your shelf, and every time you return to it your heart opens and your consciousness expands - great, that works too.

A teacher can also be someone who is no longer alive. Many people in Christianity follow a teacher who died two thousand years ago, or in Buddhism, one who died 2600 years ago. A living, flesh-and-blood teacher has advantages. The fact that they are physically present in a human body before you, continually reminds you that this realization of free consciousness is available to you. God, free consciousness, and the teacher are the same. All three are the nature of the self, just different expressions of the same essence. Q. Where does the teacher leave their ego when meeting with students? It’s hard for me to understand this lack of ego. The idea that a teacher is a mirror and comes without an ego makes me uneasy.

A. Don’t worry about that. Let go of the idea of an ego. Let it go. If it bothers you, simply focus on the fact that the teacher doesn’t want or need anything from you. If you see the teacher starting to gather demands and conditions, telling you what’s allowed and what’s forbidden, starts managing your life, your doing, then they’re probably not the right teacher for you. A teacher is like a compass - all they do is constantly point you towards free consciousness. That’s the only thing that interests a true teacher. Through them, you can always return home. The finger always points in the direction you want to develop. Part I Stop the Suffering Stop the Suffering Now that we have prepared the groundwork and fine-tuned our intention for growth, we can begin discussing the four evolutionary stages of the maturity of consciousness. We will start with eliminating suffering.

Suffering is one of the most universal experiences of human existence. Yet, what if it didn’t have to be? In When the Wave Remembers the Ocean, the first part of our journey addresses the heart of suffering, offering practical insight into how to break free from its cycles. In the journey towards spiritual liberation, the imperative to Stop the Suffering stands as a fundamental milestone. Suffering, in its many forms, is born from attachment - attachment to desires, fears, expectations, and the illusions of permanence in an ever-changing world. These attachments cloud our vision, distort our understanding, and bind us to a cycle of emotional and spiritual unrest. But what if the path to freedom begins with the decision to no longer suffer, to relinquish our grip on that which causes conflict, and to step into a state of awareness that transcends it?

Part I: Stop the Suffering explores the profound importance of recognizing suffering not as an inevitable part of life, but as a signpost pointing towards deeper truths. It is here, in the willingness to let go, that we find the key to true liberation - a state where inner peace, clarity, and a higher connection to the divine become not only possible but natural. This section will guide us through the process of understanding suffering, its roots, and the powerful transformation that occurs when we learn to rise above it. We begin with the fundamental question - how can we live without suffering? This question challenges our most deeply held beliefs about life, prompting us to explore the roots of suffering, rather than seeing it as an inevitable part of life. Is suffering truly something external, or does it arise from within, shaped by how we interpret our experiences?
