Next, we dive into specific emotional struggles such as anger - its nature and how to manage it. Anger is often a mask for deeper pain, but by understanding its roots, we can disarm it and lessen its power over us. Similarly, we confront the idea of mistakes and how to reframe what we perceive as errors or failures. These reframes are crucial, as our belief in right and wrong often exacerbates suffering, when in reality, mistakes are simply learning experiences. We also explore injustice, another potent source of suffering. How do we deal with situations that seem profoundly unfair? This chapter encourages us to shift our perspective from one of victimhood to empowerment, recognizing that life is not about fairness as we imagine it, but about how we navigate these challenges. In the chapter about self-worthiness, we discuss the idea that a single core belief - often related to self-doubt or feeling unworthy - prevents the sincere seeker from awakening.

We come to realize that reality never works against us. This message emphasizes that reality simply happens without an agenda, and how we respond to it is our own choice. Instead of resisting difficult moments, we can use them as opportunities to explore unresolved issues within ourselves, with true awareness and accepting the present as it is, even when engaging in change. We finish this part by acknowledging the importance of the story we choose to believe and identify with. That story creates the context of our existence, our self-image, and our relationship with life itself. Live Without Suffering White Path Meeting October, 2022 Q. How do I reduce the suffering in my life? A. First, what is suffering? Suffering is a code word for all the negative emotions we experience from time to time, like frustration, anger, violence, rage, revenge, and all that. In ancient times it was called ‘Suffering.’ Today, we sometimes use the word ‘Stress’ to describe the same thing.

It’s important to note that suffering is experienced in various ways such as mental stress, emotional stress, and physical stress. We can find it in all the layers of our existence. It’s the reason we cannot fulfill our potential and why we miss the unique opportunity to expand in the present moment. This is suffering. The thing is, most of us are so used to living in suffering, with suffering, that we don’t acknowledge the fact that there is an alternative way of living where suffering is not a part of the story anymore. Suffering is not a destiny or karma. You know, things happen and that’s it, I’m suffering. What can I do? This or that happened to me, or I made some terrible mistakes. You blame the world or blame yourself, and turn yourself into a victim of circumstance, and that’s it. Some people don’t even know that there is an option to live without suffering, that it’s realistic and achievable.

I am about to share that knowledge with you. I am preparing the grounds and making sure you realize it’s going to be useless for you if you don’t use and apply this knowledge. I could invent the ultimate cure for all illnesses in the world where if you only swallow one pill you will never be sick again. A magic potion. But that potion will be totally useless for you if you don’t choose to swallow it. Do you see what I’m saying? So, this is your responsibility now. Make sure that you choose to go beyond the drama, choose to live a life free of suffering. Whatever the price may be. However uncomfortable or intimidating or far-fetched it may seem in the beginning. You stick to that resolution. This is what I want. This is what I want more than anything else! What do I want? To stop suffering. Are you Ready for a Life Free of Suffering? Before learning how to stop suffering there is a fundamental question we need to address. The question is - are you ready for a life free of suffering?

This is not a theoretical question or a hypothetical question. This is a serious question to ask yourself. A life free of suffering means - no more aggression, no more drama, no more frustration, anger, or disappointment. No more! Are you ready to live like that? Honestly? Because I tell you, there are many reasons to stick to suffering. Most of humanity chooses to stick to suffering whether it is because they are not aware that there is an alternative or they choose suffering over peace, as ridiculous as that may sound. There are many good reasons, strong reasons, to hold onto suffering. It serves a purpose, and you need to consciously choose peace over suffering. It is guaranteed that if you choose a life with suffering and keep holding onto the victim position, whatever you learn here today will not work. It will just be another interesting piece of information that doesn’t affect your life in any way because you don’t want to change. Not because it’s not effective but because you are not prepared to use it.

So, before you learn how to end suffering or how to apply it to your daily life, you need to look in the mirror and ask yourself this question: Are you willing to give up suffering? Reasons to Stay in Suffering I’ll give you a few reasons why people choose not to give up suffering. It is very comfortable to stay in the position of a victim because you don’t need to take responsibility. As long as you are not responsible for your suffering, somebody else is. When will I be happy? When you change. When you learn how to speak to me. When you give me what you promised, whether it is confidence, attention, or love. When will I be happy? When reality changes. When I have more money or a different job. You know? These are all examples of what you may have in your mind as a condition for your own happiness and a sense of contentment. In this position - what can you do? You remain a victim of circumstances. It’s very easy. Even though suffering is not nice, or a positive experience, still, it allows you to stay stagnant or in a lazy position.

The second reason is even deeper. Suffering defines you. It’s an answer to the question who am I? We are so used to using suffering as an answer to this question (I am the one who suffers), and the prospect of losing that identity and remaining with no answer to that question (Who am I now that I stopped suffering?) is too frightening. I am the one that used to suffer… but that’s not relevant anymore. So, who am I now? This is terrifying. No, no… I prefer my story about suffering. I hold on to it and I use it as an identity card. This is who I am, and I can explain to you why I’m suffering. It’s very justified. Let me tell you my story… These are two examples of why people choose to hold on to the drama, to the suffering, and not go beyond it. From this point onwards, whatever I’m saying is directed to those people who look in the mirror and, honestly, wholeheartedly want to grow beyond suffering! Q. How can one make that shift in perspective?

Before we get to the ‘How’ question, you need to ask yourself do I really want to? Can you imagine yourself living a life free of suffering? Do you choose that reality for yourself? Q. It is hard to imagine. A. Yes, give it a go, even if it’s hard to imagine. Picture yourself free of the drama. Q. Yes, but, (ha, there is always a ‘BUT’), sometimes it looks like suffering is coming back by itself. A. It will come back for sure. But from this point onwards it’s important to understand, to realize, that suffering is not an external entity that comes from the outside. Suffering is self-created. Yes, you will forget for sure. You will forget many times, and create new suffering for yourself, but you can remind yourself, again and again, that you created it and you can stop it. How to Reduce Suffering

So how do we do it? How do we learn to live without suffering? I’ll give you my personal guarantee that your life can change, 100%, but only if you choose to adopt these recommendations. You may have heard this before. It doesn’t matter, you listen to it as if it was the first time you heard it. And if it IS the first time you are hearing it, excellent. Allow it to penetrate through the layers of intellect that keep on trying to determine whether you agree or disagree. I say, don’t bother agreeing to anything. Take it as a possible reality, as an invitation to check it out for yourself and see if it works. If it doesn’t work, then it’s useless, so don’t worry about it. But if it does work, and you apply it regularly, I guarantee - it will change your life. Are we ready to learn how…? Good. Okay, so I’m going to say a sentence. This sentence, if applied, carries transformative potential. Again, suffering is born and raised in the gap between what is and what I believe it should have been. That’s it!

Do you see? There is a gap. There is reality as it manifests and there is an idea I have about it. When that idea opposes reality, rejects it, or argues with it, I’m suffering. That’s it. It is just that simple. It starts with frustration I’m so frustrated that reality doesn’t manifest as I believe it should. When that frustration builds up untreated, it ferments and turns into anger. When that anger builds up untreated, it ferments and turns into all the violence and drama you experience in your life. Mind the Gap So, every time you feel that you are contracting, angry, frustrated, violent, and you get carried away by the drama and all the noise around you, consider it to be an opportunity to remind yourself. An opportunity to remember:

This is something I created. All these negative emotions that I experience are a result of my own creation. Now, I remind myself that I chose to grow beyond it! I remind myself that, more than anything else, I am interested in living without suffering. So, I stop, and I look for the gap. I give it a name. Where is the gap? What idea do I have that rejects reality? Q. Can you give an example of how that applies in real life? A. Let’s say I spoke to you very harshly. You have the idea that I should never speak to you like that. Your thoughts are..? Q. How dare you speak to me like that! A. The idea will always be a version of that kind of opposing thought. Where is the gap? I spoke to you in a certain way, and you have an opposing idea about the way I should have spoken to you. These do not correlate. That is the gap. Like they say in the London subway – ‘Mind the Gap’. Identify the gaps. Do it every time you experience stress or negative emotions. Remember, suffering is born and raised in the gap between what is and what you believe it should have been. You are Not a Victim

Naturally, the next question is okay, how do I close the gap? First, it’s important to realize your newly acquired empowered position. Usually, you feel like a victim. When you suffer, you blame, and there’s nothing you can do about it. You’re powerless. Even if you try to change reality, it’s an attempt led by your suffering, right? This is called ‘Karma Yoga’. What is Karma Yoga? Karma Yoga is an action that is born because of your suffering, your ego, and your ignorance. Of course, that leads to more Karma and more things you would need to harmonize later on, or that life would need to harmonize for you. YOU put yourself in the position of a victim of circumstances. But now, when you realize this is your own creation, YOU have the power. You created it, you can stop it. It has nothing to do with circumstances. This is a huge realization.

My suffering was never about what happened or about what you did to me or any mistake that I made in the past. My suffering was always about me rejecting reality, preferring an idea I have over reality as it manifests. When I see the gap, suddenly, I gain back the power. I can do something about that, realizing it’s my own creation, it’s my own ideas, my own opinions. I can definitely do something about that. I can close the gap. How to Close the Gap How to close the gap? The first thing you need to do is a prerequisite to the first step. Identify the gap: you should never speak to me like that. There is the way you were spoken to and the idea that you have about the way you should have been spoken to. These are not similar. There is a gap. What to do? There are three steps to close this gap: Add Humility Choose an Opposite Paradigm Drop All Paradigms Let’s discuss the three steps in more depth. Add Humility

Remind yourself you don’t truly know what should have happened, even though you have a very clear idea about it. Realize it is only an idea, an opinion. It doesn’t matter how justified intelligent, humane, beautiful, or perfect your idea is. It’s just an idea. It is important to realize and to remind yourself that you don’t know. Our intellect has this tendency to be very determined. I know! But the truth is you don’t truly know. You don’t know how someone should speak. How could you know? Did you open the book of their life and read the actual script, as it was written by the creator? You don’t know what should have happened. How could you know? Again, it doesn’t matter how beautiful your ideas are. Children should not die at a young age! What did they do to deserve that? Why should they live only two or three years on this planet? What’s the point? You don’t know, and it’s designed so you would not know. It is important to realize and remind yourself of this. Add some humility, some humbleness.

You don’t know what should happen. You don’t know what they should have said, how they should have reacted, or what they should understand. All those ideas that you have about the circumstance, you don’t know. You don’t know. Byron Katie has said, “Some people dedicate their lives to arguing with reality and reality wins only 100% of the time.” Right? Because reality happens whether you like it or not, whether you agree or disagree. It really, really doesn’t care about your opinion. The present moment is manifesting, that’s it. Remind yourself that you don’t truly know. This is like adding lubricant and allowing the wheels to start turning. Without that, it will be difficult to close the gaps. That’s the first step. Choose an Opposite Paradigm.

Choose an Opposite Paradigm to the paradigm that created the gap in the first place. Opposite = 180 degrees. In our example, instead of believing - you should not speak to me like that - now you believe - that’s exactly what you should have said, word for word, at that exact time, in that exact intonation. And how do you know that to be true? Because that’s what happened! Instead of adopting an idea that rejects life, now you adopt an idea that describes life. Why would you do that? That seems irrational. You do that because you choose to stop suffering. That’s why. You choose that over your ideas of what should have happened and how reality should exist. See? Anyway, your idea is just an opinion. Do you see that? Whether it rejects or supports life, it’s just an opinion. This is an idea you have. It’s a thought. So, now you choose to adopt the thought that describes life, instead of rejecting it. It takes some skill, but more than that, it takes your commitment, and your willingness. It requires your conscious choice to stop the suffering.

Now you have an idea that actually describes life, instead of rejecting it which means there is no gap. There is no gap! Your idea actually correlates with reality, describing it, supporting it. If there is no gap, then there is no suffering. That’s it! Now, I dare you to try it every time you suffer. Stop and remind yourself - this is something I created and I choose a life without suffering. Okay, where is the gap? What do you believe should have happened? You remind yourself I don’t know what should have happened. Now choose the 180-degree opposing idea. That is what should have happened, not my preferred idea. How do I know that? Because that’s what is happening. Now there’s no gap. If there’s no gap you don’t suffer anymore. It might look a bit artificial in the beginning, but remind yourself again, and again, and again. It doesn’t matter if it feels artificial or fake, just do it. Do it until it becomes natural and easy. Choosing an Opposing Paradigm

I can continue giving examples. Every time you feel contracted, every time you feel frustrated, angry, violent, desperate, all those negative emotions, there’s always a gap that you created and now you choose to close it. And you close it, okay? The third step in closing the gap is a bit more delicate. It’s for people who have practiced closing the gap for some time. I am going to share it with you anyway. You can apply it if you’re ready. Drop all paradigms Realize that paradigms are just opinions and ideas that stand between you and a whole heart and a willing soul. Paradigms prevent a complete experience of life as it happens in the present moment, so drop them. When you realize paradigms don’t serve you in any way, you drop them. It’s not good or bad. It’s not useful or useless. There are no cons or pros. You don’t need that anymore.

A consciousness free of paradigms is truly available to experience life. Every time there is an idea you have about reality, it doesn’t matter if it supports life or rejects it, you drop it. Then you’re fully available, truly available, to experience the present moment. This is a bit more delicate, and it takes some practice. You can concentrate on the first two steps. Remind yourself that you don’t know, be humble, and adopt an opposite paradigm - one that describes reality instead of rejecting it. Do that again, and again, and again, because guaranteed, you will forget, and you’ll find yourself in the drama once again. But now, when you’re in the drama, you can remind yourself - oh, just a minute… I choose to live without drama. It is more important that I detox from it. Then, identify the gap and apply the steps we have talked about to close the gap: add humility and adopt an opposite paradigm. Last, if you can, drop the paradigms altogether and make yourself available to experience life in its totality. Suffering Versus Sadness White Path Meeting October, 2022

Q. How are you doing? A. I have to say I am quite sad lately because of what’s happening in Israel and Palestine, but also happy to be here with you now. It’s important to say that sadness is not suffering. The fact that I feel sadness doesn’t mean that I’m suffering. Do you see that? Sadness is just another emotion that we are invited to experience from time to time. Sadness is not a problem. It is just the opposite side of the scale from happiness. How do you know that you are happy if you’ve never been sad? You would not know. Opposite values are complementary, they complete each other. Sadness is just another emotion. It turns into depression when you are opposing it, do you see that? What you resist, persists. Pain is not a problem, it’s the opposite of pleasure, isn’t it? When does it become a problem? When you resist, then it becomes chronic pain, you see that? Then it’s suffering. Allow yourself to experience what life has to offer. It is not always comfortable, or nice. Sometimes it’s painful or sad. Q. How do you stop suffering in sadness?

A. In sadness I’m not suffering at all. I’m just sad. And that passes. Sadness fills my happiness with meaning. It deepens my happiness, and the other way around. I don’t reject sadness. Dealing with Chronic Pain Q. How should I deal with chronic physical pain? A. Embrace it. Embrace your pain and rejoice with It. I know it sounds strange, but you only have your body for a finite number of years, and living in a body means that we also feel pain, just as we feel pleasure. We can taste, we can smell. We can hear because we have a body. We can experience life in the physical realm thanks to our body. So don’t reject the pain, allow it, embrace it, rejoice in it. Soon you won’t have a body anymore and you will miss the pain. I guarantee - you will miss the pain. Q. I met with a thought and chose not to identify with it, that was possible. A. Now you know, it’s possible! And from now on know it’s your choice. You can reject the pain and suffer. You can embrace the pain and rejoice. What do you want? How do you want to live your life? Dealing with Emotional Pain and Grief

Q. Same approach for emotional pain, such as grief? A. Definitely! Again, remind yourself - I don’t truly know. I don’t know. Be humble. When should people be born? When should they die? I don’t know. When you believe This person should not have died, you create a gap. Do you see the gap between reality and your idea of what should have happened? Adopt the opposite view. This person died at exactly the right moment. How do we know that to be true? Because they died…at that moment. Now, you’re free to experience grief without suffering. See that? It may be sad, of course. It’s sad when people are taken away and leave a big hole as they go and it takes time to fill that hole, if that is even possible. Sometimes it is just a big hole that we must get used to, but that’s not a problem. I once said that our purpose in life, the reason that we came here is to learn how to gracefully let go, elegantly. Q. Sometimes, the sadness is overwhelming.

A. It may feel like it is overwhelming but this is an illusion. You know, sometimes the experience that life suggests seems so immense that it feels overwhelming. You may think No, this is too much. I cannot handle it. It’s beyond my capacity. But know that this is never the case. Life cannot suggest for you an experience that you truly do not have the capacity to hold, whole-heartedly. It is just you not knowing, not realizing the magnitude of your true Self. You don’t know how great you are, how vast you are. You don’t know that any experience is always smaller than you, just like any play is always smaller than the theater hall.

Do you see what I’m saying? Any play, no matter how dramatic it may seem, is always smaller than the theater hall it is played in. Just like that, your consciousness is bigger than any experience. You just don’t realize. You don’t know yourself yet to be that big. You convince yourself that this is too much. But this is never the case. KNOW THYSELF, and then no trauma would ever be marked on you again. No trauma. Because you will always be available to experience whatever life has to offer. Q. It hurts, and it’s difficult to embrace. It’s a daily practice. I must learn to elegantly let go. A. Fantastic! People say, “Oh, this sounds so difficult.” And my answer is always, “It’s more difficult to suffer.” Isn’t it? It’s way easier to let go. Think about it. Which is more difficult? To live clinging with your fists closed, fighting life, protecting yourself against life. Or relax and let go. Which is easier to do? Hmm? Stop Trying to Make Sense

I encourage you to stop trying to make sense. Do you know of the musical group Talking Heads? Did you listen to their album Stop Making Sense? If you didn’t, listen to it, it’s fantastic. Remind yourself that it is not about making sense. It’s not about your intellect getting the point. It’s about your heart choosing to open. The way to do that is to let go of the intellectual ideas of what is good or bad, what should never, or must, happen. The journey is 30 cm, from the head to the heart. It is up to you to make that journey. To do that I gave you three steps, and now it’s up to you.

You can ask yourself - do I want to live a life free of suffering? If so, every time you feel contracted, every time you are drawn back into the drama, stress, and suffering, locate the gap. It could be 50 times a day. It doesn’t matter. Locate the gap, give it a name, and now remind yourself - I don’t truly know. Choose a paradigm that is opposite to the one that created the gap in the first place. Then drop the paradigm. Yes, remember this. Now you’re back in the present moment. You see what I am saying? Take this week to practice. Let’s meet again next week and we can share our experiences. What do you say? I love you very much. What is Anger? White Path Meeting April, 2022 Q. You said a whole heart isn’t angry, and a whole heart does cry, please explain... A. Anger isn’t an emotion served to us as part of the human emotional prism. Anger is an outgoing result of our resistance to these emotions. Crying happens when I’m sad. Sadness is the opposite of happiness. Happiness and sadness sit on this scale of human emotions. Anger is me avoiding and resisting.

Q. That’s the second time you’ve calmed me down today because lately, I’ve been crying a lot. A. Go on, my dear. I’ve also cried a lot in the past few weeks. It’s part of the deal. You won’t be joyful if you’re not sad. Q. It’s also possible to cry out of joy and excitement. A. Correct. Q. Crying over loss, is that an open heart? A. Yes. I told you the story about Krishnamurti. Q. Yes, but at our age - who remembers? A. In short, his brother died, so he cried and cried. His pain was so deep that the people, his students, the people around him couldn’t bear it. They left the room and let him be alone with his grief. After two days when they came into the room to see what was happening with him, they saw that he was sitting and writing at his desk as if nothing had happened. His disciples asked him, “How did it happen that you were so sad and now as if nothing happened?” Krishnamurti answered, “If you had stayed, you would have known.” The lesson here is not to run away from grief. If you’re sad, then feel it all the way.

Q. So, do you have a list of human emotions versus a list of emotions that result from conflict with reality? Emotions like anger and frustration aren’t human emotions? A. Certainly, these are human emotions but they are self-inflicted. When we are frustrated, we realize it is a self-created emotion, not one presented to us by life. We created it when we rejected reality as it presented itself for us to experience. It doesn’t sit on the scale of human emotions that we’re necessarily invited to feel. These are emotions we can spare. We do not need them. Frustration, resentment, anger, disappointment, rage, violence, depression... all of these, there’s no need for them and we can exempt ourselves from them. Exempt the world from them. On the other hand, sadness, joy, longing... these are all there for us to experience with a whole heart and a willing soul. Q. Fear? A. Fear, again, that’s on the scale of unnecessary emotions. Unless there’s a lion. We will talk about it later. Q. Isn’t longing a resistance to reality?

A. No. Longing... you long for the people you love, that you appreciate, that you value. Like I long for you... Q. But longing is a kind of feeling of a reality that doesn’t exist, like a gap between the desired and the present. A. Yes, but there’s no feverishness in it. Try to feel the longing... it’s not like until we realize our longing, we’re not calm, we’re not whole, we’re not free, we’re not happy... there’s no suffering in it. We simply experience this longing to reunite. Q. When I say that it shouldn’t have happened, for example, is that where the suffering begins? A. Right. For instance, Now I should have been in Israel physically with you, not on Zoom. Such belief creates a gap between what is and what I thought it should have been. This gap creates more frustration, which creates anger, which creates violence. Q. But there’s something in longing that asks, why aren’t you here, it’s a shame you’re not here.

A. Longing softens the heart like a softening agent. Longing to return to peace, to return home, to reunite. Longing creates the power of evolution itself. The developmental tension that exists within each of us. The longing for knowledge, the longing for truth, the longing for love, the longing for free consciousness, the longing for self-awareness. Dealing with Anger Q. How can one deal with anger? I often get angry at myself for things I didn’t do, things I didn’t say, and then I ask myself why didn’t I do it this way or that? Then I need to remind myself that this is reality. I can’t blame anyone, only myself. With that, how can I cope? A. Thank you for the question. There’s no difference in anger, whether it’s directed towards other people or towards oneself because the anger is never relevant. It does not matter if on the target there’s a picture of the enemy or our own self-portrait. As long as the arrows are shot, there’s trouble. You see, it doesn’t matter if it’s directed outward or inward. What does matter is that you are deep in the drama of judgment and criticism.

Now, let’s see. We said that suffering and fear are first cousins. There’s almost no difference between them. Because Suffering is the gap between what is and what I believe it should have been (looking back in time) And, Fear is the gap between what is and what I don’t want it to become (looking forward in time) That means it’s a plus and a minus, but there’s still a gap that is created by the intellect. When you find yourself angry at yourself or others, what does it mean? It means that, for too long, you were frustrated that reality didn’t unfold as you believed it should have. The dynamics of violence are like this - we open a gap between what is and what we believe it should have been, and then the emotional experience is frustration.

The first thing you feel is frustration. You’re frustrated that reality doesn’t manifest according to your ideas. And if this frustration ferments inside you long enough, it turns into anger. And if this anger is not dealt with and it ferments inside you long enough, it turns into violence. That’s the dynamic of suffering. So, what to do? Close the gap. Instead of continuing to complain about reality and about the people around you, or about how you act within this world, you remind yourself what’s more important to you - the drama or keeping a whole heart towards reality. If you choose to keep a whole heart, then all you need to do is close the gap. How to close the gap? As we mentioned - add humility, adopt a paradigm that supports reality instead of contradicting it, and then, let go of all paradigms. Intimately, become available to life. Q. Seems like a life’s work… A. How long does it take? The same time it takes for you to give up a belief. How long does it take to give up a belief? Q. It sounds easy but it’s not, it’s very hard.

A. It’s not easy, but it’s harder to suffer. More–hard–to–suffer. What’s harder? This (clenched fist) or this (open fist)? Q. First, I need to give up the belief that I don’t need to suffer. Sometimes I feel like suffering is part of everyday life, it has become built-in suffering. A. Worse, it defines you. It becomes the answer to the question who am I? I am the one that suffers. That’s who I am. Q. Exactly, you know it’s terribly hard to get rid of it because as soon as I solve one problem I suffer from, I find something new to suffer from. A. Totally, that’s what we’re talking about, it’s an addiction to drama, folks. Drama has a very addictive quality, extremely addictive! And like any addict who wants to recover, the first step is to admit that you are addicted. Say, Yes, I’m addicted. Q. Is there a pill? Something simpler?

A. Actually, there is a pill, I just gave it to you. Now you need to swallow it. You will choose to swallow the pill the moment having a whole heart towards reality becomes more attractive than the drama. When will that day come? I don’t know... up to you my dear. What we shared here is a key to a breakthrough for each of us. I invite you to take this invitation seriously, with a clear mind. Realize the addiction to the drama to the point of complete identification with it, to the point that it defines you. This has a transformative quality for each of us. There are No Mistakes White Path Meeting May, 2022 Q. Yaron, can you talk about how to learn? After all, I want to improve, so I don’t want to repeat these mistakes. Every time something happens, I can’t just keep telling myself it’s just drama, you’re addicted. I can’t just dismiss it.

A. Everything you do in the realm of Doing has consequences and implications. If you act out of inner disharmony, the result of your actions will be to scatter disharmony around you. If you act out of inner harmony, the result of your actions will be harmonious. But nothing you do, harmonious or disharmonious, is a mistake. Meditate on this piece of knowledge. Reality is not flawed. Your actions are not flawed, and the results your actions have caused are not flawed. It’s not a mistake, it’s not a malfunction. God didn’t get confused. Reality always happens in divine accuracy. How do I know? Because that’s what happened. Free yourself from the idea that something else should have happened. Allow yourself to become a perfect conduit by lowering internal resistance. Now that you are free from disappointment, frustration, and anger, you can return to reality and learn from your actions and their consequences.

I don’t know what else I can say: I handed you the invitation, I gave you the tools, I gave you the expiration date of the medicine. What else? The doctor can’t force the pills down your throat. Q. I know, I need to train on it all the time. A. And release yourself from the idea that it’s a process, and now you’re entering a new developmental path, that maybe at the end of which you will be redeemed. What About Responsibility? Q. What about taking responsibility? A. Feeling responsible is all about accepting the present moment. If you reject the present moment, you place yourself in the position of a victim, wronged by life’s circumstances. Realizing there are no mistakes means you are available to fall in love with reality as it happens. Be in love. Feeling responsible is an outward sign of love.

Responsibility doesn’t need to be taken. Responsibility is an outward act of your love for the object you refer to. It’s not a decision you make - oh okay, I’ll take it on, that’s the responsible thing to do, that’s the right choice - because then it becomes another burden, another load that you carry on your shoulders. The invitation is to grow in the direction of a whole heart, and the more whole-hearted you are, the more responsible you become. Then, it won’t feel like a burden or like a weight, it will be a blessing. This is an invitation to expand the circle of love, to open the circle of love, not the circle of responsibility. Dealing with Injustice White Path Meeting February, 2021 Q. I see some injustices that always used to immediately upset me. Now I’m more able to step back and breathe. But still, I see injustices. So, what does it mean to love them?

A. Excellent question. What is injustice? Injustice is an idea we have about the reality we encounter. When what we see contradicts what we believe to be moral, right, or just we tag it as ‘Unjust’. That’s injustice. It belongs to the family of frustration, anger, resentment, and disappointment– the same family. These are ideas we stick onto reality, preventing us from freedom, from peace, from surrender. We prefer the idea we have about reality over reality itself. And what happens then? A gap opens up. A gap between what’s happening and what we thought should have happened. And within that gap, we suffer. Q. But if someone is suffering, me or someone else, why should I love it?!

A. Because that is your nature. The alternative is for you to suffer. How will you help the world? Will you help the world more if you suffer in it, or when you love it? Remember the story about the ‘Bodhisattva’? This is the meaning of the word Bodhisattva. It’s consciousness that gets engaged in helping people grow and stop suffering as an expression of the ultimate type of Love. Ask yourself, how can you do the work of helping people stop suffering if you yourself are driven by suffering? It’s like declaring yourself to be a ‘soldier in the army of peace.’ What does that mean? There’s no such thing. Either you’re a soldier, or you’re a man of peace. If you want to help people stop suffering (you know it from your own life experience) become a personal example. People won’t stop suffering if you explain to them that it’s important and worthwhile for them. People will learn from you how to stop suffering when they look at you and see you free from suffering and say, oh, I want that too. How did you get it? I’ll have what she’s having… Be an Embodiment of Love

The message and energy will spread out of love - not out of suffering. If you go into the world believing it’s broken and needs fixing, your actions will be driven by suffering. A disharmony that translates into action, and the result of a disharmonious action is more disharmony. But if harmony with abundance, with fullness, with love, translates into action through you, the result of this action is Akarma-yoga. It doesn’t add another stamp, it doesn’t disrupt the balance. If it’s too hard to love it, start by accepting it. Reality doesn’t get confused. God doesn’t make mistakes. You only have ideas about it. And then the question is what do I prefer - my ideas or my whole heart? We’ll always come back to this core question. What do I prefer? The drama, or a whole heart, and a willing soul? That’s the only question. There won’t be another question. Q. Yaron, how do I drop my ideas about what should happen?

A. The only and last attachment that interests us is growing towards a free consciousness. Any other idea we have about reality, how it is supposed to happen, how this world is supposed to operate doesn’t interest us anymore. The love within us translates itself into action, harmony translates itself into harmonious action, and the result of this will be more harmony, within us and around us. And if that means we go to a protest, then this will be the pure expression of love in action. And if that means we stay at home, then that will be the pure expression of love in action. The occurrences out there don’t confuse us anymore. Just like the movie playing in our heads, there’s no difference, it’s also an occurrence happening out there. Ideas, thoughts, objections, good and evil, concepts, sensations, and feelings - all the occurrences, all the conduct, don’t interest me anymore.

The only thing that interests me is the position of the observer, remaining open and soft. The observer is invulnerable to all these occurrences. Just like the theater hall is not concerned about which play is now playing on the stage. Comedy or tragedy - what does it matter? The theater hall allows it. Similarly, our consciousness, when clear, allows reality to occur. It is no longer threatened at all by this reality. The Root Cause of Exhaustion White Path Meeting October, 2022 Q. We're talking about suffering, and I find myself, since the beginning of the pandemic, living in the gap. I was fired from work because the studio I worked at closed, and I found myself avoiding taking any action. Not sending CVs, not going to interviews. I feel so exhausted.

A. Did you ever ask yourself what causes you to feel exhausted? That's exactly it, as you described it just now. It's never the work we do. It's always the hidden ideas we hold while doing something. For instance, you’re washing dishes, but you believe someone else should have washed these dishes. When you split your attention in this way, you burn your energy, your Prana. Energy is wasted there. It's not the action itself. No matter how hard or intense the work may be, even if it's hard physical work, at the end of the day, that's not what makes you tired. What makes you exhausted is this inner struggle with reality. It's very important to be completely clear about this. When we are involved in doing something that generates joy for us, we don’t believe someone else should be experiencing it now instead of us. We get lost in the moment and don’t even notice the time going by or the energy spent. So you see that when you are free from conflicting ideas, you are available to unite with the action and there is no energy loss in this case.

When people tell me it's really hard to release this inner struggle, my answer will always be, ‘Yes, that may be, but it's harder to suffer.’ Our life’s energy is burned in this gap between what is and what we believe it should have been. You feel tired, even if you haven't done anything. You could burn your energy being in bed all day, believing you should do something else or fearing your energy will be drained away by something that might happen in the future- someone will need your attention or something will take up your precious time. Whatever happens, accept it, love it. Stay in the present moment. Close this gap within, this split awareness. Instead, love what is, love what is happening right now. That's first. Then, deal with the fear and make sure it's not fear that steals your energy and prevents you from joining the natural flow of life.

Rejecting the present moment, which causes exhaustion, translates to a physical manifestation of tightness and rigidity and a mental manifestation of fear and anxiety. On a bodily level, embracing the present moment means releasing tension and contractions. When you are contracted it's hard for life to flow through. Make sure you find these contractions, breathe in deeply and release them - relax and exhale them. On a mental level, it's about remembering that exhaustion acts as a distraction from the fear you are experiencing - taking you away from the present moment and acting as a forethought about what might happen. Thoughts—have—no—power. Thoughts are just a movie your intellect projects to you, it's not real. Q. I see that I am trying to escape, trying to avoid something. There's a voice saying you're doing this just to avoid feeling pain. Pleasure and Pain are One and the Same

A. Pain is not something we need to escape from. Pain is something we're invited to experience from time to time. Because we have a body, and this body hurts sometimes. Pleasure and pain are one and the same. The fact that we sometimes hurt is a given. We agree to the pain, just as we agree to the pleasure. They are simply two sides of the same coin. No need to avoid the present moment just because it might be painful. Not at all. Q. But that's what happens when I'm not looking, I'm afraid of the pain, of disappointment, of... all kinds of pain. A. When do you get disappointed? You get disappointed when you have ideas about what the result of your actions should be. You cling to these ideas. Then these ideas don't materialize in the reality you encounter. What to do to avoid disappointment? 1. Give your 100% 2. Surrender completely to your choice to do something 3. Release yourself from the demand for a specific result

Don't do A so that B or C will happen. Do A to do A to the best of your ability. If B, C, or D happens, offer it to the Divine. The outcome is not your area of responsibility. You don’t know (humility). The result doesn’t matter. We said it's not the doing, it's not the choice, it's not the specific path you’re on, but the degree of your commitment to the process, as it unfolds. If you do A and B happens - great. If you do A and C happens - fine. If you do A and nothing happens - excellent. Q. And what if I'm not dealing with something because I'm afraid? A. It means you're stuck there on a rock in the middle of the flow. Q. That's the feeling. A. Yes, so if you want to join the flow, remember that it doesn't matter if you're flowing from the left or the right, or if the water is cold or warm, pleasant or unpleasant. What does matter is that you jump already. See, doubt and fear take us out of the water and put us on the rock. And now we're waiting...

I'm not sure, maybe I should be on the right side… maybe on the left side… I'm not certain yet... Maybe on the right side it will be more effective… maybe on the left it will be less pleasant… Meanwhile, what's happening? Life goes on. But you’re not participating because you’re on the rock. When doubtful, burn the doubt. Make a decision. Remind yourself that whatever you decide doesn't matter. That's not where the secret lies. What is important is that you jump off the rock actively participate and engage in life. Don’t fear life. Be involved, exposed, vulnerable, sensitive, and loving. Q. I feel like saying this bluntly. I have always felt that those sitting on the fence are missing out. There's no better way to say it. The unfamiliar and the unknown, in any field, are scary. This means it's much easier for us to stay where we are because it's familiar and we more or less know how to deal with it. And when we're heading into the unknown, it's scary. The outcome might eventually be good, but the way is frightening.

A. The outcome doesn't matter. The outcome is predetermined. We all finish 6 feet under. That is the outcome - that's it! You might have strong opinions about fence-sitters, but these opinions do not serve you (like any other strong opinion for that matter). More interesting is how we encounter life. How much freedom do we allow ourselves to experience life? Do we live it fully, with a whole heart and a willing soul? Am I Worthy? White Path Meeting June, 2021 Today our excuse to meet is to discuss the issue of worthiness. I’m going to just say a few sentences and then leave the stage for questions. I’m a big advocate of the idea that there is only one belief that stands between the sincere seeker and an awakened consciousness. And the trick is to identify that belief. One Core Belief

Usually, it belongs to the family of beliefs about whatever is lacking. I’m not developed enough, I am not mature enough, I still have so much to learn, I have issues to resolve. There are all kinds of self-doubts in that category. As long as I identify with those beliefs then there is no room for an awakened consciousness to blossom. Many years ago, I discussed this with a leading neurosurgeon who runs a pain clinic in Israel. He was the first in Israel to introduce hypnosis as a way of treating patients with chronic pain and I discussed the power of hypnosis with him. I shared my thoughts about how we might use hypnosis to implant the suggestion into our minds that can tackle these core beliefs and replace them with something that will be more authentic and help us to wake up. Later, I realized that meditation is designed to help us let go of all suggestions, both positive and negative, allowing us to meet reality naturally and at our own pace. The Story You Are Identified With

One of the repeating common beliefs I encounter with people on the path to an awakened consciousness is that they truly don’t believe they are worthy of it. Of course, that belief is not only reflected in the spiritual path. It reflects on any choice, any relationship, and any interaction that we have with life. If the core belief is that we’re not truly worthy to be happy, to experience all that goodness, to enjoy life, to flourish, to succeed, then that’s the reality that we create for ourselves. This is something important to understand if this is not already fully clear to you. The story that you tell yourself creates the reality that you experience. It’s not the other way around, even though people tend to confuse the two. The story is not the consequence of your reality. Reality is the consequence of the story that you tell yourself.

If you tell yourself that life is brutal and dangerous, that you need to walk through life carefully, and diligently, and make sure it doesn’t hurt you, then I can guarantee that this will be your life. Do you see what I’m saying? And if you believe that life is a beautiful opportunity to experience and blossom within yourself, then this will be your life. In the context of the topic of today, if you believe that you are not worthy, then that’s it. You are not. We are here today to look at that core belief. To look at it honestly and courageously. To, once and for all, understand where it is coming from, and how is it affecting you, your life, your decision-making process, your relationships, and your spiritual path, and what can you possibly do to grow beyond it. That is my prologue. Now the stage is yours. Happy to have your questions. Q. What about the use of unworthiness to avoid disappointment?

A. Yes. The use of unworthiness to avoid disappointment. When are we disappointed? When we have expectations. And what is the role of expectations? The role of expectations is to reduce our joy, right? When we expect something, we cannot truly enjoy it if it does happen because there is no spontaneity there. And if it doesn’t happen, then we are disappointed. So next time you are engulfed with expectations, my recommendation is to offer it to the divine. Whatever happens in the future, offer it to the divine as a gift. Don’t be concerned about the future anymore and bring yourself back to experience the present moment, free of expectations about what should happen in the future. You don’t need to be bothered with expectations. Just remind yourself they are there to reduce your joy, and you’re here to enjoy life. That’s the point. So, what do you do when you feel unworthy? You reduce the expectations you have about yourself, and life. Consciously reduce it, to minimize the pain of disappointment. How Do You Choose to Live Your Life?

Is this the way you want to live your life? Trying to manipulate your way to minimize the pain? Think about it. Be honest. To minimize the pain. That’s why you are here? To go through life with minimal pain? That is a shame and that’s doomed to fail because life is painful, guaranteed. Living in a body is not convenient, not comfortable. It’s sticky and messy. Being a pure consciousness is much more elegant, for sure. But you have a body, and you have a limited time to enjoy your presence in a body. What do you want to do with that limited time? Do you want to fake your presence here, as if you are an etheric being, formless? Do you prefer to avoid this opportunity you have? Or do you agree to experience life fully, in the physical realm? That is painful. Of course, that is also pleasurable. But if you’re not willing to experience the pain, you will not truly know the pleasure. Ask yourself, how do you want to live your life? Avoiding the pain? Or embracing it together with everything else life has to offer?

Q. Is awakening the purpose of life, or is living an awakened life the goal? A. There is no difference. It’s the same. And it’s not a purpose, it is inevitable. Don’t tag it as a purpose or a goal that you should reach. There’s nowhere to go, you are already there. You don’t need to reach anywhere. You don’t need to find a different version of yourself that is more enlightened than the current one. No better or more promising circumstance awaits you to allow that to manifest. As long as you believe you haven’t arrived yet, I guarantee you won’t get there. There is no difference between an awakened consciousness and living life consciously. An awakened consciousness cannot live life unconsciously. Don’t worry about that. Q. It seems like unworthy is reverse pride, like the opposite of pride.

A. Yes. What is this sense of unworthiness? Let’s look at it for a moment. You know, it’s that innate belief that, as you are, you’re not good enough. For some reason, you see it more with women than with men. It could be because men are too thick to be bothered about it, and women are a bit more sensitive to the feedback they receive from other people. It could be a cultural thing, where traditionally in many societies men are promoted over women. It could be a biological thing. It could be the consequence of the way we evolved the species, where women are more connected to the feminine, which is all-inviting. Keeping the family, sustaining it, and feeding it. And men are more connected to the masculine. They go out, they hunt, and they lead the family or the tribe forward to seek food. They are busier with the doing. Seeking Approval

Whatever reason created that reality, the bottom line is that too many people, and specifically too many women, feel that they are not good enough as they are. There is this constant drive to prove themselves worthy by pleasing other people. A constant pull to do the right thing. To meet the expectations of other people, if not to exceed those expectations. Why? So, they can get that label of approval - I am good enough. Or, in the worst case, they don’t even believe that acquiring this label is a possibility. Either there’s no way to prove that I am good enough, or I am simply not good enough, and that’s that. They don’t even bother trying to please or find approval because they don’t believe it exists, or that they are worthy of it. Once you identify with that story, that’s it. This is your life. Neither life nor circumstances can persuade you otherwise. You create that reality for yourself. If you believe you are beyond hope, I guarantee, you are beyond hope.

This is something to look at. What is the fundamental story about myself that I identify with? Look beyond the image that you try to portray. Look beyond the mask that you put on. When you engage with other people, look in the mirror and ask yourself truthfully what is the fundamental story that I tell myself about myself? If that story has chapters in it that carry the message of I am not good enough as I am, I tell you it is extremely important that you recognize that. I am an Addict It starts with you being aware of that. Just like in AA. Hello. I’m Yaron and I’m an addict. Acknowledge it. Be aware of it. Don’t run away from that truth, even if it is really painful. Then we can start discussing what to do with this, but if you’re not even aware of it then there’s no place to start from. What was the question? Q. That unworthiness is the reverse of pride.

A. Oh yes. So, what is pride? I am good enough. I am better than you think and better than you have ever seen before. You know, both are aspects of ego. A separated illusion of self that builds a story to identify with. I am good enough or I’m not good enough, it doesn’t matter. These are two sides of the same coin. Okay, let’s continue. Q. Is unworthiness a mental construct or a universal concept? A. Universal concept?... I don’t know how to relate to that. The universe has no concepts. The universe exists without any definitions. I wouldn’t know how to reflect on that. But unworthiness is part of the story we tell about ourselves as humans. It’s an idea, for sure. Nothing to do with the ‘universe.’ It has to do with myself observing myself, and relating to myself. Q. It’s selfish to say I’m not worthy, so it’s the same thing. A. Is it selfish to say I’m not worthy? I would say it’s egoistic to say I’m worthy, and it’s egoistic to say I’m not worthy. Both are aspects of the same coin. The coin is called Ego. Intellect as a Barrier

Q. It seems innate to assign a value to ourselves as we compare ourselves with the world. We occupy ourselves with worthiness. It seems as a way to understand how we relate to our society. Why is that? What is our purpose/direction in such a world we live in? A. First of all, there is a discussion about the question WHY. If you go back to my recordings, there is a whole track that you can listen to about the question why? Highly recommended. In a nutshell, ‘Why’ is always arguing with reality. And yes, the way our intellect works is by observing reality and comparing it with references, right? Of course, the first and most fundamental comparison the intellect makes when referring to other situations is deciding if this situation is good or bad, right? We have a concept of what is good. We have a concept of what is bad. What we’re experiencing now - is it good, or is it bad?

There are many, many other types of judgments that the intellect is making on the reality that we experience. I’ve talked about it in many situations before. The bottom line is that any kind of judgment keeps us distant from an intimate experience of reality. It doesn’t matter if the intellect decides that this is good, or if it decides that this is bad. It doesn’t matter if it is referring to external circumstances or the image that we see in the mirror, right? If we look in the mirror and the intellect tell us that we’re bad, that’s what we believe. That’s it. We’re bad.

How does the intellect make that judgment? Because of past experiences, right? There is the whole story of us coming to this world, raised in this particular family, to these particular parents, in this particular tradition, this culture, this religion, whatever. We collect these inputs that the surroundings are giving us, about us, and eventually, we create an identity around that. Too often, that identity is not good enough. You can do better. You should be better. Look at the Mandelbaum’s, their son is a doctor. What about you?

What’s the point of using the intellect to try to understand life and to categorize ourselves? You come to a room and, immediately, you have an opinion about the people in the room. Just by the first sentence, the way they look, the way they dress, you already have an opinion. And not just an opinion, but you also rate yourself according to them. Where am I in comparison to him? Am I above or below him? That automatic way you relate to other people is not helpful. They say one sentence and that’s it, you’re in a loop. I wish I was in their position; they are so charming; they are really impressive. Or, Pffff. Who is this miserable person? I am much better than them. Why is it important? Why do you have to categorize yourself like that? Why not just stay open to meeting people where they are, as they are? Why not meet yourself where you are, as you are, with no preconditioning, no expectations, no judgment, not good or bad? Hmm?

Here is a practice I can suggest. Tomorrow, meet the people you encounter as if it were the first time you’ve met them. Free of the story you tell yourself about them. Free of any ideas and preconceptions about them. See that person as if it was the first time and reflect on how it changes the encounter. Intellect vs. Mind Q. What’s the difference between intellect and mind? A. I urge you to go back to my previous book, ‘Available to Love’ and read about the 7 layers of existence. There is a whole chapter called The Mind - 3rd level of Existence. And the chapter called The Intellect - 4th level of Existence. There are guided meditations that go along with each chapter. Dive deep into that knowledge.

In one sentence I can say that the mind is the movie that we see, that reflects a picture of reality to us. And the intellect is the movie critic that sits there, looking at the movie and creating an opinion about it. This is the difference between the mind and the intellect. More on this in the chapter on ‘Fear in the Mind’ later in the book. For now, this is just a nutshell, but it’s crucial to understand what we’re talking about here. Q. Do you judge someone running towards you with a weapon? Do you treat everybody the same? Because you have to assess a situation, particularly if there’s some sort of danger.

A. Assess the situation, and remind yourself that fear is only useful when the situation presents clear and immediate danger, which is rarely the case. When was the last time somebody ran towards you holding a knife? I hope it was a long, long time ago, if ever, right? Usually, it’s just a story in your head about what may happen or could happen, and you try to prepare yourself to be ready for an imaginary situation. There is no need to be a slave to those kinds of fears. If you need to prepare yourself to be ready to meet the danger if it comes, then you prepare. But don’t be obsessed about that. Make sure you are available to experience life, at this moment, as it happens, okay? Because currently, everything is okay. We are just sitting here, talking, you know? There’s no lion in the living room that we should be concerned about.

Think about it. When you believe a thought like But what if I’m not worthy, can anything good come after the word worthy? Anything you can grow with? Anything that supports life? Could anything that may help you blossom be hiding behind these words? If I’m not worthy, then… Self Knowledge is the Cure The only reason that you can ask the question What happens if I’m not worthy? is a lack of self-knowledge. You don’t know who you are yet. You believe a fake story about yourself told by other people and by your previous experiences. That’s the only reason such a sentence can be generated. I am not worthy. Now what? The only way to go beyond that self-inflicted belief is self-knowledge. Know yourself, know who you are. Know the magnitude of your consciousness. Then you realize this question is completely futile. Am I good enough? Who is good enough? Good enough for what? It’s completely futile.

You are not just good enough, if that’s even a way to reflect on oneself. You are the definition of perfection, divine perfection. There is no real separated You that builds an ego around that realization. It’s like the ocean complaining that it’s not wet enough. Can you imagine the ocean complaining that it’s not wet enough? When you hear yourself saying something like - but what happens if I’m not good enough? - just wake up to tell yourself - wait, wait. I completely forgot who I am. I got caught up in this fake story that I keep telling myself, which doesn’t represent reality at all. I tell you - it doesn’t matter what happened in the past. All those incidents from that story, which you now use to justify your belief that you’re not good enough, happened for a reason. They happened so that you could learn and grow through the experience. The fact that you turned them around to create an identity of a victim, an identity of unworthiness, of not being good enough, is just a symptom of a confused identity.

This is an opportunity to take a deep breath in and remind yourself that you are not the story. You are not the story. Whatever happened in the past, whatever feedback you may have received from other people, from your surroundings, your school teachers, your parents, your friends, your partners, do not build an identity around it. This is not who you are. You are not your story. It does not matter how many times you look in the mirror and tell yourself this is who I am. These are my abilities. These are my disabilities. These are my strengths. These are my weaknesses. These are all external shells that may build your persona, but they are not who you are. You are Eternal

Remember, everything that begins must end. Everything that starts must finish. Everything that was born must die. You don’t belong to that realm. You are eternal. These are all external shells that you are invited to gently peel off if you are truly interested to know who you are. I’m going to pause because there are many questions. You can practice this guided meditation that helps you better differentiate between the temporary and the eternal: I am not my story. Q. The seven levels of existence that are recorded were amazing. I recommend that you read it. A. Yes, in my previous book ‘Available to Love’ I elaborate on the seven levels of existence. It will help you dive deep into this knowledge of understanding the nature of self.

Q. I understand the mind is what you perceive with. I understand the mind perceives the world and the intellect interprets it and assigns value to it. Are we supposed to suppress the intellect and what we are learning from our experience? Or are we changing how the intellect assesses the experience, meaning changing our intellectual measuring stick when we determine what is good or bad? A. The bottom line Is to realize that whatever judgment the intellect has, it keeps you away from an intimate experience of reality. It doesn’t matter if the intellect is for or against. As long as there is a judgment there about the situation, about the experience you currently have, it stands between you and the experience. At first, we do replace beliefs that are harmful and obstructive to us with beliefs that are useful and allow growth. But eventually, we drop our opinions altogether and allow ourselves to embrace reality without the veil of our opinions.

Q. It seems we are living in a conflicted state, where our societal expectations and mental constructs of how to exist clash with our spiritual truths. A. This is a repeating question. There is no conflict! Don’t create or be identified with any imaginary, limited perspective of life. An awakened consciousness is wide enough to include all aspects of life, joyfully and harmoniously. It cannot exclude anything. If you have to divide the world into two, it’s not about good or bad. It’s not about being beneficial or harmful, it’s about ignorance and knowledge. So, if you have to divide it into two, see when you are led by ignorance. For example, ignorance about the nature of your own self, versus when are you led by the knowledge of the self. Not just as a concept or a philosophical theory, but knowledge in the biblical sense of being one with the isness of things: I am that. Don’t be too concerned about a seemingly conflicted world out there. The world is perfect. Nothing to fix. It’s already perfect. You just open your heart to whatever you experience. That’s it!

One Way to Relate to GOD Q. I wonder if everything is a judgment except God. A. Wow. That’s a beautiful insight. Is everything a judgment except God? Let us ponder about that for a minute… This truly brings us closer to the truth. As long as there is an opinion or a judgment, there is no direct experience. God can only be revealed through direct experience. You cannot talk about God, you cannot describe it, explain it, and you cannot relate to God in any way. Just directly experience it. And if there is an opinion about it, there is no home for direct experience. In many ways, that’s a very accurate way to look at it. Everything is a concept, except God. So yes, at the beginning of your journey, it’s about creating a new story instead of a story that tells you that you’re not good enough. Now there is a new story, more authentic, and more accurate, that helps you realize that you are worthy. You are not just good enough. You are as good as can be! But that’s also a story, right? Just a more useful story on the path to an awakened consciousness.

Eventually, you will be invited to let go of all the stories, good or bad, and just be. Free of any preconditioning. Free of any concept. That’s why an awakened consciousness is so fresh. All the time, fresh. It doesn’t come with that baggage of I know, I believe, I identify with… Even that I itself is not there anymore to take ownership of the experience. Q. What is the root cause need for our stories? How are the stories part of our perfection? What is the root cause? A. Why do we create stories? Why do we need them? How are they part of our self-identity? Good question. We need stories to generate a sense of meaning and a secure relationship with reality. Through the stories, we create what we call a comfort zone in which we feel in control and protected as we try to understand life. We can manage it better - minimize the pain, and maximize the pleasure, right? Minimize the loss, maximize the gain.

An awakened consciousness pops the soap bubble. There is no comfort zone. Everything is invited in, pleasure as well as pain. Everything is part of a harmonious flow that an awakened consciousness allows. Not just allows - generates. For that, you don’t need a reason, you don’t need a story, you don’t need preconceptions, you don’t need the intellect at all. I said on many occasions that the ultimate understanding of a fully matured intellect is that it’s not here to understand. That’s it. Once it dawns on you that the intellect is not here to understand life, to help you ride the horse and remain in control, you allow the horse to take you, to lead you, and you just enjoy the ride. The intellect doesn't play an important part anymore. I often say to my partner, “This is my opinion, but it’s just my opinion. It doesn’t matter. It has no importance.” Yes, I have opinions. But I never take them too seriously. Everybody has opinions, they are a dime a dozen. Who cares…? Use your Mind Carefully Q. So, our minds lie to us?

A. All the time! I mean it generates a fictional picture that is supposed to describe reality for us. And we relate to that very narrow, broken picture as if it was the reality. Then we judge it. We are completely lost in the way we perceive life and our role in it. As we grow on the path, we allow that expansion of consciousness to generate a much, much more accurate perception of what is actually happening. And there is very little self-engagement in it. You realize that life doesn’t happen to us, or for us. Life reveals itself to be just a flow of phenomena that we glide through. As Leonard Cohen once wrote, “Tell the people that you saw me passing through …” Q. We create stories to entertain our reality… A. Yes, many times. As long as you remember that this is just entertainment and you don’t take it so seriously. That’s a start. Because usually, it’s so dramatic. We are just lost in the drama. A good way to start is to remember that this is just entertainment. Q. What is the mind? Electrons? Synapses?

A. Yes, it’s the five senses collecting information, and those synapses collect all this information and build an image of reality for us. It creates a superposition of all that information into one picture, and this is what we relate to, this is what we are aware of, right? This is why it’s called awareness. We are aware of what the mind is telling us, but we are not aware of everything else that happens, because our mind is very limited in this capacity to show us the full complexity of reality. Go back and read about the 3rd level of existence in the chapter about the mind in my book ‘Available to Love’. It tells you all about it. Q. When I put into context where thoughts come from, it blows my mind. A. Yes. Beautiful. Compassion as a Bridge Q. Other than feeling compassion for those suffering from a sense of unworthiness, do we take action?

A. Beautiful question. Compassion is a good start. Don’t judge, don’t critique, don’t try to persuade. Don’t try to educate. You just have compassion, especially if you find someone who believes that they are not good enough. Have compassion and be there for them. I’m here for you. I’m not judging you to be good or bad. It doesn’t matter to me. I’m here for you. Tell me, how can I help? Give them a hug, whatever they need. Offer a glass of water, you know, small gestures of kindness. If they are sensitive enough to see, to recognize that unconditional love, they will come, because, knowingly or unknowingly, this is what we are all looking for. This is what we are longing for - unconditional love. So, if they are sensitive enough to recognize it, they will follow. Otherwise, it’s also okay to let them awake at their own pace.

Q. I had a thought earlier when you were talking about the feeling of unworthiness being more common in women, and I wonder if that is true. I don’t believe it’s true because, not that the points you made aren’t valid, but I think many teachers teach that when you get down through the layers, into the core beliefs, that it often is about I’m not good enough. And I wonder if maybe men are just better at masking it. A. Yes, I did mention this earlier. Maybe men are just too dim to care about it too much, you know? They are focused on the task ahead and they just plow through it regardless, because they are driven and they have a vision. They are not allowing themselves to be too concerned about Am I good or bad. That’s the tendency of masculinity. The bottom line is, whether you are a man or a woman, look in the mirror and courageously and honestly see if you have a version of this story: As I am is not good enough, so I’m not worthy of all this goodness that life has to offer.

Q. The reason I bring it up is because of the previous question about offering compassion when you see it. But I think sometimes that version of unworthiness is really hard to see not only by yourself but from other people. It manifests in ways that are layered and masked, where you can’t see it. And that’s a harder place to offer compassion, especially if it feels threatening or directed at you. A. You have to realize that as long as there is an element of ego there within you, persuading you that you are a separate entity that has to take care of itself, driven by your ambitions and the prospect of gaining and losing, that’s already a version of I’m not worthy. And, yes, sometimes that story is very prominent, and sometimes it’s well hidden under all the masks.

Whether you present yourself to be a winner, or you present yourself to be a loser, these are the aspects of the same coin, right? So, if you feel you’ve met that in another person, or you feel you met that in yourself looking in the mirror, in both cases being compassionate is a very good start. Don’t judge other people for not knowing who they are, and don’t judge yourself for not knowing who you are. (Let me give you a spoiler: you are Love. But listening to it, and knowing it are two different things). Q. Society helped shape these opinions and illusions of ourselves, perhaps intentionally. Do they require us to awaken? Is it part of the evolutionary process? A. Yes. This is the way it’s designed. We are born without an ego. As we mature, we put on an ego, like a costume, and then we come to a time when we are invited to take the costume off. That’s the way it’s designed. So don’t be too disappointed about that. Reality Never Works Against You White Path Meeting September, 2023

Q. I deal daily with 2 employees who speak disgustingly and disrespectfully to me, behaving as if they own me. Unfortunately, I find myself disturbed by them and my thoughts are occupied with them often. They raise thoughts in me like what is it about me that allows them to speak to me like this? Maybe I’m not strong, perhaps I’m not worthy because I can’t deal with them, and so on. The feeling is terrible. The conclusion I come to is that I have to get them out of my environment. I see this as the only way to deal with it. They are like an evil force and I am weakening. I fight with them, strengthen, and fall again. That’s the reality. Is that reality or just my thoughts, my interpretation? What do you say? A. Here's a tip that might help. Take it as a given, a law of nature, a lesson from the Present Moment: Reality never works against you.

This moment never works to harm you. It’s not working for you, but it’s not working against you. This moment never works against you because this moment doesn’t stop to ask itself if it suits you. This is impossible because it could suit you, but be very unsuitable for the person standing next to you. There’s no way to please everyone. Even if the present moment were there to please you, you're constantly changing your mind about what you want. Today I want this, tomorrow I want the opposite. You see, it doesn’t work. Just like the present moment, you don’t need to try to please other people. The Present Moment has no agenda, it doesn’t stop to ask itself if what’s happening now suits you. It just happens, that’s its role and that’s what it’s been doing since creation. The Present Moment just happens. How you encounter it, that’s your business, not the Present Moment.

When you’re faced with a reality that you’re uncomfortable with, that you find difficult, that you’re struggling with, it’s an opportunity you are given by life to check what else is unresolved within you. An awakened awareness is never struggling with the Present Moment. Even when it joins the masculine forces of change, it doesn’t do it because it believes that the Present Moment is flawed and needs fixing. It does it simply because the masculine energy takes it there, and it actively joins the change that is happening naturally. When you act, make sure it is not from an agenda or some personal interest that leads you to believe that only after reality changes will you be calm, free, and happy. Q. So, I understand that whole religious thing. We’ve passed Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. According to the Jewish tradition, now God sits and evaluates each of our actions, and for bad deeds, we receive punishments, and for good deeds, we receive blessings. Is this really the right way to present what we have to do here in life?

A. I encourage you to YouTube a guy named Bill Burr. I don’t know if you’ve heard of him. Bill is an American stand-up comedian, sharp as a razor, who talks about his relationship with religion, how he grew up in a religious household, and how he slowly distanced himself from religion. He talks about this idea that God sits and examines the souls who act according to the criteria of ‘did good’, ‘did bad’, ‘you go to paradise’, ‘you go to hell’. It is hilarious! You see, people find stories to give meaning to their lives. When they believe in their stories it becomes their truth. How many times have we said this? Here too, in these meetings, we’re telling a story. You choose, if you want to adopt it, then it becomes your truth. There’s no one story that is truer than another story. The question is, what story works for you? If you ask me if I believe in a God who sits and examines my kidneys and heart and decrees on me to heaven or hell - no, I don’t believe in that.

I’m not a big believer in anything. I’m a very limited man of faith. Faith is not a prerequisite for the path I’m on. Either I know it from direct experience, or it’s a story. I don’t demand faith from myself or from people who walk the path I’m on. Check out all the suggestions you meet in our meetings and see if they are right for you. If they are, cool. If not, keep looking. What is the Story You Choose to Believe? White Path Meeting December, 2022 Q. Are you saying it's all just a story in the end? A. Just a story. A story that tries to mediate reality to you. I remind you of the third stage on the way to closing the gap between what is and what you believe should have been. The third stage is to let go of the paradigm altogether. Let go of it. Be exposed. Be vulnerable. Be accessible to reality as it unfolds, without interpretation. When awareness is wide enough, it doesn't need a mediator.

This is also written by the band Sheva in their song Come in Love - “You don't need a mediator between you and divinity, you and the being, you and the experience." Wow, I remember their words by heart. If I find myself confused and entangled with my interpretations of reality then it's an opportunity to remember that I'm drifting away. Q. Yaron, so how does it manifest in practice? Does it mean that at the end, if something happens to me and I'm analyzing in my head and say no, it's not a real fear, there's no lion in the room, and I change my thinking, does time narrow down to zero in this process as if it's not happening, and then there's only calmness? A. It's not at the end, it's in the midst of every movement. It hides in the space you have in your head between one thought and the other thought. It's not something that will come at the end of the road when you're ready. This is one of the classic mistakes of people on the spiritual path. ‘Me? I have a long way to go. I need to grow. I'm in a process. Sound familiar? I’ve seen that sticker on people’s desks, ‘I'm in a process’.

It's not at the end of the road. If it's not relevant now, it's not relevant ever. There's no road. There's no process. Q. The question is, what will happen the next time I have these thoughts? A.
