Up to you... Pause for a moment, return to meditation, allow this movement to happen, and see if you can encounter the space between the phenomena. Between thoughts, emotions, sensations, thoughts, emotions, sensations... Suddenly there's space. The clouds clear for a moment and you can see the sky. Q. Thankfully I notice I have fewer negative thoughts, which is already progress. I also think directly about proper and accurate execution for me, but the thing is, it's a bit tiring... A. What is tiring? Q. This thinking, changing the paradigm and everything we discussed, the whole process...

A. Don't change it then. If it's hard for you to change the paradigm, give it up entirely. Jump straight to the third phase. Let go of the paradigms, without preconceived ideas. There is no problem with that. It is a shortcut. But then it means you're truly giving up. It's neither good nor bad. It's neither advisable nor inadvisable. It's not necessary. It's not unnecessary. It's happening, it's occurring, and you’re here to allow this occurrence to manifest and that's it! Moving on, with a whole heart, without resistance.

Remember that the doing, the choice of what to do, is a result of the realm of being and not the other way around. We tend to believe that our being is the product of all the doing, of the realm of events and actions. If the outside is good and pleasant, then we will also feel good and pleasant, but if the outside is stormy and rainy, then we also cannot be calm inside. But the truth is the opposite. Our being gives birth to our choices, the doing, and how our choices fulfill themselves in the material world. Therefore, I suggest paying less attention to what is being done and more to who is doing it and their state of mind.

When the one who does is free from suffering and fear, you'll see that these choices manifest themselves harmoniously. It no longer needs to bother you at all, it just happens. You become a tool in the hands of life itself. You allow the natural and harmonious flow of life to happen. There's no need to be preoccupied about what to do, or what to choose. This becomes unnecessary. Like hesitating between a biscuit and a piece of wood laid out on the table. What would you choose? Part II Grow Beyond Fear Grow Beyond Fear Fear is one of the most pervasive emotions we face. It limits our growth, traps us in our comfort zones, and holds us back from fully experiencing life. In this second part of When the Wave Remembers the Ocean, we dive into the nature of fear - what it truly is, how it shows up in your life, and, most importantly, how to Grow Beyond Fear.

In the pursuit of spiritual liberation, rising beyond fear is a crucial turning point. Fear, like suffering, is deeply rooted in our attachment to the known - our desire for safety, certainty, and control in a world that offers none of these things. Fear binds us, not just to the external forces we dread, but to the internal limitations we impose on ourselves. Yet, what if the true path to freedom lies in confronting fear, not as an enemy, but as a gateway to deeper understanding?

In Part II, we explore the transformative power of moving beyond fear, unraveling its sources, and recognizing it as an illusion born from separation - from ourselves, from others, and from the divine. To rise above fear is to step into a space of trust and surrender, where courage is not the absence of fear, but the choice to act in spite of it. By embracing this process, we unlock the door to spiritual liberation, where freedom, peace, and connection await. Part II offers insights and practices to help guide us through the journey of transcending fear and discovering the limitless potential that lies beyond it. We begin by exploring Fear vs. Surrender. In the first part of this chapter, we learn to meet fear in the three essential levels of our existence - body, mind, and spirit. How does it manifest and how does it influence our ability to experience life?

The second part of this chapter goes on to discuss the opposite force to fear, surrender, where we learn how to apply this force in those same three levels of existence and we come to realize what a life free of fear looks like. Next, we distinguish fear from worry. While fear is an immediate response to perceived danger, worry is a mental loop that keeps us trapped in ‘what if’ scenarios. Understanding the difference is crucial because, often, we become paralyzed by imagined fears rather than real ones. From here, we explore the fear of pain - both physical and emotional. Pain is inevitable, but our fear of it often amplifies its impact. What if we could face pain without being consumed by fear? By addressing this, we can break free from the cycles of avoidance that only serve to deepen our suffering. The wounds of the past often shape our present fears. We explore how to process trauma without letting it define who we are, transforming it from a source of fear into an opportunity for healing and strength.

One of the greatest barriers to growth is the fear of leaving our comfort zone. We cling to the familiar, even when it no longer serves us, because stepping into the unknown feels risky. This section challenges you to take those steps, showing that the freedom we seek lies just beyond the edge of comfort. We also dive into vulnerability - often perceived as weakness, yet in reality, it’s one of our greatest strengths. Being vulnerable means showing up authentically, without the protective layers we’ve built to guard ourselves against rejection or hurt. Learning to embrace vulnerability allows us to live more fully and connect with others on a deeper level. Another major fear that many of us carry is the fear of not being loved. This fear can lead to people-pleasing, emotional walls, or isolation. We’ll unpack the roots of this fear and explore how to cultivate self-love, which naturally reduces the anxiety of seeking external validation.

This section also addresses how to overcome doubt. Doubt can be a crippling force, making us question our decisions, our worth, and even our ability to succeed. We’ll learn how to recognize doubt for what it is - a temporary state of mind - and how to navigate through it. Fear often arises because we resist certain feelings, believing they are too overwhelming or too painful to face. But emotions, when fully felt, can guide us towards healing and growth. When we stop fearing our emotions, we will be able to embrace them, allowing them to flow through us rather than control us. In Grow Beyond Your Fears, we will learn not to eliminate fear but to change our relationship with it. Fear doesn’t have to be an obstacle - it can be a teacher, showing us where we need to grow, and ultimately helping us remember the deeper truth of who we are. Just like the wave that feels isolated from the ocean, fear is the illusion of separation. As we work through this section, we’ll come to see that the wave is never separate from the ocean, and fear is never separate from the opportunity to surrender.

Fear vs. Surrender In every aspect of life, we encounter two opposing forces - fear and surrender. Fear often presents itself as resistance, tightening, and the need for control, while surrender is its opposite - an expansive, freeing force that opens us to deeper levels of peace and inner freedom. This chapter, Fear vs. Surrender, is a structured journey through six meetings, designed to explore these two fundamental forces and their impact on our body, mind, and spirit. We begin by understanding fear - how it manifests in the body, how it affects the mind, and how it clouds our spiritual essence. Fear often shows up on the physical level as tension, restlessness, or even illness. On the mental level, it presents as worry, anxiety, or doubt. On the spiritual level, fear can distance us from our true nature, creating a sense of separation from the vast flow of life. By learning to recognize fear at each of these levels, we can begin to disarm its power and stop letting it dictate our choices.

Once we have a deeper understanding of fear, we turn to the practice of surrender, which is not about giving up, but rather letting go of the need to control outcomes. Surrender is a conscious choice to trust the flow of life, even when we cannot predict or manage its course. On the physical level, surrender feels like the release of tension - learning to relax and allow the body to move with ease, rather than holding on to stress. On the mental level, it’s about letting go of rigid beliefs and expectations, freeing the mind from endless loops of worry. And on the spiritual level, surrender connects us to a greater intelligence, inviting us to flow with life rather than resist it.

Through these six meetings, we will dive deeply into the interplay between fear and surrender in the body, mind, and spirit. You’ll learn practical techniques for recognizing fear’s grip in your life and how to soften into surrender, allowing for the natural unfolding of inner freedom. This chapter is not about eradicating fear, but about transforming your relationship with it. By surrendering to the present moment, we grow beyond fear, moving closer to peace and true liberation. Each session is designed to build upon the last, offering you tools, insights, and reflections to guide you on this journey from fear to surrender. As you progress, you’ll experience the profound shift that occurs when you let go of fear and embrace the power of surrender, leading to greater resilience, clarity, and spiritual connection.

Let this course be your invitation to discover that, just like the wave is never separate from the ocean, you are never disconnected from life’s natural rhythm. Fear can only hold you back if you resist the flow, but surrender allows you to merge with life and experience the true freedom that comes from within. Fear in the Body White Path Meeting June, 2023 Welcome to the first session in a series of six meetings during which we will explore fear. What is the nature of fear? What is the source of fear? How is fear manifested within us on three levels - body/breath, mind/intellect, and spirit. In the last three meetings, we will examine surrender as the opposing force to fear and how it manifests on these same three levels - body/breath, mind/intellect, and spirit. At the end of the six meetings, we will experience a life free from fear... at least we will progress in that direction.

Let’s say a few words about the qualities we seek in this meeting and how it can be most successful for us to participate and express ourselves. The first thing is to ensure that our cup is not completely full. We assume that we are all wise, knowledgeable, and familiar with the teachings, but we are here to learn something more. To be able to learn something of evolutionary value to us, it is important to ensure that there is room in the cup which can be filled. In order to do this, we must ensure our cup is not full. The second thing is to check our listening. There are three types of listening. There is intellectual listening where the intellect meets what is said and examines it in relation to what it already knows, saying, Aha, yes, yes, I already know this, I agree with this, or conversely, I know the opposite, I do not accept this. The problem with this type of listening is that we cannot learn anything new because we only let in what we already know, accept, and agree with. Do you see this? This type of listening only partially helps us.

Another type of listening is when the intellect is not involved; we listen like it is pleasant music. But even there, something is missing because when the music ends, nothing remains to work with. The experience ends along with the music. Therefore, we seek a third kind of listening. A combination of intellectual listening where the intellect works, investigates, and processes, but the heart remains open, and we allow everything to enter like pleasant music, even if we do not necessarily agree in our listening. During our meetings, there are two qualities that every student needs - courage and honesty. Courage is an essential quality because if we continue to tell ourselves only what is pleasant and comfortable and avoid facing the truth because it might be too painful or shocking, we will prefer to keep telling ourselves stories. Honesty is essential if we are to continue growing towards the truth. Without honesty, this is impossible. Courage and honesty - let’s ensure we bring these two qualities to every meeting.

Why do we invite ourselves to grow in the light of understanding fear and surrender? We know from experience that fear is one of the most significant forces shaping how we live, how we make our choices, how it reflects in our relationships, our partnerships, our encounters with the world. Life is managed by fears, some known, clear, and well-understood, and some hidden from view, working beneath the surface, yet still shaping how we allow ourselves to live. Therefore, confronting fear, learning about fear, and most importantly, rising above fear is perhaps the most significant step towards a life of freedom. I would say this is the definition of freedom. Free consciousness is consciousness that does not experience fear. Let’s start looking at fear and understand what is happening there. Two Essential Types of Fear

There are two types of fears we will address. The first type is fear which appears in the face of a clear and immediate danger. When clear and immediate danger reveals itself in the present moment, we fear. We agree that when this event happens, fear has a meaning and has an important role. This is why fear was born - to protect us and enable us to survive. When there is clear and immediate danger, it awakens us and prepares us. It pumps adrenaline into the blood, increases the pulse and blood pressure, makes us think fast and react quickly, and helps us react effectively. In this instance, fear is not a problem. It is our best friend. This is relevant only when the danger is clear and immediate. When there is no room for interpretation. If it is not a clear and immediate danger, it is not a clear and immediate danger. Q. A clear and immediate danger is something that physically harms us or attempts to harm us physically? A. As opposed to...? Q. As opposed to being in debt and fearing I might get fired.

A. A clear and immediate danger is a truck about to run me over. Standing in front of me is a robber who wants to steal my money and threaten my life. My husband comes home drunk and upset, looking for a reason to turn violent. Q. And if tomorrow I am called to the office and fired? A. If something might happen in the future, it is not a clear and immediate danger. A clear and immediate danger is a reality that threatens our physical health immediately. This means that on a safari trip, a tiger is standing behind me and is about to devour me. Q. What about an imagined reality that is likely to happen and cause unpleasant things? Is it not a danger?

A. Clear and immediate danger reveals itself only in our physical reality in the present moment. A clear and immediate danger reveals itself in the present moment and clearly and tangibly threatens our physical or mental health. When we see a tornado column in front of our house, that is a clear and immediate danger. Fear was born to keep us alive and healthy, to ensure we survive. It is not a problem when fear appears in the presence of clear and immediate danger. At that moment, it is time to respond wisely to the danger and stay alive. Up until this point, fear is not a problem. You see? We are here in this body to experience life. If our body is hurt, or taken, we cannot continue doing that. That is why life is sacred. Cherishing our body and keeping it safe when danger rises is a natural behavior.

However, life gives us very few opportunities to face clear and immediate danger. There are not many such situations in the modern world. How often have we gone to the zoo and found tigers roaming outside their cages? It almost never happens. We live in a protected environment that shields us from clear and immediate dangers. Most fears are psychological. Psychological fear is not designed to help us survive because our survival is not at risk. This fear only disrupts and interferes. It prevents us from being present with what is happening in the moment, and keeps us from merging with life, from loving, from living. This is the fear we will encounter in this series because the essence of spiritual development is to love, to meet, to be available, and to merge with life. If fear stands between us and this, it has no place, no role. It only disrupts and interferes.

So, what to do when this type of fear arises? Open your eyes and look right and left. Is there something threatening you at this moment, not in a moment, but right now? Is there a clear and immediate danger? If you do not see a lion standing in front of you, the fear you are experiencing now is unnecessary and redundant, and I invite you to rise above it. The first place to encounter this fear is in the body, which is the first station. Q. Can I ask about a fear that I might not know which category to put it in? For example, if a husband is afraid of his wife and therefore does not cheat on her? A. Only if she is holding a knife and advancing towards him with threatening steps. Q. And if not? What kind of fear is it? It’s a good fear, isn’t it?

A. First of all, being afraid of your wife is always good. However, for our purposes, we intentionally divide fear into two very clear groups, leaving no room for interpretation. Fear that is open to interpretation is the second type of fear, okay? The fear in the face of clear and immediate danger is not subject to interpretation. No two people will identify it differently. Q. So, according to you, if it’s the second type, a man should not fear his wife and should cheat on her? A. I never said that one should cheat. As a rule, I don’t make statements with the word ‘should’. The best I can do is create an invitation, and you choose what to do with it. Let’s move forward a bit more.

Q. Let me ask about a more grandiose example. Jews in Europe, in Poland in 1939, who recognized that the Nazis were exterminating Jews, and had to decide whether to stay in Poland or flee or immigrate to Israel. They recognized a kind of imaginary danger that was happening somewhere in Czechoslovakia, Austria, and Germany. Jews were being turned into ash. Was that a clear and immediate danger when they had to decide whether to stay or leave? A. Ah... that’s a good question. It obviously proved to be an impending danger, but the direction was entirely clear. Some people recognized it and fled. When the potential for danger is there, you prepare to deal with it. There’s nothing wrong with that. But your attention stays in the present moment, remaining available to experience it.

See how we are trying to validate this invitation in extreme points? We are saying If it works at the edges, it surely works in the middle. However, tomorrow morning we don’t need to face Hitler. Tomorrow morning, we need to face our boss at work, the cashier at the grocery store, and the person who cuts us off at the traffic light. The question is how we manage our reality, not necessarily some idea of an alternative reality. In our reality, can we identify when we are being controlled by psychological fear? Another point we mentioned last week, which is also relevant to your question, is that we act in response to the reality that reveals itself. To avoid being controlled by fear in our decisions, the recommendation is to ‘take care of business, not to worry.’ Remember, in Hebrew, ‘to worry/take care of business’ is one word, but in English, there are two phrases - ‘to worry’ or ‘to take care of business’. Don’t worry, I’ll take care of it. In Hebrew, we use the same word but mean two different things.

So, when something needs to be done, to organize in the face of a problematic reality, then we prepare and do what needs to be done. If that means packing and moving to another country, then we pack and move. But don’t be wrapped up in worry. Don’t be controlled by fear. Are we clear on fear in the mind? It’s just an idea, a movie running in my head. A movie about all the terrible things that might happen. Q. Yaron, what you’re saying is that after I identify that I am in a state of fear, like a physical signal, then there is this process of checking if we are in a lion-like situation. Now, there’s a thought process to dissolve this psychological movie and turn the action into something concrete, not just a movie. Is that what you’re saying? A. We haven’t reached that point yet. That belongs to the second half of the workshop. In the first half, we are just observing the dynamics of fear - how it happens, how it builds up, and how it is experienced on all levels of our existence. We are not yet trying to eliminate it. We are just trying to understand it and how it operates.

In the second half of the workshop, we will dedicate time to understanding how we can grow beyond fear and replace this force called fear with another force called surrender. That’s when we will begin to uncover deeper and deeper levels of freedom. At this stage, we are just inviting ourselves to understand these two types of fear - the one we experience when there is danger and the one we experience even when there is no danger. How is it experienced in the body? How is it experienced as a thought, as an idea in the mind? A movie? A horror movie? The country is falling apart. Civil society cannot handle the stress. We are facing the destruction of the Third Temple. People will start shooting each other in the streets, hunting each other for dinner... Ugh... the mind keeps going... a movie. At this stage, check if there is a lion. If there is no lion, understand that you are in a movie. Start to track this movie. See how it plays out in your head. Whoever does this, just this, has already done most of the work. Realize that we are talking about a movie. Fear in the Body

The first thing we notice is that when the body is afraid, it reacts in the same way as if the danger was clear and immediate - the body contracts. Blood pressure rises, the pulse increases, and adrenaline flows through the body. This can be at a subtle level or a truly paralyzing level, but the body responds to psychological fear as if there was clear and immediate danger. The body does not know how to make the distinction. Studies have shown that thinking about an apple and holding an apple in your hand creates almost the same CT scan image in the brain. The experience is the same. If I say lemon, lemonade, lemon, lemonade, you will start to feel the juices flowing in your mouth as if you are actually drinking a glass of lemonade. Think about a lemon, and I squeeze lemon juice... Can you taste it? Q. Can you overcome the feeling of hunger just by thinking? A. It is possible. Some yogis live only on prana. They hardly eat any food.

Back to fear in the body. The body reacts as if the danger is clear and immediate. If we are driven by fear, and this is the dominant quality that leads us, it means the body is constantly in defense mode against a non-existent danger. This leads to symptoms of wear and tear. The breath becomes unsettled and the body lives in constant stress. This wear-and-tear has a price, ending in chronic diseases like diabetes, heart attacks, strokes, and many other related outcomes. Our body is a sophisticated machine with qualities we are still learning to understand, but it also has a threshold capacity. When the threshold is exceeded, it cannot contain anymore. Eventually, the barrel fills up, and when it starts to overflow, we experience symptoms. How do we know the body is afraid? The body’s reaction is always one of contraction. It contracts in an attempt to protect itself from existent or non-existent danger. If we want to grow beyond fear on the level of the body, the first thing we need to do is identify this contraction. We will train ourselves to identify this contraction.

Q. It is uncontrollable. A. It can be resolved once identified. Every event in the world of phenomena is uncontrollable. This moment is inevitable. It is already happening. Q. What will we learn? A. We will learn to identify the contraction and understand that the body is afraid of a non-existent danger. Inevitably, we will meet this contraction as we meet all phenomena. There is no point in arguing with the world of phenomena. Arguing with the world of phenomena is the definition of suffering. This matter must be completely clear. Do not argue with the fact that you found a contraction in your body. Deal with the contraction without internal conflict. When this happens, it is ideal that the contraction is identified as early as possible, when it first arises.

To be able to identify the tension, we need to improve our communication skills with the body. Some people possess this skill naturally. Some claim that it is easier for women than for men, but the task is the same - create an open, two-way communication channel with the body. When the body speaks, we will be available to listen to it. Our mind will be alert enough to receive the message. Sometimes it will be almost imperceptible, and sometimes the body will scream so loudly that it will be impossible not to hear. The first thing we want to do is to train and strengthen our ability to communicate with the body. This is just a skill, and it is a muscle that we consciously choose to strengthen. Heal your Relationship with your Body I encourage you to practice this meditation that focuses on the body. The invitation here is Hello body, I am here for you. What can I do for you? Talk to me. Practice this every day. As the communication channel with the body becomes more sophisticated and clearer, it will be easier for us to identify the tension in real-time as it occurs.

The places where the contraction will be located most easily are in the second, third, fourth, and fifth chakras. It can also be experienced in the first, sixth, and seventh chakras, but there it will be on an energetic level. We will also find the tension in the breath - the breath will be difficult, restrained, not flowing smoothly and comfortably in and out. It will feel like we are lacking air. At this stage, it is important to emphasize that we are not yet trying to deal with the fear or eliminate it. We are not trying to treat the tension, but only to identify it. To encounter it. You can keep a journal to monitor these contractions as they occur.  Be aware. Be conscious in real-time as it happens. For now, just be able to identify it. This is 70% of the work - just identifying it is enough.

This contraction is the physical expression of our unwillingness to surrender to the moment, to what is happening. The body is the medium through which we interact with the physical world, with this moment, with reality. The fear is the physical expression of our unwillingness to be involved, to be in love, to embrace, and to merge with what is. We are in avoidance, saying No, this is not for me. The contraction is the physical expression of this avoidance. The energy of sexuality, the kundalini, is the energetical aspect of this connection, and the contraction we experience in the body is an expression of our unwillingness to merge with life, with life energy. The kundalini is choked within us. Awareness and the Body’s Role in Recognizing Fear Those who can become aware of the body’s signals, the ‘yes’ and ‘no,’ (contraction vs expansion) have taken a significant step towards using this body more effectively. In our context, the body can begin to be used to identify when fear governs us. Fear in the Mind Hi dear people.

Your homework was to dedicate time to noticing when we feel contracted and when we feel relaxed. I also provided a guided meditation to help improve communication skills with our bodies. Would anyone like to share their experiences? Q. I discovered that I am full of fears. I didn’t realize it, not to this extent. I feel fear when something in my body hurts, causing me to contract. If I see blood, I contract. If a bill arrives in the mail, I contract. Even an SMS notification makes me contract. Every message and every sound of an SMS notification causes contraction. If I’m told I need to be tested, my body contracts significantly. If I’m told there’s something wrong with my body, it almost throws me into stress. When I feel alone and have no one to consult, my body contracts. There were many opportunities in the past week... Q. I’ve noticed two things. One, my stress level is always high. And two, the contraction follows a thought, not necessarily an event. A. Yes, it’s excellent that you’ve made that distinction. It’s a significant step on the path out of that existential stress.

Recognizing Fear in Body, Mind, and Spirit We’re in the first half of the workshop, still not trying to solve fear, kill it, or get rid of it. We’re just getting to know it and meet it on three levels - body, mind, and spirit. Already, we can say that an unequivocal recommendation to grow beyond fear is to know that it exists, that it’s in the body, and that the body contracts because of it. That’s what we worked on last week. When this is experienced, when you realize that fear governs you now, it’s about opening your eyes and looking for the lion, looking for the clear and immediate danger. Sometimes the body is reacting to a danger that you’re not yet aware of. This can happen too. Open your eyes and look for the danger. Is there a danger? React and defend yourself. If there’s no danger, then it’s a different story. The fear you’re experiencing now is unnecessary. It only disrupts, spoils, and prevents you from fully experiencing, prevents you from realizing your full potential, and prevents you from living life fully.

Q. I observed the sensation, and it was sometimes hard to distinguish between contraction as a reaction to fear and, for example, self-criticism. The sensation was a contraction, and it wasn’t entirely clear to me how to identify which was which. A. Today, we will slowly become more and more intelligent in understanding fear and how it works within us. But self-criticism is also driven by fear. Otherwise, we wouldn’t be busy forming opinions about ourselves. Fear has no brand. It’s a generic label for the emotional/mental system that prevents us from merging with the present moment. It distances us and says No! When the body contracts, it says ‘No!’ When the body expands, it says ‘Yes!’ Now we climb another step on the ladder. We spoke about why it is so important to stop fearing fear, to recognize it, and to understand the dynamics of how it develops and manages us daily.

If anyone has ever wondered - What is free consciousness? How is it characterized? How can I recognize it? - this can be one of the answers to that question. Free consciousness is a consciousness that has stopped fearing life. We are on this journey to stop being afraid of life. So, we discovered the body is contracted. We opened our eyes and looked for the lion. There was no lion. Now it’s time to start the work... or at least continue the investigation. At this stage, we’re not doing anything effective about it. We’re just continuing to discover fear on deeper and deeper levels. Today, we invite ourselves to meet fear on the level of the mind. Understanding the Mind What is the mind? The mind is the organ within us that allows us to encounter reality as we are capable of digesting it. Let me explain what I mean.

Imagine a movie screen. We sit and watch the screen, encountering an ever-changing image that constructs a reality for us. This reality is composed of three types of occurrences - emotion, thought, and sensation. The combination of these three, each birthing the other, creates an image of reality with which we engage. Let’s talk a bit more about this tool called the mind. This organ is designed by evolution to allow us to see on the screen what we already know as possible. If we don’t have an image of something as a possibility in our minds, it is highly unlikely that it will be translated into a reality with which we can engage. There needs to be a ready-made template of such a possibility so that the mind can say what is happening now is like the template I have, so now I have a reference point.

Another function of the mind is aggressive filtering. It screens out from all that occurs around us only what it deems necessary for our consciousness to perform a task. This is an evolutionary trait. In the days when we were fleeing lions on the savannas, the mind could narrow down everything around us to just the most effective escape route or the tallest tree to climb so the lion wouldn’t catch us. It filters out what we don’t know is possible, and also what it thinks is not relevant for us or what we are not ready to digest. I invite you to practice the guided meditation (page 98) about the Mind, where the difference between the observer and the object of its observation is noticeable. The Mind’s Challenge The challenge for those on the spiritual path is to improve this tool called the Mind - to expand it. To allow more and more of what is truly happening to be experienced by learning more patterns, and more possibilities. By broadening the filter, more information can come through the five senses and be received as reality.

It's said that an awakened consciousness is broad enough to no longer filter anything, exposing us to much more subtle levels of existence to which we are usually completely blind. Suddenly, we can see auras, recognize subtler frequencies of reality, and so on. What was once considered esoteric becomes reality for us simply because it is now being projected on the movie screen, just like other experiences we have naturally encountered until now. Our challenge is to refine our mind; to enhance it so it can pass through more of the great light with as few distortions as possible into our awakened awareness and onto the screen. Expanded Consciousness

Sometimes, people wanting to feel what it’s like to live with an awakened consciousness take such leaps through psychedelic drugs. And it does work in the sense that the filter stops working for a while, throwing us into very subtle levels of consciousness and exposing us to levels of reality to which we were previously blind. But everything has a price. When this regulator is shut down, the consciousness is bombarded with so much information and exposed to such delicate complexities of reality that it can collapse into itself, leading to an overload. This is what happens to people who do this recklessly. It can result in a difficult-to-repair malfunction. The mind goes into overload, and it’s a problem that’s hard to fix later. We can expand the mind’s capacity by learning and adding more and more patterns and by practicing meditation. Meditation helps our mind become more attentive and allows for subtler levels of being and reality to be experienced. Q. Is the mind shaped by our stories?

A. Yes, our personal stories also impact the mind. When we say my story, we are referring to the fifth level of existence - everything we have experienced up to today, including our culture, language, education, and the reality we have encountered along the way. Of course, this influences us. The more pluralistic and open our education and culture are, the more they present us with possibilities and teach us broader thinking and acceptance of others. This way, the mind becomes a tool that allows for more of what is happening to be experienced. If we grow up in a fundamentalist society that dismisses anything outside its framework not only as irrelevant but as a real threat, then our mind becomes very limited and narrow, allowing only a very restricted reality to be experienced. The Role of the Mind in Fear Now let us see how this is relevant to our lesson on fear. In the mind, we encounter the birthplace of fear. This is the realm where we face our fears because, in the mind, we experience one of three phenomena - emotion, thought, or sensation. Their combination builds our reality.

What is fear? Fear is just an idea, a thought. From the beginning of this lesson, we have moved away from fears that are a response to clear and immediate danger. Now, we are not afraid because a lion is in front of us. We are afraid of a potential future reality that might present a lion - an idea. So, we encounter a threatening thought, and we react to it as if it is the reality. The body responds to this thought as if it is truly happening. This happens in various intensities, but that is the dynamic. In the mind, we discover fear in its essence. This is its substance - a thought. For example, it could be a phone call from your boss telling you to come to his office. Immediately, you’re terrified, breaking into a cold sweat. You start imagining all the terrible things that could happen. You are immediately covered by worst-case scenarios and respond to them as if they are the reality. He is about to fire me so I better get prepared with my contingency plans. Who do I know in my field? Maybe they can help me get a job…

Q. But that protects you in a way. You are mentally prepared for your boss. A. You are mentally prepared for the worst-case scenario with your boss. But I am here to claim something different. This mental preparation does not help you. It hinders you. We will examine this slowly. Our challenge is to refine our minds. To enhance them so they can pass through more of the great light with as few distortions as possible into our awakened awareness. This way, we allow finer levels of reality to be experienced and overcome the unnecessary fears that prevent us from living life fully and realizing our potential. Understanding Fear in the Mind In the Mind, we encounter movies - horror movies about all the things that aren’t happening but might happen later. This is another important thing we learn about fear. Fear takes us from the present and throws us into the future through a futuristic movie playing in our minds. In the present moment, there is no clear and immediate danger. Otherwise, we wouldn’t be having this discussion right now. We’d be busy trying to climb a tree quickly.

Fear takes us into the future, saying, sure, there’s no lion in front of you now, but that means nothing about five minutes from now. Fear is an impression from the past that we project onto the future of the present moment. Something terrible happened to you, or to someone you know, or that you read about in the news, and now you fly forward in time and tell yourself God forbid, let this not happen again. This is fear in the Mind. That’s how it is experienced in the Mind. Thoughts run, run, run, and you follow them to what might happen. Q. What is the difference between experience and fear? There is a life experience that teaches you and helps you imagine how the future might look based on what is happening now. So, what is the difference between fear and life experience? A. Life experience teaches us that every time we are governed by fear, we lose. Reality loses. The scenery loses. Do you remember the story about the scenery?

When the White Path first began, in one of the initial lessons, a student shared a story about a road that goes down from Jerusalem to the Dead Sea. Every time she had to travel this road, she remembered herself as a child being very, very afraid. Every time she had to go through that road, she closed her eyes and wished for the end. After we went through the lesson about fear, she decided that the next time she traveled that road, no matter what, she would open her eyes and allow herself to experience whatever happens, even if it was the last thing she did. She said it was an amazing experience because she discovered how beautiful the road is and how incredible the descent to the Dead Sea is. She said, “I gained the scenery.” So, I told her, “The scenery gained. It gains your awakened consciousness to experience it and give it the meaning of beauty.”

If your life experience hasn’t brought you to free consciousness, it may be lacking. Perhaps, with all due respect, it’s time to grow towards something new that your life experience has not yet recognized as an immediate reality. What do you think? Q. I understand that the scenery gained her consciousness to fill it with the meaning of beauty, but what is in it for us? A. Nothing. We won’t be here in 50 years! It doesn’t matter. Something much bigger benefits. Much bigger than me and what’s in it for me. Understand that the part of you asking these questions is called the Ego. That ego is doomed, unfortunately. We’ll get to that soon. It’s a bit early. Thoughts run through your head - movies, futuristic horror films play on your mental screen. You react to these movies as if they are reality, as if the danger is clear and immediate. Your body reacts that way. Your psyche reacts that way.

The response is like a response to a real danger - trying to avoid it, escape it, eliminate the problem that isn’t even there yet. You are entirely tense in resistance, completely bracing yourself against an imagined reality. This is what happens when you experience fear in the mind. Homework for the Sincere Seeker I suggest some more homework for you. In the coming week explore the faculty of the mind, how fear appears there, and how fear in the mind is translated into the body. You have already encountered listening to the body over the past week. So, refine this practice, continue to practice it, and see the place where it started. When does the body contract? In most cases, it isn’t because there was a clear and immediate danger. It was a thought, an idea, a movie running in your head. You got stuck in it, caught up with it, and believed it. You reacted as if it were a real danger. I invite you to do this practice, a very significant and critical practice for those seeking a life of freedom.

Q. Can I ask something? I don’t quite understand the difference between this lesson and the previous one. If last week I was aware of contractions, then now what? To be aware of what? A. Become aware of the contraction and then ask, why did it happen? Why did your body contract just now? Practice listening to your body and identifying contractions in real-time. You felt a contraction in your stomach - wait, your stomach is contracted. You have a lump in your stomach. Then you immediately pause. Wait, why? What happened? Why did it contract? Rewind the mental ‘movie’ 30 seconds back. What was happening?? You will likely find some idea you were resisting, some possibility it presented. Last week, the focus was only on the physical contraction, regardless of its source. To meet the contraction without trying to solve it. To see and feel it as it happens. Now you can add checking why. Why did it happen? What was the thought that birthed the contraction?

It could be something very subtle. Someone walking down the street without a mask during the pandemic, and you tense up thinking, Here’s another one who doesn’t care about anyone. You have an idea in your head, an idea that causes the body to contract. Create these bookmarks for yourself. Every time the body contracts, check what thought caused this contraction. If you happen to encounter a clear and immediate danger that causes the body to contract, note it down. Although, usually, it will be due to fictional, futuristic movies presenting you with possibilities of future danger. Fear is a generic name for all the ideas and thoughts that cause us to avoid and resist. Q. Any argument with reality causes contraction in the body? A. Yes, you can word it that way. Alternatively, we said that fear and suffering are first cousins.

What is the definition of suffering? The gap between what is and what you thought it should be. And fear is the gap between what is and what you don’t want to happen. It’s almost a nuance. They are essentially the same; thoughts that divert you from what is to something else in the past or future. When you are in that gap between what is and what might happen or between what is and what you believe should happen but isn’t happening, the body contracts. We give all these contractions a generic name - fear or avoidance. Maybe we should call the next workshop ‘Avoidance versus Surrender’, but ‘Fear’ sounds more attractive. Q. What happens when the fear is realistic, for instance, now in the era of COVID-19 and the recession? Suppose someone hasn’t found a job for seven months. He fears he will become poor or never find a job again. That fear is realistic. What is wrong with this fear?

A. It’s not about labeling fear as good or bad, right or wrong. We no longer evaluate our behavior in terms of right or wrong. There is only free consciousness and consciousness that is not yet free. The question is, what kind of consciousness do we want for ourselves and for the scenery waiting for us? Your question is ahead of its time because we are not trying to solve the problem but just to learn about it. If we solve everything in the first two or three meetings, no one will show up for the fourth session. Remember, do not worry - just take care of things. Do what you need to do, but ensure you are not governed by fear. If you need to find a job, do what is necessary to find a job. If you need to make contingency plans for potential future realities, then create those plans, but do not act out of fear. Acting out of fear and acting out of responsibility are two entirely different things. Responsibility does not stem from fear but from a force that is the opposite of fear. Love. Do what you need to do. Just make sure that you are not governed by fear.

Living Fully Versus Living in Fear When you live governed by fear, you live alongside life. You utilize only a fraction of your potential. Q. If we are contracting because of things that actually happened, like terror attacks, how does this relate to fear? A. You can experience sadness and sorrow without contracting. To feel sadness because of inhumanity such as a terror attack is entirely natural. As part of the human fabric, we feel this pain. But we do not suffer because of it, we do not get angry, and we do not become frustrated or bitter. Instead, we become proactive and do what is right in the face of such inhumanity. Q. If we are contracted, then, is it because of fear? A. It is because we believe it should not have happened. We view it as a cosmic mistake, thinking God got it wrong. When we are trapped in this belief, we live alongside life, utilizing only a small part of our full potential. Q. How can we think differently?

A. The secret is to understand that it is just an idea. It’s merely your intellect encountering the image on the screen and forming an opinion about it. You can have a negative, critical opinion, convincing yourself that it was a terrible mistake that should not have happened, and then you are governed by frustration and disappointment, leading to inevitable violence. When you are driven by your beliefs about what should have been, and those beliefs contradict reality, it is almost inevitable that you become violent. Violence doesn’t necessarily have to end in murder, but even yelling at others because they don’t understand what is clear to you is violence. Or manipulating others to change according to your ideas and expectations. Q. So, if I go to a protest and shout because I am angry, am I violent? A. Protests, at least some of them, are not against anything. Many protests I’ve seen on TV are not against something. They are for love, compassion, listening, and humanity. Can’t you see that? Allow your mind to expand. What do you allow in?

Q. I don’t agree. This may have happened at the margins. The main focus was a lot of anger about the situation. A. That may be, but the question is which team do you prefer to be associated with? Do you want to belong to the group driven by anger and frustration, leading to disharmony and violence, or the group driven by love? Understand that it does not matter what reality we face. Reality can be joyful and happy or shocking and terrible. An awakened consciousness is not intimidated by either. It is not detached from life, saying Let the world burn, this doesn’t concern me. Quite the opposite. It is deeply involved. Everything that happens is a part of it, everything affects it, and it influences everything in return. It is aware of this. This nature of the awareness is what makes it free. It does not act out of suffering, frustration, or distress. It doesn’t try to avoid or manipulate reality to fit its own system of thought, regarding what is right, just, moral, and humane.

Q. I am absolutely certain that rape shouldn’t happen, that it is unnecessary. I don’t want to open up all the possibilities of alternative thinking. I’m sure it didn’t have to happen! A. Then, I’m sure you’re suffering... Q. Why? Do you think there’s a possibility that it’s meant to happen? I don’t understand. A. I stopped arguing with life. Someone once asked Byron Katie if she considered herself enlightened. Her response was, “I don’t know if I’m enlightened, I’m not exactly sure what that means, but I do know that I stopped arguing with life.” She continued to say that some people spend their lives trying to argue with life but they lose 100% of the time because reality is stronger than our thoughts and opinions, no matter how just or moral they may be. Q. So when you hear something like that, you simply say I’m not arguing with that part of life? A. The alternative is to suffer.

Now, it doesn’t mean I’m not going to act to eliminate human suffering, to elevate human consciousness, to make it more developed, more advanced, and naturally, more humane. The consequence of the elevation of human consciousness will be that such events will cease to exist. But, if they don’t cease to exist, I won’t be frustrated, angry, disappointed, or vengeful, and I won’t act violently. Q. So, what drives you? A. Love. I don’t act because of what isn’t, but because of what is. Q. You were talking about love, but I think you’re referring to something else. I have the sense that you’re talking about something that’s not love. In a state of a whole heart and willing soul, would you accept such an event? A. The alternative is to suffer and suffering won’t make you more effective in influencing reality harmoniously. Inner disharmony manifests as disharmonious action and has a disharmonious effect on life. That’s the math of life. When the heart is whole and the soul is willing, that is the ultimate expression of unconditional love. Q. What do you mean when you say ‘Love’?

A. That’s what we’ll discuss a little later. We won’t cover it today. Today we’ll just get a teaser. Love is the power that is the opposite of fear and resistance. When we prefer the idea, it’s forbidden, absolutely forbidden, for such an event to happen, we’re consumed by rage, frustration, and disappointment. We’re wrapped in bitterness. There’s no harmony coming from this mental state. When we act out of that state of mind, it is called ‘karma yoga.’ We’re just producing more karma for ourselves and for the society around us. About Desperation Q. You’re talking about anger, but I think you’re overlooking the deep despair and powerlessness that’s here, especially if you’re a woman. Perhaps it’s fitting to notice that for a minute. Let’s discuss despair. A. Desperation is just sadness that won’t go away, that is stuck. Why is it stuck? Because we resist it. What you resist, persists.

As Rabbi Nachman of Breslov said, “There is no despair in the world.” What did he mean? I don’t know. I’m a small Breslov Hasid, but I have the sense that he meant that despair is in our minds, not in the world. When do we feel despair? When disappointment accumulates. The barrel of disappointment gets filled up, and then it starts to overflow. And then it becomes despair. We have thoughts about what should have been. The thoughts are magnificent, just, moral, and humane. But they’re just thoughts in our heads. Reality proves to us that it’s not working out as we thought, as we believed, as we hoped for. We’re frustrated and disappointed until the barrel is full, until we despair. When we despair, a few things can happen. The first thing that can happen is that we lose hope and become apathetic. Another thing that can happen is that we burst out with anger and violence towards everyone we meet, taking out our frustration on them. We become the mercenary of our own ideas, with the sword of justice and righteousness we behead anyone who disagrees with us.

The third thing that can happen, and this is something that many of us don’t emphasize enough, is that desperation has a great transformative potential. When we’re truly desperate, nothing seems important enough to us to hold onto, to fight for, and that can be translated to a meaningful transformation towards freedom. Free awareness doesn’t fight over ideas. It is broad enough to hold onto an idea with the same level of importance, or non-importance, whatever you choose to call it. Nothing Restricts Free Awareness When you’re desperate, remember that this too can be an opportunity, a leap to freedom. But then, go all the way with the desperation. Truly surrender and let go. Let it take you deep into the truth of who you are, and something new will emerge from there. I suggest reviewing this conversation again to allow everything to be fully understood. Everything is Legitimate? Q. You say that awakened consciousness allows every idea. Does that mean that I can think that rape is legitimate? A. If it’s truly free, then awareness isn’t examining reality in these terms at all.

It’s real, it’s realistic. How do we know it’s realistic? Because it happens. That’s it. All the things we put on it distance us from it. We’re putting all this aside. Q. If everyone learned from you, then there wouldn’t be people who changed the world. For example, Martin Luther King. If he thought like you, that there’s no good or bad, we’d still be in the Dark Ages. A. I claim there’s a different power that isn’t driven by fear, anger, need, or attachment. A stronger power that drives human evolution. I can present an even longer list of people who changed human history not because they were driven by Good and Bad, but because they loved. In fact, if you think about it, MLK Jr. belongs to this long list as well.

What is more relevant is to check what kind of human being you want to be. Do you want to be a human being who is dedicated to cursing reality because you believe it’s messed up and that what is happening should not happen? That it is a mistake, a failure, that God is sleeping, and hasn’t woken up yet? Or do you want to be an expression of free consciousness, of all-encompassing love? This is the only relevant question for someone who is walking the spiritual path: What kind of quality do I want to bring to this world? Q. What’s the connection to God? If I say I don’t want someone to be the prime minister, then what does it have to do with God? It’s people. A. First of all, in our case, the prime minister is God…. Aside from that, God is just a brand, you know. A brand name for reality as it unfolds. God = The Present Moment. Q. So how do we act to change the existing, if we believe the existing isn’t good? Are we indifferent? A. Heaven forbid….

We’re involved, we act, we touch life, and allow life to touch us. We’re not blocking experiences anymore and we’re full partners. Full partners. We’re part of it. We’re more than partners. We’re not even talking about two. It’s one. One awareness that experiences all of this. I’m but one aspect of this Wholeness. Q. I don’t understand. A. It’s all okay my dear, it’s not something that needs to be understood. Q. Let’s assume Martin Luther King Jr. had an open mind like yours, then he would have accepted both the idea that slavery is okay and the idea that slavery is not okay. But to rise up and change that, you need to have an opinion, just like you have an opinion about rape and you’re going to change that. You’re going to give life imprisonment to anyone who ever rapes. He can’t simultaneously think that slavery is not okay and okay. A. I never take my opinions too seriously…

Let’s take this example of MLK Jr. and apply the three-stage technique we learned to close the gap. First, he believes that slavery is not okay, so he suffers (i.e. frustration anger, violence…). Then he believes that slavery is okay and he stops suffering. But he is still opinionated about it. When he finally chooses his love over his opinions, then he’s free to transform himself to be an expression of unconditional love. This is the definition of a harmonious flow of life. That is how he became such a prominent leader, in league with Mahatma Gandhi, Nelson Mandela, and others. We all know what usually motivates us. It’s a sense of lack, a sense of need. There’s an idea that if we’re not hungry, why should we get out of bed and go to work? Why should we do anything? I’m saying there’s a much more significant force, at least in my eyes, than a sense of lack and need. That force is what motivates us to act, much more than the narrow structure of our personalities and our ideas.

This force is much bigger, much more universal, and it flows through us, allowing all these happenings to occur. It’s not connected to our personal opinions about what’s right and wrong. It’s not about morals, justice, and so on. I’m inviting you to examine what motivates you to get out of bed and face the world, face life. Is it thoughts of frustration, disappointment, violence, need, or lack? Or is it the opposite? Imagine being involved in change that is not instigated by opinions. The way to harness your energy to harmoniously engage with the flow of life is to drop your opinions about slavery, rape, or any other event. Then, and only then, you ensure your motivation is free of suffering because you’re not craving or averting the reality you meet. Is the Distinction Between Good and Bad Helpful? Q. Does the distinction between good and bad necessarily hide a sense of lack, or fear?

A. The distinction between good and bad puts us in an unavoidable trap. If it’s good, we try to hold on to it, to protect it from being damaged. If it’s bad, we need to change it ASAP into good, because we can’t accept it as it is. In both cases, we’re in a trap that distances us from reality, from our encounter with reality. There’s a gap between us and life, and that gap is filled by my thoughts and opinions. Free consciousness doesn’t hold onto that gap. It’s simply open. I haven’t yet entered into the intricacies of how to create change but we will talk about it later. For now, let’s just examine this trap, examine the mechanics of it. I invite you to simply observe how it manages you. What causes this contraction? What idea do you have in your mind? When you encounter an idea that is stealing your awareness from the present moment, how do you respond to it? Without trying to fix anything, just observe it, observe this dynamic. Q. Thoughts come like lightning. It’s like trying to catch a lightning bolt. Like that song, “Oops, I did it again...”

A. It’s not a problem. We’re not trying to kill ideas, not trying to defeat them. We’re just observing them. And that means doing a rewind and looking back. Ah, 30 seconds ago, I had this idea. And now I’m contracted. So, recognize it. No need to be upset with yourself. Oops, I did it again. We’re not trying to avoid it. We’re just being aware. Okay, so let’s dedicate the coming week to doing our homework. I recommend practicing the mind meditation to help you encounter the mind directly. We’ll meet again next week and invite ourselves to face fear at the level of the spirit. Fear in the Spirit White Path Meeting June, 2023 So far, we have discussed fear in the first two levels - Body and Mind. Today, we are moving on to the third level in our journey into the depths of fear. This level is called ‘Fear in the Spirit’. At the level of spirit, we can address fear at two further sublevels, one more obvious and one more subtle.

On the more obvious level, we talk about the ego as the producer of fear. The ego is the factory. That’s where fear is born. So, to understand this issue, it is first important to understand what the ego is, especially for those visiting for the first time. The terminology must be clear. What is ego? For the sake of this discussion, the ego is not just the definition of someone who thinks they are great, wonderful, magnificent, and noble. The ego is equally the definition of someone who thinks they are worthless, a loser, crushed, and trampled by life. In both cases, there is an entity that refers to itself distinctly and separately. This entity that refers to itself as either great or worthless is called the ego. That part within me that constantly convinces me that I and the other are not the same thing, that it’s not one fabric but two. There is me and there is the other, and we are negotiating all the time. That’s the ego. Whether I’m big or small, it’s still me. This I that attributes qualities to itself, that attributes a distinct identity to itself, is the ego.

The Wave and the Ocean The most effective way I’ve found to illustrate this so it will be easy to understand is through the metaphor of the wave and the ocean. Think of an ocean, calm and tranquil, from which waves occasionally rise. Miraculously, one of these waves gains self-awareness and becomes conscious of itself. This self-awareness begins to ask itself questions like: What do I want? What do I need? What’s in it for me? I want to be green. I don’t want to be blue like everyone else. I want to express my uniqueness. I see the shoreline approaching, and people... guys… we are about to crash! What’s going on with you? I want to sail backward, not towards the shore! Such ideas of a separate self-awareness flood the consciousness of this wave more and more until after 30-40 seconds, like all waves, it crashes on the shore and merges back into the ocean from which it was never separated.

The fact that the wave doesn’t remember it’s part of the ocean doesn’t mean it’s not part of the ocean. It means it lives a life of forgetfulness. Hence, the invitation is always about waking up from an illusion. Waking up from the dream. Seeing the wave not as a separate and distinct entity that is supposed to look after itself, alone and negotiating with life, but simply as a temporary oceanic expression. We are a temporary oceanic expression. This is the essence of spiritual awakening. As long as this does not happen, we experience ourselves as separate and distinct from others, from the world, from reality. This oceanic expression is very temporary. How long does a wave live? 30-40 seconds? Not much. Then it returns to the ocean, and another expression rises. Right, so 70/80 years? 90 years? 100 years? What is that compared to eternity? Have you ever thought about that? It’s not even a hiccup.

The wave is managed from a place of separateness and alienation as if it is foreign and not connected to abundance. It does not see itself as an oceanic expression so it is not connected to the ocean’s energy. It constantly feels as if it has to generate all this energy by itself, for itself. The context of that journey is always one of lack and deficiency because there is no connection to abundance. The ego, which causes us to experience alienation and foreignness, constantly convinces us that there isn’t enough. The whole journey becomes about trying to take, trying to get, more and more. And the little we manage to get, we protect dearly, heaven forbid that it is taken away. A whole life managed out of fear that stems from a sense of lack and deficiency, need, and dependency. Our encounter with life becomes just an endless opportunity to take, to fill ourselves from the outside in, and to protect the little we have. This is the starting point from which we go out into the world. I don’t have. I don’t have. Give me. Give me. Q. Yaron, what does the ego need to protect?

A. The illusion of itself. Because it knows that when the illusion disappears, it will die. The ego is a very sophisticated creature. Very sophisticated. And it has very special ways to convince us that its existence is the only true security we have. It keeps filling us with fears about losing control. It would say something like: Are you crazy? Surrendering? That’s dangerous. Take responsibility. Create a safe environment for yourself. Life is a battle and whoever isn’t strong enough loses. One of the ego’s slogans is ‘Take Responsibility’. One of the significant criticisms of people who walk the spiritual path is that they don’t take responsibility for their lives. It’s considered a kind of escape from real confrontation with life. Do you recognize this? Come on, forget this nonsense. Grow up already. Take responsibility.

Q. But on the other hand, there is a phenomenon where people don’t take responsibility, they expect someone else to give them what they lack. The state, their spouse, their children, their parents. Why should I be responsible for my room? Let my mother clean it. Why should I serve in the army? Let others do it. A. If you truly love your country, you won’t ask yourself if it’s important for you to take responsibility. You’ll just take responsibility, whether it’s through military service, national service, volunteering, or simply being a good neighbor to the people who live around you. You’ll find a way to contribute because of that sense of belongingness, which is derived from your love. Responsibility won’t be some idea that you adopt because it’s important, fair, or moral, or because it’s the mature thing to do. Rather it results from the love inside you, from the connection you have with the object of your love.

If responsibility is something you take on yourself because it’s important, or because you’re trying to act mature, it will always be a burden, a load, and at the first opportunity you find, you’ll give up. You’ll cut some corners. Or you’ll find other ideas to play with. Responsibility is not an idea. Real responsibility is a result of love. Of connection. Of your connection with the object you’re responsible for. It’s not an idea, it’s simply the way this connection is expressed. A life that is managed by the ego is a life that is based on lack and absence. Your encounter with the world, with reality, will be an encounter that is managed by the ego’s mantra. What do I need? What do I want? What will I get out of it? Q. What is the role of the ego? Does it have any role at all? A. The role of the ego is to create the tension to reunite, which is the propelling force of evolution. Q. Tell me again, Yaron, why do we need the ego?

A. The ego builds an illusion of separation, behind which lies the longing. The longing to return home. The longing to reunite. The longing to stop this separation within us, and to experience unity as an existential experience. To melt away the boundaries where I end and the world begins. Key Points: The ego creates a sense of separation from others and the world, which can lead to feelings of lack and need. True responsibility comes from a place of love and connection, not from a sense of obligation or duty. The ego can be a catalyst for personal growth and awakening by keeping one last I want - I want to be free! Q. It’s very interesting because a newborn baby doesn’t really have an ego. The ego develops slowly. At first, he and the whole world are completely one.

A. Exactly. Look at babies, they are great teachers of Zen Buddhism. They will simply show you what a human being looks like before feeling separated and not distinct. When she is sad, from her point of view, the whole world is sad. When she is happy, from her point of view, the whole world is happy because there is no separation. The ego starts to work and develop the moment our needs and wants are not met immediately. This happens almost as soon as we come out of our mother’s womb because until then we don’t even know what a need is. Right? Even before we’re hungry, there’s already food going straight into our stomachs. Everything is quiet and calm, we’re floating. Heaven. And then we suddenly come out into the light and cold, and it hurts and it’s hard, and we’re stressed and screaming, and our umbilical cord is being cut. Oh, what a mess.

Slowly an experience of lack is built up. We’re hungry, but we don’t get food. We keep getting hungrier. Wait, hey... that wasn’t the agreement between us. This lack builds up over the years. We find ourselves a separate and distinct entity or at least one who experiences themselves as separate and distinct, and who begins to engage in some kind of negotiation, bargaining with life. I don’t have enough, so life will have to find a way to provide it for me. That’s how the ego works. Q. But you said ‘Fear in the Spirit’, that it all started with the fact that there are two sublevels, one of the ego... A. Yes, I’m checking your alertness. It’s coming... But first, let’s finish talking about the ego. Our entire system of fears stems from there. It stems from a sense of lack, want, and need. All psychological fears, all of them, stem from there. If you want to delve into the depths of fear, you will find that there are only two fears. All other fears are just derivatives of these two basic fears.

The first fear is the fear of not getting what you believe you don’t have. The second fear is the fear of losing what you believe you have managed to achieve: that which is ‘mine’. These are the two fears. There is no third fear. All other fears are simply derivatives of these fears. Do you understand what I’m saying? For example, you’re afraid of losing your job. This is the fear of losing what you believe you have. What do you have? You have security. You have stability. You have income. You have status. You’re afraid of losing all of that. You managed to achieve it and now You’re afraid of losing it. Or, you're afraid of being alone. What does that mean? Not getting what you believe you don’t have. You don’t have love. You don’t have stability. You don’t have acceptance. You don’t have someone to take care of you. I don’t have… I don’t have… and I’m afraid life won’t give me that. These are the two fears. There is no third fear.

At this point I want to invite you, in the coming week, to check your psychological fears, and try to associate them with one of these two groups. Take the fear that you are experiencing at a given moment and figure out what type of fear it is. Are you afraid of losing what you believe is yours and that you’ve managed to achieve, or are you afraid of not getting what you believe you don’t have and that life is supposed to provide? This is an essential part of our journey beyond fear. In the second half of our workshop, all that remains is to do this... burning of chametz, just the final touches, that’s it. How Does Fear Manifest in the Deeper and More Subtle Level of the Spirit?

Okay, now we’ll take a few minutes to address fear at the more delicate level of the spirit. This is a fear that we often do not characterize directly because fear is very much associated with the level of personality. Rightly so, because most fears are experienced directly at the level of the persona, the ego. What is a persona? It is a combination of your story (the fifth level) and the ego (the sixth level). But there is an even deeper level that we experience at an existential level, and this is the soul’s fear of experiencing this life. The resistance to the very fact that we are here. The resistance to the human experience. Something very deep inside us, very delicate inside us, doesn’t really want to be here. This causes us to surround ourselves with a kind of defense, a shield.

It is a defense against encountering life. A defense that stems from our unwillingness to be here in a body and to experience the time span we are given. I can tell you that, personally, I encounter this avoidance very much. It’s a fear that’s very familiar to me. This is my first memory. The realization that I am here. Again?? I was sure I was done with it. Another round? That was a very big disappointment. I could not find my place on this planet. A true sense of astonishment. This was the context of my very existence for years. In my early years, naturally, I was not able to translate it to this terminology. As a kid, I didn’t feel I belonged, disconnected from everything. Always a bit weird. As the years went by, I grew to realize what I was feeling was a resistance to the very human experience. Q. This fear can awaken not only as a child but as an adult as well.

A. I can say it took me years before I was able to explain it to myself in this terminology; the sense of alienation, the estrangement, the lack of belonging, and the incompatibility I felt over the years. One can certainly awaken to this at a later age. Q. But why do you call it fear? As a person who has experienced it since childhood, I can tell you it’s more of a burden. Just a burden... A. Fear, as we said last week, is a generic label for the entire emotional spectrum that causes us to avoid, resist, to reject. We said it’s just another aspect of suffering, right? Suffering is the gap between what is and what we thought should have been. Fear is the gap between what is and what we don’t want to happen. It's the same thing with a negative sign. So, this whole experience of avoidance - I don’t want this. It’s uncomfortable for me. It’s unpleasant for me. It scares me - is what we call Fear, the opposite of surrender.

Q. Does the fear of lack of meaning fall under this subtle fear of actually having no meaning in life? What am I doing here? What am I contributing to? To whom am I contributing? Does it fall under this fear? A. Certainly. But again, it’s important for me that you are aware of the fact that even here, what drives the avoidance is the experience of separateness. It’s still a life that is an expression of a separate and distinct consciousness seeking meaning for itself. What am I doing here? Why did I receive a body and have to experience all this samsara all over again? Where is my gain? And still, although it’s a more subtle type, it’s a type of separate and distinct consciousness, preoccupied with avoiding and resisting. For now, we do nothing to solve it. We are only identifying and recognizing it. Stop fearing the fear. Make it completely clear. Understand where it is born, and how it navigates our choices and our encounters with life. Let’s summarize what we’ve covered so far, and then I invite you to ask questions.

Fear is born from the illusion of lack and deficiency, need, and dependence, which itself is born from a sense of alienation, from separateness, or at least the illusion of separateness. This system of fears serves itself. Actually, it serves the separateness and alienation and tries to convince us - usually quite successfully - to create a whole heap of defenses around us to ensure that the little we have is preserved and protected from life. This affects the entire way we engage with life, with reality, and within our relationships, which are always managed by negotiation. I don’t have enough. I’m giving too much. I should get me and give less. They should give more and get less.

This manifests itself through scenarios running in our heads, convincing us that all the terrible things being projected in our minds are really about to happen, and we need to prepare accordingly and manage ourselves against the constant and endless threat that life offers us. This manifests itself in the body, within an endless system of contraction and a state of defense, at varying levels of intensity. We’ve now outlined the entire spectrum, where it’s born, how it manifests, and how it impacts our system - body, mind, and spirit. Questions... Q. How do we deal with this fear? What you are suggesting is not realistic. It’s a fear that runs through our minds, but the body remembers, and the mind remembers. A. Regarding how we deal with it, we will start talking about that next week. So far, we are not trying to fix it. We are just encountering it. We are learning to recognize how it looks, and how it manifests. We are not yet trying to solve the fear or kill it, but only to recognize it and befriend it.

Q. I have a question about the ego. Is there no situation where the ego helps us grow? Is it only negative? A. Excellent question and the answer is that we don’t measure it in positive or negative ways. We must refine the way we examine our reality. A free consciousness does not categorize its encounter with reality as good or bad, positive or negative. This is what the intellect constantly tries to do - to decide if it’s good or bad. But a free consciousness knows it’s neither good nor bad, it just is. Q. Often, people talk about the ego as something negative. The ego controls us. For example, if we get hurt, it’s our ego. There are many situations where we take our ego and make it something big that controls us. Dropping the Good and the Bad

A. The Ego is neither good nor bad. The Ego is NOT. When you encounter this illusion as a phenomenon, what do you do with it? Do you choose to meet this phenomenon, learn from it, and grow to be free from it? Or do you choose to continue being managed by the endless stream of fears that the ego creates for you? Either way, it’s not good or bad. It just is. With your permission, let me take you back to the Garden of Eden. Do you remember what happened there? God says to man, “Take this, I created it for you, go enjoy life, and have fun.” It’s written almost in these words. “Go, go enjoy.”

There was only one thing He told Man not to do. Just one thing to avoid. Do you remember? Don’t eat the fruit from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. (If you want the exact phrase as written in the Old Testament - Genesis 2:16 “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden, but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil”). This is the first conversation between God and Man. The first true commandment. We all know the story but somehow miss the point of it. Or maybe it was intentional because the system needs us to believe that there is good and evil and we need to be good and avoid evil. We will tell you what good and evil are. Good is A, B, C, and D, and evil is E, F, G, and H. This is good and that is evil, and you’ll act according to what we convinced you is good and you will avoid evil if you wish for our approval. Q. So is the message that once you start dealing with good and evil, you’re expelled from Eden? A. Exactly. The gates are open, but to enter you need to let go of the idea that you know better than God about what is good and what is bad.

The ego is neither good nor bad because the ego is not. The illusion of the ego exists. The question is, what do we do when we recognize this illusion? God says, “Leave it alone. Let it go. This is my domain. If there’s one thing I ask you to do, it is to leave it to me.” But Man says, “No, no, no, I want to know what good and evil are. I want to decide what good and evil are.” So God says, “Fine, go. Go decide. If you want to come back, the door is open. But you can’t decide this for me. You don’t know.” Q.
