Does that mean that the ego is actually the catalyst for our entire life’s journey so that we can awaken? A. Absolutely. The longing for home is what creates the developmental tension that allows for the evolution of consciousness. I know that to some of us, this sounds like a poem, too theoretical, but that’s okay, we can listen to it like a poem too. It’s not necessarily something that the intellect can wrap its head around and say ah, I understand.

Q. If we have a consciousness that you call free consciousness, becoming part of the ocean, does that mean we are part of some matrix? A. The matrix has a negative connotation, right? It's as if there’s some mastermind behind us managing us for its benefit, for some other interest that isn’t related to us, and we are just pawns being played for someone else, someone bigger. It has a negative connotation. I wouldn’t translate it that way. A free consciousness recognizes the meaning of its life from a place that is no longer separate or distinct from the fabric of existence. And if there’s an interest here that we serve, it has nothing to do with my personal life, how much I gain or lose. Expanded Consciousness Q. Are we just another leaf on the tree, among many leaves?

A. Yes. And therefore, the movement of a true seeker is always in the quality of zooming out. It will always be a zoom-out, as large as you can imagine. The challenge is to see the broadest context that our consciousness can contain regarding our existence in a body on this planet. Within the broadest context, such personal questions as what I want, what I need, and what I will gain, have very little meaning. They are hardly visible. It is like when the pixels are small and the resolution isn’t high enough to see individual pixels. So, it is with our personal dramas. It’s not interesting. It is insignificant to the bigger picture. When we zoom in, to the pixel level, and live only from what I want/what I need, it’s very hard to see the big picture. Occasionally, we need to pull out a periscope from the submarine and look around. Q. The caveman who lived in groups of 50-100 people and dealt mostly with survival, was he a person with a freer consciousness than the modern man?

A. I don’t know if I would put it in terms of freer or less free, but certainly, the consciousness was less developed. Because consciousness is constantly evolving (constantly), it grows. The universal consciousness grows, not necessarily the individual consciousness of each of us. The individual consciousness of each of us is an aspect of the evolving universal consciousness. So, it was certainly less developed, and its ability to interpret the reality it encountered more accurately, or with higher resolution, was more limited. But it was appropriate for its time, to deal with the reality that the caveman faced. As consciousness matured, the physical reality we created for ourselves also changed. Now, we are less occupied with survival, running fast to climb the highest tree to escape the lion. There are no lions. We have new challenges.

Alright, so in the coming week, I invite us to make one last push to confront fear in all its forms. How it manifests in the body, how it is experienced as a psychological movie running in our heads, and to go even deeper and identify which of the two groups it belongs to. Do you remember? The fear of not getting what we believe we don’t have, and the fear of losing what we believe we have managed to achieve, what is ‘ours’. And to see how the ego tries to maintain its illusion within us through this whole heap of fears based on absence and deficiency, need, and dependence, which arise from the illusion of separateness. Next, we will begin our journey towards transcending fear. Another force will replace it. Another force that will fill us instead of fear - surrender. Surrender in the Body White Path Meeting July, 2023 Ready to start the journey out of fear? (Silence…) Alright, let’s assume you said yes in your heart

Today we’ll talk about surrender at the level of the body. What does that mean? First of all, we’re talking about the force that is opposite to fear. We said that fear is one of the most significant forces shaping how we allow ourselves to live and experience our lives. What will be the force that replaces fear? The name I gave to the force opposite to fear is surrender. Surrender as an emotional expression, and even before the emotion, an expression of the intention of the experiencer - to stop avoiding, to stop resisting, to stop running away from life. Because that’s what fear does. Fear prevents us from fully living what is. We are convinced that what is, is bad because the intellect decided so. What is, is dangerous. What is, is undesirable. We need to avoid it, manipulate it, or change it. And until it changes, we won’t be free.

The force opposite to avoidance, to fear, is surrender. Behind the surrender is the internal willingness to stop resisting and avoiding. The first place, the immediate place where this agreement is experienced, is the body because the body, as we have said, will always be the mediator between us and the physical reality we encounter. In this sense, we can say this is the first place where it happens, but it is also the last place where it happens because the body also has its desires. It also has fears embedded in it that it doesn’t always give us access to, or at least to their source. For instance, various types of traumas and hidden memories are embedded in the body at the physical and energetic level, causing it to contract and try to avoid the potential of a certain situation. So, what do we do?

First the strategy, and then the tactics. The strategy is the choice of the experiencer - your choice. Your choice is to stop being afraid and to stop living life diluted by fear. Your choice is to agree. That’s the strategy. Without it, the tactics won’t work. Making small cosmetic changes makes fear less scary, but it is always there and continues to manage us. If we truly, truly want to grow towards free lives, a strategic decision must be made. A conscious choice to rise above fear. To say YES. To agree. This must happen before we embark on the journey towards understanding what surrender is. Q. Start agreeing to what? To avoid fear? Why agree to that? A. To agree to this life as it is. To agree to the present moment. As it happens. For better or worse. For beauty and ugliness. For joy and sorrow. For high and low. For fat and thin. For light and darkness. To say YES to this. To say YES to that. Start agreeing.

Q. So Yaron, what you’re saying is first of all to agree to want to be spiritual, to agree to want to do the work at all. To agree to look at the fact that there is another side to life beyond... A. I don’t know if I would enter into such definitions... The word ‘spirituality’ has many interpretations, some very far from my understanding of what spirituality is. But the sentence ‘say yes to life and stop resisting life’ doesn’t need interpretation. It is a paradigm shift from fear to surrender. From no to yes. Life happens, around us, within us, every moment. That is reality. It’s not something you need to go search for. You just need to wake up and recognize that it’s happening. Now there are two possibilities: To manage a relationship with what is happening based on fear, resistance, and the experience of lack and need, or To agree that what is happening, pleasant or unpleasant, is life, and to commit to fully experiencing it. That’s the strategy, and it must precede the tactics. Q. There’s no ‘no’ here at all, only ‘yes’?

A. A free consciousness doesn’t say ‘no.’ It doesn’t even know what that means. It has no reason to say ‘no.’ Why do we say ‘no’? Think about it. Why do we say ‘no’? Q. Because there’s an alternative. Because we think there’s a preferred alternative, so we say ‘no’. A. Because we think that what is happening here is not good enough or not accurate enough. It doesn’t meet our expectations and demands, and it doesn’t fulfill our needs and desires. Thoughts kill innocence. We say no, no, this isn’t good, or not good enough, or not accurate enough, or not perfect enough, no... this isn’t. A free consciousness cannot use this word at all. It doesn’t know need or desire. It doesn’t manage its encounter with life through this filter of what’s in it for me. So why would it resist?

Let’s assume for the sake of discussion that we are still not experiencing free consciousness as an existential state. We make this choice consciously, even though at first it may be a bit artificial because for now, you don’t experience freedom from need and desire. At the moment, you experience need and desire many times a day: I don’t have enough respect. I don’t have enough acceptance. I don’t have enough feedback. I don’t have enough love. I don’t have enough money. I don’t have enough freedom. I don’t have enough status. Etc., etc., etc. Or, the little that you have is threatened, and if you don’t defend it fiercely, it will be taken away: My respect is threatened. My salary is threatened. My relationship is threatened. My love is threatened. My comfort is threatened… The bottom line is that it’s always somehow related to love. I don’t have love, or I have love, but it’s threatened. Although you have not yet reached the expression of unconditional love as a natural state of being, you consciously choose to stop resisting this life, as it happens. This is where it starts.

The Ultimate Choice Q. And it’s not like there is a choice. Because it happens anyway. Resist, don’t resist. It’s not like you have a choice... it’s an illusion that you have a choice, but it’s either suffering or going with the flow. A. That’s the choice. That’s the choice! Accept! The alternative is to suffer. Now, we’ve already talked about this in different contexts. We say there is an alternative to suffering, so why would anyone suffer? But it’s not that simple because the addiction to suffering is harder to break than a heroin addiction. The addiction to the drama that suffering creates becomes an existential definition. That’s who I am. Who am I? The one who suffers. And let me tell you why. Because I have a long, detailed, empathy-inducing story about why it’s important, just, and moral for me to keep suffering.

Until you reach a developmental place where you prefer free consciousness over drama, over a life of suffering, it won’t be resolved. Even if you went to a psychologist and managed to resolve the bad relationship you have with your mother from 30 years ago, the consciousness that identifies itself around suffering will find another story to cling to, fueling that identity. Who am I? The one who suffers. So, what will you be without suffering? Who will you be without the drama? It’s too frightening. You have no answer to that question, and it’s simply… too much. You create drama just so that this identification won’t die. Choosing Surrender

The strategy of surrender starts with a choice, with this ultimate choice of the experiencer. Stop resisting the fact that you are alive and stop resisting life as it happens. Once such a choice is made, and you make it the most important choice of your life, one that overcomes every distraction and every opportunity to dive into a new drama, into resistance, into avoidance, then the change begins. Then the switch happens. This switch can be fueled so that the wheels start turning faster and more effectively. This cart won’t stop every time there’s an uphill. You will have the ability to pass these uphills that life offers because it’s more important to you. It becomes a deeper and deeper expression of a real choice. Eventually, it becomes an identification, a new updated identity for you. Who am I? The one who stopped suffering. Eventually, you will also let go of this identity, but for now, it’s an identity that pushes you towards freedom. Releasing the Tension and Contractions

Now that the strategy aspect of our journey is clear, let’s focus on the tactics at the level of the body. First of all, we have already refined our two-way communication with the body, yes? We’ve worked on this, and we continue to work on this, and we are aware of when our body reacts as if there were danger. Reacts with fear. Reacts with contraction. We know how to identify this contraction when it happens, in real time. If we’re not there yet, then we practice this more and more. Now what we do is release the contraction.

For instance, we discovered a contracted belly, we opened our eyes and saw there was no lion, so this contraction is pointless, it doesn’t help us, it only interferes. Now we release the contraction. How? We take a big breath, channel it into the contraction, and fill the contraction with prana, with air, with oxygen. We gather into this breath all the tension, the stress, all this poison, and exhale it out. Again, we take a big breath, fill the belly, fill the contraction, and exhale it, relax more and more. At first, it will take a few minutes. The more skilled we become, the more immediate the effect is. Five such breaths are enough, and the contraction relaxes. You can imagine, if you want, a flower bud tightly closed, and with each exhale, it grows a bit and opens, and after 5 breaths, the flower is open.

Find the technique that works for you. Release the contraction. You will see that when the body is relaxed and calm, there is no fear. There cannot be fear without it having a physical manifestation in the body. If there is no physical manifestation in the body, there is no fear either. It works both ways. This is temporary, of course, because our mind immediately runs new movies, and then the body contracts again. But even if it’s temporary, it’s effective. The diligent student will continue to practice this exercise every time they find the contraction in their body.

Now, if someone wants to do a deep cleanse and reset the system on a physical level, there are many ways to do this. The method I most recommend as effective is the Art of Living Course. What we teach in the Art of Living is a very powerful exercise that helps the body release a lot of emotional, energetic, and physical tension that the body accumulates over the years. It’s like cleaning the system and starting fresh. Or you can find other ways to do this. You can use the help of a therapist, or do it alone or in a group. The intention, the tactic, is to release these unnecessary contractions from the body. Q. Is this the surrender? A. This is the physical aspect of surrender. The body gradually starts to release from these contractions, and more and more relief occurs in the face of reality. You become more relaxed in the face of what happens. On a physical level, you feel relaxed.

I told you about Gurudev when he visited Jerusalem during the Second Intifada. There were a lot of riots, it was very unpleasant if you remember. Someone asked him if he felt comfortable visiting Jerusalem during such a turbulent time. His answer was tinged with amazement as if he didn’t quite understand the question. He said, “I bring comfort with me. It’s not something I look for in the place I go.” Do you understand? Q. If he applies the method well, he has no resistance to any reality. For him, it could be a peaceful island with coconuts and a clean sea, or it could be a chaotic city. A. Exactly. And by the way, while we are referring to Gurudev, if you’re looking for an example of what fully realized consciousness looks like in this regard, I recommend finding an opportunity to meet with Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar.

Okay, so the tactic is to release the contraction, and the outcome of this release is increased relaxation in the face of the reality we are currently experiencing. Comfortable or uncomfortable, calm or turbulent, more and more quiet is experienced, at a very physical level, in the face of what is. This is an experience that never ends, it only grows and grows. The quieter we become within what is, the more intimate our encounter with what is becomes. There is less distance between me and what I encounter. This distance is created by the ego to maintain its illusion within us, and when it has fewer tools to do this because we are reducing its arsenal, the experience of alienation diminishes. Suddenly, there is a direct, increasingly intimate encounter with what is. This is called Tantra. This encounter where the experience of alienation, separation, absence, lack, bargaining, this whole story, this whole saga, melts into an experience of unity. This is a tantric experience of connection to reality. If anyone has ever wondered what Tantra is, in a nutshell - that’s it.

In our context, the process starts with a consciousness that agrees to stop resisting and relax in the face of this encounter with reality. This relaxation makes the encounter more and more intimate until the two disappear and become one flesh. This is a completely physical experience. It is not an idea. It is not philosophy. The tantric connection with life is completely physical and real. I hope each of you gets to experience this in one situation or another. Many times, this will occur in the context of sexual intimacy. There is something in this encounter between lovers where there is complete surrender to the experience. That’s the key. I stop being the one who acts and the one who initiates, and I am completely submissive, without any defense, totally devoted to my partner, totally devoted. It is a consciousness that says, here I am, take me… I hope you get to experience this. If you haven’t yet, hurry up and do it. What happens is that the separate, needy self, the one that wants something out of this act, simply disappears, and something else is born, something greater.

As described in the Old Testament, “And the two shall become one flesh” (Genesis 2:24), a greater unity is born there than the two who are playing with each other. This is the meaning of tantric sex. It’s simply another technique to immediately experience Tantra, physically. There is no I or You anymore. Q. This can also happen when I stand in front of a stunning view and it takes my breath away. I also feel complete unity with the universe, with nature, with... the same thing?

A. Absolutely. The special thing about this tantric encounter through an intimate meeting with one person is that this intimate closeness can be very threatening. Naturally, we are very quick to feel like wait, wait, wait. What do they want from me? I need to protect myself here. In such an encounter, it is very easy for us to be driven by fear, but the power of choosing to surrender to the experience can make it deeper, and more intimate. Do you feel this energy? Now, it is clear that it is not limited to sex. Sex is one of the most popular ways to experience this. It’s not a coincidence that Tantra and sex have almost become synonymous. But it’s certainly not limited to that. Sex is just one of the ways to experience Tantra.

If we reduce the definition of Tantra to two words it would be NO I. There is no separate and distinct I that wants and needs. There is a merging and solidification into something greater. This is a completely physical experience. It is not an idea. It is not some movie running in our heads of what could be. It is a direct physical experience in our encounter with reality. The willingness to say yes, and this quality of complete surrender to the point where our private lives are no longer interesting. There is something much greater here that we want to surrender to. What do you say? I’m sure there are questions. Even if they are embarrassing, ask them. Q. What is this greater thing that I want to surrender to?

A. This is one of these leading questions with no single answer that will be completely accurate and ultimately correct for everyone. But if I may attempt to answer this question, in one word, it is Love. Instead of being a consciousness driven by fear, be an expression of love. Instead of being driven by need and desire, be an expression of abundance and fullness. Instead of sharpening differences and alienation, be an instrument for connection and unity. Or, in one word - Love. What do you say? Q. When I meet a person, and it activates something in me, how can I connect? What can I do? A. It starts with being aware that you are contracted. Look for the clear and immediate danger, which probably wasn’t there, then identify the story you are telling yourself. It is based on some impression in the mind that prevented you from a real, intimate encounter with the opportunity life gave you to meet this person. Fear is often of the unknown, of what feels unfamiliar. Stay Elastic

Many years ago, there was a cinema in Tel Aviv called Cinema Paris on HaYarkon Street. At the entrance to Cinema Paris there was a wall in the building next to it. I think it was a bank branch. In the wall there was a niche, a Bauhaus element, and in the niche in the wall lived a homeless man. He was always with a shopping cart. Every time I went to a movie, he was there with his cart. I used to give him a lira each time I met him. One time, I went to Cinema Paris, I think I went alone, not intending to meet anyone, and I waited with the lira in hand to meet this homeless man, but he wasn’t there. For the first time, he simply wasn’t there. So, I took the opportunity and sat in his place and turned myself into a homeless person to experience what it means to be homeless, how it feels. It was one of the most amazing experiences I’ve had. Q. How much money did you make?

A. Ha! I sat there until midnight when people stopped walking around. The street was empty. It was quite amazing to step out of the defined comfort zone of who I am and what I am, and switch roles. Experiencing life through the eyes, through the perspective of someone else. The ability to be flexible enough in this regard, I think, is critical to allow this energy to flow. Not to be stuck within the belief of what I am, who I am, what I need, what I want, what I need to be careful of... Q. How did you come up with this idea at all? A. I didn’t plan it. It came naturally. Q. How old were you? A. I think... 23... I don’t remember exactly. Allow yourself to be flexible and you will see a new world, and a whole network of experiences that was blocked until now, will suddenly open. Life will start speaking to you in a completely new way. And you will be attentive enough to hear it.

Q. Yaron, it sounds like the strategic choice is the hardest part of this whole transition to surrender. You skipped over it quickly and moved to the tactics, but it seems to me like the most problematic part. Doing breaths and identifying contractions sounds easy to me. A. Right, that’s why we said the tactics won’t work without the strategy. Thank you for straightening me out. I didn’t dwell on it because there’s not much to say here, friends. It’s written in the Song of Songs. I can’t argue with the Song of Songs, “Do not awaken or arouse love until it so desires.” (Song of Songs 8:4). It’s not something you can force. Everyone is invited to ask themselves have I reached the evolutionary stage where drama stops being more attractive than the opportunity for a life of freedom? If you have reached that stage, then you can create this invitation, nothing more is needed, just create the invitation.

If you feel that evolutionarily you’ve grown enough and experienced enough suffering, and you don’t need it anymore, you are ready to stop the cycle of Samsara. Or, at least create such an invitation that this cycle within you will stop. It’s not something we can really stop alone. If you feel that evolutionarily I am ready, I am ripe, then this is the strategy you adopt now. It’s not even a choice anymore, it’s... There’s this Zen saying, ‘When the fruit is ripe, it falls by itself.’ You don’t even need to pick it off the tree. However, don’t judge yourself if you feel it’s not the time yet. That’s okay. You belong to the group of students who jump for joy when they are told there are still a thousand leaves on the tree. That’s completely fine. These lives are here for us to experience, fully and completely. Q. Yaron, I didn’t quite understand the moral of that story about the leaves and the tree. Is it important?

A. Two monks, one young and another old, are traveling along. Suddenly they meet a clairvoyant man. The man promises to tell them their future for food. They give him some food. The clairvoyant said to the old monk, “Do you see the hill over there? You still have as many lives to live as the number of trees on this hill.” The old monk gets very upset as he believes he already learnt everything he needs to learn and is ready for Moksha. The clairvoyant man continued to tell the young monk, “You see the number of leaves on these trees? This is the number of lives you still need to go through.” The young monk jumped for joy, “So much more to experience and learn, YES!” The story tells that the young monk instantly reached moksha at that point… We can be sad that there’s one more round, or we can be happy that there are a thousand more rounds. Each according to their level of maturity. Some people enjoy these lives so much and wish to live them over and over. Why not?

Q. But when you told it, I felt like the older person was the one who understands, and the younger person is the one who understands less. Weren’t you being judgmental? A. Not at all. If anything, the old man doesn’t know how to enjoy what he has. Remember it is Just a Game. Q. I’d like to bring this down to something practical and every day. Often when there is a deal to be made, a purchase, or something like that, it opens the door to an experience of separateness. How do I get the best price? How do I make sure I don’t pay more than I think I should? A. I always tell my son that one of the characteristics of a free consciousness is that it recognizes it’s all just a game. This entire experience is just a game, but it’s not afraid to play the game, even though it knows it’s just a game. It recognizes it’s a show and it’s not afraid to stand on the stage and play the role.

If reality directs us to a place where we need to play a certain role - let’s say I work in sales, and I want to get the most money for what I sell - then that’s my role. How much value do I create for the company I work for? I enter negotiations and explain why it’s important, why my product is the best in the world, and why the customer will never regret buying my product and not one of the ten thousand other competitors, etc. But my performance and motivation to excel are not driven by fear. They are not driven by stress, distress, need or dependency. It’s simply a part of the game now.

The scene happening now in the play is a sales scene. I play the role of the salesperson. I do the best I can in that role. But it’s just a show. It’s not real. What’s real is that I give my all in my choice to play the role. That’s also what makes good actors, right? Good actors are those who naturally convince us it’s a documentary, not some Hollywood drama, and that it’s really happening. Their performance sweeps us away because it looks so authentic. The actors are completely identified with their roles, right? That’s what makes the movie so fascinating. So it is here too. On the one hand, I allow myself to play the role as best as I can, and on the other hand, I always remember that it’s just a movie. There’s nothing critical in the circumstances of the world that may or may not happen that I am dependent on. Q. So it’s all a show, but there’s no real drama. A. There isn’t. Even if the show is dramatic. It’s just a show. Thus spoke the Buddha: (now your ears are perking up?)

How to do something so that the result of that action does not cause more suffering? When choosing to do something, one does the best one can, with a whole heart and a willing soul. Then one releases oneself from the demand for a specific result. The result is to be given as an offering to the divine. Whoever does what they do in this way will not experience suffering. Only complete surrender to the doing. A free consciousness does the best it can with everything it does. It gives 100% into the present moment; into the doing of what is. It releases itself from the demand for a specific result. This way, the result of the doing will not be suffering, neither for itself nor for those around it. Who else? The goldfish is flapping out of the water. What do you want to do with it? Fry it or ask it for a wish? Q. Letting go of the drama. Is this what’s meant by the saying ‘don’t take life too seriously because you won’t get out of it alive anyway’? A. Life is a deadly killer. 100% mortality rate. What else...?

Q. Can I share? I am becoming more and more aware of when I resist things or argue with reality. I am a farmer and there are trees that I grow. I water them and put in effort to make the irrigation work. But we’re not alone in the world. There are jackals, porcupines, woodpeckers; all those guys who wreak havoc on the pipes. Every time I open the water there is damage. Sometimes it’s just a small burst, and some sprinkler goes off unexpectedly. Sometimes it’s a complete tear in the line and then the water makes a lake. Irrigation is war. I’ve been in a mental war about this for years. Lately, I can remind myself, there is damage, that’s clear, and you need to fix it. But it isn’t a mental war anymore. This has changed from the mentality of they’re doing this to me. This is the small and important gap I recognized in myself. There is reality, even if it’s unpleasant, okay. But I don’t fight it, I don’t add more. I don’t paint it in another color. I started to be aware of this. It has become so important. A. Wow, powerful! Can Love Prevail?

Q. There’s a saying that goes, ‘Facts don’t care about your feelings…’ A. You reminded me of a story that happened many years ago when the White Path was just starting. About 4-5 neighbors would come to sit with us on the balcony. One of them was a lieutenant colonel in the army. He would come straight from the unit in uniform before going home. On one of those magical evenings, he told a story: “I’m a warrior. That’s my profession. I get paid for it. I’m a military man and war is the medium through which I express my professionalism. My boss, a brigadier general, was a very tough man with whom I had a long history of clashes and disagreements. I needed to get approval from this brigadier general for a project I was leading. I knew in advance it would cost me blood, sweat, and tears because you can’t get anything without a fight.

After the last lesson we had here, I went back to my office and I told myself I would do the opposite of what I usually do. I invited him to my office. He came full of fighting spirit, as usual. Contrary to what I usually do, I set up a table for him, made him coffee, and we talked about our shared past. I showed interest in him and showered him with love and respect. At the end of the meeting, the brigadier general offered me, on his own initiative, what I intended to ask for, and to my astonishment, everything happened on its own, opposite to my usual conduct.”

It was a life lesson for me to hear a lieutenant colonel say that. There’s added value in this lesson. Life can be a war, completely. For some of us, life is experienced as such. I am here to create an invitation for an alternative that might be just as effective, maybe even more, as long as we set our goals a bit more intelligently. And today the most significant goal, which will manage our continued encounter with life, is the strategic agreement we adopt - to say yes to life, as it happens. With leaks in the pipes and without leaks in the pipes. Yes? Surrender in the Mind White Path Meeting July, 2023 Let’s continue where we left off. The invitation was to pave paths that will allow us to grow towards a fearless existence. I know this sounds challenging. Why challenging? Because we are so used to encountering reality through the eyes of I want, I need, what will I get out of it. And when it doesn’t work out, we experience resistance.

Our responses are a result of the built-in resistance. An experience of lack and need meets life, and it is busy in a kind of manipulative negotiation with life to get what it doesn’t have. The way it comes to expression is through resistance, oppression, anger, rage, frustration, bitterness, and disappointment. This whole range of emotions stems from our basic resistance to what we encounter. We are here to describe an alternative. What would life be like if we stopped resisting it? Without anger. Without rage. Without frustration. Without disappointment. Without bitterness. Without violence. One of the first things people say is, okay, so I become this kind of pathetic spineless person who is not involved with life. But the alternative we are describing is not like that. It is the opposite.

It is difficult for us to imagine such an alternative simply because we are so used to being managed by the gap between what is and what we thought should have been. We are managed by these negative emotions that sprout out of suffering. But another force can drive us to action, and it is not based on lack, want and need. Rather, it is a result of full self-awareness, which means abundance. Love that has no conditions or reservations. If we don’t want or need anything from this life, what will our lives look like? Q. One big nothing. A. One big nothing? That is, if I don’t want anything from life, then there will be no encounter with life. Is that what you’re saying? Q. No, on the contrary. A. So explain...

Q. I can give an example. Let’s say I go to a meeting with my boss - some kind of employee satisfaction meeting, or some kind of salary negotiation. If I come to this conversation with certain expectations that I will get a raise or positive feedback, that means I am motivated by a sense of need. I need more money. Without that sense of lack, I wouldn’t be motivated to persuade my boss to give me a raise. A. Let’s translate this into a training tool that you can take with you and use now and always. The next time life allows you to be scared of something, something that might happen, you do two things. The first thing is you open your eyes, look, and see that there is no lion in the immediate vicinity. The second thing is to remind yourself of your strategic choice. Which is to say YES to life. To say yes to what is. Whatever happens.

To take it a step further, remind yourself that you don’t want or need anything from whatever is happening in front of you. I am free from need in my encounter with what is happening. This allows you to be more relaxed in the face of reality. I don’t need anything. Even if you do not yet experience this as an existential truth and still feel a need behind your encounters, it doesn’t matter - pretend. Fake it until you make it. Pretend you don’t need anything from the encounter or the person in front of you, may it be your boss, your partner, or whomever. You don’t need anything from them. They have nothing you are truly lacking. Without them, you are still complete and fulfilled. Q. But Yaron, that’s not true. A. You know what’s true? What you decide, that’s what’s true. Friends, this must be completely clear. Our lives as they are experienced are a result of the story we tell ourselves. The story we tell ourselves can put us in the position of the victim, and the story we tell ourselves can take us out of the victim experience. You decide which story you want to tell. Okay?

Q. Can you get into his example and face the boss and know that either he will fire you or he will give you a raise? Can you really say to yourself that it doesn’t matter? A. It doesn’t matter. Do you remember the nature of the stream? Its focus is narrow and temporary and very worried about its journey back to the sea. If it goes down this valley, then maybe in the other valley it would have gained something that isn’t in this valley, or maybe in this valley, it would lose something that it wouldn’t have lost in the previous valley, etc., etc. The way back to the sea is treacherous and dramatic, critical for the consciousness of the narrow stream. But the ocean isn’t bothered by the way the rivers make their way back home. It doesn’t matter.

There is a beautiful Hebrew song called ‘Go Wherever You Go’ by Yael Levy that says, “For from me you came and to me, you shall return.” Expand the consciousness to the consciousness of the ocean. Know that the temporary experience, the one we are experiencing at any given moment, is not that important. Sometimes we gain, sometimes we lose. Sometimes we get something out of it, sometimes we get nothing out of it. In the end, we will lose everything. Life is a losing game. It doesn’t matter. What is important and meaningful is not the specific way the river flows. What is important is the degree of dedication and devotion that we can muster to experience this path fully. How? With a whole heart and a willing soul. That is what is important. That is our responsibility. It’s the only thing that we can influence directly. Surrender in the Mind

Let’s move on to today’s lesson. What does surrender in the mind mean? What is surrender in the mind? We said that in the mind we meet fear, whatever it is. Fear is a movie that runs in our heads. An idea or thought about what might happen. In the mind, our challenge to grow beyond fear is expressed in our ability to recognize a very significant fact about thoughts. And that is that thoughts have no power. All thoughts... no... power. If we compare the realm of the mind to a movie theater where a movie is being projected on the silver screen and we are sitting there watching, then the images that run across the screen have no power. It’s just 25 or 30 frames per second, which are translated in our brains into the movie that we relate to.

The movie itself has no power. There’s nothing there. It’s just you, the observer, who looks, believes, and gives meaning to this movie. If you do that in the cinema theater then it’s for entertainment, but if you do it inside your head, it becomes the drama of your life. When you meet a thought and believe it, and let it drag your consciousness towards a disturbing reality, a frightening reality that might happen, and treat it as reality, as if the lion is there, then what happens is that the thought has all the power in the world. You gave it that power. But the thought itself has no power. It’s just another event that happens in the periphery of the observer. Just like an itch on the nose. It is another phenomenon that happens. Do you understand what I’m saying?

Thoughts appear, thoughts disappear, and most thoughts come uninvited. Just like that! They suddenly appear in our consciousness poof! And we get caught up in this thought or image that appeared and turn it into a kind of movie that rolls out all the terrible things that might happen. Then we start to shrink, more and more. Oh! All the drama! We can be spared from all of this when unequivocal knowledge follows every thought. I know the concept that Thoughts-have-no-power is a bit contradictory to some of the New Age concepts we’ve learned over the years. These concepts try to explain to us that we create our reality. Just change your negative thoughts to positive thoughts, and suddenly your life will be hunky-dory. This lesson, in my eyes, is very inaccurate. Whoever developed it and sent it into the world did not fully understand the true message here. What does affect your encounter with reality, what does create reality for you, is not the thoughts you send out, but the intention of the observer.

The intention of the observer translates itself into the world of phenomena through thoughts, feelings, and sensations. Or, if you will, the strategic decision translates itself into tactics, which translates itself into experience. And the experience is also in thoughts, which happen there in the periphery. But the one who navigates this business is not the thought, but the observer. The one who meets reality. I don’t know if this difference is clear enough, but it’s the clearest I can draw. Q. Try again, it was not so clear. At least for me...

A. On the Mind level, our challenge is to remember that thoughts have no power. The fear you are experiencing now is just a thought. It has no power. You are the one who gives it power if you choose to believe in it. This horror movie runs in your head, and you follow it, dragged into a reality of ever-increasing contraction. But if this thought comes to mind and immediately afterward, like a shadow, the realization follows that thoughts have no power, then you will see that this thought will no longer have claws. It will no longer be as scary as it once was. You are the one who chooses to tell the story to yourself and remembers that your life is a result of the story you tell. You have the power. Not power to the thoughts, but rather, power to the one who meets the thoughts.

When we refer to the intention of the observer, it may be, for example, to allow a conscious mind that meets reality without fear. This is the strategic decision you made. This intention completely changes your encounter with the world of phenomena. A complete shift in the way you view life. You realize that the world of phenomena has no power. You have the power. The Power Lies with You The power lies with you. Not in the world of phenomena. You give the power to what you want to give the power. You want to give power to something real. Not to a movie. Not to an illusion or to things that might happen. You choose to give it to something real, true. And what is the truth? The truth is - what is. Everything else is open to interpretation. What is, is already happening. Do you see that? The present moment is inevitable. This is what is.

To this, we give the power. And within what is, there is no lion. Otherwise, we would be having a different conversation, right? If there was a lion, we would have been busy reacting to the lion much earlier. But within what is, there is usually no lion. To the present moment, we give the power. Instead of being carried away by the movie that runs in our heads, into an imaginary reality of endless fears and anxieties, we bring our attention back to what is, and there we rest. There we relax. There we become open and accessible. Open and soft. A great deal of freedom is revealed to us when we wake up to this clear realization. The world of phenomena - emotion, thought, feeling - has no real power. I give it the power. I - the one who observes and meets it.

Q. Yaron, the lions are in the head, as it were. The imaginary lion, the psychological lion is in the head. Now, why would ten people be in the same situation and one would see a lion, and the other would be the most relaxed in the world? Because the one who has a lion has all sorts of ideas in his head about what life should be like and... Why are you laughing? A. I’m laughing because the idea of a lion in the head is so absurd, and yet it’s something that so many of us experience. We create these imaginary monsters in our minds that make our lives so much harder than they need to be. The truth is, as you said, there is no lion. There is only what is. And what is, is not a threat to us. It’s not against us. It is simply reality. The more we can relax into reality, the more we can let go of our expectations and our fears, and the freer we will be. Q. So why do we create these lions in our heads? Why do we make our lives so difficult?

A. There are a few reasons. One reason is that we’re afraid of change. We’re afraid of the unknown. We’re afraid of what might happen if we let go of our control. Another reason is that we’re addicted to drama. We love the feeling of being in control, even if it’s an illusion of control. We love the feeling of being important, even if it’s because we’re making ourselves into victims. A third reason is that the drama we create generates an identity for us. Who am I? The one that needs to keep protecting itself against life. But the truth is, we don’t have to live like this. We can choose to be free. We can choose to let go of our fears and our expectations. We can choose to live in the present moment. Q. Can you articulate more about the gap and how to close it? A. In cases where there is no real lion about to attack, the gap is always between what is - reality as it actually occurs - and an idea you have in your head about what it should have been. Or what must never happen. An idea you have in your head, yes?

First of all, know that this is why you are afraid or suffering. Not because of reality as it occurs but because there is a gap between reality and the ideas you hold about reality. This must be completely clear, as clear as daylight. Your entire reaction to reality will be a result of these negative feelings. Understand that reactions generated by negative feelings will be less harmonious. The results from these reactions will also be less harmonious, for you and everyone. What to do? What to do to close this gap? With the three-step method we have talked about before - add humility, adopt a paradigm opposite to what created the gap, and eventually drop all paradigms. And now we must put it into practice. It’s not enough to know this as a philosophical idea. You have to practice it. What do you say? Questions... Who hasn’t spoken today?

Q. This week’s practice went very well for me. It was almost frightening how well it went. What was frightening was to abandon the anxiety. I found myself thinking but what will happen when something really serious comes along that I have to deal with? What will happen when the bad news comes? Then I realized how much I was waiting for some bad news or something bad to arrive. I intend to continue practicing and many thanks for that. Regarding what you just said about accepting reality. I know in my head that you are right, but... I can’t. For instance, violence against women. I simply can’t, my body contracts. Murder of women. How do you deal with that? There are a thousand other things. This is what burns inside me right now. What do you do with it? A. You love. The alternative is to suffer. Do you truly know when people are supposed to be born and when they are supposed to die? Really? When you prefer a free consciousness over anything else, including justice, is when you realize your true nature.

Imagine yourself dealing with life’s situations, pleasant or unpleasant, wanted or unwanted, driven by love and not by fear or suffering. Totally and completely accepting the present moment instead of rejecting it. Of course, the sanctity of life comes first. We do whatever is needed to protect it. When led by love, the action called for will unveil itself in real time. So, when you say you are frightened to abandon your anxiety, you can look that fear in the face. I can guarantee this fear belongs to the family of the fear of losing control. Worry is a substitute for control. We worry when we feel we are losing control. Stopping the suffering does not mean we stop relating or caring. In fact, it is the opposite. Stopping suffering increases compassion. Compassion is all about experiencing your neighbor's pain and happiness and relating to it. So, do you see that when you drop your opinions you are so much more available for your effective loving response? Surrender in the Spirit White Path Meeting July, 2023

Welcome to our concluding session on fear and surrender. So far, we discussed how fear is found in all levels of our existence - body, mind, and spirit. We said that the opposite force to fear is surrender, or our strategic willingness to stop resisting life. Instead of saying ‘no’ and trying to avoid or manipulate life to make it more suitable or comfortable, we make the dramatic decision to say ‘YES’. The basic, primordial willingness is to say ‘yes’ to life. I am here to experience life fully. So ‘yes’ in the body means, first and foremost, that the body stops being tense, stops avoiding, and stops protecting itself from reality. We help it do this by real time identification of the contractions, releasing and relaxing them.

All alternative medicine is built on different variations of this knowledge - identifying the blockages, the energetic and physical contractions within the body, and releasing them. We can be our own Ayurvedic doctor, for the sake of this discussion, simply by increasing awareness of when you are tense, of when your breath is held. Then releasing, breathing in and releasing, breathing and releasing, again and again, until a relaxed and calm state becomes the default state of your body. We talked about surrender in the mind, which means knowing that our thoughts have no power. The movies running in our heads have no power unless we choose to believe in them, unless we choose to get carried away by the drama they present to us, then they have all the power in the world. They become the engine, the driving force, and then the movies running in our heads become who we are and how we encounter and react to reality. Then we are completely lost.

Surrender in the mind means encountering thoughts, emotions, and sensations without getting carried away by them into identification. This is the magic of meditation. Meditation reminds us again and again that the world of phenomena is peripheral - it is not who I am. It is just another phenomenon happening, a thought running through our heads, an itch on our noses. Both are the same thing. It is just another phenomenon we are invited to experience at a given moment in life. Our willingness to say yes to the world of phenomena, to stop avoiding it, to stop manipulating it, comes from the strategic decision we make to stop fearing life, with the unequivocal knowledge that no experience is beyond our capacity. No experience is beyond my capacity!

Pleasant or unpleasant, a free consciousness is spacious enough to allow both pleasure and pain to be experienced with the same level of openness and comfort. Why? Because that is what exists in a given moment. What exists is the most accurate definition we can create for ourselves when we ask ourselves, What is the truth? The truth is what is. That is the truth. Everything else is an interpretation of the truth. Q. Isn’t the truth subjective? Doesn’t everyone see a different truth?

A. Our mind is a very sophisticated tool. It filters everything that is happening and allows only what it is preprogrammed to identify as necessary for our survival or for the successful completion of a certain task to be experienced. And indeed, the picture of reality is experienced differently in each mind. If our mind doesn’t know that a ship exists, that there is such a thing, it won’t see the ship. It will only see ripples in the sea. If our mind doesn’t know that a giraffe exists, it will say there is no such animal, even if it is looking at one. If our mind is not prepared, not sharp, and not aware enough, then when a gorilla passes through the room, it won’t be aware that there is a gorilla in the room. Do you remember the experiment with the gorilla? Q. You said that nothing is too big for us. Nothing is beyond our capacity. My mind likes that sentence and likes to test it. It puts me in more complicated and challenging situations. Choosing the complicated way instead of going the easy way is kind of a challenge.

A. There are many ways one can walk to reach the light. There is the path of the lover, the path of the philosopher, the path of the warrior, etc. There are those whose path is built on challenging themselves more and more, further and further, and the farther from the comfort zone, the better. So, go for it! The comfort zone is a very problematic area. Besides being comfortable, it has very few advantages. Those who dare to challenge themselves and move away from the center of their comfort zone, towards the boundary, find that their developmental path is greatly accelerated. I highly recommend making it a regular practice. The further you are from your comfort zone, the more your system is constantly challenged, and you grow very quickly. Q. I am in a very strange phase. Nothing is too big for me. I have simply stopped understanding everything. I am not in my comfort zone either because I don’t even know where my comfort zone is - I am completely lost.

A. In the journey towards self-knowledge, at least in the journey as I see it, we gradually separate from false identifications and let go of preconceived ideas we have about what is right, what is wrong, what is needed, what is just. We even let go of identifications on the level of who I am and what my role in life is. I am not the body. I am not the breath. I am not the mind. I am not the intellect. I am not the memory. I am not the ego. So, what remains? Remain Defenseless Once, someone told me, “Yaron, you take everything away from me. You leave me with nothing.” I replied, “Very good. You’ve been listening.” This is not trivial - the willingness to give up everything. Some do it because they are mature enough. They have reached a developmental level that allows them to do so. Some do it simply because life does not give them an alternative. Life physically takes away from them everything they were used to holding onto and using as a crutch.

At this point on the journey, where we have nothing left to hold onto, nothing to lean on, no anchor that creates the illusion of stability, no reference point with which we can identify, is a very dramatic, critical, and inevitable point in our developmental process. If you are truly dedicated to this process and it is always your top priority, there is no way to avoid reaching this point in the process where you truly feel adrift and there is nothing left. The void is empty. See if you can deepen the meditation into this empty void. Do not avoid it. Do not fear it. Do not try to create new, artificial anchors to feel a bit more secure or to gain some comfort. Q. Yaron, I don’t understand how… A. Wait, wait, don’t continue! Very good. What I am saying now does not need to be understood. It is important to know that our intellect finished its role somewhere between the previous meeting and this one. It has no role anymore.

Today’s meeting will be challenging because our intellect is not supposed to understand it. I invite you to listen with different ears. Listen with the heart, not with the head. Facing the invitation to grow towards free consciousness, the intellect tries to create an example, a paradigm, or something it can hold onto and say here is a concept around which I can organize. But the call today is not to organize. The call today is to surrender to the chaos. Life is not organized. Life is chaotic, and the only sure thing about it is its inevitable end. Q. So what is the concept? A. There is no concept. Enough. From here we let go of all concepts. Q. Don’t we recognize the limit? The limit of our ability?

A. Our ability expands to contain what is without labeling it, without giving it a name, without arranging it within some logical framework and saying, Aha, okay, I understand. Because we don’t understand, and that’s what we surrender to. We don’t understand. I’m telling you in advance that today’s meeting is going to be very problematic for the ego. The ego is going to be exposed in all its nakedness. The entire drama is about what I want, what I need, what I get out of it - this drama prevents us from living a life of freedom. Shift from Avoiding to Surrendering Q. Can you give an example? A. When you walk through life led by the ego, you are tense, and frightened, with a sense of endless lack and deficiency. The ego tries to maintain the illusion of control by expanding the illusion of understanding the world and making sense of it. There is no freedom there, there cannot be freedom there. What drives you is fear, a contracted consciousness, an avoiding consciousness.

The greatest teachers search for the button to help students make the shift, from an avoiding consciousness to a surrendering consciousness. All the techniques, all the knowledge, all the philosophy, all the practices - everything is aimed at making this shift. However, no one can make this shift but you, only you. Not understanding is very good, but avoid the feeling of detachment. There is no need to feel detached from it just because you don’t understand it. What replaces logic is an open heart. Just because you don’t understand the world doesn’t mean it isn’t a part of you, or that you have no connection to it. Now there’s no intellect separating you from it, so you are completely available to experience it, to engage with it, without fear. And yes, sometimes it is experienced in a subtractive way - I am not this, not that. As the layers fall away from you, what is hidden behind the layers, the essence, is gradually revealed. Let us talk for a moment about this essence.

This essence is always of the quality of love, simply because there is no better word. Consciousness that has stopped fearing discovers love as the material it is made of. It discovers love as the material from which the reality it encounters is made. This is not necessarily love as an emotion between two people, but love that dissolves the differences between the two, melting the two into one. The ego knows how to create the illusion of separation. Me and the others, me and you, me and the world, me and reality. Whole lives are led by the experience of alienation, separateness, division, and duality. But when the ego loses its grip, what evaporates with it is the alienation, the separateness. What remains is love. The love that turns all this separateness into one great unity. There is no longer me against life, me negotiating with life. There is no longer this separate entity called ‘me’ at all. Love Consolidates all Separateness This entity melts into a much larger experience, which is the movement of life itself.

When this movement of surrender in you is stronger than the ego’s power to scare you and prevent you from having a direct and unmediated encounter with life, what you discover is love as an existential state, not just an emotion. This love consolidates all separateness into one great unity, where what was once ‘me’ is just one aspect of it, no more important or significant than any other aspect. And all this drama around the separate and distinct existence of who was once ‘me,’ no longer plays. Q. Is everything one entity? Does this openness, this enlightenment mean that there is no longing for anything, that we are one entity? Is that the intention? A. There is no need and no dependency, so the longing is not personal. It’s not that I want or need something. The longing is to be an active participant in this celebration called life and the evolution that life itself undergoes. Longing comes without need or dependency. Try to imagine longing without need and dependency. Q. Doesn’t that negate the word ‘longing’?

A. No. There is no restlessness behind longing. When you want and need something, until you achieve it, there is always a feeling of restlessness. But in longing, you are a participant in this evolutionary movement. If there were no longing, there would be no movement, right? Longing is the force that drives evolution, and your longing is your way of participating in this movement. Not because you want or need anything. You already know that you will get nothing out of it. That’s not the point at all. Q. I think I am in that place where I don’t feel the longing. I don’t feel the movement. I don’t feel anything.

A. This is likely a form of self-defence. If we don’t feel anything, it means our emotional receptors are suppressed and stifled because the emotion is too painful. There’s no such thing as not feeling anything. Numbness is a form of protection. Our body experiences emotions-thoughts-sensations. This happens all the time. If we don’t feel it, if we don’t experience it, then something in our receptors is blocked. We block it only because we’re afraid. Let’s be clear: the pain waiting for us there when we open those receptors is too great, so we say it’s better not to feel anything. You Be the Giver Q. Because surrender sometimes carries the risk of getting hurt...

A. Life suggests both pain and pleasure. Surrender carries the risk of feeling the pain, and I tell you, those who try to dodge the raindrops and stay dry will get wet like everyone else. I once had a physics teacher who proved mathematically that those who run in the rain get wetter than those who walk quietly in the rain. His surface area relative to... anyway, in short, mathematically, it’s proven! If it’s raining, it’s better to stand and say thank you quietly instead of trying to escape the rain. We enter this journey already knowing that we will lose what we believe is ours. As Rumi said, “Before death takes away what you are given, give away what is to give?” We embark on this journey not because we know we will get something out of it or because we try to gain something from it. This drama of what I need, and what I will get from it, must become less attractive at some point in time than our willingness to surrender to and love what is. Otherwise, we will remain stuck in this loop, it will never end, not in this lifetime and not in the next.

Q. I am afraid to lose my motivation, what drives me, because… then what will remain? And that’s the problem. Like, what? Will I give up all of this? For what? What will I get? What will I gain? Supposedly we are in a loop like this. And you say that first, we need to exit this mode of what will I get? A. Right. Don’t worry about the doing. The invitation here is not towards some kind of phlegmatic apathy. Well, I guess I better just stay in bed. We simply stop being driven by need and dependency, which was the emotion we were so used to identifying with as a motivational force. We go looking for food because we are hungry. If we’re not hungry, why would we go looking for food? Now the invitation is to mature and replace this motivational force of absence and lack, need and dependency, with a new force. A force that is never lacking. A force that is an expression of abundance. Abundance that is not limited within the small, defined scope of who I am or of what I have.

Abundance is life itself, of which I am an expression. The motivation is not mine personally, to go out and show the world that I have achieved. The motivation is of life itself, to live, to be experienced, and to gain meaning. The landscape wants our open consciousness to gain a sense of beauty. Remember the story about the Dead Sea? The landscape waits, the scenery benefits, not me. Q. What I understand is that for someone enlightened, it doesn’t matter at all who they live with, where they live, what they do in life. Everything is fine... A. Everything is fine as long as you are not living in resistance and you are a part of the flow. Sometimes the flow takes you right, and sometimes it takes you left, but you are part of the flow. You are not creating whirlpools. You are not creating karma during this movement. Q. How do you choose a partner in such a case? A. Without fear! Q. So if I accept everything that happens in life, then what does it matter who I live with?

A. It doesn’t matter. There are people whose nature allows us to open our hearts more easily than others, so it depends on the path you are on. If you are on the path of the warrior, the one who constantly challenges themselves, then you choose the most difficult one. Be with them and open your heart to them. Let go of this romantic idea that you came here to find a specific soulmate, the one and only individual with whom you can live a fulfilled life. A fulfilled life means to open your heart to what is. Q. All the great inventors who shaped modern society - Einstein, Pasteur, etc. - weren’t they driven by I want, I need, I want to be the best, I want to save the world? Weren’t they driven by ego?

A. Some of them probably were. I didn’t know any of them personally, but I assume some were driven by ego. The world of science is filled with a lot of ego. I’m not saying that lack and need, want and dependency aren’t motivational forces. On the contrary, they are the most dominant and common motivational forces. I’m just saying there is an alternative. Some people have changed the world without being driven by lack and need, want, and dependency. The question is, what type of person do you want to be? That’s what matters here. Q. I actually think that in science, if you come with an agenda or if you’re full of opinions or assumptions, then you can’t see reality. You’re not open. A. There’s a great story about Archimedes. He wasn’t sitting and thinking, ‘how do I solve the world’s problems?’ He was simply taking a bath, and suddenly...EUREKA!

Many people who work in research, science, and the arts, creative people in general, often report that their major breakthroughs occurred not when they were busy solving a specific issue, but rather when they were working on something mundane or unrelated.  Even for us, when we try to solve something or remember something, it somehow eludes us. But when we let go, then… DING! It comes to us. It’s not I found the solution. It’s that the solution comes to us when our minds are relaxed and broad enough. It’s not that we can’t be driven by fear - on the contrary, fear usually does drive us. We are here simply to present a sane alternative. An alternative that will take us further than fear can - so far that there will be no one left to enjoy it. Q. Yaron, people ask me, ‘What are you doing?’ I say, ‘I’m not doing anything, and that’s okay with me.’ When I hear you, something in me feels relieved, so I’m in an okay place. Who in me or what in me feels this relief?

A. Only you can know that. Look, an open heart is not something you can fake. If the heart is open, we know it’s open. If the heart is contracted, we know it’s contracted. It’s just a question of how much honesty we bring into this observation. Courage and honesty. When we really look at ourselves, is our heart open and expansive, allowing and loving, or is our heart partially open? Is our heart conditioned? Is our love conditional? Are we still afraid of life? Afraid of ourselves? Afraid of the encounter between ourselves and life? How this translates later into Doing is not that important. It doesn’t matter if we are professors at a university or beggars on the street. It’s completely negligible. It’s much more important if we stop avoiding, and stop resisting. If we stop being afraid of life, we become a lover of life. It’s not related to doing or experiencing. It’s not even related to the experience. It’s even before the experience. It’s the experiencer itself - how open and expansive is the experiencer? How much does it allow itself to dissolve into the experience?

Grow beyond the Realm of Phenomena Q. When the ego is screaming or the mind is scaring, is the practice to silence them? A. No, no, no! The practice is not to silence the world of phenomena. God forbid. The practice is to constantly remind ourselves what is more important and to bring us back to the observer’s position. Ultimately, we don’t practice to kill thoughts or to replace one belief with another. We practice to remember, again and again, that the world of phenomena is not who we are. The phenomena can happen. The mind can continue to be frightened. But that is not who we are. What is more important to me is how much devotion, how much surrender, how much openness, how much ease, and how much love I want to add to this world. How much YES! I want to add to this world. Q. But didn’t we say there is no I at all?

A. When there is no I there is no need for practice. But if this ‘no I’ is not yet established in our being, then there is the practice that constantly brings us back there. I drift to the I, and I return to the No I. I drift to the noise, and I return to the silence. I drift to the gap, and I return to what is. Q. To what is, always returning to what is, so that is the practice. Can you summarize all the practices we should take from this workshop, the practical aspects? A. All the practices are aimed at bringing us back to what is. Into what is, we add love, a whole heart. We stop resisting, return to what is, and stop resisting. We surrender to what is, again and again, shedding everything that hides what is from us, what prevents us from meeting what is, truly. Then we surrender to it, love it, and disappear into it. Q. How does fear manifest in the context of relationships?

A. Relationships, if we are honest, almost always begin with and are managed from an experience of lack and need. What we call infatuation and then love was not truly love in the pure sense. There was a whole pile of preconceived notions and conditions about what was supposed to happen. How the partner was supposed to behave. What they were supposed to do. How they were supposed to react. How much love they were supposed to return to me. How they were supposed to reciprocate my love, etc. True love has no prerequisites. A free consciousness does not condition its love within relationships. It uses the relationship as an opportunity to give the abundance it has found within itself, as itself. Q. In my experience, it seems more appropriate to apply this after a relationship is built. It seems very illogical to build a relationship this way.

A. Yes, our logic is trained within a system of culture and social contexts based on lack and need, want, and dependency. Can relationships exist where the force leading the encounter is not lack and need, want, and dependency? And even more important than that question is, do I want my relationships to be like that? My partner does not need to give me anything. There’s nothing I lack that they have and until they give it to me, I will remain lacking. That’s not why I am in a relationship with them. This can be a challenge for you. Next time you enter a relationship, see if you can do that with no expectations, no demands, no fear of any sort. See what kind of relationship can grow out of that state of mind. Surrender of the level of the spirit is all about accepting the fact that we are in a body experiencing life. We are surrendering fully and allowing love to replace existential fear so we can melt into the present moment, with a..? (Everyone…) Whole Heart and a Willing Soul.

Thank you very much for being part of this journey into fear and surrender, and I wish you days of clarity and uncompromising love. The Difference Between Fear and Worry White Path Meeting September, 2023 Q. Lately, I’m constantly dealing with the question of whether I’m acting out of fear or if I’m just concerned about whether things will work out. I’m in a situation where I’m not working much so I’m mostly staying at home. I’d like help with this, to figure out whether I’m acting out of fear or just taking care of business. A. For those who haven’t heard it before, let’s explain. First, the difference between fear and worry. Fear is living in the gap between what is happening now and what I don’t want to happen later

This happens when you’re afraid. It means there’s a thought in your mind creating some imaginary, scary idea about a possible future. You find yourself getting carried away by that thought and reacting to an imaginary reality as if it were happening now. That’s called fear. The way your body responds to this imaginary reality is very similar to how it responds to a real situation, where there is a genuine, clear, and immediate danger. The body doesn’t truly distinguish between these two types of situations. The heart rate increases, breathing quickens, and muscles tighten. One is imaginary, and the other is real. Now let’s discuss worry. Worry is what substitutes a sense of control

In Hebrew, worry can mean both ‘to worry’ and ‘to take care of.’ People say, don’t worry, I’ll take care of it, using the exact same word. So, you can use the wisdom of the Hebrew language. If you find yourself worrying, ‘just take care’ of it, and don’t let fear guide you. When there’s a reality that requires your attention and care, you simply take care of business - doing what needs to be done to prepare, to be ready. But don’t do this because you are driven by fear. Do it because it’s the right thing to do at that moment. How do you know what is the right thing to do at a certain moment? It is derived out of love, not fear. Now, how to know if you’re acting out of fear or love? It’s just a matter of tuning into your body’s signals. When you find yourself contracted, it is fear. When you are afraid, your body tightens because you are acting out of some resistance to a reality that isn’t really happening. It’s just something in your mind and this resistance creates contraction. Q. What if I don’t feel this contraction?

A. If you don’t feel the contraction and you’re acting with internal ease, doing, preparing, or acting from a place of internal relaxation, without resistance to what is, then there’s no problem. No problem at all. You are now within this all-allowing space. Q. But how do I know if I act out of fear or not? A. The most accurate criterion I can give to clarify this point for you is to look for internal resistance to what’s happening. Right now, if there’s resistance, if you live in a gap between what is and what you believe should have happened, or what you don’t want to happen, there is a gap inside you, and your awareness isn’t resting in what is. Then, you are acting out of fear or suffering, which are two almost synonymous words. Here you will always find contraction in the physical body. But if there’s internal ease and relaxation, a whole heart, then it doesn’t truly matter what you choose to do, whether you choose to go out and meet people or stay at home.

The secret isn't in the realm of ‘Doing’ at all. It doesn't matter if you choose to go out or to stay in. The secret is not hidden in the world of ‘Doing.’ There’s no point in dwelling on choice A versus choice B. When awareness is completely clear, you will find there is never a crossroad where you truly need to make a choice. It is all just a harmonious flow. The natural flow of life simply chooses for itself, and you’re here to enjoy the ride, to align your prana, your life force, with this flow. If there’s something you can take as a task, it’s to refine your conduct within this flow of life to ensure that you’re not contracting against life. You’re not agitated by life and the outcomes of your choices. The secret is not found in the outcome of your choice but in the extent of your surrender to what you’ve chosen and its consequences. I’ll say this sentence again: The secret is not found in the outcome of our choice but in the degree of surrender we manage to bring to that choice.

When you choose something with one foot in, and the other foot is busy with the ‘what ifs’, that’s where the human drama lies. If I had chosen differently, maybe the outcomes would have been different. Maybe I would have gained more there and lost less here. You’re still torn inside, with a split awareness. The human drama exists within a fragmented consciousness, a consciousness unable to surrender. So, don’t worry about the choice. It will sort itself out. Focus on surrendering to what you choose or what life chooses for you, whatever it may be. You Are Not the Doer Q. I disagree with you. I feel that I did choose, it was not chosen for me. A. So the question arises, who is this I that chose? Who is this I that says I choose? Q. It’s philosophical. A very philosophical question.

A. It’s a philosophical question, but philosophy is not a curse. The philosophical level is a level we have no choice but to reach during an intelligent investigation. This means we can continue to argue about what’s right, moral, advisable, worthy, etc., on one level, but there’s also the philosophical level above it. Eventually, after we calm down about the doing, we’ll also need to address the level of being. What core belief is hidden behind the statement I choose? Q. The belief that I chose my role as a mother and as an adult and that I chose to be part of society. So, I must accept the rules, right?

A. The leading question here is, what remains behind the title ‘ME’ when I am no longer a mother, no longer holding a senior role in society, no longer someone’s spouse, not in a profession, and even the story that has accompanied me over the years no longer serves as a reference point for me? What remains beyond all these definitions? Beyond memory. Beyond the experience of distinction and detachment. Beyond my intellect that interprets reality and forms opinions about it. Beyond my mind that processes all the inputs reality provides and turns them into the picture I relate to. Beyond the breath, filling and emptying the lungs with air at every moment. Beyond the body itself. What remains there? Who will this I be then?

The White Path we are on is the path of realizing the seven levels of existence. Along this path, we go through each of these levels - body, breath, mind, intellect, memory, ego.  What remains after all these fall away is the Self. At each stage, we learn to recognize that level of existence, to embrace it, to understand the relationships we maintain with it, and to transcend it because we realize that it’s not enough to define what we call I. So, we move on - I am not the body, not the breath, not the mind, not the intellect, not the memory, not the ego, so what’s left? When the attention is there, in what remains, we can return to the question and ask again - who is this I that defined itself through the decisions made about its life and role, creating an identity around these decisions? What’s left after all definitions evaporated? That’s who I am. Today we’re firing heavy artillery with these important questions. All Rivers Flow Back to the Ocean

See clearly that the secret is not in the choice. There is not one choice that’s more correct than another. It’s not in the doing. Don’t try to sort out which one is the right choice among all the possibilities. There’s no such thing. The invitation here is to avoid choosing something and then believing that you should have chosen something else. Believing the choice you made isn’t good enough, precise enough, correct enough, that’s where the drama hides, not in the choice.

A parable I love is the parable of the consciousness of a stream versus the consciousness of an ocean. When your consciousness is narrowed to see only what the stream passes through at that moment, then it seems very dramatic, whether you turn left or right. Everything changes, the path changes, the view changes, everything changes. But when your consciousness is the consciousness of an ocean... What does it matter? It will come from the left, from the right, from below, from above. Because it comes from you and to you it shall return. Right? All this drama of left or right doesn’t matter. When you find yourself in such a maze of what will be, which way to turn, just remember to zoom out and adopt the consciousness of the ocean. If what you choose to surrender to is not precise in the next second, then you can choose something new and surrender to that. Also good. This is an invitation to check. Every encounter with life is, again and again, an invitation to check: Who am I with all this? Who am I truly?
