What will you be when all your concepts, reference points, and identifications are no longer relevant? What will remain? Now, this day is coming whether you want it to or not. You just make sure that an awakened consciousness saying YES! comes before the angel of death… Grow beyond trying to identify yourself within the world of phenomena. Dealing with Fear of Pain White Path Meeting January, 2021 Q. What do we do with the fear of pain?

A. What do we do with the fear of pain...? We give up the belief that pain is bad. Remember the story I once told? A man was involved in a car accident and taken to the hospital ICU. Just when the doctor came to check on him, he woke up. The doctor asked him how he was feeling. He replied, “Dr. I’m a bit dizzy, but overall, I’m okay.” The doctor takes a pin and pricks his leg. “Do you feel the prick?” The man says, “No, I don’t feel any pain.” Is that good or bad? He goes into physical therapy and after a few months, he starts to walk again. After a year, he’s at home mowing the lawn and a thorn gets into his foot. “Ouch,” it hurts, there is pain. Is that good or bad? You see, pain is neither good nor bad. It’s all a matter of context. Pain is just a phenomenon that we sometimes receive the opportunity to experience. Like a scratch on the nose. Like a passing thought. Another phenomenon that we receive the opportunity to experience. Pain is not a problem. It’s simply the body’s invitation to pay attention to a specific area. That’s all.

Q. How do we compare the pain in your toenail to the pain of cancer? A. It’s simply more intense and more prolonged. Q. So there’s fear. A. But why not lovingly accept that you now have this set of symptoms to experience? Q. How can we lovingly accept painful side effects, a host of side effects? I find your answer very hard to accept. A. The alternative to accepting is to suffer. That’s even harder. Q. But in any case, we suffer, if not from pain, then... A. Wait, wait, stop! Pain is inevitable. Suffering is optional. By definition, together with the fact that we have a body, it means we have an opportunity to experience pain in the body. Also pleasure. Think about how many souls are waiting to join and experience the physical life, with the pleasure and the pain that life has to offer.

Now, I hope I’m not revealing anything new to anyone, but this body is going in one direction. In the direction of decay. But the consciousness living within the body can go in the opposite direction. Even though the body is decaying, the consciousness living within the body can grow and flourish from the experience of being within the body because it’s intertwined with life, which is about to end. If our identification continues to be with the body that is decaying, our consciousness will also dive deep into oblivion along with it. When consciousness isn’t identified with our body as our existential definition, but uses the opportunity the body provides to engage in life, to enjoy it, and to experience pain or pleasure, it isn’t doomed to decay with the body. Quite the opposite. About Guilt White Path Meeting March, 2021 Q. How do you reconcile releasing all phenomena as they happen with being responsible for your actions? For example, if you drove drunk, how can you let that go?

A. Guilt arises when you believe that what happened shouldn’t have occurred. You believe it’s a mistake, and because it happened, someone must be blamed and punished. Some people find it easy to blame others, while some blame themselves. Q. But if you drove drunk, aren’t you at fault? A. Of course, needless to say, do not drink and drive. If you hurt someone, you are sensitive and compassionate enough to recognize the pain you inflicted. You make sure to avoid doing it again (realize that this is very rare in the first place because a whole heart rarely hurts other people). The path of love promotes non-violence and does not rely on rules, regulations, or guilt to guide our decisions. As we’ve said before, where you suffer is in the belief that that person shouldn’t have died. It’s a mistake, this happened against the Book of Life, against God’s will. As long as you think you know better than reality about what should have happened, you suffer. Guilt is one aspect of that suffering. Reality unfolds on its own. Responsibility is not related to guilt.

Responsibility is a derivative of love. It’s not that the responsible person is guilty, or I am responsible because it is my fault. If you love something, do you choose to be responsible, or are you naturally responsible? Let’s say you have a new business or project you love - do you feel you should take responsibility for it? You have a new baby - do you take responsibility for her, or are you responsible as a natural outcome of my love for her? Act wholeheartedly and willingly, then release the outcome. Expand the circle of love, not the circle of responsibility. Responsibility follows as the love expands. Sexuality is a major source of guilt. Sexuality is wrapped in so many contradictory ideas of guilt that almost inevitably we repress it. Very few people have this channel open, and when they do, they become lovers of life. Sometimes enlightenment is described as a state of endless orgasm with life, merging into life. All this does not happen when we are busy with guilt.

The kundalini, wrapped in so much guilt, is repressed within us and prevents us from being fully present with what is. This is translated into the physical and energetic body. Breaths become stiff, short, and restrained. Breaths that do not satisfy the system with oxygen/life. This is another indicator we can use to know that our body is operating out of fear. Here is some homework: Pay attention to when you experience breath constriction. Shine a light on it as it happens and release yourself from the automatic need to get rid of it. Develop your communication skills with your body to be able to recognize this in real-time. The guided meditation on breath that I shared earlier can help. Be Humble Q. If I hurt someone, was it meant to happen? Can a person go and murder another, and that’s what was supposed to happen? Can anyone act without restraint, believing that’s how it should be?

A. Restraint is required when the motivation to act is not an expression of unconditional love. We create our karma as long as we act from egotistical motives, from a consciousness of lack and absence. We create ripples in our karmic world and either we, or reality, will need to soften those ripples to return to a steady state of complete peace. It’s important to understand that reality is stronger than any idea we hold. If our ideas contradict reality, the result is suffering. We don’t truly know who should be born, who should die, who should be hurt, how much, and why. We need to ensure that our choices are guided by a free consciousness, devoid of constrictions, so we don’t create ripples in the karmic world. This is Akarma Yoga - an action that is an expression of unconditional love. Q. Are you saying we should love every murderer?

A. Love is not a choice, not something you direct consciously and deliberately through moralistic, egotistical motives that assess its worth. Love is an infinite movement that flows outward and gathers everything inward. If you want to be an expression of love, stop manipulating how it pours out. Love radiates outward equally in all directions and gathers everything inward. If you want to be an expression of love, you don’t need to manipulate or set conditions on how it flows. Love will know how to flow. Q. In life, we are overwhelmed and attacked by everything happening, and sometimes we can’t even notice the contraction. A. Contraction is a physical experience. It cannot be imagined. It happens, and all that is required is gentle attention. Life is never bigger than what you can handle. It’s always you who gets scared and closes off first. Q. I feel attacked. A. This is the time to remember who you are. Life can never give more than what you can handle unless you have managed to convince yourself otherwise. Q. What does it mean to be free to fully experience?

A. Stop running away from what is. Some people faint when the event seems too big. Wake me up when it’s over. The diligent student stops avoiding this moment and stops denying their ability to cope with this moment. Q. You have a sick child in the hospital. What are you supposed to do? A. A child lying in a hospital is painful. It wounds the heart. But it’s not too much. You have the strength to deal with it. You don’t need to avoid it. The sane alternative is to open your heart and fully experience this pain, wholeheartedly and willingly. If you believe the idea that everything is a mistake and your son shouldn’t be in the hospital, that’s where suffering is created, and from it, more ripples of suffering arise. The sane alternative is to meet reality as it happens. Anyone who thinks we came here not to experience sorrow or loss - I’m sorry to shake up those ideas. All these experiences will be felt. Whoever is not open to sadness will never know true joy. Whoever is not open to life will never know themselves.

Q. Contraction in the body is a physical memory from childhood, and then it just comes up. A. Yes, many times it is a hidden memory triggered in the body. This week, identify the automatic response as it happens. If your mind is free enough, you can notice what happened outside that caused you to contract. We will continue to address this. Leaving Your Comfort Zone White Path Meeting June, 2024 Q. I never feared the coronavirus. I had no fear. I went out. I didn’t stop myself from leaving the house, meeting people, and going to the supermarket. At first, I had a huge resistance to wearing a mask. But as an Israeli living this reality of the war between Israel and Palestine, I find myself experiencing fear and pain.

A. Anyone dedicated to the growth and expansion of consciousness, and who wants to encourage development in their life, is first invited to step out of their comfort zone. Our comfort zone encourages stagnation, almost inevitably. As someone who lived outside of Israel for many years already, I can now recognize that one of the rare qualities of the Holy Land is the crazy pressure cooker people live in. All the energy is compressed, everything is under pressure, and nothing is taken for granted. You need to fight for everything. On the one hand, it’s very uncomfortable to live this way. But on the other hand, there’s a rare element in it that awakens people and prevents them from sinking into a self-induced slumber. This vibration of life stays alive, always calling for development, change, creativity, and innovation. This energy lives in our country, and people bring it to life in exceptional ways. There aren’t many places like this in the world. You can complain about the fact that you live where you live, but you also need to recognize the other side of the same coin.

Q. I live in California, and I 100% agree with what you said. North America is missing something energetically. This situation tells me to stay here and not to move back to Israel. A. Just note that it shouldn’t be interpreted as if we must do this or that. Nothing in our external reality prevents us from being free at this moment. Not living comfortably and challenge-free on one hand, and also not living very pressured and compressed on the other. Nothing in our external reality forces us to be this way or that. I just want you to see the big picture and the broad context of our existence within a changing environment.

Whoever tries to confine themselves within some comfort bubble, feeling safe inside it, believing that life can’t harm them within that bubble, is not necessarily working for their own benefit. Maybe it’s more comfortable there, but if you want to dedicate your life to development, you are not helping yourself within that comfort zone. It’s more likely that you’ll find stagnation there. At least the measure of it in your life will be more significant than the periphery of the comfort zone. Whoever wants to dedicate their life to development will always challenge the periphery, really challenge the edge of their comfort zone, and will try all the time to see how much more they can distance themselves from it. Again and again, to feel comfortable with the fact that life is unpredictable and uncontrolled. Q. Do you mean not to chase challenges? Just when a certain reality comes, to accept it as it is? Because there are people who are always looking for excitement in life, looking for challenges, and seeking big things.

A. It could be. Some people always want to seek thrills, and other people prefer a quiet life. Remember, the secret is not in the realm of doing. The secret is in the realm of being, in the inner experience of quietness, of ease towards what is. And within this experience, whether you stay at home or go out, it doesn’t matter. If you run outside seeking thrills because you have an overwhelming inner restlessness that needs some kind of external balance, then that’s not what I’m talking about. Or alternatively, if you’re stuck at home because of an impending and dreadful fear of what’s outside, and you’re just looking for some way to protect yourself against life, that’s also not what I’m talking about. But when there’s inner ease, when there’s an experience of well-being towards reality, it doesn’t matter if you stay at home or go out. Q. I keep forgetting that. How can I remind myself? Remind Yourself Again and Again

A. There are ways to help ourselves remember. I’m a big advocate of ceremonies. A ceremony is vital on the spiritual journey. Many traditions and religions are filled with ceremonies. They are an opportunity we give ourselves to remember, again and again, daily. Remind ourselves what is most important to us. We can light a candle or take a 10-minute break every couple of hours, that helps us remember. Or even taking a deep breath every time we find ourselves carried away by some movie in our heads instead of being with what is. We will describe more ways to remind ourselves soon. What is Vulnerability? White Path Meeting November, 2023 Q. What is vulnerability? Is vulnerability also fear? What exactly is it? A. Vulnerability… Being vulnerable means outgrowing your fears. Being vulnerable is shedding the protection layers that you wrap yourself with, allowing life to touch you intimately whether it’s pleasurable or painful. Vulnerability is a sign of a mature consciousness growing beyond fear.

When fear guides you, you keep negotiating with life, and cravings and aversions govern your choices. You cling and you resist. You know what? What you resist, persists. What you oppose, remains. Your resistance gives it the power to stay. You give it strength. Whatever you put your attention to, grows. You pay attention to the blessings in life, and the blessings grow. You pay attention to the difficulty, misery, and distress in life, it grows. Life has both this and that. You are the one who applies the focus and allows it to grow. You pay attention to the pain, you resist - it becomes chronic pain. Sorrow that you resist becomes depression. Fear that you resist becomes a phobia. Everything you resist - grows. Everything you love - grows. Everything you put your attention to - grows. And then the question arises - what is more important to you? Where do you want to put your attention? Now that you know it’s the engine of growth, the development of creation, where do you choose to put your attention? Q. Is there a difference between Fear and Phobia?

A. Phobia is a fear you refuse to deal with. It sticks. How do you deal with a phobia? Everything we learned about fears is relevant here: Make sure to release the contraction in the body; Use the breath to add life to the contracted area; Use the mind to remember and remind yourself, that it’s just a thought, it’s not real, there’s no lion in the room, and thoughts have no power. Unless I believe them, then they have all the power in the world, because I give them that power. I give it with my attention; Use the intellect, explore fear, and get to its roots. Why is A scary? Because of B. Why is B scary? Because of C. Why is C scary…? Discover that either you arrive at an empty station, where, in fact, you are not afraid, or you arrive at a central station where you discover that what scares you is one of: The fear of losing what you believe you have, or The fear of not getting what you believe you don’t have. Then, seal the deal, with two steps to enlightenment:

The first step is to know that you are nothing. If you are nothing, then you have nothing to fear losing. The first fear has gone. The second step is to know that you are everything. If you are everything, then how can you need anything? After all, you are everything, and everything is yours. The second fear has gone. Welcome to enlightenment. This is the ultimate state of vulnerability. Q. When you’re saying it, it sounds simple… A. “The Truth is as simple as the breath,” wrote the Israeli band Sheva. Q. I have another question. Can you explain what the difference between interpretation and thoughts is? A. Interpretation is constructed from thoughts- ideas, opinions etc. Q. Right, but then if I interpret the environment in a certain way and it’s not that, it’s a kind of thought, again I’m entering into such a loop.

A. Thoughts are phenomena that occur on the fourth level of existence- the Intellect and are experienced in the third level of existence - the Mind. The intellect is pushing preconceived ideas about reality - what’s true or false, what’s right or wrong, what’s advisable or inadvisable, etc. Interpretation is just one family of thought, a certain type of thought that the intellect streams into the mind. You can say that thought is the building block, and interpretation is what is built now from these LEGO thoughts in your possession. You can build a tower, you can build a villa, you can build a hut… So, vulnerability invites us to move beyond the mind’s desire to protect and shield, and instead, to let go, surrender, and embrace the fullness of our humanity regardless of what we think about it. A Return to Our Authentic Selves

To understand why vulnerability is essential for spiritual growth, we must first consider what it means to be vulnerable. Vulnerability is the state of being open to the unknown, to possible change, and to the potential for pain. It is an admission that we do not have all the answers and that we cannot control all the outcomes. This openness is often difficult for the ego, which thrives on certainty, security, and a sense of control. Yet, in a spiritual context, vulnerability is a doorway to the present moment and a pathway to our authentic selves. When we strip away the defenses, we have built to protect ourselves, we confront the essence of who we are. In this raw, unguarded space, we become more in touch with our genuine feelings, desires, and fears. This is where true self-awareness begins. Spiritual growth is, at its core, a process of becoming more aligned with our true nature, and vulnerability is the lens through which we can see ourselves without distortion. The Illusion of Control and the Fear of Vulnerability

A significant obstacle to spiritual growth is the illusion of control. The desire to control our environment, our experiences, and even other people is often born out of fear - fear of the unknown, of rejection, of failure, and of loss. By clinging to control, we create walls that keep us from the very experiences that can expand our awareness and bring us closer to the truth. Vulnerability, on the other hand, requires us to release our grip, and to let go of the need to dictate how life unfolds. The fear of vulnerability is rooted in the belief that if we are open, we will be hurt. This fear is not unfounded. To be vulnerable is to risk disappointment, to expose ourselves to criticism, and to admit that we are not invincible. Yet, while vulnerability exposes us to pain, it also opens us up to love, connection, and joy. In resisting vulnerability, we limit not only our capacity for suffering but also our capacity for all the other emotions that give life depth and meaning. Vulnerability as a Gateway to Connection

At a fundamental level, vulnerability is about connection - connection to ourselves, to others, and to the divine. When we allow ourselves to be vulnerable, we let down the walls that separate us from others. In this state, we see that we are not alone in our struggles, our fears, or our desires. This shared human experience fosters compassion, empathy, and a sense of belonging. Vulnerability allows us to move past superficial interactions and engage in deeper, more meaningful connections. In relationships, vulnerability is the cornerstone of intimacy. It enables us to show up as we truly are, without pretense or masks. When we are vulnerable with others, we give them permission to be vulnerable too, creating a space of mutual trust and understanding. In this space, spiritual growth thrives, as it is nurtured by genuine human connection and the love that flows from it. The Role of Vulnerability in Letting Go of the Ego

The ego is deeply invested in maintaining an image of strength, certainty, and invulnerability. It fears exposure because exposure means relinquishing control and admitting imperfection. However, spiritual growth often requires a dismantling of the ego, a process that cannot occur without vulnerability. By embracing vulnerability, we begin to see through the ego’s illusions and recognize that our true self is not diminished by openness or perceived weakness. On the contrary, our true self is revealed through these very qualities. When we are willing to be vulnerable, we challenge the ego’s narrative. We begin to see that our worth is not tied to our achievements, our appearances, or our ability to be in control. Instead, we discover that our true value lies in our authenticity, our compassion, and our ability to be present with whatever arises. In this way, vulnerability is a tool for ego transcendence, helping us to peel away the layers of false identity and move closer to our essence. Vulnerability as a Pathway to Healing

Healing is a central component of spiritual growth, and vulnerability is essential to the healing process. Often, the pain we carry is exacerbated by our efforts to suppress, ignore, or control it. Vulnerability invites us to confront our wounds and acknowledge our suffering. It allows us to sit with our pain without judgment and to express our feelings openly. By being vulnerable, we permit ourselves to feel and to release emotions that may have been trapped within us for years. This emotional release is healing in itself, but it also paves the way for deeper insights and transformation. Vulnerability helps us to see that our wounds do not define us, but rather, they are part of the tapestry of our lives. When we embrace our pain and allow ourselves to be vulnerable, we begin to heal, not by erasing our scars but by integrating them into a more profound sense of wholeness. The Transformative Power of Surrender

Perhaps the greatest gift of vulnerability is that it teaches us the art of surrender. Surrender is not about giving up, but about yielding to the flow of life and accepting whatever arises with grace. When we are vulnerable, we stop resisting the natural rhythms of existence. We allow ourselves to be shaped and transformed by our experiences, trusting that each moment, no matter how challenging, carries a lesson and an opportunity for growth. In surrender, we find peace. We realize that we do not have to fight against life, but can instead dance with it, embracing both the highs and the lows. Vulnerability teaches us that there is a profound strength in letting go, in trusting that we are supported, and in knowing that we have within us the resilience to face whatever comes our way. Fear of Not Being Loved White Path Meeting November, 2021 Q. I experienced the fear of not being loved. I manage to let go of that place, but still, I find myself returning to it from time to time. Is it ego, or is it fear?

A. Ego equals fear. They are not two different things. I would say it’s simply the lack of self-awareness. If we need to judge this world in dualistic terms to negotiate reality for ourselves, then the only criteria I recommend using is ignorance versus knowledge. It will never be good versus bad, desirable versus undesirable, etc., as we usually do. Q. Can you give an example?

A. What you’ve just described is an example. When you’re enveloped in the belief that you don’t have enough love, that you need love, it signals a lack of self-awareness because self-awareness reveals itself as the source of love. A spring cannot be thirsty, it’s contrary to its existential definition. How can a spring be thirsty? Unless it doesn’t know it’s a spring. It sees the droplets of dew around it, so it believes it’s a dewdrop. It just hasn’t awakened yet. It says, look, the dewdrops appear in the morning and disappear at noon, so I must be like that too... My love is limited and temporary. But, you see, the spring itself cannot truly be thirsty. If you feel lacking, it’s because you’re not connected to abundance, which is who you are. If you feel you lack love, it’s because you haven’t yet discovered yourself as the source of that love.

One of the classic mistakes we make when we enter into relationships is believing that our partner will redeem us from that lack, from the absence. There’s no such partner. Even if they’re called Richard Gere and they ride a white horse. There’s no such partner, and there is not supposed to be. It’s not fair to burden them with this responsibility. I don’t have, so you will provide for me. It’s a recipe for a destructive relationship. Q. If I have expectations from the environment, people, reality, or nature, in such a mindset, do I need to remember that nothing is really for me in this world, not even my partner? A. When you live in a contracted consciousness of absence and lack, every encounter with life is in the context of trying to fill up and receive. You feel the lack, so you go out to get what you don’t have. What’s missing here is self-awareness. If you encounter thoughts like I don’t have love, or I need someone to give it to me, it’s an opportunity to awaken and remember that you still have a lesson to learn about who you are. What do you say?

Q. Absolutely right. Thank you. Q. Earlier, you said something about when the angel Gabriel will come... what? Will we be enlightened? A. No. I said the moment the monitor stops showing us the movement of ups and downs, of forgetting and remembering, is the time we need to prepare to meet the angel. Q. So, if someone remembers all the time, they have nothing to do here in this world? A. If someone remembers all the time, they begin to do the real work they came here for. Q. And what is that? A. To give meaning to reality. To be an active participant in the evolutionary process of our collective consciousness. To become another force driving this movement, driving the evolution of consciousness. And there are also, rare as they are, what they call Bodhisattvas.

Bodhisattva is the maximum developmental resource of consciousness. The story tells of a Bodhi who reached enlightenment within the body and dedicated his life to the development of human consciousness. When he left his physical body, the story goes that all the angels of paradise gathered at the gates of Heaven to promote the entry of the Bodhi, and when the Bodhi tried to enter the gates, he managed to get only one foot in but couldn’t get the other one in. So, they said to him, “Bodhi, what’s wrong? Come in, become one of us.” The Bodhi replied, “I cannot enter into paradise while a part of me is still suffering down there. My role will be to illuminate the souls of all beings.” He descended in spirit, to continue this work. This is called Bodhisattva. (It’s a song for the soul; it doesn’t need to be understood.) Q. Sometimes, some people hold themselves enlightened and it’s not exactly true.

A. There are all kinds. What’s relevant for each of us are these points in time when one forgets, and the points in time when one remembers and asks oneself again, What’s most important to me? Being correct, feeling comfortable, feeling protected, and receiving all that I believe I lack? Or having an open heart towards what’s happening? That’s it, no more questions. That’s the only and last question. Q. If I’m angry, does it mean I’m not with a whole heart? A. Yes. A whole heart isn’t angry. A whole heart can be very powerful, very sharp. A whole heart isn’t necessarily always soft and mellow like that, right? A whole heart can be very powerful. Very influential. But not because it’s angry, not because reality contradicts some idea it had about what should be. But simply because what’s needed at this point is a boundary. Q. And then, do we feel the difference in energy? A. Definitely. You don’t feel contracted towards what is. There’s no frustration, so there’s no anger, so there’s no violence within you. Q. Is it not personal? A. It’s not personal. Q. Can a whole heart cry?

A. Absolutely! Completely. Totally. It can’t resist crying. Or laughing… Q. I think you’re teaching us a kind of language that doesn’t align with society. If you want to be whole-hearted and willing, but those around you don’t understand and continue their violence, how does this duality work? A. They’ve already told us, ‘Be the change you wish to see.’ People will come, they’ll stand in line. When they see this love in you, when they see this spark in your eyes, they’ll stand in line and say ‘I want that too.’ They’ll have strange ways of saying it, but that’s what they’ll tell you in so many words. ‘I want that too. Where do I get that?’ Don’t worry about other people. And remember that no event we receive the invitation from life to experience is truly beyond our capability or capacity. Overcoming Doubt White Path Meeting November, 2023 Q. Yaron, what about the doubts, doubts about me, about the method, and about the teacher? I can say I am still doubtful.

A. Excellent question. What is doubt? Doubt is an idea, a thought, which by its definition tries to convince us that the reality occurring in front of us is not accurate, is not correct, and is dangerous. It’s something we need to avoid. We need to create an alternative. That’s doubt. See, we mostly doubt Goodness. If we categorize it as bad, we don’t doubt that. If someone tells you they hate you, you don’t doubt their sincerity, but if they tell you they love you, you say: “Really, do you really mean that?” Now, it’s important to understand that doubt prevents surrender. Instead of surrendering to life as it is happening, doubt positions us on the fence, and sends us back to sit on the fence. There we sit and wait until clarity comes and a decision is made. Or until we get tired of it and life takes us from there. In this sense, doubt is a kind of obstacle that prevents flow, that prevents harmonious progress, that prevents us from experiencing fully. We must see this.

Western society sanctifies doubt as some ideal of the thinking person, the person who has the independence to make choices, to make decisions by their free will, right? Which is all well and good, but in the end, what we usually find is that we keep running around in circles. Life happens and we are stuck with our doubts on the fence. There are several ways to deal with doubt, but the bottom line of all these ways is to burn the doubt. Doubt is simply blocking my progress, blocking me while life moves on. Burning the doubt means making a decision. Sometimes the decision is to flow left and sometimes the decision is to flow right. What’s important is to join the flow! A broad consciousness, a holistic consciousness, a free consciousness, is not interested in a specific choice of left or right. It’s not relevant. It’s not interesting because all the rivers... flow to the sea. They come from the sea and flow back to the sea, and the sea doesn’t care if you came from the left or the right. You are just an extension of it. Make a choice and jump into the water.

When you’re in the water-surrender. Surrender to the flow. Surrender to your choice. Go with it. All the way. If you are truly dedicated to your ultimate choice to move towards a free consciousness, the next time doubt arises, you won’t give it power, you won’t give it weight. You won’t let it delay you because what matters to you is the movement. The forward movement towards free consciousness is what matters, not the ideas that come up and try to convince you that here you may gain and there you might lose. Those thoughts are not interesting. They are just ideas and movies running in your head. They are simply not interesting. And if it doesn’t interest you, you don’t give it power, you don’t believe in it. And if you don’t believe in it, you are free from it. Free from the doubt.

Think about how powerful a person who is free from doubt can be. Such a person can either be enlightened or very dangerous... If what drives him is the ego, he can easily become a dictator. People will easily follow him because they themselves are full of doubt and confusion. But if what drives him is love, nothing more is needed. What do you say...? Q. Can I challenge what you’re saying a bit...? A. Always. I have no doubt Q. The goal is to reach free consciousness, but how do I know that the method you are presenting is the right and good way to do it? A. The only way to know is to surrender to it. You can’t know this if, with one hand you are flowing with the stream, and with the other hand you are holding onto the bushes of the riverbank. The only way to know is to surrender. I’ll tell you, between us, it doesn’t matter what method you use. If you chose this way and it doesn’t fit, fine! Go choose another way, but surrender. The heart of the matter is the surrender. Not the teacher. Not the method. Not the technique. Not the technology. Just your whole heart that says:

HERE I AM. THY WILL BE DONE. Q. But isn’t that how cults are formed...? A. There is one primary criterion in choosing the right guru for you - ensure that in front of the teacher, your degrees of freedom expand and do not shrink. A teacher under whom you become more free, open, and accessible, is a teacher worth paying attention to. A teacher to avoid is one under whom you feel that you are shrinking and contracting. One where he is huge and you’re only getting smaller. One where you find more and more rules and commandments that prohibit you, defining for you what is good and what is bad, creating a very rigid framework of conduct. One where your degrees of freedom are shrinking within this connection. If this is the case, run for the hills. But we will talk about this later. Q. How do I make the right choice? A. Where would you turn if you weren’t afraid? Making the Right Choice Q. At that moment, there was no clarity about it. If there was, there wouldn’t be doubt. That’s the heart of the matter, isn’t it?

A. You are attuned to your body. Trust your body. People who work with their bodies notice when the stomach tightens and when the stomach relaxes. The stomach tightens when I am afraid. The stomach relaxes when the fear dissipates. You can ask the body, where to go now, right or left? and look for contraction or expansion. If there’s a contraction in both options, then two things are possible. First, recognize that the body is in an unhealthy level of tension, so through the sadhana, through spiritual practice, we can lower the general tension level in the body so it will be easier to notice the release when the body relaxes.

Second, remember that it doesn’t really matter what you choose. What does matter is that you surrender to that choice. Did you decide to go left? Fine.  Surrender to the left. Give it your best. Release yourself from the demand for a specific result, and simply open your heart. And if life navigates you out of this choice towards another direction, another choice, great! Surrender to that. Remember, the movement of free consciousness is not a stagnant event where there is no encounter with life.

A free consciousness is a consciousness that allows perfection to evolve into a new and greater perfection in an infinite evolutionary process. We progress from one state of perfection towards a greater, broader, more holistic state of perfection. But it’s not that the previous state of perfection was lacking. Try to connect to this energy. It’s not something that needs fixing. It’s not something that needs changing to bring about perfection. Perfection is already present within the Present Moment, within the whole heart we bring to this moment. Perfection translates itself into action, towards a broader perfection. We don’t need to be worried about the choice. The choice itself doesn’t matter so much. What does matter is that our hearts remain open. Don’t Fear Your Emotions White Path Meeting August, 2023 Q. I wonder why sometimes your teachings make me want to cry. Do emotions get in the way of self-realization?

A. No, no. Don’t hold back the emotion. Let it flow. Be courageous enough to cry when it comes. Or laugh when that comes. Emotions are not a problem. Maybe something deep inside you is awakening, and that can be very emotional. It’s okay to be emotional. Don’t be afraid of your emotions. Emotion is an experience. Embrace it - whether it’s happiness or sadness. Q. Do those emotions get in the way of self-realization? A. The only thing that can get between you and self-realization is your intellect trying to figure out what the hell is going on. Trying to label your experiences. The Buddha said this 2,600 years ago. Craving and aversion are the cause of misery and suffering - craving the ‘good’ and aversion to the ‘bad’.

A mature awareness evolves beyond that. Self-realization is all about growing beyond the intellect. Realizing that your intellect doesn’t help in this regard. Thinking I need to figure out what the hell is going on here, I need to stay in control is not helpful on the path. I’m telling you, the ultimate realization of a fully matured intellect is the understanding that the intellect is not here to comprehend everything. A fully mature Intellect realizes Its own limitations and understands that reality is much more mysterious than it can grasp as a concept or idea. When it matures to realize that, it lets go, and then you become available to make the journey back to your heart. What is self-realization? It is an explosion of the heart that is not bound by any idea anymore. No fear. No reservation. Not about life. Not about myself. Not about the future. Not about the past. It is completely available. Available to love. Q. Yes, I will take that 30 cm trip, from head to heart. A. Good. Let’s all embark on that trip. As soon as you leave, you arrive. That’s it, you are home.

Dealing with Trauma White Path Meeting January, 2022 Welcome everyone. Our focus today is on a profound topic - trauma. We’re going to explore what trauma is, how it affects us, and, most importantly, how we can free ourselves and grow beyond it. I’ll start with a brief introduction. The rest is up to you and your questions, so don’t be shy. This is your chance to take an active part in moving beyond trauma. Are you with me? Trauma is a sensitive subject. It affects all of us, so we’ll approach it with care and compassion. Remember, growth comes through honesty and courage. There is no way around it. Facing trauma requires that we stop lying to ourselves, stop trying to maintain an artificial image of who we are, and just be honest.

What is trauma? Let’s clarify it so we can move forward. Trauma is created because of an event that we weren’t fully available to experience. At the time this particular event occurred, we failed to muster enough resources to cope with reality as it was happening and we experienced that reality as beyond our capacity. Therefore, we did not experience it fully. If we don’t allow ourselves to experience the present moment fully, in real-time, it is recorded as trauma in the body. The next time reality presents itself as a potential for a similar occurrence, the body immediately returns to the trauma and reacts in a way that is completely disproportionate to what is actually happening. Reality is Never Truly Beyond your Capacity Q. So you're saying, for example, that on the battlefield, during the same event, one might experience it fully, whatever that means, and the other might log it as trauma? What does it mean to fully experience a traumatic event, completely?

A. There is no such thing as ‘a traumatic event.’ An experience is never traumatic in itself. It's important to understand this. The experience varies in its intensity, but it is never traumatic. The way you allow myself to meet the experience can create trauma. We know this from life. Some people experiencing the same event manage to go through it peacefully, whereas others retreat into trauma. What is important to remember is that reality is never, ever beyond your capacity. It's a law of nature - God/Nature does not invite you to experience what you cannot truly handle.

If you believe this is too much, it is only because you have not yet learned to recognize the strengths within you. Life is not too big for you. Under any circumstances. As consciousness matures it realizes that it is greater than anything life can throw at it. Your consciousness exists even before the experience itself, whether it is calm or dramatic. It's not just a matter of time or space. It's hard to put into words, but it exists much earlier. Think of a story that completely sweeps you away for hours. Your consciousness is not tied to the story. It is the book itself. It is the material from which the book is made - the cellulose and the ink. Ways to Avoid Reality There are many ways to avoid reality as it happens. We can run, hide, have an out-of-body experience, freeze, or fight. But in all these cases, we’re unwilling to just be there, fully exposed. This avoidance leaves a scar on our body-mind complex. A scar we carry. This is trauma.

We are all scarred in some way. No one is untouched. Some scars are minor, and some are deep. But we all have them because we all avoided reality at some point. Right? Life gave us painful experiences that left scars. To prevent that kind of pain from happening again, we put up a shield. Like medieval knights with their armor, we cover ourselves in iron to keep life from hurting us again. Instinctively, we react to extreme events by armoring ourselves so we’ll be prepared if it happens again. This armor dulls the pain but at a cost. Life can’t touch us as deeply. Do you see what I mean? We protect ourselves, but in doing so, we stop allowing life to truly affect us. We become insulated from both pain and joy, and we stop allowing life to mold us as it could. Trauma Leads to Avoiding Long-term, trauma usually leads to avoidance. We bury ourselves deeper, hoping to avoid being touched by pain again. Does that sound familiar? Instead of staying open to life, we armor up and shelter ourselves.

Some people, the daredevils, live on the edge and need to keep raising that edge to feel alive. Like adrenaline junkies, they chase intensity. Similarly, we might feel that to be accepted, loved, or worthy, we must experience pain. To walk the middle path, as Buddha described it, I suggest balancing exposure to pain with exposure to life’s pleasures. This is a good indication of freedom - being open to both pleasure and pain. Awakened consciousness means being fully exposed to whatever life brings. Check your motivation. Are you exposing yourself to pain because you believe it’s the only way to feel loved, or gain acceptance and approval? Or are you simply open to whatever life offers, whether painful or pleasurable? Addiction to the Drama Q. I seem to create chaos.

A. Why do we create chaos or drama? It’s a profound realization about ourselves. We create drama because we’re hooked on it. Without it, life feels dull. Like those daredevils, without drama, life can seem pointless. We may even define ourselves by our experience of drama, and without it, we feel lost. So, we create drama to avoid facing who we are without it. Drama becomes a drug, and if life isn’t dramatic enough, we stir it up to get our next fix. The realization that we’re addicted to drama is significant. As with any addiction, the first step is acknowledgment. ‘Hi, I’m Yaron, and I’m addicted to drama.’ Then, you respond, ‘We love you, Yaron. We accept you as you are.’ Right? Q. I feel trauma in my mind, but I don’t remember a specific event. I kind of feel it, and don’t feel it. I’m not sure.

A. Sometimes the cause of trauma is buried in our subconscious. We may know exactly when the trauma occurred, remembering the event vividly. Other times, we can’t recall it. We might have been too young, or our mind blocked it out because it was too much to handle. We’ve locked it away in a hidden part of our soul, hoping never to face it again. But avoiding it doesn’t solve the problem. The suppressed memory still affects us, creating internal contractions. Some say these scars are karmic imprints carried over from past lives. Whether we remember or not, the influence on our present life is very real. We’ll discuss what to do about it later. For now, we’re focusing on understanding trauma and its impact. See Yourself in the Eyes of Your Master Q. I can’t see myself objectively. I have no external view of myself. A. If you can’t see yourself objectively, find someone who can act as a mirror - a trusted friend, a therapist, or a spiritual teacher. They can reflect back to you with love and compassion. Sometimes, just seeing yourself in another’s eyes helps.

Internally, look for signs of contraction in your body, emotions, or energy. When you feel compressed or protective, it’s a sign that there’s something you need to release. When you’re young and someone breaks your heart, you often close it to protect yourself. But closing off your heart can take years to undo, and sometimes it never opens the same way again. Many years ago, my son was in fifth grade. His girlfriend broke up with him, and he cried in his room. I hugged him and whispered, “I know it’s painful, but promise me you won’t close your heart. Even if it hurts, keep it open.” This is how we generate karma - by trying to protect ourselves from life’s pain. Pain vs. Suffering Q. I suffer from pain. I want to grow through joy instead of suffering. A. Pain and suffering are not the same. Pain is a sensation, whether physical, emotional, or energetic. Suffering happens when we reject, avoid, or judge that pain. Do you see? Pain is inevitable, but suffering is optional. Q. Can you feel pain without suffering?

A. Absolutely. Pleasure and pain are two sides of the same coin. Some mystics, like Indian fakirs, use pain as a way to connect with the divine. When you allow yourself to feel deeply, you open up to both pleasure and pain. While we’re in a body, we shouldn’t reject pain. It’s part of being alive. Q. Is the subconscious real? Can I access it? How can I not remember what happened to me? A. These are great questions. Yes, the subconscious exists. It’s a well-known psychological concept. It’s like an underground current affecting us, even though we can’t see it. Just because it’s not available to the conscious mind doesn’t mean it’s not influencing us. Steps to Grow Beyond Trauma Now, with this understanding of trauma, we can consider what to do next. If you feel closed, tight, or protective, it’s a sign of unresolved trauma. What should you do?

The first step is to forgive yourself. You did the best you could at the time. Trauma isn’t an accident, nor is it a mistake. It’s simply an event you were not able to fully experience in real time. It wasn’t your fault, and it didn’t happen against you. Don’t victimize yourself by thinking this was a terrible mistake. Life can be cruel, but it’s not personal. The scar you carry can be an honor because it shows that life touched you. That’s why we’re here - to let life touch us. So, forgive yourself. Just as you forgive others, extend that compassion to yourself. Everyone is doing the best they can. If they act cruelly, it’s because they’re suffering and disconnected from their true nature. I Do Not Know Q. I was physically and mentally abused. How was that supposed to happen?

A. We don't know. It’s part of the mystery, that eternal mystery. We don’t know, and we will never know. Trying to find a reason or justification is pointless. What we do know is that it happened. And how do we know that? Because it happened. It’s an opportunity to remind ourselves of those lines from a Leonard Cohen song: I need you to carry my children in. And I need you to kill a child. You know who I am. It may not seem fair or just to our human perception. We often ask, ‘What did this young boy do to deserve that?’ But arguing with life leads to suffering. Arguing with what is happening now, as it unfolds, is the very definition of suffering. Some people spend their lives arguing with life, but life always wins, 100% of the time. Life happens, whether you like it or not. So, what should you do with trauma? First, you forgive - yourself and the other person. Let go of the idea that this was a terrible mistake that shouldn't have happened. Carry that scar proudly, with honor. Life touched you, and that’s exactly what you’re here to do - allow life to touch you.

The Importance of Dealing with Trauma Q. Why is it important to deal with trauma? A. In the context of spiritual growth, dealing with trauma is essential because we too often identify with it. It becomes part of our identity, answering the question, ‘Who am I?’ But trauma, like any other experience, can hold us back from progressing towards liberation. It’s essential to go beyond trauma. Trauma creates aftershocks, and if we allow these to define who we are, we become stuck. We are here to allow life to touch us, in every way. The freer we become, the more exposed to life we allow ourselves to be. An awakened consciousness says YES to everything life has to offer. You Are Always Bigger Than Your Experiences Q. Couldn’t doing that trigger PTSD?

A. PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder) is exactly what we've been discussing. PTSD is that automatic reaction of closing back into your shelter because you believe it’s too much. You keep reliving the trauma over and over again, being reactivated by life’s circumstances - like a robot, with no apparent control, unconsciously believing it is the way to avoid additional pain. But there’s a universal law: Life will never suggest a situation that you truly cannot experience fully. As you go through life, know that whatever it offers, however intense, can never be beyond your capabilities. If you believe you can’t experience it, it’s because you don’t yet understand how big you are, how generous your consciousness is. Whatever happens, it happens because you can experience it fully. If you adopt this state of mind, you will never generate new trauma. Q. So many people have trauma. All of us in the world. Millions and millions.

A. Yes, all of us. It’s not just ‘so many’ - it’s 100%. Everyone has been touched by life, in one way or another. Don’t judge yourself for being scarred by life. Carry it proudly, knowing that life touched you. So how do we deal with PTSD? Traditionally, you go back in time to re-experience that event in a controlled and safe environment, assisted by a trained therapist, this time allowing yourself to fully experience the event. On the spiritual path, the invitation is to expand your consciousness. Realize that your consciousness is bigger than anything life can throw at you. You are the theater hall, always present, always containing whatever happens on the stage. You are always bigger than your experiences.

Once you understand this, you realize you don’t have to behave like a robot reacting to triggers. You can choose how to respond. You are not bound by automatic reactions. Peace is your nature. It’s revealed as you grow. Peace doesn’t depend on external situations, and nothing can take that away. You can become an expression of unconditional love as we interact with life. Wake up, and you are free from that bond. Part III Embrace and Love Life Embrace and Love Life After confronting suffering and moving beyond fear, we now come to the transformative stage of learning to fully Embrace and Love Life. In the first two parts of the book, we focused on resolving our relationship with the external world. Now, the flow of focus and energy begins to turn inward. In this third part of When the Wave Remembers the Ocean, we explore the path to inner freedom by accepting life in its entirety and discovering the harmony that arises from this deep acceptance.

When suffering and fear no longer hold sway over our lives, we enter a space of profound freedom where loving life and fully embracing it becomes not just a possibility, but a natural state of being. Without the chains of fear and the weight of suffering, life unfolds before us in its purest form - a canvas of infinite beauty, opportunities, and connection.

In Part III, we delve into the transformational experience that arises when we release our attachments to pain and anxiety, allowing us to engage with life from a place of deep love and appreciation. With fear gone, we no longer resist the unknown but welcome it with open arms, seeing every moment as a gift, every challenge as a lesson, and every interaction as a chance to deepen our understanding of the world and ourselves. This is where life becomes sacred, and where joy and peace are no longer fleeting experiences but the foundation of our daily existence. We will explore the shift that takes place when we truly begin to love life as it is - unfiltered and alive - awakening to the boundless possibilities that emerge when we embrace it fully. We start with determination on the path. True transformation isn’t about perfection - it’s about persistence. Determination means showing up for yourself, over and over again, especially when things get tough. Inner freedom is cultivated through sustained effort and the decision to stay committed even when challenges arise.

So much of our suffering comes from being attached to things - material possessions, roles, and outcomes. Freedom from the realm of phenomena helps you step back from the impermanent world of appearances to find peace in the deeper, unchanging reality beneath. By stepping out of this attachment, you can find a peaceful center that isn’t shaken by life’s ups and downs. Life is a blend of light and dark, joy and pain, success and failure. To truly love life, we have to accept all of it. Embrace the wholeness of your experience, recognizing that each moment - whether good or bad - holds wisdom and opportunities for growth. Moving towards embracing life leads us to explore the masculine and feminine within us. These energies represent structure and flow, action and receptivity, logic and intuition. Finding balance between these two forces allows us to experience greater harmony within ourselves and in our relationships.

The tension between the masculine and feminine helps guides us towards integrating these energies for a more balanced, holistic experience of life. Finding the balance within helps us grow towards inner freedom. Learning to release resistance, fear, and attachment, and to flow with life’s natural unfolding, wherever it may lead is the ultimate goal of embracing life fully. You will learn how to cultivate that inner freedom, so you are no longer bound by the external world but instead grounded in an inner peace that stays steady no matter what happens. The Importance of Determination on The Path White Path Meeting August, 2022 Q. How does determination fit with a reality that we are supposed to embrace? Determination leads us forward. We are driven by an inner force that can lead us to good places (on the positive side). Isn’t that in conflict with accepting reality as it is?

A. You feel there’s a contradiction between determination and accepting reality. Excellent question. What is determination? It’s the focus of intention. It’s very masculine-oriented. It is what we direct our resources towards. To accept what is, to love what is, is very feminine. A free consciousness knows how to harmoniously dance with these seemingly opposing forces. The symbol of the Yin and Yang, that’s its message. The feminine and the masculine complement each other, creating a harmonious movement. Sometimes reality requires precise intention, but we don’t continue forward out of frustration, anger, and resentment. We accept reality and continue in the direction we intend to go.

How do we know when to stop? When love starts moving in another direction. We’re not dependent on the journey’s outcome. Our happiness isn’t dependent on the end game. Our happiness is expressed in this step we’re currently taking towards the goal. If love moves somewhere else during the journey, it’s okay. We are not on the journey led by hope. We’re not dependent on circumstances. We’re happy to walk the path, with complete flexibility. The masculine is sometimes more dominant than the feminine. And sometimes it is the other way around. We dance with that internal movement. So, determination is our ability to stay focused on the ultimate goal -Awakening. It means consistently choosing an open heart and a willing soul whenever life tempts us to slide back into conflict and drama. Choosing this path again and again is probably the most important quality of a sincere disciple.

Q. When we talked about freedom, it didn’t align with unconditional love for me. Can freedom go hand in hand with unconditional love, or does it create a minefield? In unconditional love, there needs to be sacrifices. If I’m sacrificing, I might be sacrificing myself. A. Allow me to clarify for you. Unconditional love cannot come at the expense of oneself because you ARE unconditional love. That’s who you are. When you are connected to your true SELF, you’re expressing your true nature. When you think it contradicts because you might have to make sacrifices, you’re going back to seeking freedom in doing, in experiencing. What do I gain? What do I give up? There, the ego element is dominant. Go back to the original definition - freedom isn’t derived from circumstances. It is not derived from what you do and what you abstain from. It’s not related to your choices.

Freedom is a whole heart that agrees to say YES to whatever is, whether it’s similar to or contradicts the ideas you have. These ideas no longer interest you. The accountant who does these calculations dies. What exists is a flow of love. It's the expression of who you are. The one agreeing to stop fearing. Fearing what? Fearing not getting what you believe you lack and need life to give you, or losing what you think you already have. Q. Is this what you sometimes see in people who have nothing? A. Anyone who travels in India sees this often - people who truly have nothing still have a smile on their faces and a sparkle in their eyes. It’s not because fortune has favored them, but because something in the culture of India helps people embrace joy more deeply.

Let me give you some homework. Let’s remind ourselves to find peace, freedom, inner calm, happiness, and love that are not dependent on anything. A peace that isn’t a result of circumstances and is not because something specific happened. Find it as an answer to the question, Who am I? See if you can trace freedom, happiness, peace, and love that are unconditional, and not reliant on anything. Let's focus our intention on this inquiry. The Realm of Phenomena White Path Meeting November, 2022 Q. Yaron, could you please explain or briefly go over what the phenomenal world is? A. Everything that is experienced belongs to the phenomenal world - emotion, thought, sensation, and their combinations, which create our idea of reality in the material world. It could be an external experience of having something or an internal experience of having a thought or an itch on the nose. Everything that is experienced belongs to the phenomenal world. Consciousness reveals itself as the background that allows experience to happen.

Q. Throughout the introduction, you mentioned wrong ideas and false identifications. Essentially, is the shedding process about letting go of ideas and identifications, whether wrong or not? A. Attachment to ideas is never recommended because they are what you have based your identity on until now, and they are not who you are. You are not your body. You are not your breath. You are not the mind - the phenomenal world. You are not the intellect that judges the phenomenal world. You are not your story - the memory of what has happened to you up until now and all your preconceived ideas. You are not the ego that creates an illusion of separateness between you and what you encounter. Consider what is experienced once separateness ends. There is no longer someone separate and distinct experiencing it.

The I itself changes its quality. It is no longer I am experiencing. Normally, one might say, Wow, how beautiful, how wonderful, ‘I’ met God, God spoke to me. As long as the experience is perceived through the lens of a separate and distinct experiencer, it is erroneous because it is disconnected from the context of oneness. It’s like a wave trying to convince you that it is truly the most wonderful wave the ocean has ever produced, collecting praise for itself, creating an agenda around it, forming an identity. I am the most wonderful wave! I, the most wonderful wave. I am the most special, the most talented wave. Or conversely, I am the most miserable wave, the least impressive wave here, the poorest wave. Whatever the ego generates, whether positive or negative, is all the same.

It is a mistaken identity because the wave does not truly have a separate identity. It is merely an expression of the ocean, unique, special, but an oceanic expression, not a separate wave. As long as you claim this identity for yourself (I, the separate and distinct one) it is erroneous because the true context of your existence is not expressed. Q. When we finish asking the last question, at the end of it all, we are all the same, we are exactly the same. Here we are very different, but when we finish the process... A. Look, I must interrupt. A statement is an echo - air passing through vocal cords creates a word, which enters the microphone, is converted into an electronic signal that enters your ear (or in the case that you are reading this, your eye), and is received by your brain as an idea.

So now you have a new idea, We are all the same, there is no difference. See if you can meet this suggestion beyond the idea of it. It is not just an idea. Do not treat it as an idea. See if you can hear the invitation behind the word: unity. This invitation is not intellectual. It is not an idea. It is not another concept. Aha, yes, I understand. The I understand is not the entry door you are seeking. Q. I don’t understand. A. Ha ha… very good. It’s never about the words, ideas, or concepts. We’re not replacing an old idea with a newer, more sophisticated, more accurate, more spiritual one. That’s not the point. We don’t have much choice within this medium, but the keen listener (or reader) will seek the silence, the invitation to silence hidden between the words, between the ideas, and between the concepts. This silence existed before there were ideas and before there were identifications.

This silence has no end. It doesn’t stop where my physical body ends and your physical body begins. This silence is the backdrop against which reality is experienced. Reality doesn’t start or end. This isn’t something we can intellectually say, Aha, yes. Even if the intellect says, Aha, yes, it’s just a new, sophisticated idea that we adopt. That’s fine, but understand that this is just the beginning of the journey. What we’re doing is swapping old ideas for new ones to refine the focus of our search, but the search doesn’t stop at ideas. It goes beyond ideas, beyond identifications. What is Happiness? White Path Meeting January, 2022 Q. Is a happy person (I assume there are at least two such people out there) a person who is enlightened or a person who has brought their ego to the highest level? A. Define ‘Happiness.’ Q. No suffering, no opinions, no dramas, smiles a lot, joyful, loving.

A. The absence of suffering is a very significant station on the way to free consciousness. Free consciousness no longer deals with our personal suffering. There’s no more personal interest, no filter of how is this experienced by me? The experience reveals itself as part of the fabric of the collective experience, so it’s no longer I who suffers, or I who stopped suffering. There’s no more I. Happiness is a matter of definition, but for the sake of discussion, let’s say I am joyful in being happy just as I am joyful in being sad. In this sense, happiness is simply the opposite emotion to sadness. Joyfulness, however, describes the nature of the background upon which all experience is perceived. It is the innate appreciation of the opportunity to experience the present moment, as it unfolds. It’s not even my nature - I, Yaron, the small, limited being. It’s the nature of the stage itself. The stage is happy to provide the opportunity to experience whatever is experienced - sorrow or happiness. Do you understand?

If we’re talking about happiness in this context, it’s not personal. It doesn’t belong to a person. Thus, a Joyful person is not necessarily happy all the time, but they are an expression of free consciousness, which stops identifying itself through the phenomenal world. Q. So, theoretically, could it be defined as a person who has managed to fulfill all their ‘I wants’ and then was able to relax? A. That’s not necessarily the path. Some people manage to relax without fulfilling all they want. The desire itself just relaxes, regardless of the final outcome, the phenomenal world managed to produce for them. This state is sometimes referred to as Dispassion. Dispassion is your ability to be passionate about whatever you are experiencing, without an attachment to a specific result. Know that you are not the doer. In Sanskrit, this is called VAIRAGYA. Whatever you choose to do, do it passionately, 100%, and release yourself from the attachment to a specific outcome or a result.

We already agreed this has nothing to do with our personal benefit. That is not what we are dealing with. Dispassion is another aspect of spiritual maturity. If this is what you are truly seeking, dispassion is a quality you are welcome to strive for. We said that on our path, I want to be free is the last desire, and then the desire disappears, and then the I disappears. Q. This is something intangible, something divine, isn’t it? If there’s no I and I am nothing, then I am not tangible. A. I avoid framing such experiences within an idea, as it’s meaningless. Let’s say you adopt a new definition of yourself. Okay, so now there is no ‘I’. Who am I then? I am God. Fine, but what does that mean? I recommend you stop trying to identify yourself by dropping one identity only to adopt a more refined, sophisticated one. Find God in the eyes of your partner If you’re sincerely seeking God, you may dedicate yourself to finding God in the eyes of other people. Seek God in the eyes of your partner - it might be easier to find God there.

Q. You give the word ‘nothing’ a kind of positive connotation. I assume most people see the word ‘nothing’ with a negative connotation. It’s even an insult. A nobody. A. Yes, you’re right. This nothingness has a threatening element, especially if you encounter it through the ego, because the ego needs a context, it needs something relative to which it can create an identity for itself. I compared to someone else. But if there’s nothing else there that you can relate to and identify with or against, it’s indeed very threatening. In Christianity, this is called ‘the Dark Night of the Soul.’ There’s a certain void into which you fall after the edge of the cliff has disappeared beneath your feet. Into this void, you plunge without any reference point. It can be very frightening. Despair can be helpful there, or alternatively, complete surrender. You agree to lose the last points of support, your last holds, and let the mystery take you. The Nature of Unconditional Love White Path Meeting June, 2022 Q. What about unconditional love? What is it?

A. Usually what we experience is a combination of love and fear. We feel the love or a nostalgic memory of love we once felt, and we feel fear. Fear is often the dominant force. Fear of losing what we think we’ve already achieved or fear of not gaining what we believe we lack - social status, security, comfort, stability, etc. Unconditional love isn’t mixed with fear. It’s devoid of fear. All the drama of losing or not receiving dissolves. Sting once sang about it, If you love someone, set them free. Unconditional love isn’t mixed with fear. It’s just pure, undiluted love. The nature of love is to spread, to touch, to embrace, to contain. Pure feminine power - like a mother putting her baby on her breast after birth. The baby hasn't earned that love, she loves him. However, the fear starts immediately - fear he won’t nurse, fear he will get sick. It’s hard to find love devoid of fear.

For me, the first time I encountered this quality was when I met my teacher, Sri Sri Ravi Shankar. To me, he is the perfect example of unconditional love. His love doesn’t require anything. How do I know if the teacher I chose suits me? My teacher doesn’t need me to prove myself worthy. He loves me unconditionally. The White Path leads us to a life without fear. Q. It’s hard to do this... to live without fear. How can I do it? A. Let’s put the question of how we do it aside for now. Let’s remind ourselves that we’re on a journey towards free consciousness. Free, among other things, from fear. Free consciousness cannot be startled by life. It cannot be both threatened and free. Life isn’t threatening to a free consciousness in any way. The eternal cannot be intimidated by the temporary. That’s where we’re headed. Q. What is the answer to the question of what to do in a given situation? A. You’ll know what to do when you are free from fear. Q. When I am in the mindset of ‘I don’t know’, is there freedom there?

A. That’s what I’m talking about. It means freedom from the world of experiences. It means stopping the labeling of experiences as good or bad. You give up all these ideas and preconceptions, and the illusion that you know what’s necessary or unnecessary. They block you from being available to experience the Isness of things. Otherwise, you’re trapped by your ideas. If your ideas oppose reality, you fight it. If your ideas are in favor of reality, you think this temporary condition is good and try to hold on to it, fearing change. Whether it’s ‘good’ or ‘bad’, you’re still trapped.

The mindset I don’t know is free to experience with a whole heart. A heart cannot be whole if it holds onto an idea about something. If it prefers an idea over reality, it’s not free to fully experience reality. Consciousness goes beyond preconceptions. This is the third stage of closing the gap. Adding humility is the first. Adopting an opposite paradigm is the second. The third stage is giving up the paradigm. It means that you have no idea about it. Or, at least, your ideas about it don’t interest you. Your opinions do not matter. What you are interested in is to open your heart to what is. Think about how many conditions you have regarding reality. You believe that if reality aligns with the imaginary movie you have in your head, then all will be good, then you can be happy. This is never the case. It’s an illusion. Reality never gets confused. It’s exact, in divine accuracy. You get confused when you prefer your ideas over reality. Karma and Me White Path Meeting April, 2023

Q. Last week, I brought up the issue of resentment. And you told me it could be karma. And I want to ask you, how do we not deal with karma? That is to say, every time there is something karmic, what do I do? What do we do at all if there is karma? A. Excellent question. I don’t remember our conversation from last week, but let’s address your question this week. It’s an interesting question. First of all, we need to understand what karma is. We need to let go of the idea that karma is related to reward and punishment. It’s not that if you do good things, good things will happen to you, and if you do bad things, bad things will happen to you. On the White Path, we know there is no such thing as good and bad. We do not fall into that trap. This is the first thing you need to know about karma.

Secondly, recognize the fact that undisturbed reality is an expression of silent harmony, like a very quiet lake. Crystal clear and calm. The waters of the lake are smooth like a mirror. But into this silence, we sometimes introduce noises. Like when we throw a stone and ripples form in the water. Then there is a ripple and another ripple that comes to correct that ripple, and so on. Slowly, the lake returns itself to a state of quiet thanks to these ripples. This is karma, a situation where reality restores itself to a state of harmony. When do we introduce noises and disturbances into this harmony? When we ourselves are disharmonious. When we act out of fear, suffering, ego. Karma yoga is action stemming from ego, from fear, and it creates karma. It creates these disturbances, and then reality corrects itself, and this correction is called karma. Q. So, a person who has karma needs to wait for reality to correct it? Is there nothing they can do?

A. First of all, their life is an expression of this correction. They don’t need to wait. It happens all the time. We come with these imprints from previous incarnations, from childhood and the scratches we carry with us, and because of them, we act and make choices. Every time it comes from fear, we add a bit more karma to our story. Reality corrects this as we go along. Sometimes it manages to correct it in this incarnation, and sometimes it continues and tries to correct it in future incarnations. This is karma. Can karma be burnt? Absolutely, yes. How do we burn karma? We learn to love reality wholeheartedly and face life with a willing soul. The moment my life becomes an expression of unconditional love, with my entire being wholehearted and willing, karma will no longer affect me. Q. It seems very general to me. Wholeheartedly and with a willing soul– it seems very general. I’m not focusing on something I want to change. Your answer is very important to me, and the definition of karma is not enough for me. A. Then ask the question again.

Q. The question was, what do we do with resentment? A. What is resentment? Q. It’s something more than hatred sometimes. I hold onto it, keep it. I don’t let it go. A. Why? Q. Because I don’t know how to do it. A. The question is if you want to. Q. Of course I want to. Of course, I want to.

A. Let’s believe, for the sake of this discussion, that you really want to. And it’s more important to you than being right, and more important to you than proving to others that they understand you were right, and they were always wrong. If it’s more important to you to let go of resentment and keep your heart full and your soul willing, then every time your clash with reality leads you to contract and resist and get angry and criticize and hate or hold resentment, every time this happens, remind yourself, wait, no, no, no, this is not what’s most important to me. What’s more important is to remain with a whole heart. In real-time, when you feel the contraction in your throat or your stomach, tell yourself, no, this is not what I seek. What I seek is to remain with a whole heart and a willing soul. To choose this again and again. On the day when silence becomes more attractive than drama…

The reason we refuse to surrender to silence is that we gain something from the noise. Here I am raising several possibilities. I am not necessarily claiming this is valid for you, but giving examples of why one may hold onto resentment: It keeps you in the position of the one who is right. Boosting your ego. Feeling better about yourself. It keeps you in the position of the victim. It’s very pleasant and comfortable to be in the position of the victim because you don’t have to take responsibility. It provides you with self-definition: Who am I? The one who was wronged. What will I be without this belief? Leave me alone, it’s too much for me. I’ll have to reinvent myself.

But if you are truly sincere in your longing to grow beyond the drama and surrender to your choice of keeping a whole heart, then every time life makes you contract, you’ll remind yourself, no, no, no. This is not what I’m looking for. Take a deep breath, let go of the ideas you have about the issue, and fall in love again with what is. This is how karma is burned - by repeatedly falling in love with what is. Eventually, karma will have no place to attach itself. Everything will be polished, and it won’t be able to stick, like Teflon. Fall in Love with What Is Q. Yaron, how do you fall in love with what is? I know all the techniques of closing gaps, but it’s still technical and doesn’t put me in a place of love. I feel rigid. In this way of doing this and that, I feel rigidity, and I ask myself how can I reach the softness of love instead of this rigidity which is all about rules and methods.

A. The softness comes to fruition in the third stage. Remember? The first stage is adding humility. The second is changing the paradigm to the opposite of what caused the suffering and falling in love with this new paradigm, instead of clinging to the idea that started the suffering, the idea that contradicts reality. The third stage is the stage of softness - the stage where we give up all paradigms. We no longer have ideas about what is. We only have love. Imagine how soft we can be when there are no opinions we attach ourselves to anymore. Q. How do you fall in love? A. What closes us off and makes us rigid are our positions, ideas, and opinions. We have ideas about the matter and the ideas are very rigid. I know what should be, I know what is good and what is bad. As long as reality does not align with our ideas, then we are rigid, we suffer, and we create karma. But once we give up our ideas, not for or against, not good or bad, then we are completely available to experience everything that is. An experience free of judgment equals love.

Write that sentence on your refrigerator. Q. What a long way one must go to not be judgmental. A. What would you be without this belief? Q. I would be accepting, I would be soft, I would be loving. Right now… A. So, what is more appealing to you? It’s just a belief. It’s not real. You are creating this reality for yourself. If you believe there is a long way to go, I assure you, there will be a long way to go for you. If you believe it’s a matter of lifetimes, unequivocally, it will be lifetimes for you.
