You are creating it. See that you choose your beliefs carefully. Or even agree to give up your beliefs entirely. Not for nor against. Then you are free to love what is. You discover there is no way at all. There is only reality. Wow, this is like poetry happening here today. Q. You are prolific today. A. Luckily, it’s being recorded. What else? Q. You know, you’re absolutely right about me having opinions about matters. It defines me. A. Here is the question worth keeping in our basket and pulling out whenever we are tangled with a bunch of ideas.

What would I be without this belief? Again and again, ask this question. Q. It’s really scary to give up all these things. A. Oh, if it’s scary, it’s a sign you’re getting closer to the edge of the cliff… Remain Innocent Q. In the end, I’ll be like a baby who hasn’t yet formed an opinion. He has no thought about what is right. He is just open. A. When they ask my teacher, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, “Who are you?” He says, “I am a child who never grew up.” And he is 67 years old (2024).

So don’t be afraid that you won’t know what to do. You will. You don’t become a helpless baby - that’s not the developmental process. There may be a stage where you feel lost. The judgmental center within you, which was busy managing and controlling, evaporates, leaving you a bit bewildered as you face reality. Some people go through this phase, but it’s temporary. Soon, the ability to manage life returns as the dust settles, and new realizations integrate into the newly revealed Self. Accept this period. There is no fear - only an expression of love, compassion, giving, and abundance that flows from within outward. It generates action without self-interest. Without an agenda. Without karma. Q. I want to ask something. Where does creativity fit into all this?

A. Life is creative. That’s the nature of life. It’s part of the femininity, the feminine element of life. Look at how creative life is. How it manages to animate everything happening around you and adapt to changing circumstances to ensure continued existence. Creativity happens spontaneously without you controlling this process. You can’t force the muse. You have inspiration, and then real creativity happens, real innovation. It’s not because of you, and it’s not thanks to you. It arises because you are free from the drama of being someone for a moment. Love translates itself into creation.

The potential exists within masculinity. Femininity translates it into experience. A man plants the seed, and the woman builds life from it. Masculinity creates the silence, the space within which femininity can create. The feminine responds to the masculine-inspired invitation which permits the dance where creativity happens spontaneously. Don’t try to cultivate these qualities of being creative. My talent, me, me, thanks to me. That’s not it. You are just the channel through which creativity happens. It happens when you are free from I want. I need. What will I get out of it? Q. Creativity is essentially part of the universe reflecting on individuals to bring it to expression. It’s a privilege to receive creativity from the universe and pass it on.

A. We all have the privilege to experience our lives. Think about how many souls are waiting in line to get a body, so they too can experience it. The line is endless. We have won. Let’s take advantage of this opportunity. Instead of waiting for the experience to change and become more comfortable and more suited to our expectations and demands, let’s surrender to what is and take full advantage of the opportunity to experience what is, with a whole heart and a willing soul. Q. I want to ask something. In order to shed all the conditioning and all the ideas, does one need a sufficiently strong mental maturity to undertake this process? I’m asking if there are people who might fall apart from this. Fall apart in the sense of losing their sanity.

A. There is something in your question because spirituality is relevant to those who have a certain degree of basic mental stability. For those who come disturbed in their mind, where mental stability is not strong enough, the spiritual path may not be relevant for them, and might even be harmful. It might lead to a kind of breakdown. As we are invited to let go of our crutches, those with fragile centre can collapse. Let’s assume that everyone listening here in the circle belongs to the family of mentally healthy people. Q. If creativity truly isn’t mine, but something that comes from above, then what’s special about me? Everything comes from above, but we are also waves. The waves are different from each other. What is mine? Where is my uniqueness? A. In the fact that you are you, you are who you are. There isn’t another like you. There never was and never will be. This is a one-time event. Q. My creation, isn’t that part of my uniqueness?

A. The creation that flows through you is very unique. But it isn’t yours. The I, that thanks to whom that creation exists, is not real. The wave isn’t special, it’s just another oceanic expression. No two waves indeed look the same, and each wave is unique, but all the waves are expressions of the same unity. We are a unique, one-time, temporary expression of eternity. Let go of the I, the I that says it’s because of me. There is no such I. Certainly not to build an identity around. Who am I? I am a great artist. The one because of whom all this beauty exists. That takes us away from the truth and dampens the wonderment of the beauty. Enough for today? Q. It was fascinating. Embracing Life’s Totality White Path Meeting July, 2022 Q. I don’t know how, during one conversation or by listening to anyone speaking to you, Yaron, I’ll be able to reset my thinking or experience a place where I can enjoy multiple aspects of pain, as you mentioned. It doesn’t compute for me. A. Pain is not bad. Q. Then why do we cry? A. Because we’re sad. It’s okay, we’re human.

Q. Right, but crying from pain is not the same crying that comes from a place of love. Why are we afraid? I-I’m not afraid to love, but I’m afraid of the pain. A. That’s a question you’ll have to ask yourself. Q. I’m also bringing it up here in the hope someone can give me some direction, some thought. Maybe you can? A. Pain is not the problem. Pain is an experience you’re invited to have in a given moment. When you can love the pain as you love the pleasure, then you’ll be free from this resistance, from this realm of phenomenon that occurs. Q. How can one enjoy physical pain, how can one? A. Fear is the resistance to the phenomenon life invites us to experience now. It’s suffering. Fear and suffering are almost the same thing. The suffering we experience is because we believe what’s here is not good. It’s not right. It’s not accurate. It’s not desired. It shouldn’t even exist. When will I be happy? When will I be able to love again? I’ll be happy when what’s here changes, turns over, or disappears. Only then I’ll be free, fulfilled, or enlightened.

But that’s not the case, friends, that’s not it, that’s not the truth. The truth is that true happiness/fulfillment/enlightenment are not dependent on changing circumstances. They are not a derivative of changing circumstances. Just like the room we’re in now doesn’t depend on what’s happening inside it. Just like the stage in the theater hall doesn’t care if a comedy or a tragedy is being played on it. Just like the cinema screen doesn’t get excited if a drama or a comedy is being screened. What does it matter? It doesn’t matter. Q. Pain is a phenomenon, right? A. Correct. Pleasure and pain are one and the same. Those who don’t want pain don’t know true pleasure. Those who don’t want sorrow don’t know happiness. They don’t know. Why? Because they’re busy complaining and avoiding instead of experiencing. Instead of experiencing what is, they’re busy complaining, evaluating, grading the situation. They’re not truly free, they’re not free. So, life waits. Life waits. For what? For us to turn around. To turn around to love. To love what is.

Q. It reminds me of when I was a girl and complained about a headache. My late father would say, “It’s there to remind you that you have a head. Be happy.” A. Don’t fear pain, friends, don’t fear. Unfortunately, this body is on a downward path. It might take another 20 years, another 80 years, it doesn’t matter, the path is certain. But that says nothing about the consciousness that is living and experiencing life through the body. The body can decay but consciousness can rise, and the secret is not to resist the experience the body offers. Neither to resist nor to identify with the body as an answer to the question of who am I? Q. It’s clear to me that from the day I was born, I got a ticket in one direction. I do not doubt that. I don’t want that ticket to end too soon.

A. Do you know when the journey will end? It will end at the right moment, exactly on time, divine timing. How do I know? Because that’s all there is. Nothing else. We have ideas about how things should be but those are just stories, not the truth. In philosophy, asking What is truth? has occupied the greatest minds. The best answer I can give is the present moment. What IS, is the truth. The closest description of truth. Do you want to live a life of truth? Return to what is. In what is, expand. Become accessible, exposed, and vulnerable. Say YES, with a whole heart and a willing soul. Growing Towards Inner Freedom White Path Meeting September, 2022 Q. What is freedom?

A. That’s an interesting question, and each of us should define it for ourselves. This question belongs to the family of the leading questions. These are questions without a definitive answer. The only way to approach it is through negation. Freedom is the absence of coercion. A free consciousness is not enslaved by ideas, conditioning, or narrow perspectives from education or culture. It’s a consciousness no longer bound to any event, to any occurrence. Neither for nor against. Free to be fearless and innocent. Simply an expression of love. That’s freedom. Freedom isn’t a vacation or the ability to do whatever you want. It’s not about filling voids. True freedom is a state of being, a freedom of consciousness. Don’t confuse it with action - what you’re doing or avoiding isn’t the point. It is called INNER freedom since you stop searching for it outside of us. Q. Will you give us an example?

A. We all have these unique opportunities where we experience NO SELF. Sometimes spontaneously, or after deep meditation, and we wake immediately, craving the experience again. We take it as the desired pinnacle of our spiritual journey and we want to go back and recreate it for ourselves. This is a fallacy. The secret does not lie in a specific experience, (as beautiful and profound as may be), but rather in the experiencer. No experience is inherently better than another. Some are pleasant, others challenging, and some very unpleasant, but none is preferable. Categorizing experiences only enslaves us. Stop chasing experiences and repose in your SELF. No experience is preferable. There’s no hierarchy. If we start categorizing our experiences like this, we are enslaved to experiences. We will not find freedom there.

The freedom I speak of is a consciousness broad enough to say YES to every experience, whether it matches or contradicts your expectations. The race for specific experiences stops. God isn’t waiting in some other experience. A free consciousness is revealed in the present moment, whether it’s trivial or divine. That’s freedom. Q. Sitting in front of a computer all day versus sitting by the sea all day. They’re not the same, are they? A. No, they’re not the same. Experiences vary. Some are adrenaline-filled, others are mundane. The goal is to stop being dependent on circumstances. If you can only be content under certain conditions, there’s no freedom. Sitting by the sea is nice, but if you label an experience as good or bad, that’s a trap. True freedom is loving what is, whether it’s a computer or the sea. If you interpret the experience as good, then it’s good, and if you decide it is bad, then it is bad - for you.

Attachment, craving, avoidance, and desire create the trap. A free consciousness doesn’t categorize reality this way. It prefers to love what is. Sometimes what is, is a computer, and sometimes it’s the sea, sometimes neither. You can choose to reject or to love any experience. That’s the freedom of choice. We’re not talking about the freedom to choose what to do when we talk about inner freedom (assuming, for the sake of argument, that you really can choose and that choice is a thing). If your choice stems from some ego manipulation seeking where it can enjoy more or where it can suffer less, there is no freedom. We need to explore another question - what is choice? The illusion of choice only happens when there’s an ego that directs me in life, and it always exists in the context of absence, lack, need, and dependency. I don’t have enough comfort. I don’t have enough tokens of love. I need more.

If you are an expression of abundance, you are no longer governed by lack. If you are an expression of love, then love flows. It doesn’t hesitate or become preoccupied with where to flow. The entity that seeks to earn more or lose less disappears. Love alone knows where to fill and where to flow. Let me share a story from my time in India. Years ago, I witnessed a remarkable moment during a Puja ceremony at an Ashram. A group of young priest apprentices were chanting ancient mantras while Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar performed the rituals. Suddenly, I noticed Gurudev looking at one of the apprentices with a knowing glance. He seemed to sense that the boy was struggling to remember his part. As I watched, the apprentice’s face turned pale, and he appeared to be panicking. Gurudev motioned for the boy to come closer. The apprentice, filled with fear, hesitantly approached him. To my astonishment, Gurudev invited the young priest to join him in the ceremony, entrusting him with the sacred objects used to complete the Puja. This is a rare honor, usually reserved for experienced priests.

The entire interaction was performed with grace and subtlety. If you hadn’t been paying close attention, you might have missed it entirely. For me, it was a powerful lesson in the nature of unconditional love. It knows where to flow, what to fill, when, and how much. There’s no drama. We’re not here to cling to the good and avoid the bad - that is just an ego-created illusion. A free consciousness experiences whatever is, whether pleasant or unpleasant. It doesn’t categorize reality. Freedom is realizing a whole heart and a willing soul in this moment as it happens - then you are free. The upliftment you’re talking about isn’t dependent on circumstances. It’s not that there’s just one type of experience where you allow yourself to develop and flourish. Your heart is open regardless of the experience. Whatever happens in this moment, that’s where you are in love. That’s what you are in love with. If you’re dependent on circumstances, you’re enslaved. Q. Who determines the circumstances?

A. The collective consciousness. Contrary to the idea that you create your own circumstances, you are part of the collective consciousness. Q. So, being in silence isn’t necessarily better than being in noise? A. Correct. It’s not better, or holier than watching the news. In a silent retreat, we aim to go beyond the experience, even beyond the experience of stillness, but we find in stillness the answer to the question who am I? We artificially shut out the noise around us - communication, cellphones. We calm all the surrounding noise. Usually, there’s so much noise. The retreat invitation’s title is: Silence is who you are - Remaining silent brings you there To recognize that silence is your true nature, you can start by muting the background noise. Once you know that silence is your true nature, circumstances no longer threaten it. Silence always lies beneath the noise. You just need to close your eyes, breathe, and remember who you are. When life’s circumstances no longer threaten you, you are free!

Q. I have an image of a small child. What is this whole journey of life about? We are born with free consciousness, slowly corrupting it, and wanting to return there. Are we succeeding or failing? A. Mysterious, isn’t it? Why do we come without an ego, build an ego, only to one day receive the invitation to grow beyond it? The question you’re asking is like asking why God created the Garden of Eden, let us taste it, and then kicked us out. For what? What is He teasing us with? Why would He do that? The answer to that question might be to ignite the longing. The longing to return and reconnect. It’s the evolutionary force; God’s own development is propelled by it. To me, Why do we have an ego? and Why did God kick us out of heaven? are the same question. We long to return. That longing to return and reconnect is the power that promotes the evolution of consciousness, of God Himself. It’s the developmental force. In Eden, there’s stagnation. Everything there just exists. There’s no development.

To have development, there needs to be tension. We develop an ego and then are asked to grow beyond it. The Cosmic Dance White Path Meeting February, 2023 Q. You were talking about masculine energy changing. This is the first time you’ve mentioned it or the first time I’ve heard about it, and I would be happy if you could clarify a bit more about Masculine and Feminine energies.

A. Sure. The universe is built and operates through the tension between two forces. The force of attraction and the force of repulsion. The extrapolation of these two forces creates all the mechanical and energetic forces in the universe. To the force of attraction, we attribute feminine energy. This is the force that collects, connects, pulls everything towards a singular point. The masculine force is the bursting force that goes outward to search, seek, conquer, to break boundaries. That’s masculine energy. Masculine energy works for change, for evolution. The balance between these forces allows life to exist in the physical realm. It is the same in the personal world of each of us. The challenge for us is to create this balance within ourselves, first and foremost. And then, within our relationships. Q. What did you say enables life?

A. The balance between feminine and masculine energy. Think of an atom. An atom is composed of a nucleus with electrons orbiting it. The electrons constantly want to escape, at the speed of light they want to escape from the nucleus. But the nucleus’s force of attraction keeps the electrons within the structure of the atom and allows for the existence of matter. And if one electron escapes, then another electron from the atom next to it replaces it so that the physical existence of the atom’s structure can still be maintained, without which there would be no matter. This is the interplay between matter and energy. Again, it’s all a metaphor... The structure of the atom as we learned in high school is a metaphor. No one knows what really happens. It’s not like there’s really a nucleus and, like a moon orbiting around it, an electron that suddenly disappears from existence and appears elsewhere in the electron next to it. No one knows how it happens. But let’s leave that to physics lessons. Q. These two energies need to be balanced, should they equal zero?

A. The zero you’re talking about is not an absolute zero, it’s a neutral zero, right? Within this zero, there can be a very high potential level. There’s an equilibrium between feminine energy and masculine energy and that’s what allows for the existence of matter and energy. As I said, what’s relevant for us is to ensure that we understand this interplay between feminine and masculine energy, and to create within ourselves a balance between these two forces. If we’re too feminine, then we tend to become submissive. We tend to become life’s doormats. When feminine energy is too strong, it’s very easy to slip into passivity. When masculine energy is too strong, we lose touch with reality. We try forcibly to create a world that operates according to our own laws. And there’s something very violent about operating from a place of inherent non-acceptance, from a very selfish place of I know, I want, and I achieve.

The balance between these two forces is very significant. It creates a harmonious movement within the flow of life. Remember, we are all built by these two forces. It is not that if you are a man, you are masculine, and if you are a woman, you are feminine. We are all a combination of these two forces. Just search within and see what force is generally more dominant within you, and see if you need to work to balance them. The Cosmic Dance Within Relationships Q. Why are relationships so complicated? A. Let us look at this through the lens of the cosmic dance of the masculine and feminine energies. What is there in this encounter? What are these energies? What are their qualities? How do they operate in the world? How do they function within each of us? How do they reflect on the relationships we have with ourselves, with our partners, and with life itself? Fascinating, isn’t it?

If we go to the story of the creation of the world (at least as the physicists describe it), just as time started, all matter and all energy exploded into being. The scientific world doesn’t explain what existed before this explosion, but let’s assume for the sake of discussion that there was potential energy waiting to materialize, to manifest as matter and energy. This potential energy was the primary feminine force. We attribute the quality of femininity to it. The explosion, this burst, is the moment when the masculine force was born. This burst has masculine energy.

By the way, it is very interesting to see that since these two energies moved from the level of potential to the level of matter and energy, the one that dominates this cosmic balance is the masculine energy. If we take all the feminine energy that wants to collapse this universe back into the singularity and compare it to all the masculine energy that wants to make this universe explode towards infinity, we find that the universe itself is still growing. It’s not even growing at a constant rate. The universe is growing at an increasing rate. This is quite amazing because if we go to Newton’s laws, (F=MA force equals mass times acceleration), for acceleration to occur, there must be a force acting on the mass. It turns out there is some force that still doesn’t have a name or known source causing this whole thing to expand at an ever-increasing speed, at constant acceleration. Ultimately, we discover that the masculine energy in the cosmic balance of the entire universe still prevails over the feminine force that wants to make everything collapse back inward.

Why is it important to know and recognize these forces? It’s important for several reasons. First of all, within the invitation to grow on the spiritual path, there is a sub-invitation, another invitation, which is always to zoom out. From the private to the collective. From the personal to the transpersonal. We tend to be very addicted to our personal drama, to the personal story of each of us, and when we hear, for example, an invitation to dance the cosmic dance, of femininity versus masculinity, the immediate need arises to solve some specific problem I have. Me with my partner, me with my mother, whatever... Maybe if I learn the White Path, I can solve some specific conflicts I am currently dealing with in my personal life.

That’s okay, but without the broader context, something will always be missing in the desire to deal with a personal drama because a personal drama is never disconnected from the broader context. It is always a personal expression of a much broader context. That’s how we look at it. What happens in my living room is always an expression of something much larger than the personal. It’s a private manifestation of a broad, collective phenomenon. That’s why I repeatedly encourage people who ask personal questions to ask them in the circle because it’s always relevant to everyone. Two Opposite Energies

When we look at the broader context of the encounter between these two energies, we discover that it is embedded in the most basic fabric of life itself. There are two energies that are opposite in their essence and nature. They are opposite in direction and opposite, you could even say, in the purpose for which they were created. One was born to disperse, and the other was born to unite. The tension between the desire to escape and the desire to unite allows for the existence of a physical world of matter and energy. Without this, it’s impossible to create matter or energy. As we mentioned, the atom structure is a good example. Some materials are inherently more feminine, with greater atomic balance, making it harder for their electrons to escape, known as insulators. And there are materials whose electrons are in a very delicate balance, meaning a small flick is enough to disrupt the atomic structure. These materials are called conductors. Think about the analogy between electricity and spiritual development and how beautiful it is to see the similarity between them.

The basic law of electricity is: Voltage = Resistance x Current (V=RI) The equivalent on the spiritual path is: Potential (creation) = Resistance (you saying NO) x Current (the flow of life) In other words, as resistance decreases, the flow of life increases. This means that even in life itself, when there is potential caused by tension - between the masculine and the feminine, between the question and the answer, between my wife and I - when there is this tension, the tension of life, it allows for development. But the more resistance there is within us, the less flow there is, and we feel stuck.

This is very beautiful to me. Even in the structure of matter, we see this interplay between two energies and its balance that allows the atomic structure of matter to exist. Without it, matter would disappear, scatter, and turn to ash. Some scientists claim that this is what the end of the universe will look like. The masculine energy will ultimately win the battle, and the forces tearing the universe apart will become so strong that the forces pulling it all back in will collapse, and the matter will cease to exist. From dust to dust, on a cosmic level. Q. Yaron, something isn’t clear. In the structure of the atom, there is the issue of the proton and the electron. Do the electrons always want to escape? A. Yes. That’s what happens when there is an electric current. We won’t delve into a physics lesson, but it’s very interesting to see how it happens. By the way, no one truly knows how it happens. That’s why there is quantum physics, which tries to create a new system of laws because mechanical physics is no longer relevant here.

There are various ways to illustrate this phenomenon called electric current. Broadly speaking, for people to understand how it works, when two atoms have a suitable potential difference, an electron from one atom breaks free from its proton’s grip and jumps over to join the neighboring atom. For the neighboring atom to maintain balance, it releases an electron to jump to the next atom. And so, a flow of electrons is created, always flowing from high potential to low potential. Where there are many electrons, they flow towards where there are fewer electrons. Think of water. Where there is a lot of water, it will always want to flow towards where there is less water. Q. And the electrons are the feminine force? A. No, the electrons are the masculine force that always wants to escape. Electrons, given a chance, will flee. Just give them the opportunity and they will immediately try to escape and find a different reality. Q. Like any man...

A. It sounds familiar, doesn’t it? Ah, yes, that’s how men behave. I urge you, however, not to rush straight to how this translates to the behavior of you or your partner or spouse. Let’s leave that aside for now. Again, today we are focusing on the broader context. Different Qualities of the Masculine and the Feminine I want to invite us to try to characterize the qualities relevant to each of these energies. As we said, they are fundamentally opposed in their nature. They are not designed to work together. They are designed to work against each other, just like two opposing vectors. The masculine movement wants to go outward, to escape from the path. It wants to burst. It wants to explode. Think of the energy of the Big Bang. It wants to break everything apart and fly as far away as possible.

The feminine movement, the opposite vectorial force, is the movement that wants to take all this and bring it back inward, to unite everything back into this singularity point. On the cosmic level, these are two completely opposite forces in their motion, in their vector. And there is no cosmic balance; the masculine energy is stronger than the feminine energy today. Why? No one knows, but that’s apparently the situation. Q. I wanted to ask about the masculine explosive energy and the energy that wants to return to the singularity point, the feminine energy. Where does the theory or the statement that one is masculine and the other feminine come from? Why is each represented this way?

A. Good question, why do I call this one masculine and that one feminine? Simply to have a common terminology. It’s like asking why a cypress tree is called a cypress tree. When I say cypress tree, you have the image of a cypress tree in your mind and not a eucalyptus, okay? We give ourselves names so we can speak the same language together. Looking back, why is explosive energy associated with masculinity and collapsing energy with femininity? If we look back at the history of humanity, we see this repeated in all cultures, all traditions, all religions. This is terminology humanity has used throughout the years. It’s not something I invented today.

What I want to invite us to do now is to characterize the different qualities of masculine energy versus feminine energy. It’s important we understand these definitions. This is before it translates to the persona, okay? We are still talking about qualities of energy, not necessarily about any specific person or man or woman. Let’s leave that aside for now. We are only looking at the energy itself, how it operates, what kind of qualities it brings with it, inherent in its direction of movement. Characteristics of the Masculine So, let’s tune our consciousness to the quality of masculine energy, the explosive energy.

Several qualities characterize this movement, this energy. First of all, the movement is linear. It starts from the source and tries to reach its destination as quickly as possible, like a straight line connecting two points. It’s not an energy that meanders. It is an energy that tries to go straight, taking the shortest path from point A to point B. It is also structured, meaning it operates based on predefined patterns. It has the quality of light, like the sun - an energy that bursts outward. The Chinese call it Yang. If we talk about Yin and Yang, then Yang is the masculine energy. It is a giving energy, like the sun providing warmth and light. It belongs to the right side of the human body and the left side of the brain. It is an energy of freedom, an energy that cannot stand being confined. It always wants to burst out.

Masculine energy is very directional. It’s logical, and associated with the exact sciences, reason, and rationality. It is highly focused, goal-oriented, and precise. Masculine energy is an energy of concentration. It also has a certain stability - once it chooses a direction, it sticks to it and doesn’t get easily distracted. Q. Yaron, where do we learn about these characteristics, like the masculine energy being explosive? Where’s the proof that this is indeed masculine energy? A. Again, call it whatever you want. We agree that two different, opposing qualities in nature sustain life in the physical world. We could call them Joel and Sarah. It doesn’t matter what names we give them. But we recognize the fact that these two energies exist, their movements are opposite, and the tension within these movements is what allows for the existence of life in the physical realm. So, we call them, for the sake of the discussion, and also out of respect for the history of human development, feminine versus masculine. Q. And they can be measured?

A. Energy can be measured, yes. If you are a physicist, there is a way to measure the amount of energy, and it is always relative. Energy is always measured relative to something else. Q. You could also relate this to two types of energy, like love on one side and fear on the other. A. We haven’t gotten there yet, but yes. We are on our way. Q. Love expands, and fear contracts. A. Exactly. The feminine energy wants to unite everything. Feminine energy is an expression of love that wants to turn everything back into one. Masculine energy is energy that tries to escape, that is afraid. Q. But if you say feminine energy, think about where it comes from. Isn’t the desire to bring everyone together come from fear?

A. We are already getting into nuances... Love, in its essence, is very feminine. What is love? Maybe we need to refine this terminology. What is love? The most wonderful definition I know of what love is-the universal force that turns separation into unity. It’s almost the definition of what we have defined as feminine energy, this force that wants to bring everything back to one, to unity. This has feminine energy.

Fear is associated with masculine energy. But let’s leave that for now. We will talk about how this translates to our persona later. Let’s go back to masculine energy because we haven’t finished describing it. We said it has a certain stability, reliability, and independence. It cannot stand being tied down, it cannot stand being confined or enclosed. It has a certain discipline. Think about the military. The military has a very strong masculine quality. In masculine energy, there is something very secure, calm, and self-assured. Something that can convey a sense of security and protection. It can also be the quality that defends. In terms of elements, those associated with masculine energy are fire and air. It is relatively quick, to the point, and also has an inherent rigidity. Characteristics of the Feminine Now let’s describe feminine energy. How is it characterized? What are the qualities of feminine energy?

If we said that masculine energy is linear, then feminine energy is cyclical. Feminine energy is characterized by creativity. It loves to improvise. It can handle different kinds of realities much more easily, and it is much more compatible with various possibilities.

Unlike masculine energy, which sees the goal and heads straight for it, feminine energy is much more open to nurturing its surroundings, being aware of everything that happens along the way. You know that invitation in almost every spiritual path - set yourself a goal, but don’t forget that the journey happens in this moment, with each step you take. So, don’t forget to look at the flowers along the way to your goal, keeping a certain balance between the two forces. Heading towards the goal is masculinity. Looking at the flowers along the way is femininity. If we said masculine energy is like the sun, then feminine energy is like the moon. The moon absorbs the sun’s energy and only reflects it back, echoes it back, but it doesn’t have that intense power of the sun built into it. If we say masculine energy is light, then feminine energy is darkness. If we said masculine energy is Yang, then feminine energy is Yin, the receptive, absorbing force. It belongs to the left side of the body and the right hemisphere of the brain.

Feminine energy is an energy that knows how to surrender at the level of devotion. It has something empathetic, something containing, something that knows how to embrace, accept, and love. It flows. It doesn’t insist. It allows. It has something sensual, round, something that knows how to fill where there is a lack. Very adaptable. Very soft, patient, intuitive, emotional. The elements associated with feminine energy are water and earth. It happens slowly, unlike masculine energy which tries to move quickly. Feminine energy is in no hurry. It moves slowly, sinks in, and is very sensitive. These two qualities are opposite in their direction, and each has a whole set of traits or qualities built into their movement, built into the very fabric of existence, of the energy itself. Even before it translates into persona, it’s important to see these qualities inherent in the energy. The Dance in the Context of Spiritual Development

How is this translated into spiritual development? Those of you with a keen eye might have noticed there is a recommended chronological order for those who want to develop spiritually. The first stage belongs to the invitation of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar - know that you are nothing. There is something very feminine about this - the ability to accept, to embrace, to surrender, to love, to stop trying to escape, to rise above fear. There is something very feminine, very authentic, about the ability to let go and surrender. Know that you are nothing. This means the first invitation on the spiritual path is to enhance the feminine quality within us, to make it easier for us to accept and love what is, and to let go of the drama. At this evolutionary stage, the spiritual path is characterized by nowhere to go, nothing to do… The second stage is - know that you are everything. This is the call to grow, to expand, to discover who we are as the entire universe. It includes the invitation to burst outward.

After we have let go of the resistance, the need to be an individual, to sing our unique song, to exclaim but what about me, what will happen to me? then suddenly there is the possibility to grow towards masculine energy. So, even on the spiritual path, there is a kind of chronology of healthy development that is first feminine in its quality and only then masculine. Let’s summarize. When we zoom out as far as we can, we see that in the fabric of life itself, there are two basic energies whose tension creates the possibility for life in the physical world. All matter, all chemistry, and all physics arise from the tension between these two energies. Each energy has its own set of characteristics that emerge from the movement of the energy itself.

There is one more important thing to note. In the most basic fabric of matter, these two energies will always exist. Just as within each of us, these two energies are always at play. Being a man does not mean I only harbor masculine energy. Not at all. Female energy plays a role as well. Sometimes one is more dominant than the other. We will talk more about this next week. But even in matter, even in physical life, everything we encounter has both energies at play. Sometimes masculinity wins, and sometimes femininity wins. There is always tension between the two. In the past week, as I warmed up for today’s meeting, I encountered what life had to offer through the lens of femininity versus masculinity. What interested me when looking through this lens was to see which energy is winning now. Let me give you an example.

The previous car I drove was very masculine in its essence and energy - in the way it sat on the road, in the message it projected around it - very masculine. It was powerful and attention-seeking. It had unforgiven suspension - every bump was felt. I sold it and bought another car, which had a completely opposite energy. It was very feminine, very soft, very accommodating, and not attention-seeking. When I drove it, it was like floating above the road. It did not resist anything. It allowed everything. I pressed a little on the gas and the car glided, effortlessly - very feminine. In the coming week, I invite you to find the expression of masculinity versus femininity in your daily life. Be aware of it, of what you encounter now, what is leading. You will see it’s a very interesting game - masculinity versus femininity. How do these forces constantly interact with each other in your life? Q. Is it always either/or?

A. No, it’s always both, but there is almost always one that is more dominant. Rarely do they create a balance, which ideally, we strive for in our spiritual development. Q. That’s the nirvana we all want to reach... A. Not necessarily. If we are talking in terms of mysticism from Eastern teachings, the crescendo of spiritual development is when the Kundalini bursts through our seven chakras - from the first chakra to the crown chakra. This movement of the Kundalini bursting outwards is a very masculine movement. So, it’s not necessarily that we need to reach some equilibrium, some balance. I may even encourage something different. If you are looking for the key to development towards freedom through these two energies, don’t seek equilibrium. Seek to amplify the feminine energy first of all: acceptance, containment, allowing, loving, soft, devotion, beyond any doubt. Or, find a perfect balance (it doesn’t really matter…). I don’t want you to construct concepts about the right order or balance. If it sounds like I’m contradicting myself - GOOD!

Expand your consciousness to allow all possibilities. Balancing the Masculine and Feminine Within White Path Meeting February, 2023 We have discussed the two eternal forces that dance with each other, enabling life to exist in the physical realm - the masculine and the feminine. The masculine is the centrifugal force that seeks to escape, to push through, to break barriers, constantly evolving. The feminine, on the other hand, is the centripetal force that pulls everything back to the original point, bonding all things in love. The balance between these two forces is what allows life to exist and develop. I invited you all to explore how these forces behave in your own lives and relationships, and you are welcome to share what you’ve discovered. Who wants to be the first one to jump into the water today? Q. Can you talk a little bit more about balancing? A. So why balance those two forces? Like any healthy system, it needs to be balanced. Otherwise, it's not working harmoniously.

If masculine is dominant and feminine is suppressed, we might get a bit too aggressive, or too ambitious without paying enough attention to the details. We might be unconcerned about other people's feelings, only concerned about our own mission, and not compassionate enough. With too much masculinity you might plow through towards an end goal but are unable to sustain the journey. Or, if the feminine aspect of ourselves is too prominent and the masculine is suppressed, we feel stagnated, we feel a lack of inspiration, and our life lacks meaning. Or we might feel disempowered, dependent, or overwhelmed. Balancing these is important. What usually happens when trying to balance the two forces is that rather than balancing from within, people go outside of themselves to search for something. To fill the lack, to compliment themselves, right?

A person, who is typically more masculine by nature, meets another person, who is typically more feminine. Together they combine their qualities where they feel they can balance each other. This can be nice, but unfortunately, it is not sustainable. If what glues them together is a sense of lack and dependency, they become codependent. They feel that we need each other to stay balanced and stable. If that is taken away, they feel threatened again. An awakened consciousness is a consciousness that is manifesting this balance independently. It's an expression of those two forces working, dancing harmoniously with each other, regardless of what is happening out there. It's a beautiful song that is sung through us, harmoniously, regardless of the circumstance.

As you probably realize, remaining balanced is also crucial to allow a healthy relationship with other people. You don't come to that relationship demanding, you are already resolved. Imagine a relationship where partners are already resolved. They don't need each other. They join because they love, not because they need to. Then they dance the cosmic dance together. Such a beautiful difference between the two, don't you agree? Once you realize how those two forces work within yourself, consciously make sure they are balanced. Q. I have an example to share from my week of this very thing. I was taking down the holiday lights for an elderly neighbor. I wanted to accomplish the task quickly, while the neighbor needed me to listen… (Everyone is laughing) A. Yes, the part of you that wanted to accomplish the task quickly is masculine, and the neighbor needed your feminine energy to sit and be available to listen.

Q. Well, what I did was become aware of it, because of our discussion last week. Then I took a deep breath, smiled at myself, thought about the masculine and feminine energies within me and chose to put down the lights, and listened patiently. A. Of course, let me stop here for a minute and say, it doesn't stop there. This is not the final station. Once you are not dependent anymore, and you are a manifestation of a balanced and harmonious dance between those two forces, then you realize that the illusion of YOU being self-sufficient has evaporated.

That YOU doesn’t truly exist. That YOU that wants to be self-sufficient, that wants to be balanced, that wants to achieve that goal, that YOU is just an illusion of separateness. It might need to go through that process, from being dependent to being independent. From being unbalanced to being balanced. But once balanced, it's easier to let go of the idea that you had to go through that journey and achieve that goal. Don't get too hung up on the illusion of I made it. I am now independent. I'm such an amazing achiever. Then you are just stuck again in the same trap, just wrapped in a different wrapping paper. See what I am saying? So, don't get too hung up about that. Q. Balancing of the masculine and the feminine, sun and moon. Are they contradicting each other?

A. No, the Sun and the moon are not contradicting each other. Duality is always about contradicting. Do you see that? There's good versus bad. There is the right thing to do, and there is the wrong thing to do. This dichotomous view of the world is artificial, created by humans so we can better understand what the heck is going on around us. The moon and the sun exist, and don't contradict each other. They complement each other. What seems to be opposite values, are never truly opposite. They are just various versions of one truth, complementing each other, and creating a holistic structure of reality. So, an expanded consciousness does not see the world in this type of dichotomic way where it must be either this or that. I discussed with a beautiful friend recently about how to incorporate spiritual values in the corporate world and business, as it may seem contradicting. He asked, “If you are not driven by ego anymore, by that sense of competition and profit/loss, then how can you succeed in your business?”

I answered, “An expanded consciousness doesn't view the world in this dichotomous way - either this or that. Both are there, the Yin and the Yang, both are there. You can be successful in business and strive for excellence while being free from fear and a sense of lack and need. Free from the illusion that only when you reach your goal or your destination you can feel achieved, happy, and accomplished. You can be both. Any scenario is warmly loved and accepted, whether it fits your expectations or contradicts them.” An awakened consciousness does not exclude anything. Q. Is it more a matter of polarity?

A. Yes. Polarity. The negative charge and the positive charge. This is exactly the tension that allows life to exist. Think about it. If there was only positivity, only masculine energy, the universe would expand to infinity and disappear like the soap bubble. It would just disappear. And if there was only negativity, only feminine energy, it would collapse back to its original point and disappear again. You need to have that polarity to sustain life. The polarity between them allows life to exist. That is not a problem. The fact that they are polar, is not a problem. It's the way it is designed with divine accuracy. Q. I meant the energies of the sun and moon, masculine and feminine. A. Yes, I'm talking about the same thing. The physical presence of the sun and the moon and the energy of the sun and the moon are the same. They don't contradict, they compliment. You see? The sun is masculine (giving) and the moon is feminine (receiving). Q. Okay, and can you enjoy the journey to the goals? Because goals can change along the way.

A. Definitely. Usually, we get too stuck on a specific desired result. It's a very important reminder. Never get too stuck with the idea that only when you reach a certain goal, you will be happy. That's ensuring you will never arrive. Beyond that hill, where you stuck that flag, there is always another hill with a different flag, right? You believe, I’ll be happy when A, B, C and D will happen. You stick that flag in to create some sense of direction in your life, which is good. Don't get stuck with the idea that only when you reach there, you'll be happy because you'll never be truly happy that way. Happiness is that journey, for sure. Happiness is that acknowledgment of the opportunity you received to experience your journey in a physical body. May it be pleasant or unpleasant. May it feel good or bad, doesn't matter. May it meet your expectations and your plans or contradict them, whatever. Q. What is the difference between unhealthy masculine/ feminine and the ego? A. I would say that balancing the two is a sure gateway to evolve beyond the ego.

What is ego? Ego is the illusion of separateness. You versus the world. What do I want? What do I need? When you interact with life from a separate point of view, this is ego. It's like the wave only remembering itself; that temporary expression that flows above the ocean, but is completely oblivious to the ocean. When you expand beyond your ego you are reminded, awakened from a dream. You are never separated from the ocean. You have always been and always will be an oceanic expression. So that sense of separateness dissolves. Once you wake up to that realization, in order to stay awake, balancing between masculine and feminine is crucial. Otherwise, you are always led by that sense of lack. I lack this, I lack that. I lack purpose in life, or I lack love. There's always something that you feel you lack, and that sense of lack will persist and won't allow you to let go and grow beyond that Illusion. Do you see what I'm saying?

It's important that this work is a priority. If you are truly interested in expanding your consciousness and growing beyond your drama and beyond your sense of separateness, to truly manifest that potential that hides within, then, this work is essential. Make it a top priority. What do you want? You want to be an expression of a harmonious, balanced dance between those two forces. Once that is expressed through you, waking up to the realization that ego is an illusion is closer than ever. Q. What exactly does it mean for a woman to have masculinity? A. It's important to understand, we all have both forces in us. It's not that women are only feminine and men are only masculine, not at all. Both these forces build us, physically, emotionally, mentally, and spiritually. They are not always balanced. Commonly, men have more masculine energy. The masculine force is more dominant, either because of natural reasons or because of upbringing. Women typically have more prominent feminine energy.

What I am saying here is that as individuals, it is important to make sure that we are invited to balance those internally, as much as we can. We don't let go of our femininity but we add masculinity if we feel we lack that. Or the other way around. Until there is no lack, there is no need anymore. We don't need anything from the outside to complement us, to feel complete and balanced. How to Balance the Two? Typically, if you are a woman who feels more feminine and lacks masculinity, then try to see what exactly is lacking. Many times, it's a sense of purpose and conviction. Whatever it takes, you just go for it. Go for it and achieve it, you know? Even if it means that it takes you a bit further outside of your comfort zone, it doesn't matter. You just go there. For example, if you set a goal to do your Sadhana every day, your spiritual practice, 20 minutes of meditation, Yoga, whatever, you do it. Never mind the distractions - the kids, the husband, you know? Life is full of distractions and excuses to not do it. You just do it, like a soldier, that’s it!

A feminine phenomenon that I keep seeing with women, more than with men, is that sense of unworthiness. You might hear that record playing in the background. You're not worthy, not really. You feel you need to prove yourself worthy. Again, it could be because of genetics, it could be because of cultural upbringing, it doesn't matter. So, what is the masculine way to react to that record? Ignore it! Let it play. You just plow through any doubt, any inhibition, because you have a goal. What is your goal? To be free. That's it. In Sanskrit, it is called Sankalpa - that clear, focused intention. This is what I want! This is what I am going to achieve. That’s it! Q. How do I know whether I am feminine or masculine? Do I need both in life? A. You cannot avoid it. You have both, you are both. We all are. The challenge is to see what is more dominant, and what needs some compensation to achieve a balance.

You are welcome to engage in some self-observation. What is more prominent in me? What needs some compensation? And then deliberately, intentionally, put energy into that. You know, in life, whatever you put your energy into, whatever you focus on, that grows. So, you don't even need to do much. You just need to focus. If you lack masculinity for example, then you focus on the masculine side of yourself. Put your attention there, and it will blossom. Put your awareness there. I want to expand more on the masculine, let life show me how to do it. It will happen. For sure. Q. Do you think that when there's unhealthy masculine or feminine it's just an imbalance? A. Definitely. What is unhealthy masculinity? It's an individual that lacks compassion, obsessed with their own needs and wants. Their path. Their convictions, right? By being obsessed only with that, one can easily trample on and harm other people.

What is an unhealthy feminine? As femininity is the energy that connects, an unbalanced person might take upon it all the sorrow, all the pain, all the blame. They don’t feel worthy of being happy or to blossom as feminine. They shut down, become a doormat, and try desperately to please. They turn into a tool for everyone to use and abuse. When you're balanced, naturally, you become a healthy manifestation of these two forces dancing together. And remember, it starts with you choosing to become a harmonious, balanced manifestation of the two forces. Q. Is it possible to be feminine at one point in time, and switch to masculine? A. One point in time? It happens a hundred times a day. Every situation calls for something else within you. That's why you need to be aware. See what is jumping up first when reacting to situations. What is the reflex? How do you react? See if that is mostly feminine or masculine, and then see if you can balance it. Q. A few sessions ago you told us to be a doormat. So, what's the difference now?

A. So first of all, I never guaranteed that I would never contradict myself. I’m just making sure I keep you on your toes. This is one of the most beautiful things I found on the spiritual path. I found it with my teacher. I go and sit in his presence, and I hear him speak about something, and it's so beautiful, it's so harmonious. I say, “This is the truth. This is God speaking the truth, it cannot be described better than that.” The next day, I come and sit in his presence, and I hear him saying the exact opposite of what he just said yesterday and I say, “Wow, this is so beautiful, so harmonious. It couldn’t be described any better.”

Why is that? To make sure you don't get too hung up on ideas and concepts, and don't create an opinion, that again, becomes a barrier between you and reality. Don't create a new concept. Your intellect can be flexible enough to hold an idea and then let go of it just as easily as it held onto it in the first place. Don’t get stuck with any opinion, or any point of view. Remember that an expanded consciousness embraces all opinions, all points of view. There is no one better than the other. Now specifically, there are two types of doormats. There is the doormat that puts itself into that position because of a lack of self-value because it doesn't believe it deserves better than being treated like that. Being humiliated is the only way it can hope to achieve attention and love, which it so desperately needs (or so it believes).

The other type of doormat is a beautiful one. A doormat that just lovingly reacts to a situation that requires a doormat because that is the harmonious way to allow life and love to flow in a given situation. It's a beautiful kind of doormat, a majestic doormat. Free from egoistic agenda. You can be the Peasant or the King You're not stuck in any position. You are flexible enough to be in all positions, and all are required. Sometimes you are the peasant. Sometimes you are the king. Do you see what I'm saying? And if you are confused, that is beautiful. Don't give up on that position. Stay confused. That's a sound feature of maturity. Q. Women who are bossy are considered masculine. The women on my maternal side are bossy and demanding. I can see that being bossy and demanding got me nowhere. A. Okay. So, you need to develop more feminine energy. Allow yourself to soften, to surrender more. Let go of the need to be in control. Beautiful. That's a beautiful realization. Now do it. Do whatever you need to do to balance these forces.

It starts with you realizing what needs compensation, and then deliberately adding it. And then realize, you are just an expression of something much bigger than you, wanting to be balanced. You are balanced, it's inevitable. You are balanced, because you are just an expression of that dance that happens anyways, regardless of your awareness or unawareness. Q. Well I am still confused. And last week you told me that was a good thing. Just saying….… A. Good! It means I'm doing something right. Let me share a secret with you. These meetings that we hold are never about the content of our discussions. It is not about exchanging information. It's not about that at all. This is just a decoy, a bait to hook you in. You Are Not Here to Get the Point

The journey is not mental. You're not here to understand, to get the point. The day when you say, Okay, I got it, I got the point, is the day that your journey ends. You don't want to get to that day. You want to allow that journey to flow endlessly, expand endlessly. You see? It is not about getting the point. If you feel you got the point, put it aside and return to the question. The secret of these meetings is opening your hearts and surrendering. The secret in these meetings is being able to listen to the silence between the words. The true calling is silence. It is not about the words. Hmmm? Q. How do we move beyond the sense of lack? Even when we recognize it, we don’t feel it.

A. You consciously add what is missing. If you feel you lack masculinity, for example, you add it - consciously. You fake it as if you already have it. Let’s say you feel you lack conviction - then you add that quality to yourself. You don’t wait for someone else to give it to you, or for it to miraculously appear one day. You create it. You set goals and commit to achieving them, even if it’s not your nature and feels completely artificial. You do it because you want that quality to grow within you. You focus on it, and soon enough, you won’t need to fake it anymore. You will make it. So, to sum up this talk, it goes through four phases: A. You choose to develop that inner balance. B. You observe, honestly. C. You balance, whatever you feel you lack - add it to your life. And then, D. It’s all about realizing that you are much bigger than the I that wants to achieve anything. That I that wants, dissolves. If you want to grow together with your partner, here is a wonderful meditation that can help balance these forces between you two as a greater vessel. Enough for today. Part IV

Merge with Life Merge with Life As we embark on the final part of our journey, Merge with Life, we delve into the profound and transformative aspects of spiritual awakening. This stage of our evolution is defined by the melting of the ego, the dissolution of separateness. As it dissolves, we become more intimately involved with life, leading to a complete tantric union. The two are now revealed to be one.

As we move through the stages of releasing suffering, transcending fear, and embracing life with love, we arrive at the final crescendo of the spiritual journey - a complete and natural merging with life itself. This ultimate stage is not a dramatic climax but a gentle, inevitable unfolding - the point where the seeker and the path become one, where life and spirit flow seamlessly together. Having shed the burdens of pain and anxiety, we no longer stand apart from life, analyzing or resisting it. Instead, we dissolve into it. Here, the boundaries between self and the world, between the inner and outer, disappear. Life is no longer something we experience or endure - it is something we are.

In Part IV, we explore this profound realization that the spiritual journey was never about reaching a distant goal, but about peeling away the layers that kept us from realizing we were always one with life, always whole. This union with life is not passive - it is vibrant and alive with creativity, connection, and purpose. The culmination of the spiritual journey is the return to our natural state of being where we move with the flow of existence in harmony, peace, and joy, fully aware of our place in the vast web of creation.

The longing for enlightenment becomes our last desire. The exploration of different spiritual paths, each offering unique ways to help us better understand ourselves and the universe, helps shape our spiritual journey. The different possible paths touch on two key ideas. First, the spiritual journey isn’t usually a linear process. It can feel like a cycle of progress and setbacks. There are many ways to reveal inner freedom and the invitation is to expand our consciousness and break free from false identities. Second, we can’t eliminate the ego, but through awareness and observation we can reduce its hold on us until grace wakes us up to self-realization. We will look at how life’s natural rhythm, the pulse of life, involves both forgetting and remembering. The key is to avoid judging ourselves when we stumble, and instead, gently bring ourselves back to the present moment. Using the basic principles of physics as a metaphor, this section explains how reducing our resistance to reality lets more life energy flow through us, opening us up spiritually.

Further along, we see how a guru offers wisdom, support, and direction to help us through the complexities of our spiritual journey. Having a guru on our path encourages us to reflect on the deep, hidden truths of existence, the mysteries of life that lie beneath our everyday experiences. Through our guru, we are able to explore the nature of unconditional love; the limitless, selfless love that transcends all conditions. This type of love is key to spiritual awakening, fostering a deep sense of unity with all beings. There are a variety of spiritual traditions and practices out there. By understanding the diversity of spiritual paths, we can find the one that resonates most deeply with our own journey. Once chosen we can settle into our home of silence. In silence and stillness, we can find peace, clarity, and a stronger connection to our true selves. As we move through these topics, we are encouraged to open our hearts and minds to the endless possibilities for spiritual growth. Let’s embrace this journey with love, curiosity, and a deep sense of connection to the flow of life.

The Last Desire White Path Meeting September, 2021 Q. Where does aspiration or desire fit on the spiritual path? If suffering is born and raised in the gap between what is and what I believe it should have been, then if I aspire for something that doesn’t exist, am I suffering? A. You tell me… If you are sitting on the fence, and you believe that only after something happens, you’ll be happy, fulfilled, enlightened, then yes, you are suffering. Two forces drive us in life, and on the spiritual path in particular. There’s the force that brings us closer and the force that pushes away - the feminine force and the masculine force. These two forces govern the entire universe and also govern our path. The force that brings us closer helps us contain, accept, and love what is. It’s the energy of Byron Katie. The force that pushes away, seeks for more, aims for more, constantly looks forward and asks, What’s the next step? Desiring more and aspiring for more is excellent. It means we’re alive and driven by the masculine force. That’s the spirit of Jeido Krishnamurti.

Q. Yaron, the last desire you were talking about, is that the thirst you mentioned? A. Yes. As we become more refined, this thirst has clearer facets. At first, this thirst almost automatically has the face of an unfulfilled promise from life. We believe there is something in life that we deserve but have not yet received: a spouse, a car, money, status, recognition, and relationships. There is some unfulfilled promise in life, so we continue to search for it there, in life, in the material world, in the world of phenomena. Then we understand it’s not there, so we search for meaning inwardly within spirituality itself. Many times, we stop too early and get stuck in material spirituality, whether it’s religion or some kind of comforting spirituality, feel-good spirituality, psychological spirituality, or some spiritual path that is essentially a religion disguised as a spiritual path. These disguised religions frame us within what is permitted and forbidden, what is right and wrong, why we are better than others, etc.

Eventually, after exhausting the search and remaining frustrated, the attention turns and becomes focused on the seeker himself, not the search, and this becomes the most important thing in life. You want to discover the truth behind the question Who am I? and you don’t mind dying for this search. It becomes more important than anything else. Any prior idea you had, no matter how noble and exalted, does not stand in competition with the yearning for the truth. The consciousness becomes sharp like a laser. That’s what interests you, that’s what you want, and then, miraculously, the desire disappears. Then, God willing, the I disappears. It happens on its own. It’s not something you can force. Let Go of the Drama of Sacrifice Q. I am asking whether I am willing to ‘sacrifice’ who I am today for the sake of who I will become. Is that essentially what you mean? A. The term ‘sacrifice’ carries a sense of violence. Q. Yes, that’s why I said ‘sacrifice’ in quotes. Am I willing to let go of who I am today for the sake of who I will become, for who I want to be?

A. Let go of the drama of the I that sacrifices. That I is an illusion. During our conversations I have described the entire map to you. Do not judge yourself whether you find yourself far behind on the path or even just taking the first steps on it. It’s not a competition. There are no should or should-nots. I simply described the whole map, from the beginning to the end - or more accurately, from the beginning to the Now. I left the end a bit vague because, after all, we must respect the mystery. If you find yourself somewhere between these two ends of the journey, that’s fine. Just know that you’re there and ask yourself do I want to continue and how much further am I willing to go? Everything is fine. There is nothing wrong. Everything is fine.

Q. When this becomes the most important thing it inevitably brings thoughts of the price to be paid, even sacrifice. If it’s the most important, then it’s not just that I give up things that are important to me in favor of this, but maybe I also give up people around me, family and friends, because this is more important. Buddha, on his way to enlightenment, sacrificed his wife and son, causing great suffering to those around him whom he loved. That’s the price. A. Yes, true. That’s the story of Buddha. It’s not necessarily the only story one can tell, but it’s the Buddha’s story. We inevitably cause pain to those around us. It’s part of our experience in the material world. The encounter with the material world inherently involves both pain and pleasure. If you believe you can go through life without experiencing pain for yourself or others, I must respectfully disagree with you. This is what is known as Samsara - life’s inherent friction. I wouldn’t necessarily call it suffering - rather, it is pain. This friction inevitably results in pain.

It’s not the only possibility, and it could be that the process of letting go of your attachments and ideas about who you are might show no outward change. No one would know you are going through a process because this change is not a derivative of the material world. It’s not related to the DOING. The DOING can remain the same. Tomorrow morning, you get up, brush your teeth, go to work, do what you need to do, etc. The change is related to the realm of BEING. The context changes. The context changes irreversibly, but the DOING doesn’t necessarily need to change. The one asking the question, What am I going to lose here? is the ego that builds its identity around achievements and the material gain and loss it has managed to gather around itself. This attachment to the material builds walls between me and life, creating an illusion of a protected comfort zone within which you are in ‘control’. All of this is at the level of the ego. If the ego stops being the most important thing, this question becomes irrelevant. Q. But after all, it is the ego that leads us on this whole journey.

A. Correct. Up until the statement I want to be free. That’s the last desire. All other desires have already been shed. Q. So if I already want to be free and I know that this path I take will lead me to freedom, will I miss the point? A. Not necessarily. It’s a natural part of the process. There are a few individuals who have experienced full awakening spontaneously. It happens. History documents several such cases. Some people have encountered enlightenment unexpectedly, a sudden clash with Awakening. For some, this spontaneous enlightenment was difficult to process because the vessel  - meaning the body or mind - was not fully prepared. As a result, it took time for the awakened consciousness to integrate within the human body and its persona.

Most of us will not ‘win this lottery’ in that sense. Most of us, to discover ourselves as the spring, will surrender to the process. Naturally, we gradually shed preconceived ideas about what I need, what I want, and what I’ll get out of it, and are left with - I want to be free. I want to discover the meaning of who I am. This I want will take us to the edge of the cliff, where we then release even that last desire. There, the question turns into a statement: Thy Will Be Done. Different Possible Paths White Path Meeting December, 2023 Q. Regarding your description of a very structured process, a series of graduated steps that need to be taken, with a final result at the end. Is it always like this? Can’t there be a situation where you sometimes go back, sometimes forward? That’s one question. The second question is - you talk about the experience of the phenomenal world, ego included. When speaking about this inner silence, this infinity that we are trying to identify with, how do we know our ego is not deceiving us or playing tricks with us?

A. Let’s start with the first one. Remember the second question. I’ve already forgotten. The first one… what was the first? Q. We talked about the process - is it like a process, like a ladder you can climb up and down, or a circle with an ever-growing diameter, where you experience more and more depth? For me, it feels more cyclic. A. Yes. Don’t be alarmed if the silence is experienced and disappears, experienced and disappears, and then we seek it out, longing to experience it again. This is part of the pulse of life - we forget and remember, forget and remember. That’s okay. It means the heart is still beating. As long as you are alive you will continue to be invited to walk the path. There’s no ‘should’ here.

What I did was describe the entire map to you. There are countless ways for people to navigate this map. You can choose a structured path with clear signposts about what is right and wrong, like a religion or a spiritual tradition. Or you can wander this space alone and try to create your own path, which is also fine. Some people get lost, walk for a week, or a year, or ten years, and find they return to the starting point. Others describe it like some sort of spiral or coil. It seems as if they’re treading the same spot in two dimensions, but in three dimensions they’ve made some upward progress.  There are many ways and paths. What interests us is whether, along the way, we have added more degrees of freedom to our encounter with life.

We feel less constrained by preconceived ideas, by life itself, and less constrained by false identifications and our consciousness expands wider and wider. Again, I’m talking about the realm of BEING, not DOING. I’m not talking about a vacation. I’m talking about inner freedom. Don’t confuse the two. It’s not about doing whatever you want, however, you want, whenever you want, to whomever you want - that’s anarchy, not freedom. There are countless ways to climb this mountain. What matters is that the view changes as you climb and consciousness matures. What was the second question? The Ego is Tricky Q. How do I know I’m not deceiving myself? How do I know I’m not fooling myself? How do I know my ego isn’t playing a new, more dangerous game with me?

A. The ego is indeed a very sophisticated creature with cunning ways to hide and try to convince us. It steps aside, makes room, and seemingly agrees to surrender. But the ego cannot commit suicide, we need to understand that. As long as there is an I want, the ego is active, even if this I want is unimportant. Even if it’s the last remaining I want. As long as there is an I that wants, the ego is talking. The invitation here is not to try to kill the ego. It’s like Baron Munchausen trying to pull himself out of the swamp by pulling his own hair. Just be aware. This is a matter of awareness. Just be aware and conscious of how the ego works, manages, tries to hide, tries to manipulate reality, and manipulates the experience. It tries to create gain and avoid loss for you. This will always be a task of awareness. And who is aware? It’s not the ego. Awareness itself is aware. It is aware of how the ego works. It is aware of the power of the ego, the ego’s game. Mere observation is enough. Nothing more is needed. The Pulse of Life White Path Meeting August, 2023

Q. It’s interesting because when I listen to the meetings, I understand. I can see what you’re talking about as if it’s inner wisdom. But at times when I’m very tense, I simply lose it. Also, because I have this inner noise that exaggerates things, something takes it to extremes, and it always manages to confuse me anew, and I get swept up in the story. A. So what to do? Q. Aren’t you the teacher? I try to remind myself again and again. Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn’t. It feels like trying to calm someplace inside me without possessing any real experience that everything is okay. A. So you’re lying to yourself about everything being okay? Q. Something like that...

A. Okay. First of all, remember that when we forget and then remember, that’s already halfway to remembering. If we find ourselves getting swept up in the drama, it means we’ve momentarily stepped out of the drama to realize it, you see? At this point, it’s important not to add fuel to the fire with self-criticism and self-judgment, believing things like Oh, this is happening to me again. I should have known better by now. I should understand after all the processes I’ve been through. I’m lost and it’ll never go well for me. and I’m not good enough. Blah blah blah… Q. This is where I fall every time. A. No, don’t do that because then you are deepening the hole you’ve dug for yourself. This is entirely unnecessary. Forgetting and then remembering is what I call the ‘pulse of life.’ Don’t wait for a moment when you’ll stop forgetting because that might be the time to prepare for the Angel Gabriel. As long as the monitor works and there are peaks and valleys you can rest assured it is completely natural, completely human.

Don’t judge yourself as if it’s a failure just because you’ve momentarily forgotten. Calmly and gently bring yourself back to this moment and remind yourself of what’s more important to you. All of this drama will be resolved on the day when this moment becomes more attractive to you. Drama has tremendous pulling power and we’re addicted to the thrill. It doesn’t matter if the thrill is pleasurable or not, if it translates to a pleasant experience or not, as long as there’s this thrill. I’m terribly, terribly angry and vehemently opposing and I’m fiercely defending my position in the name of the holy justice I believe in. There’s something very addictive about this thrill. It becomes a kind of taste for life. When the alternative looks maybe a bit... Q. Mellow?

A. Mellow, yes, something flat... The day the drama becomes less attractive to me than opening my heart to this moment, that’s the day you’ll stop running away, avoiding. Once this happens, you know that you’re still alive, everything is okay, and you are not alone there. You are together with all of humanity. You remind yourself again and again about what’s more important. What’s more important for you? To be right? To stick to my principles, morals, preconceived ideas, and opinions about what should have been? Or do you prefer to love what is as it is happening? Between Spirituality and Electricity

Earlier we spoke about Ohm’s law-the first principle in the study of electricity. It states that voltage equals resistance times current (V=RI). Do you remember why it’s relevant? The potential exists in the voltage between positive and negative, in the voltage between masculine and feminine, and in the voltage between question and answer. The more this potential encounters resistance, the less of life’s current can pass through this conductor.
