If you are that conductor, your role is to ensure that the level of internal resistance within you diminishes to become a Superconductor. Do you know what a Super Conductor is? Its resistance tends towards zero. In nature, there’s no such thing. It’s theoretical in the material world.

However, in the spiritual world, it’s practical. You become hollow and empty. Hollow and empty. Hollow and empty of any preconceived ideas about what should be, of any inherent resistance you have to reality as it appears, as it reveals itself. And as your resistance diminishes, this potential has more opportunity to pass more movement, more life current, more prana, through you. It’s amazing how it works in life just as it does in electrical theory. It’s another aspect of the same thing. We are all made of atoms and the same electricity passes through us. The next time you encounter an opportunity where you find inherent resistance within you to what IS, you’ll remember this and choose to become a Super Conductor. Why have a Guru on the Path? White Path Meeting August, 2023

We are here tonight to use this opportunity to grow by sharing our questions - anything related to your spiritual path, your life, your ambitions, your relationships, and anything that you feel holds you back or still needs to be resolved. Now is the opportunity. So, who wants to be the first one to jump into the waters? (Silence….) Let me tell you a story. Back in 1880, in the southern part of India, a child was born into a family of Brahmins. This child, however, had no interest in religion or religious studies. He was more concerned with excelling in sports. Then something profound and life-changing happened to him at the age of 16. He spontaneously came to realize that he was about to die, and that realization shook him to the core of his being. But instead of contracting or rejecting this experience, he lay on the floor and wholeheartedly welcomed it, ready to die.

He didn't die, but his personality and perspective on life were completely transformed. When his uncle returned from a business trip and told him about a place called Arunachala, a sacred mountain in Tamil Nadu, the young man immediately knew he needed to go there. This was his destiny. Try to remember what you were doing at the age of 16. This young man packed his bag, left his family (never to return), took a train, and after a few days, arrived at the sacred Arunachala Mountain. He sat there in silence for four years. But it was not enough for him. After that extended period of self-observation, he climbed the mountain, found a cave, and sat in silence in that cave for another seven years.

People started to gather. The rumor about this special person sitting in the cave spread. People came to sit in front of him in silence, reporting life-changing experiences, just by his presence. Finally, when he woke up from that period and started grounding himself back into the physical reality of his body, he began communicating with his disciples. He found it difficult to explain the essence of his experience in words. So, he said, “Whatever I’m saying, this is just for the sake of those who don’t understand the silence, because my teaching can only be found in silence.” He said, “At the end of any answer given to any question, there is just silence.” This man was called Ramana Maharishi. If you haven’t heard of him, I strongly recommend you look him up on YouTube and read his books. They are quite fantastic. If you prefer, we can just sit here in silence. This also is quite remarkable. Unless, of course, you have a question you want to ask.

Q. I am disillusioned by the unholy practices of some Gurus. How can I separate the good aspects of their teachings from the harm they have done? A. That’s a really good question. What is the role of a Guru? What is their role on the spiritual path? A Guru is a source of light that can help illuminate your path and guide your way. A Guru is like a window that allows the light to penetrate your home and fill your house with brightness. A relationship with a Guru is unlike any other relationship because it offers a reflection of yourself that is pure and not tinted with the other person’s preconceptions about you. It is free of judgment and need. There is only one ego at play in the relationship between you and your Guru - your ego. In that sense, the relationship with a Guru is very unique. If you are truly sincere in your quest for self-liberation, you eagerly seek such a relationship so your ego can become completely clear to you. Q. How do you find the right Guru for you?

A. The criteria to use in verifying that the Guru you choose is the right one for you is found in the element of freedom. Ask yourself if, through the relationship with your Guru, you feel more or less free. Do you feel that you are expanding and discovering more and more degrees of freedom in your life and in the way you perceive life? Or do you feel that your freedom is contracting, and you are more bound by that relationship? Pick one Guru and learn from them. If you reach a point where you feel that the relationship binds you and the Guru is telling you what to do and what not to do, then it is time to find a new Guru. Gurus are not there to tell you what to do. A Guru is not a Priest or a Rabbi. Spirituality is not a religion. The true Guru is never concerned about what you do or do not do. They are concerned with inspiring you to continually grow towards self-liberation.

What you do with that inspiration is your own business. It has nothing to do with the Guru. If the Guru starts telling you to do this and refrain from doing that, and you feel more and more constrained, then you know it is time to move forward. Do you understand what I’m saying? A Successful Life Q. Thank you for that story. The theme of silence has been coming up in my life. I entered the new year pondering this quote by Frank Ocean: “Do your work in silence. Let success be your noise.” A. Good. Or, if you can’t do that, at least redefine what success is. What is a successful practice? How do you know that you have succeeded? I recommend redefining what success is. Instead of trying to define success by the results, redefine success by the measure of how much you were able to open your heart and do whatever you are doing, 100%.

If you’re doing 95%, you almost succeeded, but if you do whatever you choose to do and you do it 100%, wholeheartedly, (or as my mantra goes - with a whole heart and a willing soul) you have succeeded already, regardless of the end result. You can offer the result to the divine. The divine will manifest your 100% into a specific result. That’s it. If you want to summarize the sum of my teaching, do so in four words: With a Whole Heart and a Willing Soul. I didn’t invent these words. They are written in the Bible when King David brought his son, Solomon, to the holy temple. There, in front of all the high priests and the people of Israel, he said, “And thou, my son, know the God of thy father, and serve him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for every heart desire God.” (1 Chronicles 20:9) Q. Being in a healthy mental state to help others on the path, wholeheartedly, is challenging for me at times.

A. To the people who walk on the path that I am leading called the White Path, I repeat the essence of everything we learn and practice. The ultimate goal of all our sadhana, our gurus, and their teachings is to be able to experience life with a whole heart and a willing soul. That’s it. If you ever wondered why spirituality is there and what the point is of spiritual practice, this is the point. This is the bottom line of all bottom lines. Open your heart to include everything - any experience, pleasant or unpleasant, the divine as well as the mundane. Open your heart to that. Open your heart to the isness of things.

When are you unable to do that? When are you unable to fully experience, to fully embrace the present moment? When, instead of being in your heart, you are stuck in your head, trying to define and tag your experience. Usually, that inevitably leads to some sort of struggle with reality. Either because reality is ‘bad’ according to the intellect, so you are manipulating it to avoid or reject it, or because reality is ‘good’ according to your intellect, and now you’re trying to hold on to it and make sure it doesn’t change, which never happens. It always changes. So, when your attention goes from heart to head, your heart is closing. The whole spiritual journey is about moving 30 centimeters from head to heart. That’s it. Not too far, is it? 30 centimeters. Hmmm...? What do you say? Let’s go back to the question about the Guru and complete my answer. The presence of a Guru is so precious. So precious. Yes, you should always keep a watchful eye on using the criteria that I’ve shared. Make sure that you keep expanding and growing in your journey.

It’s crucial to keep expanding and growing in the presence of the Guru you have chosen. However, as long as you haven’t decided to leave that Guru and find someone else, my recommendation is to completely surrender. Surrender to the choice you made to follow that Guru, that teacher. Surrender is Key Surrender is the key factor in the success of your spiritual journey, and the presence of a master or a Guru can dramatically accelerate this process, especially if you are willing to surrender. I tell you, doubt holds you down. It nails you to the ground and doesn’t allow you to progress, to flow. You know the different kinds of doubt: You may doubt yourself, believing that you are not ready or not worthy. You might think you need something else - something more active, more concrete. You have many prerequisites and convince yourself that you are not ready. You may doubt the method, the teaching, or the practices that your Guru is teaching. I need something different, you might think. You may doubt the teacher, wondering, I’m not sure about him. Maybe he has some kind of secret agenda.

I tell you, burn those doubts. Know that your doubts are holding you back and preventing you from surrendering. How do you burn the doubt? Inquire, investigate, learn, ask people - do whatever you need to do. Make a decision - yes or no. It’s okay. Yes is good. No is also good. But that maybe, I’m not sure keeps you on the fence while life happens on either side. Do you see what I’m saying? You are not a part of life because you’re sitting on the fence, trying to make up your mind. Burn the doubt. Jump in and surrender to your choice and the consequences of that choice. Only then can you grow beyond your self-imposed doubts. In that sense, if you ever ask yourself what an awakened consciousness is, it can be described as a consciousness that has stopped doubting itself. It realizes It Is beyond doubt. So definitely, find a Guru and surrender. Surrender to the Guru. Finding the Right Guru Q. I understand what you’re saying about the Guru. How does one find one? Where to seek? A. Maybe you’ve already found one and just aren’t aware of it yet.

Observe how your heart feels in the presence of the potential Guru. Does your heart feel like yes, here’s my opportunity to open up and expand, or does your heart shrink? If you live in that blissful state and send an invitation to the universe saying Yes, I’m ready for a master in my life, he or she will show up. Don’t worry. They will find you. Keep your eyes open, maintain an inquisitive attitude, and keep the longing in you burning. The longing to come back, the longing for the truth - the rest will take care of itself.

Another criterion you might use is that a true master does not create an artificial gap between you and a better version of yourself. This happens far too often. They make a false promise that if you stick around, they can help you realize a better, more advanced version of yourself, which will enable you to access a ‘Greater Reality’ that, in your current state, you supposedly cannot enter. That ‘Promised Land’ is their bait. This creates a dependency between the masters and their disciples. My suggestion is to find a master who knows how to love you as you are and can inspire you to do the same. Another important criterion to use when searching for a Guru is that the Guru doesn’t need anything from you. A true Guru cannot need anything. He/she/it is already satisfied. They are the manifestation of satisfaction. You don’t need to prove yourself worthy. The Guru loves you as you are right now, not a future version of you.

How many couples do you know that stick together based on the belief that the partner can change? I know him, he can be better. He can change. That’s why I stay because I know we can improve. This is a recipe for disaster in any relationship. That’s not how it works with a true master. The master doesn’t need anything from you. If he starts telling you, ‘I need you to do this’ or ‘I need you to stop doing that,’ you should find somebody else. Run for the hills. The same goes for you, doesn’t it? The master is just a reminder of who you already are. So, if the master is not waiting for you to change, you shouldn’t wait for you to change either. Stop doubting yourself as you are, right now. The only thing standing between you and enlightenment is the idea that you’re not ready. That it’s not possible here and now, as you are. That some other/different version of you is waiting to be revealed - more mature, more evolved. Or whatever idea you keep about who you should be.

You already are. You Are That. You are that already. Complete. You are a perfect specimen of a complete and holistic being. And if there is an evolution going on, it’s only from one version of perfection to a wider version of perfection. That’s it. It’s not from a broken version of you to a fixed version of you. You’re not broken. There’s nothing to fix. If you cannot grow beyond self-doubt, then use the eyes of your master to do so. See yourself as pure consciousness through your master’s eyes. Something beautiful my grandmother taught me when I was a kid comes to mind. She said, “Have you ever noticed that in Hebrew when you want to say to someone that you like them, ‘I like you’ translates directly to ‘You find grace in my eyes.’?” That’s how we say ‘I like you’ in Hebrew. ‘You find grace in my eyes.’ Isn’t that beautiful?

So, if you cannot recognize that grace when you look in the mirror, find it in the eyes of your master and recognize that grace, which is you. You are that grace, and the master is just there to show that to you and reflect it back to you. This is who you already are. What do you say? The Mystery of Life White Path Meeting March, 2022 Q. Yaron, can you explain why people are waiting for a body?

A. Now we are diving into the depths of mysticism… it doesn’t matter. Everyone has their own set of beliefs. Somewhere inside, there is a memory (for some very obscure, for others more vivid) of the connection to a collective consciousness, to God, no matter what name is given to it, right? The connection to the abstract existed even before the material. This abstract has infinite faces and possible representations. All these possibilities live within the world, within the realm of the abstract. God Themself, 13.7 billion years ago (as the story goes) reached an evolutionary stage where they decided they wanted to experience themself in a material world, so they created matter and energy, and since then they’ve been experimenting with this thing called life in matter and energy, as matter and energy. That’s what we’re doing now within the body; experiencing in matter, as matter. Someone once asked if it’s reasonable that we as humans can hope for a divine experience. I tell you, it’s the opposite. We are divine beings now having a human experience.

Q. And people like us, who are on the spiritual path with all we learn from you, does that mean that at some point a person on this path will have to decide whether to come back here after death or to continue? A. This is less relevant. If we assume this is so, so what? What is relevant is that now, within the body, we have only one true choice. And this choice is whether to love, accept, and agree to live life as it unfolds in this moment, healthy or sick, happy or sad, pleasurable or painful, or, to reject and live within this contraction. The contraction of no, no, what’s here is not good enough, there needs to be something else. This is the only relevant choice. Everything else is stories. One of these stories is the story of Bodhisattva. Do you know the difference between Buddha and Bodhisattva? Q. That Bodhisattva waits for all people to achieve liberation and only then can he rest?

A. Not just people - all souls. All consciousnesses When the collective consciousness itself will stop suffering, then he will be free to enjoy the Garden of Eden. He dedicates all of his existence to helping souls awaken and stop suffering. You can adopt this story. Q. So does that mean such a person will keep coming back here in more and more incarnations until all consciousness… That’s the idea? A. There is such a story… Q. Is that a smile of skepticism or a knowing smile? A. Mysterious. The most meaningful, beautiful, and real things in life don’t require an explanation. They just bask in the mystery. If we already know it, somehow it loses its charm, right? Like love. If we could fully explain it scientifically and artificially create it, it wouldn’t be so interesting anymore. There needs to be a mystery and our willingness to surrender to that mystery, knowing full well we can’t or don’t want to solve it. Different Types of Spirituality White Path Meeting October, 2022

Q. Me and spirituality - what’s the deal with that? What kind of relationship system exists there? And if it can be defined to make it more meaningful and effective for me, how? A. To approach this question, the first thing we need to ask is ‘What is spirituality?’ This question belongs to the family of the leading questions. What’s special about the family of the leading questions is that they lead us to the maturity of an expanded consciousness. These questions don’t have one definite, clear-cut answer and they’re not asked to get one definite, clear-cut answer. The answer isn’t the issue. The issue is that some of us choose to make the effort to keep asking the question, time and time again. And as we’ve said, the tension between the question and the answer is what encourages the evolution of consciousness. The leading questions, those for which there will never be one final answer, are very special. Anyone who hasn’t started asking leading questions yet is simply still waiting to awaken, like an egg being incubated.

What is spirituality? I can offer a suggestion. The answer isn’t necessarily the correct or final answer, but it can help us continue the discussion. Spirituality is a multidimensional space that invites and encourages the development of consciousness. Within this space, consciousness has the opportunity to grow beyond the known and familiar, beyond the comfortable, beyond the safe, finite, and clear-cut answers towards the mystery, the unknown. Developing consciousness is constantly engaged in curiosity; revealing the new and exposing truths untainted by preconceived concepts. It allows itself to renew through endless discovery. Spirituality is an invitation. An invitation that our consciousness responds to and engages in in this process of removing layers, exposing the new and always fresh truth. Naturally, the next questions are: Who does it suit? Who joins such a process? Who responds to it and why? Why respond to it at all?

In this regard, there are several very distinct groups of people who join. In general, if we look at human nature, each of us has some kind of thirst, something we can’t formulate into words. It’s the sense that ‘something is missing.’ Usually, this thirst isn’t conscious. It’s not something you put a name to. It’s something that sits there behind the mind and doesn’t allow rest. This thirst drives us to a process of searching trying to quench it. This process of searching can be divided into three different evolutionary levels. Using the Realm of Phenomena to Try to Quench the Thirst

The first evolutionary level usually starts with trying to fill the void. We work to calm this thirst through experiences in the material world. We go into the realm of phenomena and try to fill this experience of absence. We try to achieve more satisfying, comforting experiences. It can be through relationships, extreme sports, collecting piles of money or status or honor or fame or whatever... We go into the world of phenomena and try to create a way to fulfill our lives with some gratification. This usually doesn’t create a solution, and even if it does, the solution is very momentary. What succeeded in filling me yesterday no longer fills me today. I need more than that. This search to fill the thirst and absence through the world of phenomena reveals itself as hopeless in the end. The Search for Meaning Next, we come to the second evolutionary stage of the search, which isn’t necessarily conscious. Many times, it’s born from our recognition of the hopeless nature of trying to find nourishment or find revival from the world of phenomena which leads us to the search for meaning.

Some people reach this second stage when they pass the first stage very quickly. These are usually people who come into this world more mature so they are less likely to seek fulfillment from external sources for too long. Some people never reach the second stage and continue to demand fulfillment from the outside through the world of phenomena until their last day. However it’s reached, the second evolutionary stage is the stage where we search for meaning, and even here it’s possible to divide it into all sorts of sub-groups. The first place that people typically seek this meaning is through the framework they were born into. I was born Jewish and Israeli so I’ll look for meaning in my religion and culture. Some people will stay here all their lives and are satisfied with the answers they find in their religion and culture. Other people continue the process of deeper exploration into what can be called religious spirituality.

These organizations call themselves spiritual but they operate within a framework of religion with all the ceremonies, attire, scriptures, and internal hierarchy usually associated with religion. People use religious spirituality to create an identity for themselves based on the features of their chosen path and its unique characteristics. Religious spirituality creates many claims of right and wrong, of permissible and forbidden, of what should and shouldn’t be done. It’s another type of religion with a spiritual cover.

The second kind of spirituality can be called feel-good spirituality. It is a spirituality that nurtures the feeling of feeling good, which has a lot of charm. People who have been battered by life and are frustrated by the endless search for recognition, and fulfillment, seek answers here. They search for love and joy here, at least superficially. Through the experience of feeling good, people believe they are approaching fulfillment or solving this inner thirst. In this type of spirituality, people often use chemical substances to encourage this experience of feeling good. The point here is that feeling good becomes a kind of addiction. Feel Good found at the level of experience becomes another trap because no matter how deeply we penetrate this experience, in the end, Feel Bad will always await us. Feel Good and Feel Bad are two sides of the same coin. They are the opposite sides of the same scale. We can not be free in such a journey that’s constantly focused on feeling good, pleasant, and comfortable.

The third kind of spiritual experience can be called psychological spirituality. This is a spirituality that tries to create a solution through psychological analysis of ourselves. It is what used to be called positive thinking. At the intellectual level, new patterns of thought are created through which we can encounter life more safely and less painfully. Finally, there is what’s called Pure Spirituality. Pure spirituality has some very clear characteristics to distinguish it from the other types of spirituality we’ve talked about so far.

The first thing is that pure spirituality does not try to quench thirst through the world of phenomena because our thirst does not stem from the lack of something related to the world of phenomena. This must be completely clear. We grow towards a state where we no longer have the desire for something outside of us; not power, not money, not politics or fame. No material temptation can buy us anymore. What used to throw us up and down within the world of phenomena does not have the same effect on us anymore. We can now meet the realm of phenomena with unbounded peace. Secondly, those who have realized such a spiritual level cannot want to benefit from you. They cannot want anything for themselves. They don’t need your money, your dedication, or your approval. They do not ask you for anything. They don’t need anything from you. Thirdly, speech becomes pure and devoid of violence or agenda. No lies or saying what is politically correct just to please. Even the Doing becomes pure. The doing is not faked and there is no motivation to behave pompously to create an impression or to please.

Lastly, a spiritual teacher or someone who operates from pure spirituality doesn’t need you to come back to them again and again. They will also simplify the experience of pure spirituality for you so that it becomes accessible to you. I don’t know if you’ve encountered this, but there are many teachers, consciously or unconsciously, who mystify spirituality, creating some sort of distance between you and the truth. Pure spirituality doesn’t do that. On the contrary, it makes spiritual development something very simple and accessible. These are the different types of spirituality that we encounter in the second stage of our development, the stage where we are seeking meaning. This is an invitation for us to examine where we are within this scale of spiritual development. Not the Object of Observation but the Observer

Finally, there’s the third stage where nothing we’ve said so far holds any more weight than the other; neither the external search nor the search for meaning through different spiritual frameworks. This is the stage where we remind ourselves of the sentence we said to ourselves at the beginning of the journey - nothing in the world of phenomena, nothing external, can provide a solution, and the only source to which we truly turn, the only source to which we truly attend, is the silence found behind the experience. As we found in our meditation at the beginning of the meeting, the one experiencing is not the experience itself. It’s not the words. It’s not the ideas. It’s certainly not the experiences. At this point in development, we lose interest. We lose connection with everything we believe we need to find a solution to this thirst and all our soul’s effort is focused solely on the essence of the SELF. We are entirely enlisted to expose only that. The only thing that is of interest to us, is to know oneself as the source, to know oneself as the essence.

When the spring becomes aware of itself, it can no longer be thirsty. What do we get from this? The answer is… nothing. This realization is crucial. I’m aware that it looks like there’s an inconsistency here because choices based on what do I get from this? are how we’re conditioned to operate in the world. From the day we remember ourselves, our choices are guided by what do/could I get from this? and now here comes the invitation to embark on a journey where we already know that nothing comes out of it. So why bother? Are we crazy? You might believe that yes, yes, he says nothing comes out of it, but I do get a lot out of it... my life is improving, I’m less entangled with reality, and my relationships are better. However, the spiritual path does not promise us anything. On the contrary, the quality of development on the spiritual path is a quality of subtraction, not addition. We cleanse ourselves, purify ourselves, shed ideas, and relinquish what’s called in Sanskrit ‘maya’ - illusions about who we are and for what reason we are here.

With every layer we shed, more and more of the truth regarding the question Who am I? is revealed until there’s nothing left to shed, nothing left to let go of. There’s only awareness gripping onto nothing. There’s emptiness devoid of context. There is no more context. We can not say, I am in relation to this, I am compared to that because we’ve relinquished all our contexts, all our preconceived ideas. All of our attention continues to be focused solely on the question who am I? Who am I without all these contexts? Without all the mistaken identifications? Like a laser, it penetrates through the realm of all phenomena. Such a process cannot benefit the I because, towards its end, there is no longer any I asking the question Who am I?

If no separate and distinct self ascribes identity to itself in relation to something, then it certainly doesn’t have a backpack filled with various benefits either. We embark on a journey where we are going to lose, not gain. We lose everything, including all the spiritual ‘achievements’ we have managed to gather over the years, never mind all the material achievements. Through awakening, we die. Just as people die and leave this world with nothing, leaving all their possessions to those who come after them. Most of these ‘possessions’ vanish into the depths of oblivion - honor, status, fame. In this sense, there is a similarity between awakening and death. An awakened consciousness no longer clings to any of these supports to create an illusion of stability, and thus the consciousness can be free. Q. Still, isn’t this done to improve life, to achieve peace or better control, or to get a better response to situations that happen to us? If it’s not really to achieve anything, then why do it?

A. Great question! It’s an excellent, honest, and brave question, and it’s important to ask it. I would even say that without asking it, it’s almost impossible to continue digging into this inquiry until one of two things happens - you reach the water or you give up, whichever comes first. If you reach the water, you stop being thirsty, but as you dive into the water, the I disappears. The I, the one who did, the one who arrived, that I disappears. It becomes the water. At that point the question ‘why do it?’ reveals itself as irrelevant. The only answer you could give yourself would be I have no alternative but… Q. So you want to reach the water? You still want something.

A. That’s the last desire. I want to reach the water. I want to be free. I want to be enlightened. I want… It doesn’t matter what name you give it. I want to know who I am beyond all false identifications. This is the last I that wants or the last desire of the I. And along the way, even that last desire will disappear, and then the I who wanted and needed will also disappear. Or we give up. I’ve always said that if someone prefers to give up rather than continue digging, then they should give up completely, not halfway. If you give up, do it all the way. There is a quality of freedom in this. Within despair, there is a quality of freedom because we lose the hope that something else will happen, and then we are much more available to dissolve into what already is. When you despair, you stop resisting, and then you can merge. Some people’s solution is despair. At the bottom of the pit of despair, the truth awaits. Silence is My Home White Path Meeting March, 2023

Hello everyone, welcome to this meeting of the White Path. This is our weekly opportunity to lay down all the questions, pains, doubts and everything you feel is still unresolved and stands between you and a free consciousness. So, who wants to be the first to jump into the water? (Extended period of silence...) Q. Yaron, I want to ask you something. A. Yes. Q. Does this silence embarrass you? A. No, this is my home. Q. In these silences, I feel discomfort. If you don't feel that way, I can also feel comfortable.

A. A free consciousness feels comfortable in any situation, whether there is noise or silence. It doesn’t seek comfort in the experience. It is the embodiment of comfort itself. Within this comfort, experiences happen, not the other way around. Otherwise, we continue to categorize experiences, accepting only those in which we feel comfortable. What we don’t feel comfortable with, we try to manipulate or escape from. There’s no freedom in that. Moreover, as long as silence threatens us, it means the day has not yet come when silence is more attractive than noise. As we’ve already said, this is the clear sign of the awakening of consciousness: The day when silence becomes more appealing than noise. Both figuratively and literally. Sometimes before silence retreats, people experience a kind of threat and fear where they think I'm not going to talk for a few days? That seems crazy to me. Then the days pass, and the invitation to resume speaking arrives, and those same people don't want to go back to the noise. They are wrapped in silence. Silence becomes home.

Q. I feel the embarrassment is within me as a participant. When we wait for someone to be the first one to break the silence and ask a question, there is some obligation or expectation to share. However, I feel comfortable with the silence. A. Yes. As a student on the path, this invitation to ask is the potential. The realization of the potential is the question. And then, through the question and investigation, the path to a certain kind of answer allows growth to occur. That’s why a meeting of this kind is so valuable because it focuses on the developmental potential hidden within each of us. On the one hand, you don’t need to force questions artificially just because there’s silence and you feel the need to fill it with noise. On the other hand, don’t censor yourself or repress questions because you are afraid you might sound foolish, or you worry about what people will think of you. This is your opportunity to shine through the longing for truth, to grow and develop. Shedding off Useless Baggage

There is another secret hidden here. When you ask the question, the very fact that you asked the question already takes a burden off you. You lay the question down as an offering to the Gods. The answer matters less. It doesn’t matter what the answer is. What matters is that you got rid of the question. This allows for some space to open up within you and allows you to experience the silence within. A precise answer will help you delve deeper into that silence. But just asking already allows you to be more available. In my personal experience, this has happened to me many times with my teacher. I came wrapped in fateful questions about my private life, the nature of consciousness, the essence of life, etc. The moment I sat in front of him, these questions evaporated completely, and lost all interest or meaning. All that was left was a smile of love and gratitude. That’s all. If we are enveloped in love and gratitude then we can be silent until the end of this meeting, there’s no problem with that. But if not, that’s also fine. This is the opportunity to ask.

Q. And how do you explain that when you stood before him, all your questions suddenly disappeared? A. Every question is an expression of internal restlessness. There was restlessness within me and I believed that the answer to the question would bring me peace, or at least bring me one step closer to it. Until I got an answer, there would be no peace. But when you sit in front of the teacher, you are enveloped in peace and the need for questions disappears. The questions lose their urgency because you are already there. The question is like a carriage meant to take you to peace, but if you are already there, what need is there for the question? Q. I understand that at the end of the journey we reach peace. What I wanted to ask is, what is the connection between love and peace? A. First of all, let's start with your words. My recommendation is to give up the notion that this can be achieved at the end of the journey, at the end of the process. Q. I don’t understand what you mean.

A. We have this idea that we have a path to travel, a process to complete. We have some learning to do, and some layers to shed. Each person has their ideas about what they need to do. Only after that happens, at the end of the process, at the end of the journey, will it be revealed. Give up the notion that there is a path that needs to be completed, and only at its end will it be revealed. No, that is not the truth. Nowhere to go, nothing to do…You have already arrived. Actually, you never left. Now wake up. Q. So what is there? A. There is this moment. God is waiting for you here. Now. Q. What is the moment? It’s not clear.

A. This moment is reality, the truth. God is waiting here and now. You will discover God the moment you stop looking for the divine somewhere else or at some other time. Do you understand? We are constantly preoccupied with what will happen at the end of the journey and we miss the reality where everything we hoped for is already happening. Everything we longed for is already occurring. It already exists. But we are busy waiting and expecting something else to happen. A whole life of missing out. Q. It exists, but the very search creates a state where we don't find it. A. Correct. A free consciousness does not search. It rests within what is, not within what isn't. Within what is, it finds everything we ever hoped for. Everything else is just ideas about fictitious realities that may or may not happen, each from their perspective. That's the first thing.

Now about peace and love. I would say these are two qualities that complement each other through unity. Love is the feminine aspect and peace or silence is the masculine aspect of the same thing. These are two qualities that express the same thing from a complementary angle. Peace is not just the absence of noise. Peace is the background, the silence that exists before every occurrence. Meditation at the beginning of each meeting directs us to this. Silence is the unrealized potential of reality. Everything already exists in silence before there is any occurrence. Love manifests it into a reality for us to experience. Q. For there to be peace, must there be noise?

A. No. Sometimes there is noise, and sometimes it is quiet in our physical reality. It's easier to connect to the silence when there is no noise because then there are fewer distractions, but it’s not related to direct experience. Whether it is noisy or quiet outside, the silence is not disturbed. Silence is the masculine aspect of life. Masculinity is that all allowing space, in which reality is manifested. Love is the feminine aspect.

Recognize that within the silence there is the potential for everything. Think of the singularity point that was there a second before the Big Bang. All the matter and energy were concentrated in a theoretical point somewhere in this universe. All the potential was already there. That is the silence. It has an energy of explosion, potential that is not yet realized. Love is the realization of this potential, creativity, enthusiasm, the joy of life, the creation that envelops everything and brings everything into one unity. Love and silence complement each other into one unity. Two descriptions of the same thing - one from the feminine aspect and one from the masculine aspect. Love vs. Silence Q. Doesn't love precede silence? Can there be silence without love? Why is it together?

A. Silence without love existed before the Big Bang. Before the Big Bang, there was no matter yet. No energy yet. Nothing to bind together. Love binds everything into one unity. But if everything is still at the level of potential, it is not yet realized, so there is nothing yet to bind. There was only silence. I cannot use words, only sounds. How can you say something about nothing? Ommmmm… But after the Big Bang, when matter and energy burst forth into existence, love also burst forth with it. I have never said this. This love continues from then until today to transform this entire universe, all matter, and all energy into one unity, into one living organism. We are part of it, of course. Do you see?

Love exists between bodies. The sun loves the Earth, therefore it pulls, and there is gravity. The Earth loves the moon. The proton loves the electron. But there need to be two to create this dynamic. If there are not two and there is only one potential unity, if there is not yet matter and energy, then there is also no love. There is no place for it to be. For there to be love, bodies need to move against each other. This tension is needed. Q. Do we need two poles? A. It is not a question of need. There are always two poles-the masculine and the feminine. In every situation and every celestial body. In every galaxy, there are always both the feminine and the masculine. Q. Is that the condition for there to be love in space? A. If there were no love, the universe would quickly disperse into infinity and disappear. Like a soap bubble, it would evaporate, vanish, and nothing would remain. Love, or gravity as it is referred to in astronomical terms, is necessary to gather all these celestial factors and keep them in balance with each other.

What is important in this conversation is to recognize that each one of us is part of this. It’s not some theoretical, philosophical concept happening out there in distant galaxies that has nothing to do with us. We have always been part of this, whether we are aware of it or not. We are part of this fabric, influencing and being influenced by it. This is awakening into self-knowledge. To know that I am that. We always have been. The next time we feel alone, it is an opportunity to remind ourselves that we cannot be alone because we are part of this whole thing. I am THAT. Conclusion Embracing the Ocean Within As we reach the end of our journey together, it’s time to reflect on the path we’ve walked and the wisdom we’ve gathered. When the Wave Remembers the Ocean has taken us through the typical evolution of a maturing consciousness as it learns to take responsibility for suffering, grows to overcome fear, realizes the joy of embracing life, and finally, surrenders completely to the profound merging with life itself.

As we conclude, let us remember that the journey doesn’t end here. The insights and practices we’ve discussed are tools to be used and refined as we surf the waves of life. Bitter and sweet, we remain with a whole heart and a willing soul... Many decades ago, a student on the path shared that as she progressed with the teachings, she became more and more available to love. I immediately realized that this was the perfect title for the book I was writing at the time, as that was the most accurate description I could find for the nature of an Awakened Consciousness. What is Awakening? Am I awake? If not, does that mean I am asleep? How is an awakened consciousness different? Is there anything I can do to truly wake up? These are essential questions for any sincere seeker. Indeed, simply asking these questions is often the first sign of awakening itself. This book is dedicated to uncovering the mystery of awakening by providing a clear, simple, and effective structure for self-realization. By exploring the seven levels of your existence, you will be guided to realize the essence of yourself. With each level, a series of practical exercises are provided, designed to transform your reading into a direct, existential experience. Read. Practice. Engage… Wake Up! Introduction

You have chosen to explore yet another "Self-Help" book. You may be wondering, “Do I really need another spiritual book?” After all, you have explored many similar titles, gained insights, and even collected a few memorable quotes along the way. But what has led you to this book? Is it curiosity, a recommendation from a friend, or mere coincidence? Regardless of the reason, you are once again holding a book that aims to address that persistent question that lingers in the back of your mind. While you are skilled at managing this question in your daily routine, it occasionally resurfaces, reminding you of its presence and waiting for you to engage with it purposefully. Perhaps the answers you seek are hidden within these pages. Ultimately, the responsibility for your journey lies with you. While it may seem like I, as the author, am shying away from accountability, the core message of this book is clear: reconnect with the essence of your true self, and from this renewed perspective, you can reshape your life.

As a poet insightfully noted, "This book is not intended to change your life unless you are among the few who are willing to change their life by reading a book..." Are you prepared to embark on this journey together? Qualities on the Path Before delving into this material, it is advisable to reflect on the purpose of your journey. To ensure that the insights and concepts presented here facilitate your personal development, let us consider the following: Every learning process, particularly in the realm of spiritual growth, necessitates certain qualities. What attributes are essential for a spiritual seeker to foster meaningful growth? Qualities such as honesty, curiosity, openness, and flexibility are all vital. However, I have observed that the absence of two specific qualities can significantly hinder the learning process: Humbleness and the Quality of listening. Humbleness

Humbleness is essential, as it is challenging to impart knowledge to those who enter a learning environment believing they already possess all the answers. Those who consider themselves all-knowing are often less receptive to growth and development. Let us acknowledge that we are all capable, intelligent individuals. However, it is important to create space for new insights and perspectives. We should ensure that our learning capacity is not overwhelmed by what we already believe to be true. Let us strive to move beyond the desire to debate, win, or appear more knowledgeable than others. To facilitate this, we can agree that all ideas presented going forward are simply proposals or possibilities. There is no intent to assert an absolute truth or challenge your existing beliefs.

My aim is not to persuade you, nor is it your goal to be persuaded. Instead, consider the following suggestions as options that you may choose to adopt or disregard. The only way to make an informed decision in this regard is to allow a direct experience of the teaching. Embed it into your daily life and see if it works. Remain open to all potential perspectives. One day the seeds of this knowledge might sprout… Quality of Listening The second attribute of a successful seeker is the quality of their listening skills. Listening can often be a mental exercise where incoming information is compared with existing knowledge, leading to agreements or disagreements. However, this form of listening can be limiting, as it tends to filter out unfamiliar or challenging ideas. Consequently, it prevents genuine growth. Authentic growth involves expanding our understanding beyond the familiar and venturing into the unknown.

Therefore, I encourage you to allow your critical thinking to take a step back for a moment. While it is important to process new information, consider suspending its role as a gatekeeper that only permits familiar ideas. By doing so, you can create an open environment for fresh perspectives to enter. This openness will enable you to embrace new insights and facilitate meaningful transformation. Understanding vs. Insight What distinguishes understanding from insight? Understanding fosters change; you learn as you go through life, and you develop into a more mature and wiser individual. Understanding can transform you from a small caterpillar into a larger one. In contrast, Insight facilitates transformation; it can lead you from being a caterpillar to becoming a butterfly. The butterfly represents an entirely new being. Within the cocoon, the caterpillar undergoes a profound transformation, breaking down into a mixture of molecules that astonishingly reconstitute into a completely different organism—a butterfly.

From a spiritual perspective, understanding fills you, while insight empties you. This book invites you to embrace this emptiness. Are you prepared to welcome this emptiness? Remembrance Guruji says: “My work will finish as soon as there is a smile on all the faces”. When will that happen? What else should happen to allow that? How much longer are you willing to wait? Wake up and realize: You are peace You are joy You are love Part I Seven Levels of Existence In this chapter we will explore a method designed to facilitate a renewed understanding of ourselves. This approach encompasses a comprehensive awareness, ranging from the fundamental aspects of our physical body and breath to the more subtle dimensions of heightened consciousness. We will gain new insights into our identities, enabling us to embrace increasingly intricate levels of existence—and to transcend them. We are beginning our journey towards self-discovery. Chronicle of Change

How does real change happen? A change that you can actually feel in your daily life. A change that stays and does not disappear after a week or two. My experience teaches me that real change happens in three phases: Phase I	Phase II	Phase III To achieve meaningful change in life, one must traverse three distinct phases. There are no shortcuts. In the initial phase, it is essential to engage in self-reflection and assess how you perceive yourself. Take a moment to examine your true self. Consider your current state: How are you coping today? What beliefs shape your worldview? What circumstances and fears influence your actions and your choice-making process?

Identify the driving forces in your life, as well as those elements that may be holding you back. Reflect on your motivation to take action. It is crucial to look beyond superficial appearances and the roles you play and to see yourself honestly as you are at this moment. The reflection you encounter may be uncomfortable or even distressing, but without this level of sincere self-observation, moving on to the next phase is not feasible. My personal experience has consistently demonstrated that confronting this first phase, however challenging it may be, is unavoidable if we are truly looking for a lasting change. Therefore, the fundamental invitation of this text is to take a thorough and honest look at yourself. In the second phase, you are invited to ask yourself: Do you truly want to change?

After seeing yourself, truly and honestly, do you still have a genuine longing to change, to transform? This is a tricky question. The obvious answer might be: “Of course! Otherwise, I wouldn’t be here, reading this book, would I?” That’s fine, but, as I mentioned before, it is not that simple. We all want to change until the moment we realize what this change truly means—what it requires; what we are supposed to let go of; what beliefs and conditionings we are invited to shed; how far from our well-built comfort zone we are required to move, a zone so well established over years of avoidance. Suddenly, doubts arise: “I didn’t know this would be the price; this isn’t for me. I find myself in a ‘puddle,’ but I’m used to this puddle; I know the temperature of the mud. Don’t tell me I have wings and can fly out of the puddle. It’s too scary.” Only those who say, “Yes, I want to change, no matter the price,” and truly mean it, can be invited to continue to the third phase.

In the third phase, you can learn how to change. You will learn the theory, be taught different techniques and useful tools, practice, and gradually, you will change. But only those who have gone through the first two phases will experience a truly transformative process. Those who try to find a shortcut, to jump to the ‘bottom line,’ will soon discover that the desired change is not happening and that the techniques they learned in the third phase were ineffective. They will simply join many other techniques collecting dust on some forgotten shelf, patiently waiting for the day you become available to use them properly. The Spiritual Path At the outset of our discussion, it is valuable to consider the nature of spirituality. Spirituality can be characterized as a multi-dimensional space that invites growth, accessible to those willing to engage with profound inquiries, such as: "What is the concept of God?" "What is my purpose on this planet?" "What does love mean?" "What is my destiny?" "Who am I?"

This multidimensional space is crossed by various pathways, including religions, traditions, and belief systems, all of which serve to guide individuals on their spiritual journeys. These paths offer the benefit of collective experience, suggesting that if they have proven effective for others, they may also provide value for you. Rather than navigating this vast and complex spiritual landscape alone, individuals are encouraged to consider established paths that have been tested and have successfully guided others toward personal fulfillment.

It is important to recognize that while a spiritual path can be beneficial, it should not be conflated with the broader spiritual framework it traverses. When one becomes overly identified with a particular path, there is a risk of adopting an exclusionary or dogmatic mindset. A balanced approach to spirituality maintains awareness of the broader context in which it exists. As Guruji aptly articulates, "The distinction between spirituality and religion is akin to the difference between a banana and its peel. The peel preserves the banana's quality and accessibility, just as religion can enhance spirituality for the seeker. However, it is essential to avoid the common mistake of eating the peel and throwing away the banana…" "Who am I?" This fundamental question drives the spiritual journey. Without a fervent curiosity and an unwavering desire for truth, the experience of walking this path may feel akin to navigating without a sail.

The central inquiry, often considered the pivotal question of the spiritual journey, is and will always be: "Who am I?" Without living and acting from a deep understanding of one’s true self, one may experience a persistent sense that something is lacking. To "fully establish one's potential" signifies the realization of the inherent capabilities of the human spirit that resides within each of us. A significant challenge associated with this question is that it does not yield a straightforward answer. To address "Who am I?" one must adopt an indirect approach; a direct answer is too elusive. Leonard Cohen poignantly expressed this idea in his lyrics: "You know who I am, You stared at the sun." He further offers insight: "Well, I am the one who loves changing from nothing to one." To truly know oneself, one must undertake the impossible task of gazing at the sun.

Scriptural texts frequently depict that those who attempt to behold the divine directly face dire consequences. In the Bible, when Moses requests God to reveal His face, seeking reassurance in his mission to lead the Israelites out of Egypt, God responds: "You shall not see my face, for no man can see me and live… my back you may see and not my face.” (Exodus 33:20) This underscores that to understand oneself, one must approach from an alternate perspective. Thus, as we navigate this infinite question, we can employ a method of elimination: Who am I not? This simplifies our exploration. Identifying who we are not—namely, the perceptions we hold about ourselves—provides clarity. In this book, we will focus on unmasking the external layers that obscure our true selves. As these layers are gradually removed, the authentic truth will emerge naturally and gently. The path I propose invites us to utilize the question “Who am I?” as a driving force while offering opportunities to discard false identities. This journey comprises the Seven Levels of Existence.

The Seven Levels of Existence serve as a nuanced extension of the classical triad of Body-Mind-Spirit. It is essential to acknowledge that any method of division is inherently artificial; there is no clear boundary between the Body and the Mind. Nevertheless, this framework enables us to discover subtler aspects of existence, facilitating a deeper awareness of our true Self. In the chapters ahead, we will delve into each level of existence and examine the nature of our relationships with them. We will learn to heal these relationships and transcend limitations, fostering peace and harmony within ourselves and the world around us. Seven Levels of Existence The 7 Levels of Existence, which are found in each and every one of us are: These concepts are examined in ancient texts, such as the Upanishads and Vedanta.

Navigating the Seven Levels of Existence can be likened to ascending a ladder - one whose base is anchored in the physical realm (Body), while its top reaches toward the spiritual realm (Self). To safely ascend this ladder, it is advisable to allocate time for self-reflection in a space free from external distractions, allowing us to commit to this journey fully. Now is the moment to prepare: close the door, silence your mobile phone, and make a cup of tea. This ritual serves an important purpose; it acts as a declaration: “I am dedicating this time to myself.” It is also crucial to approach the following text with an open mind. The value of this reading lies not solely in the words or the overt message they convey. Instead, the essence resides within the silence that exists between and behind the words. This silence holds the potential for growth and transformation. Attentive readers will find it beneficial to embrace the nuances and implications that extend beyond the text itself. The Body First Level of Existence The Body is not who I am It is the temple where I am hosted.

Our body is the first, most basic level of existence. When asked, “Who are you?” you might instinctively point to your chest and say, “What do you mean? I am me.” The body is our first level of identification: I am my body! But are you really? Here is the first layer you are invited to peel off. Your body is not who you are. It is the temple in which you are hosted, the vessel that carries you. Realizing this means acknowledging that there are two entities playing a role here—you and your body. And where there are two players, there is always a relationship worth investigating. So, at this moment, I invite you to look at and investigate the nature of the relationship you have with your body. Be absolutely blunt and honest; there is no need to paint a false picture, as only you are looking. In your relationship with your body: Are you attentive to your body's needs? Are you responsive to its signals? Are you providing it with the nourishment it truly requires? Examine all facets of this relationship honestly, even if the insights may not be flattering.

The relationship we have with our bodies is too often a mixture of total ignorance and unending demand. We remember the body only when it stops functioning according to our expectations or fulfilling our endless demands and desires. It is almost like an outdated, twisted contract: I will put some food in you (or stuff food in you if I am depressed), and let you sleep once in a while, and you will do what I tell you to do, when I tell you, and how I tell you. When I want to rise, you shall lift me. When I want to get there, you shall walk me. When I am in a hurry, you shall run. Our body patiently carries our endless caprices. For so many years, it has lived in this egoistic, selfish, sometimes violent relationship. Maybe it is time for a change of course. Take a time-out and see what we are doing to our bodies. Show some patience. Show respect. The body as an emotional garbage bin

Let us describe some examples of what our body undertakes: We use our body as our emotional garbage bin. We have never learned what to do with "negative" emotions such as frustration, anger, violence, rage, envy, jealousy, etc. These are emotions we all experience from time to time. Since childhood, we have been taught that it is better to hold them in. If you want to be successful in society, you better learn to hide those negative emotions. Keep them inside. As infants, when we were frustrated and cried (not knowing other means of communication), Mother came and whispered in our ears: “Now…now, don’t you cry…” A new conditioning is born: “In order to receive the love I need, I better keep it inside…”

Since then, we have gathered and suppressed so many negative emotions. The body continues to accumulate these unexpressed emotions month after month, year after year: more frustration, disappointment, anger, and rage. If we don’t allow all this stress to wash out of the body from time to time, eventually, the body reaches the end of its capacity to accumulate, and a physical symptom arises. It can start with some minor effects: a headache or nausea, fatigue, or a sleepless night. What does the average person do when these happen? We usually ignore the symptoms or take a pill since we are too busy to listen to our bodies. We have some important work to finish or a family duty to complete, or some other, “more important” issue to attend to. Now is not the time to get sick. When we ignore this body’s cry for attention, the body will try to do the work alone and heal itself. Miraculously, in most cases, the body might be successful—at least for a short while. But sooner or later, the barrel will overflow, and things will start spiraling out of control.

In this state, a whole range of psychosomatic illnesses can develop: diabetes, ulcers, high blood pressure, heart failure, and even cancer. Modern science now recognizes stress as the major cause of illness in the world. Some say the only cause of illness. I am here for you, my body. What can I do for you? So, what can we do? First of all, it is time to change your attitude and remember: The body is the temple in which I am hosted. A temple! It’s time to treat your body with more care and attention, as you would a temple. Instead of constantly asking and demanding what the body can do for you, now you can start asking what you can do for your body. Change your attitude to: “I am here for you. What can I do for you?”

This new attention we give to our bodies reveals a whole world of secret knowledge. It is secret simply because we have not been listening to our bodies. The body is an ancient being, a result of 13.7 billion years of evolution (give or take a year or two). There have been so many trials and errors to produce this amazing organism. So much so that it will take many years before we can fully understand its wonders, if at all. Reconnect with the body’s wisdom The human consciousness, by comparison, has existed for how long? It depends on when you start counting. Let’s say around 300,000 years ago when the first Homo sapiens walked the earth. On that time scale, it is not even a second in comparison to that of the body. So much knowledge and wisdom lie in our body, and yet we almost always prefer to listen to our intellect rather than to our body. We indulge in our mind’s beliefs and conditionings rather than listen to what our body knows. It’s as if Bill Gates is trying to teach us how to operate a computer, but instead, we prefer to take advice from Charlie Chaplin.

There is a whole range of holistic methods to diagnose the body, such as Kinesiology and Ayurveda. These methods can tell what is right and good, healthy or unhealthy, for each individual. Holistic medicine is based on the understanding that “the body knows” and just requires a good listener. A mature consciousness develops listening capabilities to the body and learns to acknowledge its messages. The body knows if what I am eating now is good for me or not. It knows if the cigarette I smoke now is good for me or not. It knows if I truly need another glass of alcohol or if I’ve had enough.

The question always remains: Do I stop and listen to what my body is telling me, or am I using it as my own private garbage bin? The body also knows if the situation I am presently experiencing is what I need right now or not. It knows if my choice was the right one or not. (Yes, there is a clear and distinct way to identify a “right” choice from a “wrong” one. In the second chapter, you can read more on that, but I can already give you a hint: right choice = expansion, wrong choice = contraction.) Stop ignoring and start listening So, what to do? Stop ignoring and start listening. Create spaces in your endless task-oriented schedule. Close your eyes, and look inside. Tell your body: “Hi there, I’m here for you. What can I do for you?” The body might be baffled in the beginning, but soon enough, it will get used to this refreshing approach and will respond to the new interest in its well-being. The body will talk to you in its own unique language and tell you about its wants and needs, like what is right for it, what it needs to eat, how much it needs to sleep, etc.

It is important to remember: Since the body is an ancient machine, it takes time to change. Don’t try to hurry it by demanding instant results. A change in diet, for instance, can produce meaningful results only after several weeks. One who rushes the process will soon find himself believing thoughts like: “This doesn’t work,” or “I need something else…” Be patient with your body Unlike our consciousness, the body can’t make quantum leaps. Our body takes time to get used to changes. If you have had an inspiring insight that has led to a transformation of consciousness, you might have discovered that the body still reacts as it used to. Even though the reaction of the body may not be compatible with your newly gained awareness, be patient. The body will soon follow. It will just take a little longer, and for a good reason; it has been carrying your burden all these years. Now it is time for you to show your body some patience. Reduce the level of stress in the body

Another challenge of a maturing consciousness is to reduce the stress level in the body. The energy (or Prana) that stress accumulates always comes at the expense of nurturing the body. Stressful people are always exhausted, and usually on the brink of collapse. Stress consumes our energy resources and does not allow us to live our lives fully. Are you familiar with the “shaking leg” syndrome? People sit and do nothing, but their leg keeps shaking and swaying. This is an example of a body that burns energy when stressed. The more we lower the stress level in the body, the fuller our energy reservoirs will be, and the more available we will become to experience life in all its complexity and splendor. Later in the book, we shall discover the reasons for stress accumulating in the body and the methods recommended to reduce it. Body as the Source of Happiness The body is our direct interface with the material world. It is the physical expression of your Self.

Through the body, you experience the world around you. Your five senses collect endless information about life. Through the body, you experience pleasure and pain. The trap appears when you identify sensual pleasure as the source of happiness. Then you become addicted to the physical experience that the body produces. You feel satisfied and happy when you eat sweets. So, you eat more sweets, hoping to maintain this feeling of happiness. But how many sweets can you eat? Eventually, you will feel sick. Happiness does not hide there. You feel satisfied and happy when you see beautiful sights and nice buildings. You travel further and further away. How far are you planning to go? For how long will this voyage continue? Eventually, all buildings look alike. The sights become dull. Happiness does not hide there. You feel satisfied and happy when you hear nice music. You go to concerts. You listen to music at home, in the car, on your phone, or in the office. How much music can you hear? Eventually, music becomes background noise, an escape from silence. Happiness does not hide there.

You feel satisfied and happy when you smell nice fragrances and expensive perfumes. You buy another bottle; you burn another incense. How much can you smell? Soon enough, you do not smell anything, or fragrances begin to make you feel nauseous. Happiness does not hide there. You feel satisfied and happy when you touch. You find comfort in touching or being touched. You desire more and more. How much can you touch? It becomes a bottomless pit. Happiness does not hide there. Instead of being addicted to the information entering through the five senses, wake up and see: YOU are the source of joy and happiness Your senses help to transform the happiness that is already within, to be felt and experienced in the physical world. Looking at a flower and smelling its fragrance is an opportunity to experience the happiness within. Touching, hearing, smelling, and tasting are all opportunities to experience the happiness that already lies within. Guruji says:

“A dog enjoys a dry bone and can chew on it for hours. The bone itself has nothing. But it injures the dog’s gums, so actually, the dog enjoys the taste of its own blood…” You are the happiness and satisfaction you long for. Just relax. A free consciousness is a consciousness that realizes: I am not my body, The body is but the temple hosting me Practice: Now that you are available to yourself, allow 10 minutes to quietly experience the body. Disconnect phones and other potential destructions. Ensure that no one and nothing will interfere with your quality time with yourself. Scan the QR code to the 7 Layers – Guided meditations and simply follow the recorded instructions. Link to a guided meditation about the BODY The Breath Second Level of Existence The breath is not who I am. It is the bridge between my inner and outer worlds. The breath is the second layer of existence. Like most factors that have an extreme influence on our lives, the breath is usually ignored and forgotten.

Like most important factors, we remember the breath only when it disappears, such as when we are startled and suddenly lose our breath. Only then do we remember that we are breathing. The breath is the very basis of our existence. The first thing we do when we come into this world is breathe in. And the last thing we will do when we depart from this world is breathe out. We return our breath to the source. In Hebrew, the same word is used for breath and soul. This is also true in Sanskrit. Between the first and last breath, our whole life happens. You can say the same thing about the breath you are taking right now. Take a deep breath in. Really—just do it. Fill your lungs with air. Don’t be shy; there is enough for all of us… and let go. A whole life just happened between your in-breath and out-breath. Why? Because life happens Now! We can easily chant this phrase, but when have we actually allowed ourselves to live it? Life only ever happens now

Life is never in the past. The past is merely a historical film about what already happened. Life is not in the future either. The future is merely a fictional movie about what might happen. Now is the only time when life actually occurs. Throughout history, great spiritual teachers have dedicated their entire teachings to this point alone. Be in the present moment How? Just take a deep breath in, return to your center, and relax. Breath is the royal carriage that carries you back home, time and time again, back to this moment, because it happens Now. Not earlier and not later. I cannot ask you to breathe five minutes ago or 15 minutes from now. You can only breathe right now. At this stage, I would encourage you to practice this mindfulness exercise:

Anytime during the day, when you find yourself carried away by a movie about the past or the future, and ask yourself how to get out of this endless movement, the answer will always be waiting under your nose: take a deep breath…and relax. Use the breath and guide your attention back to the present moment. Become aware of how the breath is happening in the present moment, and from that awareness, expand to your surroundings and the world around you. Notice: when you are in the present moment there are no worries, no anxieties, no remorse or regrets. Breath as a Bridge The breath is also a bridge between the external, physical world of matter and the body, and your internal world of thoughts and emotions (Mind).

Every emotion affects the breath differently. When you're nervous, your breath is shallow and rapid. When you're calm, it's slow and deep. Have you noticed that happy breaths tend to be longer inhales than exhales, while sadness has the opposite pattern? Each emotion or thought projected in your Mind expresses itself differently in the physical body through your breath. This usually happens unconsciously and involuntarily. If we're not paying attention, these subtle changes can be easily missed. Here's a mindfulness exercise to try: When you're overwhelmed by emotions, pleasant or unpleasant, focus on your breath and observe how it changes. These changes may be subtle but see if you can characterize them. The breath acts as a bridge between your inner and outer worlds. Usually, traffic flows one way: from thoughts and emotions to the physical world. But since this bridge exists, why not use it as a two-way street?

The realm of thought and emotion can feel uncontrollable. There's not much we can do about the constant stream of thoughts, feelings, and sensations flowing through our consciousness. They come and go uninvited. Medications like Prozac may offer a temporary solution, but there's a simpler way: learning to use your breath effectively. Correct breathing can bring change to your inner world. If a troubling emotion disrupts your peace, you can use specific breathing techniques to change how you feel. A bothersome thought? Breathe it out. If nervousness has affected your breath pattern until now, you can change that pattern and discover you're not nervous anymore. It might sound simple, but it works. The Breath can also help your body eliminate toxins and accumulated stress, as discussed in the previous chapter. Many traditions use breathwork as their primary tool for personal development and self-realization. The Art of Living organization (www.artofliving.org) teaches effective breathing techniques – highly recommended! A free consciousness is a consciousness that knows:

I am not my breath. The breath is but the bridge between my inner and outer worlds. Practice: The preparation is the same for each practice. Take some quiet quality time with yourself. Best to repeat these practices every day or two. Take a deep breath in… and let go. Link to a guided meditation about the BREATH: The Mind Third Level of Existence I am not my Mind. The Mind is the inner screen on which experiences are projected. The third level of existence is the mind.

The mind is the screen on which your experiences are projected. The mind collects information gathered by our five senses during the body's interaction with the outer world. It combines it with information from your inner world, such as thoughts and emotions. From this collage of information, the mind constructs an experience. For instance: The body tells the mind that the legs feel such, the bottom and back feel such, and the mind synthesizes this information to tell you that you are sitting. Certain chemicals are produced in your brain and felt by your body, and the mind interprets this as excitement, happiness, nervousness, etc. Limitations of the Mind

It is important to realize that the mind is a problematic instrument if we rely on it to understand what is happening. Because of its limitations, it produces a narrow and distorted picture of reality, as we shall soon discover. Yet, we rely on it almost exclusively when trying to create a coherent image of reality, and thus we move through life like a blind person in the dark. Research confirms that the mind allows only a small fragment of what is happening to penetrate our conscious awareness. To put it in numbers, the body is exposed to approximately 400 billion bits of information per second. Of these, the mind only allows 2,000 bits per second to reach our awareness. This is quite an extensive screening process.

Why does the mind do this? That’s a good question. Perhaps it is because it is programmed to bring to our consciousness only what is most relevant and useful for our survival. By doing so, it prevents information overload. Since our consciousness is not yet fully developed, it would not be able to cope with the enormous complexity of what is out there. If the floodgates were completely open and our consciousness was inundated with all that information without proper preparation, a state of mental collapse would be a real danger. Research in the field of spiritual trauma has shown that consciousnesses awakened too early, without proper preparation, and exposed to the incredible intensity of the present moment, often could not cope and simply collapsed. Such crises can lead to neurosis and even loss of sanity. This is another good reason to avoid the irresponsible use of drugs.

The mind acts as a regulator for this excessive flow of information. It is guarding us, keeping us alive and sane, but the price we pay is that we receive only a distorted and partial picture of what is really happening every moment, around us and within us. Maturity of consciousness means improving our mind's ability to deliver more and more of what is happening to our conscious awareness. Phenomena that we associate with the mystical aspects of life—clairvoyance, intuition, future telling, aura seeing, and so forth—are simply ways of perceiving reality as it happens around us all the time, but usually unseen by our eyes, or rather, our minds. Research has found that our eyes see much more than our minds translate into an experience. The eye sees without judgment or preconception. But for the mind to allow this stream of information from the eyes to be translated into an experience, it needs to be familiar with what the eye sees. It needs to hold within it the possibility that such a sight can exist and compare patterns.

You might be familiar with the story about Columbus’s ships. The story goes that as the ships approached the shores of America, the local Indigenous people could not see them. Their minds did not hold ships as a pattern that might exist, so they were simply erased from their perception. Only after the Shaman investigated the ripples in the ocean and slowly got used to the idea of clipper ships floating on the horizon could his mind finally grasp the notion that there was something out there, he had never seen before. He could then slowly realize the image of ships. Then, after telling his community about the spectacle floating on the water, others could gradually see the ships as well because by then their minds held the concept of a ship.
