Eventually, humanity arrived and blessed this experience with meaning through its consciousness. Humanity could define harmony versus disharmony and appreciate beauty versus ugliness. “…And God saw that it was good.” Suffering does not allow us to fill our experience with meaning

But humanity can also withhold this unique added value from God! Withhold this unique spice from the dish. How? By not experiencing reality. When do we not experience reality? When we suffer. Suffering is born from the gap between what is and what you want it to be. See how it all connects? Suffering is born from that gap; suffering is born not from the experience itself but from your inability to embrace it. You fight it and resent it because of your preconditioning, of labeling it as “bad.” “Pain is bad; it should disappear. When can I be happy? When this pain disappears.” So, you experience pain, and because you reject it, you also experience suffering.

Pain can be experienced without suffering when you see it for what it truly is: an event projected onto the screen of your mind, which you are invited to experience at a given moment. If you are unwilling to surrender to this event, then you cannot fully be with the pain, fully utilize this opportunity life has given you to know pain. Then you choose to experience what isn’t instead of what is. What happens? You miss the chance you received to let God experience reality, experience what is, experience God as pain through you, right now. This is why the spiritual path, and so many spiritual teachers, try to persuade us to cease suffering. See how beautiful this is? Only when you cease suffering can you be available to do what you came here to do: To allow God the opportunity to experience itself in matter, as matter, through you. There is a nice quote that says: “God told man: In you, only one can reside, either You or Me. Now, decide….” What do you decide? Walk Around in Circles

Q: I find myself mixing in other people’s lives and affairs, in their spaces, and I see other people do the same to me. So far, I only observe: “My space”, “His space." I see how we stumble freely into each other’s circle, uninvited. This is where my observation is currently set. This is where my investigation is. A: Do you know when we step into someone else's circle? Q: After someone steps into ours? When he lets us in? Once Byron Katie said that there are three types of circles you can step into: yours, others, and God's. Usually, we are busy in external territories. And every time you step out of your own circle, you create disharmony. A: Are you aware of the dynamics that occur when individuals enter each other’s personal space? This often arises from the perception of distinct boundaries, characterized by “my space” and “his space.” When we adhere to this belief, it can lead to unintentional overlap and conflict. This concept of separation, as discussed by Byron Katie, can be seen as an artificial construct. Q: Please explain…

A: Byron Katie tells us that we can find ourselves in one of three circles: mine, yours, and God’s. If we step outside of our own circle, we create disharmony for ourselves and our environment. What does it mean to be in “someone else’s circle”? When I hear myself say something like, “Rafael should understand…,” I wander into his circle. If I hear myself saying, “Rafael should have been a wiser dog…” (Rafael is our dog. I once joked that we have a “love-hate” relationship; he loves me, and I hate him… just kidding!), whose circle am I in now? God’s circle, isn’t it? Because it was God/Reality that created Rafael the way he is. Reality consistently shows us that this dog is exactly as he is and not different. So, Byron Katie distinguishes between you, the other, and God to constantly bring the focus back to ourselves. That is the main objective of her work: to help us stop complaining about the situation and instead use it as a mirror reflecting ourselves back to us. This is her central message. You, others, and God - are ONE

However, this distinction is somewhat illusory. I, along with others and a higher power, comprise different perspectives of the same fundamental essence. Q: The main question is on which circle can I truly influence, and on which I cannot. Otherwise, I am just wasting energy. A: The answer is that there are no circles you cannot influence. A better question to ask is: What is your motivation for wanting to change or influence something in the first place? Are you aiming to influence something because of some hidden agenda, driven by your belief that only after these changes become similar to your images and ideas, can you truly be happy? Then you are condemning yourself to a life of misery, frustration, and suffering. Let’s keep the starting point of this discussion clear before it gets lost amidst all these ideas. Three circles: yours, others, and God’s. All three are simply aspects of the exact same thing. This does not contradict Byron Katie’s work but complements it.

When I stop artificially separating myself, the other, and God, I find that you, me, and God are one. I find that God exists in me (through meditation), as well as in the other (through love), and in the space between us (as unity). Q: Explain what you mean by "Me, the other and God are one". What does it mean that there are no boundaries between people? A: There are no real boundaries, only the artificial ones we create. Let us recall the story of the ocean and its waves, which is very clear to me. Like the waves, which are not truly separated by any real boundary, we are all unique and special expressions of the same thing: the ocean. We, too, are beautiful, unique expressions of divinity, of oneness. Q: You might say that there are no boundaries. That’s nice as an idea, but here there is such a boundary.

A: No, the fact that the wave forgets the ocean does not separate it from the ocean. We may remember or forget reality, but reality continues regardless. Like the wave that remains part of the ocean even if it doesn't remember it, we, too, are part of oneness, even if we become confused along our path. Read the chapter about Unity once again. Q: It sounds as if the Consciousness is separating us. A: Consciousness does not separate. The Ego does. Consciousness, in its true essence, is unifying and all-encompassing, connecting us to the larger whole. It is the Ego, with its sense of individuality and separation, that creates divisions and barriers. While the Ego focuses on "me" and "mine," Consciousness recognizes the interconnectedness of all existence. Thought vs. Consciousness Q: What is the difference between Thought and Consciousness?

A: Consciousness allows us to be aware of a thought. A thought is simply an event experienced in the mind, like a sensation or an emotion. When we are conscious of these events, it is as if the movie spectator has awakened and is watching whatever is projected onto the screen. A constant flow of emotions, sensations, and thoughts is projected onto this screen. Consciousness is aware of all of this. This experience then receives meaning in the intellect. So, consciousness exists in the space between the mind and the intellect. Do you see what I mean? Q: The Self does not possess a consciousness? A: In the seventh layer—the Self—we experience the dissolving of our small mind, which used to experience life within a personal, separate, and limited context. It dissolves into the Big Mind. A consciousness of lack dissolves into a consciousness of abundance. When the Big Mind is experienced, there is no “I” anymore. There is something greater, eternally radiant with grace—an essence that was never born and will never die.

Why is this relevant to what we are doing here? We are engaged in a personal evolution almost entirely aimed at helping us stop suffering. Have you noticed that? The spiritual path invests resources designed precisely for that purpose—to help you end your suffering. But these resources are not there for our personal gain. Or so that our personal lives can become more pleasant. This might be a side effect, but it is not the primary purpose. Think about it this way: from the perspective of eternity, it truly doesn’t matter whether “I” choose to suffer or enjoy. In the blink of an eye, the “I” will disappear, and someone else will take my place. The wave is destined to crash, in 20-30 seconds, or in 70-80 years. It is the same for eternity. The ocean continues. The one who truly benefits from you ceasing your suffering is the one who placed you here in the first place. Because now you are fulfilling your existential purpose, which is to provide that One with the opportunity to experience itself in matter, as matter, through you.

Q: But only when I stop suffering can He do that? When I suffer, can’t He experience Himself through me? A: When you suffer, that One cannot experience itself through you in what is, because your consciousness is focused not on what is, but on what is not. Suffering arises from resistance to the present moment, a fixation on stories, expectations, or regrets that pull you away from the reality unfolding now. When you suffer, you experience what isn’t—what you believe should have happened, or what might have been. This attachment to illusion, to a fantasy shaped by the mind, obscures the richness of what is truly present. In the meantime, the opportunity to embrace the fullness of life—its beauty, its lessons, its authenticity—is lost. Freedom from suffering begins when you release these constructs and allow yourself to align with the raw, unfiltered experience of now, where life unfolds in its purest form. Now you are available to fill THAT with meaning! My True Potential

Q: I have many dreams, and I find myself drowning in them. I invest some energy here and there, but unable to focus on any one of them. I feel I don’t fulfill my highest calling, which is to feel good about myself and be full. I am convincing myself that I feel good about it, but in reality, I am unhappy. A: I invite you to revisit the chapter on fear. The only reason we are unwilling to fully commit to what we are doing is fear. On the spiritual path, we are trained to realize our full potential, to avoid the feeling that we are wasting time here and there, not doing what we are meant to do. To discover how to fulfill our full potential, we must first understand what our full potential truly is—the highest potential of the human spirit within us. Q: At my young age that’s a bit difficult. A: Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, my teacher, reached complete self-realization at a younger age than you. Don't apologize for being young. Many of us in this circle would love to be in your shoes.

What does it mean: the full potential of the human spirit within us? The spiritual path arose to help us answer these questions: Who am I? What are the true driving forces within me? A seeker on the path is exposed to the infinite potential of life, of their true Self. On the way to this realization, we become reacquainted with the nature of our relationships, our motivations for doing what we do, the reasons we avoid doing what we don't do, and the beliefs, concepts, and fears that shape our identity. For instance, a relevant lesson to your question is that of "Fear vs. Surrender." How much do I allow myself to surrender and fully commit to my choices, versus the fears that hold me back? How much do I allow myself to be 100% present with whatever my choices bring? The more connected we are with our true nature, the more our motivation in life transforms

The deeper our connection with our true nature, our essence, the more our motivation in life transforms. This happens to everyone. We used to identify ourselves as someone whose motivation was based on the idea that we don't have enough, that we need to gain something from the external world. Or perhaps we identified as someone driven to protect what little we own, lest it be taken away. As our consciousness develops, we realize this is not so important. We discover that our motivation changes. The reason we wake up in the morning and jump out of bed is no longer based on “What can I gain?” but evolves to “What can I offer? Where can I find opportunities to share the vast richness I have found within?” Q: That is assuming that you found one… A: If you haven't found it yet, that’s a sign you haven't searched deeply enough, because our true nature, the treasure of our essence, does not change. It is present within each and every one of us, all the time. Q: And if you did not find it yet, you cannot give to others?

A: You can. But then the giving might be impure, based on selfish interest or a hidden agenda. You might still be caught in the trap of “What will I gain from this?” I ask you: What will you gain from it? If you give in order to receive something, that is a trap. Q: When my preconception is that my cup is still half full, the giving is always from a limited and conditioned place; a place that keeps monitoring how much it gives, so my cup will not turn empty. A: Yes. But when you discover your essence as the fountain itself, the cup is revealed to be merely the instrument through which you distribute that abundance, rather than a frame that limits and defines your existence. Got it? Q: If I can refer to the cup metaphor, I feel that many times I give wholeheartedly to others, but not to myself.

A: The fact that you are now aware of this—that you neglect yourself, are inattentive to yourself, unsupportive of yourself, and that you need to find ways to refuel yourself—that awareness alone is a powerful position to be in. You have already done two-thirds of the work. Think of all the people who make this same discovery at the age of 60 or 70. You can now understand that, from this perspective, there is no difference between you and others. If selfless giving is still being avoided, whether to yourself or to others, it means there is still some work to be done. Death and Guilt Q: You said that we influence all the circles, ours and the others. What about death, then? Are we affecting other people’s deaths? Can someone die by the mere fact that I thought about it? Wished for it? Or maybe I do not have such an effect after all?

A: You know, my experience has taught me that the most significant and beautiful things in life are those imbued with a sense of mystery. If I can fully “get it,” it loses its charm. The things you cannot understand or grasp with your intellect are what add flavor to life, whether it be love, intuition, inspiration, or an inexplicable event that suddenly occurs and leaves you in awe. Therefore, I won’t attempt to explain why some people live and others die. I will simply add a dose of humility to this. We all are influencing our reality, and being influenced by it, as we are always a part of it. But exactly HOW, will always remain a mystery. Q: The question is: do I possess influence over death? Can I influence the time of death? It happened to me in the past that I could foresee in advance death, and then this anxiety rose in me; maybe I'm responsible for this death? I blamed myself.

A: Blame is a completely separate issue. Blame has nothing to do with death or your influence. Blame arises within you when you are convinced that something is a mistake and that it shouldn't have happened. Then, blame and guilt follow. This is true for anything, not just death. We experience guilt about ourselves, or we blame others when we refuse to surrender to reality. We cling to some ideas we have about how reality should have unfolded. “He shouldn’t have died, certainly not at this age…” as if God made a mistake. Q: I do not understand if the death happened since I saw it coming, or if I saw it coming because it should have happened. A: The best answer you will hear today is: “I don’t know…” Guruji says: “The entire spiritual journey is a journey from a firm ‘I know’ to a beautiful ‘I don’t know.’” Free yourself from the idea that reality might become confused. You will find a guilt-free life ahead of you. Blame and remorse are based on ideas you hold in your mind—ideas you prefer over reality. They will always invite more suffering.

Out there, beyond ideas of right and wrong, there is a field. I’ll meet you there Q: I sympathize with the place she comes from. If she knows whether she influences or not, it might assist her personal growth. A: The need to grasp and understand must dissolve before we can truly grow and be free. It is one of the main obstacles. We must realize that we cannot know everything. The world is far more mysterious than what we can comprehend with our limited minds. We may have occasional flashes, intuitions, or moments of clairvoyance—openings from the small mind to the Big Mind, connections that we can then interpret. Q: I'll tell you a story that happened to me. My father passed away after an argument we had. For years I lived with this guilt that he died because of me. A: So, let us take a deep breath in… and let go. Perhaps you are familiar with Rabi Akiva’s words: "All is foreseen, yet freedom of choice is given" (Jewish Talmud, Pirkei Avot, Ethics of the Fathers, 3:15)

We are influencing everything, and we are influenced by everything, as we are an inseparable part of unity—waves in the ocean. Some of us remember this and live as a manifestation of the divine interest (to experience itself in and as matter through us, here and now), while others tend to forget and live from the small mind, representing a limited perspective based on fear, lack, and defensiveness. We all influence reality constantly—those who remember and those who forget. If you act from a place of harmony and love, you create a harmonious reality. If you act from a disharmonious place of suffering and fear, you create disharmony around you. If you transmit the energy of anger, rage, or frustration, life will present you with ample opportunities to experience those emotions. This is the meaning of “intentions create reality.” If we come from a space of fullness and abundance, a place where we realize we have everything and everything is ours, then we will discover that the world is an endless continuum of opportunities to share this love.

Q: It is not like that. I also like to think that the love I give is the love I'll receive. But sometimes reality proves me wrong. I have a lovely friend who was accused of sexual harassment by one of his patients. So what? Did he invite this reality?

A: One who acts from the Big Mind and one who acts from the Small Mind both influence reality. What is relevant to investigate on the spiritual path is this: From where do you act when creating change or influencing reality? You will discover that you are granted the freedom to act from either perspective. Even God cannot force you to choose one over the other. And yet, even with this freedom, all is foreseen; we influence exactly as we are meant to, and reality unfolds precisely as it should. People are born and die at precisely the right time—not a second too late or too early—even if our limited small minds perceive it as cruel. “What did a three-year-old child do to deserve to die? How is that just?” But ultimately, reality is stronger than any value or idea we hold in our minds. Three-year-old babies do die. “Why does someone who does only good deserve this?” Freedom means becoming an expression of truth

We do not know, and it is good that we do not know. It is intended that we would not know. Our fruitless attempts to understand ensure a life of frustration that ends with a sense of total failure. These attempts prevent us from experiencing freedom. Freedom does not mean intellectually understanding truth, life, or reality. That is impossible. Freedom means becoming an expression of truth and reality. Stop arguing with reality—that is freedom. Pain vs. Suffering Q: Are pain and suffering the same? A: Suffering is born and raised in the gap between what is and what you thought it should have been. Suffering arises not from the pain itself but from your resistance to pain—from the belief that pain shouldn’t happen: “Only when it disappears can I be happy.”

Pain is the phenomenon you are currently experiencing. If you avoid the phenomenon, you suffer. If you are unwilling to surrender to the pain, you cannot experience it fully, as you could if you chose to surrender. Then you experience both pain and suffering. You place yourself in opposition to reality. And then what? You miss the opportunity to allow that one to experience what is, in the present moment, through you. See how beautiful this is? That is why the spiritual path invites you to let go of suffering. Suffering is resisting the pain caused by our interpretation of pain. Q: And then we get carried away to the circle of emotion-thought-sensation. Now we are invited to remember not to get hooked to this vicious circle. A: Well, it is about time, isn't it? What is Jealousy? Q: Is jealousy pain or suffering?

A: Jealousy is a specific idea that generates an emotion—an idea that creates pain and suffering when you believe it. It is the idea that I should have what he has—a type of fear. You believe an image of an object or reality that only when materialized can you be happy. Like fear, it causes contractions in the body: “Oh dear, I might not get what I deserve.” We are hooked on the belief that something else should have happened for us to be happy. The insidious seed of “As is, this is/I am not good enough” poisons you from within. So, you focus on trying to convince the world to conform to your ideas. Trying to push the world is destined to fail from the start. Even if, by some extraordinary cosmic event, the world did align with where you thought it should be at a given moment, it would immediately shift and move along a different course. Your happiness becomes a fleeting flash: “Hey, I’m happy… oops, it’s gone.” I hear women say they were truly happy only when their babies were placed in their arms by the midwife. Once or twice in a lifetime—that’s it? Is that all we deserve?

The spiritual path invites you: “Just relax, let go, come back to what is, and let go of the idea that it shouldn’t have happened.” “She shouldn’t have died.” “This shouldn’t have happened to him.” Then you will discover reality as an expression of joy, of perfection, of divinity—here and now. Q: I can translate it to my marriage, which was based on the idea that: ‘This moment should change’. "The children are too young now; we cannot go out and enjoy ourselves, so we'll go for some necessary shopping instead. Maybe later in a few years, we can go out on a date." We didn't realize that shopping was what life handed over for us to enjoy. "We will do this and that, and later we can enjoy." But we could enjoy what we were doing together. Everything we did was not good enough because something else, better, was waiting behind the corner. So, we wasted thirty years of marriage, on the idea that something else should happen. A: Incredible. My happiness is my nature and does not depend upon anything or anyone

It will not reveal itself later when circumstances change, because it has got nothing to do with the circumstances. True happiness is not something to be sought outside; it is already within, always present, and unchanging. Circumstances and external events may create temporary ripples in the mind, but they cannot touch the essence of who I am. When I stop identifying with fleeting emotions, desires, and fears, the ever-present joy of my being shines effortlessly. This happiness is independent, eternal, and self-sufficient, requiring no validation or conditions to exist. It simply is. Hmmm? What do you say? The Scenery Benefited Q: I believe the most important lesson in living the moment is that we seldom really do what we are doing. We are too busy with what will happen later, what people have told me, what they might say, what they did to me, and what is still left to do. Instead of doing and enjoying what we are currently involved in, we are busy with other stuff.

A: Let me share a beautiful story that unfolded in this circle a few weeks ago. It was subtle, so you might have missed it. It’s worth revisiting. Someone shared that, since childhood, she had been afraid of a rugged road descending a particular mountain. Each time she had to drive down it, she was consumed by fear and anxiety, preoccupied with what might happen. She told us that the last time she drove that road, she decided to practice what we learn here about dealing with fear and letting go—to be present and surrender. So, she drove down the road this time with her eyes wide open, aware and attentive. “I discovered the road,” she said. “I discovered it was so beautiful. I finally saw the scenery.” What I told her then encapsulates everything you can learn: “The one who benefited was the scenery,” I said. “The scenery gained because, finally, your awakened attention was there, available to experience it and imbue it with a sense of splendor.”

When we are available to experience what is—not what isn’t—whether beautiful or ugly, tall or short, pleasant or unpleasant, we allow reality to unfold. Or, in our new terminology, we allow God to experience itself in matter through us. We become God in the making. But this divine evolution cannot occur when our consciousness avoids what is. Only human consciousness is capable of this avoidance. A cat’s consciousness cannot do this. Cats cannot prevent God from experiencing itself in matter because a cat does not live in hope, bear grudges, or experience frustration. It follows its instincts, always in the present moment. A cat cannot add meaning to the experience; it simply lives what is. This is where we differ. We hold this gift—or punishment: we can choose to experience what is and imbue it with meaning, or we can experience what isn’t and fill it with suffering. Q: Little children are like that. Children don't bear a grudge. They fight and a minute later, make peace and become best friends once again.

A: Please consider her insights; she is a kindergarten teacher by profession. She knows what she’s talking about. A child is connected to the Big Mind simply because they have not yet fully detached from it while simultaneously developing their own small mind. This allows experience to unfold in each moment, even without conscious awareness. As their ego and separate identity evolve, they gradually shift to operating primarily through the small mind. Then the human drama begins. The Reason for Suffering Q: What is the role of suffering? If we say that He created us to experience what is, and not the gap, how come there is suffering in the world? A: Your question is the same as "Why did God toss us out of Heaven?" Q: This I can understand, because He wanted to experience himself in matter through us. But what is the role of suffering?

A: Suffering exists to make us want to break free from it; it creates longing within us. Many people—in fact, most people—embark on the spiritual path because of suffering, searching for ways to end their misery and find solace. “God”, you might say, “kicked us out of Heaven’s doors” so that we would long to return. He gave us a taste, a glimpse, and then: “…Go, be homesick.” This homesickness, this longing, is essential—it is what creates and drives evolution and development. Q: So suffering is the alarm clock? A: You could say that. It is the wake-up call, the stimulus. There are those—not many, but they do exist—who join the spiritual path and engage in spiritual growth not because of suffering but out of sheer passion for meaning, a longing to draw closer to the truth. A fully awakened consciousness does not seek meaning; it is an expression of it The Ultimate Truth Q: You mentioned “Truth”. I have been searching for the truth for many years. The Ultimate Truth that could not be disputed. Can you speak about the ultimate truth? A: I came to realize the Ultimate Truth!

I realized the Ultimate Truth about everything. The Ultimate Truth about everything is… that there is no Ultimate Truth. So, don’t bother searching for one. The present moment is the closest we can get to describing “Truth.” Reality is composed of endless possibilities, all of which are valid. When you choose one, all other possibilities collapse into a single experience, which becomes your reality—the closest approximation of “Truth” you can find. You choose based on instinct, preconceptions, past experiences, expectations, fears, and so on. Most of the time, this choice is made unconsciously. This is the meaning of the phrase: “You are the creator of your own reality.” Ultimately, there is no inherently preferred choice. Ultimately, what you choose has no intrinsic importance. However, it is crucial that you choose and then surrender to your choice and its consequences.

This surrender is crucial because it allows you to fully experience the reality you have created. This undivided experience enables you to imbue your reality with meaning, which is your purpose. Because what you choose to do is less important, a true spiritual teacher would not become involved in questions related to the realm of doing. A spiritual teacher is there only to present the enlightened possibility of existence—a manifestation of the realm of being. Inspiring leaders are unique because of their capacity to convince themselves, and then others, that their choice was the right one. This self-conviction makes them influential and magnetic. Free consciousness is one of the endless possibilities available for you to choose from. When you choose this above all else and rise beyond all self-doubt, you are as enlightened as the holiest of the holy. This is the meaning of the phrase: “You are already free.” And again—what you choose manifests as reality/truth for you. Don’t wait for reality to convince you it is true (good or bad). There is no such validation.

Believe it, embrace it, and it will become true for you. Now go, and change the world. Internal Battle with the Mind Q: I have been preoccupied with questions lately, especially about being present. I call it my internal titanic battle. I am truly struggling, waging war against my mind and the constant stream of nonsense flowing through it. Suppose you were to ask me about my purpose in life, my quest. In that case, it is exactly what you have been talking about—precisely that: the quest to awaken each morning with a genuine sense of freedom, independent of anything or anyone. A: What you seek is not dependent on anything else. It is not dependent on which thought you are currently thinking. The day your thoughts cease to threaten you is the day you will be free from the need to conquer them. Q: And when will that be? A: When you let go of the belief that these thoughts are wrong, or cling to these thoughts believing they are right. Q: And when will that be? A: I don't know. You tell me.

Q: There have been moments of true unity between myself and the space around me. Please forgive me; my whole body trembles when I speak of it. That is what makes life worth living—an overflowing love. Every breath feels perfect. I feel I am in the right place. Singing, dancing, sleeping—all is well. Lately, however, I find my life to be a quest to return to that state. I see the trees, their magnitude and beauty, the wispy clouds in the sky—all this beauty—but it passes me by. I feel like I am faking it, not living the life I am meant to. A: Is that true? Do you realize that clinging to this thought is poisoning you? Q: I know, but I can’t stop it. A: You cannot stop it, and you don’t need to. Thoughts are unstoppable. But they have no power. NO POWER! Q: I feel like I’m trying to empty the ocean with a spoon, struggling against my negative thought patterns. A: Let me tell you how your path of misery will end. Do you want me to reveal it? Your path of misery will end the moment you embrace these thoughts. When you stop fighting them—when you surrender fully and wholeheartedly.

Q: No way! I’ve found that when I believe these thoughts, it’s a bottomless pit; it takes me to the verge of despair. A: Listen, “surrendering” and “believing” are not the same. To surrender means to stop fighting. The fact that a particular thought appears in my mind does not obligate me to believe it. It is just a thought, a phenomenon that arises within me. A moment ago, it was in someone else’s mind; now it is in mine; a moment later, it will move on elsewhere. Q: You mean, meet it without believing it? A: Precisely! Surrender to the present moment. Now, at this moment, this is the thought I am having. You know, during our last silence retreat, I received a note from one of the participants: “What bliss—to think a thought and not believe it!”

What a joy! It is just a thought entering my consciousness. The day I stop believing it, stop fighting it, stop believing that only when it is gone can I be free, happy, or fulfilled (or any other idea I might be holding on to)—that is the day the thought will lose its grip on me. As long as I resist it, it will persist. What I give energy to grows. This is true for everything in life. My resistance keeps it alive and powerful. The day I say, “Please come; I am here for you to be thought. I am the space within which you can exist,” is the day I will meet a thought for what it truly is: another reflection on the screen of my mind. It will come, be experienced, and move on, leaving no trace. I am the gorge through which the water flows. Meditate on that.

A thought is simply an event experienced on the screen of our mind; it has no power over us unless we give it that power. It is as though you believed the robots shooting on a movie screen could actually kill you. When we believe the sequence of thought-sensation-emotion, it becomes our slave driver. But the truth is that we are free. We have always been free. Just let go of the belief that this sequence has any power and therefore needs to change. There is no point in fighting it, just as there is no point in fighting the movement of clouds across the sky. They float; that is their nature. We can fight it or enjoy it; they will continue floating. Q: Perhaps it would be helpful to add a little compassion to this understanding? We have been compelled to have a relationship with our thoughts and feelings since day one. A: You are right; we can add compassion. Just don’t let it devolve into self-pity or victimhood. That will only push you back into the cage. Creativity and Suffering

Q: I used to write songs out of my misery, and lately I do not write. What does it mean? That my suffering is gone? That it is meaningless? A: “If I want to write songs, I better suffer…” It’s an admirable sentiment. Creation born from suffering—there’s a lot of romance surrounding that notion, but very little truth. It has little to do with love if anything at all. In general, romance and love are entirely different things. “Come back to me, I am nothing without you…” That’s not a song that glorifies love; it glorifies dependency and neediness. There is another force, one not based on a constant feeling of lack and deficiency, but on abundance and wealth. We are not well acquainted with it because we seldom experience it in our daily lives. You might call it “inspiration.”

What is inspiration? It is God/nature/reality/present moment itself writing a song through us. Mozart composed divine music at the age of four. When does God write songs through us? When we are hollow and empty. By the way, we are here to sing our song! It doesn’t have to be a song with notes and lyrics. Only we can sing our song. No one else ever has, and no one ever will be able to sing our song for us. It is a unique opportunity. Get on stage and start singing, even if you are out of tune at first. Soon the show will be over, the lights will go out, and the audience will leave. Don’t be fooled by the idea that you can always sing later, at the end of your journey, or when you have learned your lesson, or when you attain enlightenment—only then… You are only one belief away from Awakening You are only a thought away, only one belief away from awakening. Let go of that belief and discover yourself as a free spirit—happy, creative, enlightened, or whatever other idea you hold about who you might be. One day… The Role of a Spiritual Teacher Q: What is the role of a spiritual teacher?

A: The Master reminds us of the context of all our questions. Their purpose is not to answer every question, as each answer inevitably invites new questions. It is not a test of the specialist’s knowledge— “Let’s see if they can handle this question…” In this circle, I find that we don’t emphasize enough why we ask and answer questions. The ultimate purpose of any answer is to bring you back to silence. If you do not reach silence, the answer has missed its mark. As Guruji says: “The role of a spiritual teacher is to turn your question into a wonder.” When you are in a state of wonder, the answer is no longer so important. What remains is silence—an awe-inspiring “Wow…!” The ultimate goal of any answer is to lead you back home to silence. Within this silence lie the answers to all questions. It is the final answer. It is impossible to reach this silence through the intellect. It is much simpler to bypass the intellect and dive directly into the silence—to return to where your journey began and where it will inevitably end. Do you understand? Q: Yes.

A: That’s good… because it’s not meant for intellectual understanding. Perhaps you can explain it to me? Q: So, say it again. A: All the practice, deep analysis, insights, knowledge, and experiences are aimed at achieving one thing: leading you back to silence—the silence that is your very being. Silence is not merely the absence of noise. It is not the opposite of speech. Those who have participated in a silence retreat (highly recommended) know this. Silence is not what happens when you stop talking. On the contrary, when you stop talking, you can hear all the noise in your head. The cessation of speech and the teacher’s invitation to rest within yourself are there to allow you to stop running away from yourself—stop running to words, to understanding, stop your obsession with control, with trying to manipulate reality, or with using this time to check your cell phone or see if others are suffering as much as you. This is an invitation to reconnect with who you truly are, beyond all this noise.

This is what happens when we meditate. When we close our eyes, the first thing we encounter is the noise—the thoughts, emotions, and sensations projected onto the screen of the mind: fears, resistance, physical discomfort, judgments, the ticking clock, other people in the room—all the distractions produced by the internal and external worlds. Why does the realm of phenomena produce these distractions? That is its nature: to change. Meditation means not getting entangled with these distractions—simply listening to them, observing them, without believing them. Now this thought is being thought: “I’ll start meditating as soon as the clock stops ticking. Only then can I meditate.” The thought is projected onto the screen of the mind. If you believe the thought and are carried away by it, you will never experience meditation. You have escaped into the drama again. “When that jerk stops their constantly ringing phone, only then will I be able to meditate.” A new drama is born.

Being in meditation means being present with this internal and external noise without believing it. Sensations, emotions, and thoughts are playing in the playground of your mind. That is not a problem; it is an experience. Slowly, over time, you will find that this white noise gradually subsides and calms down. If you have practiced meditation, you have undoubtedly encountered this phenomenon. Then, what happens? I could tell you, but it would be a spoiler, like revealing the end of a good movie instead of encouraging you to see it for yourself… Never mind, I’ll tell you anyway (but only if you promise to see the movie!).

Then, peeping into consciousness, silence appears—a silence that is always there but usually obscured, patiently waiting for us to become vacant enough to experience it. You may call it the “inner voice”, “intuition”, “truth”, “the divine within”, “the Atman”, or simply “silence”—silence not as the absence of noise but as your very essence. In meditation, this is experienced. The more you allow yourself to be there in silence, without cravings or aversions, the more silence can become an expression of you. You will discover that the next time you meditate, you will find a shorter path home and can dive deeper into the origin of your being. Eventually, you are simply there. Your life becomes an expression of meditation, an expression of what you encountered after letting go of attachment to the sequence of sensation-emotion-thought. A spiritual teacher is there to invite you on that journey home and to light your path along the way. What is in a Drama? Q: Why are we so obsessed with drama? A: What is it about drama that we prefer it over silence?

Q: We are conditioned to believe that if we possess what we see in movies, we will be happy. We didn’t have a choice; we were programmed to believe this. A: Is that true? What would you be without that thought? Q: More free, obviously. A: Ahhh… The distance between you and silence is only one belief away. Let go of that belief. Then there is a new drama to cling to—this time, not the mobile phone, but what life did to me; the place I was born, the culture, the language, the tradition, circumstances, and expectations. Each of us has our own collection of excuses for not being fully present. “My story doesn’t allow me…” All these attachments. “I’ve been through so many difficulties. Please understand: my suffering is justified; it is legitimate.” Q: But how do I become free from it?

A: There are many ways. First, you need a burning desire to be free—a willingness stronger than any need to cling to the drama, to your story. Another way is to become desperate. That might do the trick. I’ve said before: let’s become desperate—truly, one hundred percent, all the way. Let’s let go of the belief that we will ever attain what we dream of. Let go wholeheartedly, into the deepest depths of life. That’s it—this is as good as it gets; there is nothing left to achieve, nowhere to go, nothing to do. Like the Buddha under the Bodhi tree, saying: “That’s it; I’m finished here, done! I will rise no more; here are the keys. I’ve tried, I’ve failed, thank you very much.”

Desperation can be a powerful path, but only if you can be completely immersed in it. Be desperate. It will not happen before you are willing to surrender before you let go of your need for drama, before you love the divine as much as you love the material before you love silence as much as you cling to noise. Until when? Until you recognize the drama as what drives you. “He said this to me; he did that to me; that is why my suffering is legitimate, justified.” Not only justified—it becomes the main reason you wake up in the morning: to show the world why it is important for you to suffer. Who are you? You are the one who suffers. “I am suffering.” Suffering becomes the answer to the question: “Who am I?”

Until when will this madness continue? Please realize: Silence awaits. It is not something you need to find, understand, realize, achieve, or even experience. It is your very being. Silence simply waits in the background of everything we say here. The things I say here have no inherent meaning. These are just words that sometimes resonate and sometimes do not, but they will make no difference if we do not dare to let go, to sink into the silence that hides between the words, between the sentences, and between ideas. Sometimes I feel there is no correlation between the tools I use and the target I aim for. I refer to what is obvious, but as long as I speak about it and you avoid being present by clinging to ideas and concepts, it will be as useful as talking about the weather. Q: What do you mean by “obvious”?

A: You have a headache, so you go to the doctor, and they tell you that you are mistaken—your head doesn’t truly ache. So, you go to a specialist at the best hospital, and they tell you the same thing. Is it obvious or not? What are we arguing about? Your head aches! That is reality. Can you prove it? No, but it is as vivid and clear as the morning sun—you have a headache! As long as you try to break through with your intellect, you are drifting further away. Q: But we have no choice. A: Of course, we have a choice—using silence, for instance. That is why I sometimes recognize how limited my resources are. Because I am a man of words and reason. I am an engineer. I come from a place of analyzing, understanding, and investigating. These are the tools I use. However, I am aware that these tools are not always suitable for the task at hand. They cannot take us all the way.

I am talking, trying to explain, to describe the unattainable… what am I even talking about? Just be silent. Silence is there precisely for this: to replenish you with truth. Don’t wait for the next silence retreat. Create islands of remembrance in your daily routine—a ten-minute ceremony of closing your eyes and diving within. The silence I refer to is not just stopping talking but reconnecting with the essence of what I call “me”—to remember, again and again, the new context from which I meet this world, this life. Not just as a philosophical concept, but from within this expression of silence. To remember because we tend to forget. To remember from your DNA, from your cells.

Then you will find that your life becomes an expression of this silent space. You find that silence ceases to threaten you because silence has become the origin of your experience. How can silence threaten peace? Silence is the home of peace. Our actions and choices become expressions of peace. What is an action motivated by peace? It is an action without personal interest, fear, manipulation, cravings, or attachments. All these are symptoms of noise, can you see that? Q: And they are present here and now. A: There is no other time. It is entirely present. Our choices become expressions of silence, of peace. We are so preoccupied with our choices: “Am I making the right choice?” Especially in modern society, where we are overwhelmed with possibilities. “What should I say to them—this or that? Should I go here or there? Should I learn this or that? Am I making the right choice?” If you are still wondering how to make the right choice, I can offer a powerful tool: Ask yourself: “What would I choose if there were no fear within me? No fear at all!”

When your choice arises from fearlessness, it will be accurate and harmonious. When I act from silence, the choice chooses itself. It is as obvious as choosing between fresh and filthy water when thirsty. There is no real choice to be made. There is the harmonious, accurate thing to do at any given moment. I will drink the fresh water; there is no need to philosophize about it. All this confusion dissipates. I simply do the accurate, harmonious thing at the appropriate time. Simply put, the only and final choice you need to make is whether your next choice will be made by God experiencing itself through you, or by you taking the lead, looking for some personal gain. The rest of the choices will follow naturally. Reconnecting with silence means not just shutting up and continuing the same routine. It means letting go of the world and resting back in the Self. Let go. Q: I find myself in such a space when I sing. I completely disappear into the song.

A: We will discover that when we act from silence, life itself becomes an expression of this merging, of meditation. There is no need to practice meditation to be in meditation. Life is an infinite meditative practice. Consciousness agrees to experience fully and wholeheartedly whatever is. May it be singing, swimming, painting, walking, or simply observing. Divinity is found in the mundane as much as in the abstract. Each of us is meditating our own unique meditation, from where we are to where our heart opens. Being in silence means going directly to the core of the matter. Being in silence means needing no external tools on the path to our destiny. We rest in destiny itself. Q: When you sit in silence, you don’t need any tool to reach it because you are already there. Simply enjoy what is.
